السلام - ذابحا، فقال قوم: هو ذابح للقطع والولد غير مذبوح لحصول الالتئام
وقال قوم: ذابح لا مذبوح له محال وكل ذلك تعسف وتكلف.
أما الأول وهو كونه مناما، فمنام الأنبياء جزء من النبوة وكانوا يعرفون
أمر الله تعالى به، فلقد كانت نبوة جماعة من الأنبياء - عليهم السلام -
بمجرد المنام.
ويدل على فهمه الأمر قول ولده: افعل ما تؤمر، ولو لم يؤمر لكان كاذبا،
وإنه لا يجوز قصد الذبح والتل للجبين بمنام لا أصل له، وإنه سماه البلاء
المبين
وأي بلاء في المنام وأي معنى للفداء.
وأما الثاني وهو أنه كان مأمورا بالعزم اختبارا، فهو محال، لأن علام
الغيوب لا يحتاج إلى الاختبار ولأن الاختبار إنما يحصل بالإيجاب، فإن لم
يكن إيجاب لم يحصل اختبار.
وقولهم العزم هو الواجب محال؛ لأن العزم على ما ليس بواجب لا يجب بل هو
تابع للمعزوم، ولا يجب العزم ما لم يعتقد وجوب المعزوم عليه. ولو لم  يكن
المعزوم عليه واجبا لكان إبراهيم - عليه السلام - أحق بمعرفته من القدرية،
كيف وقد قال إني أرى في المنام أني أذبحك فقال له ولده افعل ما تؤمر يعني
الذبح؟ وقوله تعالى {وتله للجبين} [الصافات: 103] استسلام لفعل الذبح لا
للعزم.
وأما الثالث: وهو أن الإضجاع بمجرده هو المأمور به؛ فهو محال إذ لا يسمى
ذلك ذبحا ولا هو بلاء ولا يحتاج إلى الفداء بعد الامتثال.
وأما الرابع، وهو إنكار النسخ وأنه امتثال لكن انقلب عنقه حديدا ففات
التمكن فانقطع التكليف، فهذا لا يصح على أصولهم؛ لأن الأمر بالمشروط لا
يثبت عندهم، بل إذا علم الله تعالى أنه يقلب عنقه حديدا فلا يكون آمرا بما
يعلم امتناعه فلا يحتاج إلى الفداء فلا يكون بلاء في حقه.
وأما الخامس، وهو أنه فعل والتأم، فهو محال؛ لأن الفداء كيف يحتاج إليه
بعد الالتئام؟ ولو صح ذلك لاشتهر وكان ذلك من آياته الظاهرة ولم ينقل ذلك
قط وإنما هو اختراع من القدرية. فإن قيل: أليس قد قال: {قد صدقت الرؤيا}
[الصافات: 105] . قلنا: معناه أنك عملت في مقدماته عمل مصدق بالرؤيا،
والتصديق غير التحقيق والعمل.
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ن-س-خ (n-s-kh)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To erase, cancel, supersede, or remove something and replace it with another; the effacement of a prior ruling.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal theology, the lifting (rafʿ) of a divine address (khiṭāb) or its entailment (madlūl) by a subsequent address, not a mere clarification of scope.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage denotes actual removal of the ruling; metaphorical (majāz) usage would be taḫṣīṣ (specification), which restricts but does not annul.
- Root: ت-م-ك-ن (t-m-k-n)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To be firmly established, to have power or capacity over something; the state of being able to act.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The actual attainment of the condition enabling performance of an obligation; contrasted with mere theoretical address.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — physical or practical capacity; here used technically for the window of compliance before which abrogation is debated.
- Root: ش-ر-ط (sh-r-t)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: A mark or sign; a condition that must be met for something else to hold.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): A stipulation attached to a command that qualifies its binding force without negating its status as a command.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — a conditional clause; metaphorical — the implicit condition of non-abrogation embedded in every command.
- Sībawayh Rule: Taʿlīq al-Ḥukm ʿalā al-Sharṭ (Suspension of a ruling on a condition) — The predicate is validly attached to a conditional clause even if the condition is not yet realized, as in «إن جاء زيد فأكرمه»; the command exists in the present as a conditional address.
chapters.translation:
I say: The third chapter concerns questions that branch off from the examination of the reality of abrogation (naskh), and they are six questions.

Question: It is permissible in our view to abrogate a command before the subject has attained the capacity to comply (tamakkun min al-imtithāl), contrary to the Muʿtazilites. Its form is that the Lawgiver says in Ramaḍān: "Perform the pilgrimage this year," then says before the Day of ʿArafah: "Do not perform the pilgrimage," for He has abrogated the command from you. Or He says: "Slaughter your son," and he hastens to bring forward its prerequisites, then He says before his slaughtering: "Do not slaughter," for He has abrogated the command from you. This is because abrogation in our view is the lifting (rafʿ) of the command — that is, of its ruling and its entailment (madlūl) — and it is not a clarification that the abrogated matter falls outside the wording of the command, unlike specification (tak͟hṣīṣ). Thus if He said: "Pray forever," it is permissible to abrogate after a year the obligation of prayer in the future — not in the sense that He did not intend by the first wording to indicate all times, but in the sense of cutting off the ruling of the wording after its continuance, since its continuance was conditioned upon the absence of abrogation. So every command is embedded with the condition that it not be abrogated, as if He says: "Pray forever, so long as I do not forbid you and do not abrogate my command from you."

Since this is so, the abrogation of the pilgrimage before ʿArafah and the abrogation of the slaughter before its act are rationally intelligible; because the command before capacity is established, even if it is a command conditioned upon capacity; for the command with the condition is firm, and therefore the commanded person knows himself to be commanded before attaining the capacity to comply. Since the Muʿtazilites did not understand this, they denied the establishment of the command with a condition, as the corruption of their doctrine will come in the Book of Commands. The nearest proof of its corruption is that the prayer-worshipper intends the obligatory duty and the compliance with the command at the beginning of the prayer, and perhaps he dies during it and before the completion of capacity. Had he died before, it would not have become clear that he was not commanded; rather, we say he was commanded with a command restricted by a condition, and the command restricted by a condition is firm in the present whether the condition occurs or not. But they say: When the condition does not occur, we know the negation of the command from its very origin, and that we had merely imagined its obligation. So it became clear that it was not. Thus this question is a branch of that question, and therefore the Muʿtazilites deemed abrogation before capacity impossible, and they also said: It leads to the result that one single thing at one single time in one single respect is commanded and forbidden, good and evil, disliked and desired, beneficial and corrupting. And all that pertains to good and evil, benefit and corruption, we have already nullified.

But there remain for them two paths.

The first path: How can one single thing at one single time be forbidden and commanded in one single respect? In answering this there are two methods.

The first method: We do not concede that it is forbidden in the very respect in which it is commanded; rather, it is in two respects — just as one is forbidden from prayer with ritual impurity and commanded to pray with purity, and forbidden from prostrating to the idol and commanded to prostrate to God, Mighty and Majestic, due to the difference of the two respects.

Then they differed over the modality of the difference of the two respects. A group said: He is commanded with the condition of the continuance of the command, and forbidden when the command ceases; so these are two different states. Another group substituted the phrase "the continuance of the command" with "the absence of the prohibition" or "the absence of the prevention," and the expressions are close in meaning. Another group said: He is commanded to perform the act at the specified time with the condition that he choose the act or resolve upon it; and he is only forbidden when it is known that he will not choose it. And they made the occurrence of that in God's knowledge a condition of this abrogation.

Another group said: He commands with the condition of its being a benefit (maṣlaḥah); and it is only a benefit with the continuance of the command; but after the prohibition it exits from being a benefit. Another group said: He only commands at a time when the command is a benefit, then the situation changes and the prohibition becomes the benefit; and God only commands it with His knowledge that its imposition is a benefit with the continuance of the command; but after the prohibition it exits from being a benefit. Another group said: God only commands it with the knowledge that the situation will change, so that the obligated person resolves upon the act if the benefit remains in the act. All of this is close in meaning, and it is weak; because a condition is something conceivable as existing or not existing. As for what is indispensable, there is no meaning to its conditionality. The commanded person is not commanded except with the continuance of the command and the absence of the prohibition — so how can one say: "I command you on condition that I do not forbid you"? It is as if He says: "I command you on condition that I command you," and on condition that the command attaches to the commanded person, and on condition that the commanded act be originated (ḥādith) or an accident or other such indispensable matters. This does not qualify for conditionality, and it is not like the prayer with ritual impurity or the prostration to the idol, for division applies to those.

Whoever desires this method, the nearest expression is to say: The command of a thing before its time — its ruling may remain upon the commanded person until its time, and it may be removed before its time. So it is permissible to make the continuance of its ruling a condition in the command, and it is said: "Do what I have commanded you, if the ruling of my command is not removed from you by the prohibition of it." So when he is forbidden from it, the ruling of the command has been removed, and he is not forbidden in the very respect in which he was commanded.

The second method: We do not commit ourselves to showing the difference of respect; rather, we say: What we commanded you to do in a certain respect, we have forbidden you from doing in that very respect. There is no impossibility in this, for the commanded thing is not good in its essence or by a description it possesses prior to the command, such that contradiction would arise; nor is the commanded thing desired, such that it would be contradictory for it to be desired and disliked. Rather, all of that is among the principles of the Muʿtazilites, which we have already nullified. If it is said: Since God knows that He will forbid it, what is the meaning of His commanding a thing whose non-existence He knows with certainty, due to His knowledge of the outcomes of affairs? We say: This is not sound if the outcome of His command is known to the commanded person. But if it is unknown to the commanded person and known to the Commander, the command is possible — to test him through resolution and engagement in preparation that prevents him from types of frivolity and corruption, so that by resolution he becomes exposed to reward and by its abandonment to punishment. Perhaps in it there is a gracious kindness (luṭf) and a seeking of good (istiṣlāḥ), as will be verified in the Book of Commands.

It is astonishing that the Muʿtazilites deny the establishment of the command with a condition, while they permit the promise from one who knows the outcomes of affairs with a condition. They said: God promised reward for obedience on condition of the absence of what nullifies it — namely, transgression (fisq) and apostasy (riddah) — and punishment for disobedience on condition of its being free of what expiates it — namely, repentance. God knows the outcome of the affair of one who dies upon apostasy or repentance, yet He conditioned that in His promise. So it is not impossible that He condition in His command and His prohibition. And His conditionality is relative to the servant who is ignorant of the outcome of the affair, so He says: "I reward you for your obedience so long as you do not nullify it by apostasy," while He knows whether he will nullify it or not. Likewise He says: "I have commanded you with the condition of continuance and capacity, and with the condition that I do not abrogate from you."

The second path: On the impossibility of abrogation before capacity. Their saying: The command and the prohibition, in your view, are the eternal speech of God. How can one single speech be a command of one single thing and a prohibition of it at one single time? Rather, how can the raiser and the raised be one, and the abrogator and the abrogated be the speech of God? We say: This points to two difficulties.

One of them: The modality of the unity of God's speech, and this is not specific to this question; rather, in our view it is like their saying: The attribute of knowledge is a single state that encompasses knowledge of infinite details. Its difficulty is only resolved in the discussion of speech (kalām).

As for the second: It is that His speech is one, and it is a command of a thing and a prohibition of it. Had the obligated person known both at once, he could not conceive of believing in the obligation and resolving upon performance, and that would not be more fitting than believing in the prohibition and resolving upon abandonment. So we say: God's speech in itself is one, and relative to one thing it is a command and relative to another it is a report. But it is only conceivable to test through it when the obligated person hears both at two times; therefore we stipulated the interval (tarākhī) in abrogation. Had he heard both at one time, it would not be permissible.

As for Gabriel — peace be upon him — it is permissible that he hear it at one time, for he is not obligated; then he conveys it to the Messenger — peace be upon him — at two times, if that Messenger falls under obligation. If he does not, then he conveys it at one time, but he is commanded to convey it to the community at two times. So he commands them absolutely with peaceful relations and abandoning the fighting of the disbelievers, and absolutely with facing the Sacred House in every prayer; then he forbids them from that afterward, cutting off from them the ruling of the absolute command, just as the ruling of a contract is cut off by dissolution (faskh).

Among our companions there is one who said: The command is not a command before it reaches the commanded person; so it is not a command and a prohibition in one state, but in two states. This too cuts off and repels the contradiction.

Then the decisive proof from the side of revelation (samʿ) for its permissibility is the story of Abraham — peace be upon him — and the abrogation of the slaughter of his son from him before the act, and His saying, Mighty and Majestic: {«And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice»} [al-Ṣāffāt: 107]. For he was commanded with a single act, and he did not fall short in hastening and compliance; then it was abrogated from him.

This has been difficult for the Qadariyyah until they strained in its interpretation and split into factions, seeking escape through five aspects:

One of them: That it was a dream (manām), not a command.

The second: That it was a command, but its purpose was to obligate him to resolve upon the act, to test his inner self in his patience upon resolution; so the slaughter itself was not commanded.

The third: That the command was not abrogated, but God turned his neck into copper or iron, so it did not sever; thus the obligation ceased due to its impossibility.

The fourth: Disputing the commanded object — that what was commanded was the laying down, the placing of the forehead on the ground, and the passing of the knife, not the reality of the slaughter.

The fifth: Denying the abrogation — that he slaughtered in compliance, and the wound healed and closed. Those who go to this interpretation agree that Ishmael was not slaughtered. They differ over whether Abraham — peace be upon him — was a slaughterer. A group said: He is a slaughterer in the sense of cutting, while the son was not slaughtered due to the healing. Another group said: A slaughterer without a slaughtered object is impossible. All of that is strained and forced.

As for the first — that it was a dream — the dreams of the prophets are a part of prophecy, and they knew God's command through it. Indeed, the prophecy of a group of prophets — peace be upon them — was solely through a dream. And the understanding of the command is indicated by the saying of his son: "Do what you are commanded" — had he not been commanded, he would have been lying. And it is not permissible to intend slaughter and the placing of the forehead on the ground by a dream with no basis. And He called it the manifest trial — and what trial is there in a dream, and what meaning is there in the ransom?

As for the second — that he was commanded to resolve as a test — it is impossible, because the Knower of the unseen has no need of testing, and because testing is only achieved through obligation; if there is no obligation, no testing is achieved. And their saying that resolution is the obligatory duty is impossible; because resolution upon what is not obligatory is not obligatory; rather, it is subordinate to the resolved-upon thing, and resolution is not obligatory unless one believes the resolved-upon thing to be obligatory upon him. Had the resolved-upon thing not been obligatory, Abraham — peace be upon him — would have been more entitled to know it than the Qadariyyah. How, when he said: "I see in the dream that I slaughter you," and his son said to him: "Do what you are commanded" — meaning the slaughter? And His saying, Mighty and Majestic: {«And he laid him down upon his forehead»} [al-Ṣāffāt: 103] is a submission to the act of slaughter, not to resolution.

As for the third — that the mere laying down is what was commanded — it is impossible, for that is not called slaughter, nor is it a trial, nor does it require ransom after compliance.

As for the fourth — the denial of abrogation and that he complied, but his neck was turned to iron so capacity was missed and the obligation ceased — this is not sound upon their principles; because the command with a condition is not established in their view. Rather, if God knows that He will turn his neck to iron, then He is not commanding what He knows to be impossible; so there is no need for ransom, and it is not a trial in his case.

As for the fifth — that he did the act and it healed — it is impossible; for how would ransom be needed after healing? Had that been sound, it would have been famous and would have been among his manifest miracles, and it has never been transmitted at all. It is merely an invention of the Qadariyyah. If it is said: Did He not say: {«You have fulfilled the vision»} [al-Ṣāffāt: 105]? We say: Its meaning is that you acted in its preliminaries as one who fulfills the vision acts; and fulfillment (taṣdīq) is not the same as realization (taḥqīq) or action.

chapters.title_en: On the Abrogation of Part of an Act of Worship, Its Condition, or One of Its Sunnahs
chapters.arabic_text:
### | [مسألة نسخ بعض العبادة أو شرطها أو سنة من سننها]

مسألة: إذا نسخ بعض العبادة أو شرطها أو سنة من سننها إذا نسخ بعض
العبادة أو شرطها أو سنة من سننها
كما لو أسقطت ركعتان من أربع أو أسقط شرط الطهارة فقد قال قائلون: هو نسخ
لأصل العبادة وقال قائلون نسخ الشرط ليس نسخا للأصل أما نسخ البعض فهو نسخ
للأصل ولم يسمحوا بتسمية الشرط بعضا، ومنهم من أطلق ذلك.
وكشف الغطاء عندنا أن نقول: إذا أوجب أربع ركعات ثم اقتصر على ركعتين فقد
نسخ أصل العبادة؛ لأن حقيقة النسخ الرفع والتبديل، ولقد كان حكم الأربع
الوجوب فنسخ وجوبها بالكلية، والركعتان عبادة أخرى لا أنها بعض من الأربعة،
إذ لو كانت بعضا لكان من صلى الصبح أربعا فقد أتى بالواجب وزيادة، كما لو
صلى بتسليمتين وكما لو وجب عليه درهم فتصدق  بدرهمين. فإن قيل: إذا رد
الأربع إلى ركعة فقد كانت الركعة حكمها أنها غير مجزئة والآن صارت مجزئة،
فهل هذا نسخ آخر مع نسخ الأربع؟ قلنا: كون الركعة غير مجزئة معناه أن
وجودها كعدمها، وهذا حكم أصلي عقلي ليس من الشرع.
والنسخ هو رفع ما ثبت بالشرع، فإذا لم يرد بلفظ النسخ إلا الرفع كيف كان
من غير نظر إلى المرفوع فهذا نسخ، لكنا بينا في حد النسخ خلافه، وأما إذا
أسقطت الطهارة فقد نسخ وجوب الطهارة وبقيت الصلاة واجبة. نعم كان حكم
الصلاة بغير طهارة أن لا تجزئ والآن صارت مجزئة، لكن هذا تغيير لحكم أصلي
لا لحكم شرعي، فإن الصلاة بغير طهارة لم تكن مجزئة؛ لأنها لم تكن مأمورا
بها شرعا.
فإن قيل: كانت صحة الصلاة متعلقة بالطهارة فنسخ تعلق صحتها بها شرعا فهو
نسخ متعلق بنفس العبادة، فالصلاة مع الطهارة غير الصلاة مع الحدث كما أن
الثلاث غير الأربع، فليكن هذا نسخا لتلك
الصلاة وإيجابا لغيرها. قلنا: لهذا تخيل قوم أن نسخ شرط العبادة.
كنسخ البعض، ولا شك أنه لو أوجب الصلاة مع الحدث لكان لإيجابها مع
الطهارة وكانت هذه عبادة أخرى، أما إذا جوزت الصلاة كيف كانت مع الطهارة
وغير الطهارة فقد كانت الصلاة بغير طهارة غير مجزئة لبقائها على الحكم
الأصلي إذ لم يؤمر بها فالآن جعلت مجزئة وارتفع الحكم الأصلي، أما صحة
الصلاة وأنها كانت متعلقة بالطهارة فنسخ هذا التعلق نسخ لأصل العبادة أو
نسخ لتعلق الصحة ولمعنى الشرطية؟ هذا فيه نظر والخطب فيه يسير، فليس يتعلق
به كبير فائدة.
وأما إذا نسخت سنة من سننها لا يتعلق بها الإجزاء كالوقوف على يمين
الإمام أو ستر الرأس، فلا شك أن هذا لا يتعرض للعبادة بالنسخ، فإذا تبعيض
مقدار العبادة نسخ لأصل العبادة، وتبعيض السنة لا يتعرض للعبادة، وتبعيض
الشرط فيه نظر وإذا حقق كان إلحاقه بتبعيض قدر العبادة أولى.

### | [مسألة الزيادة على النص نسخ]
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ن-س-خ (n-s-kh)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Lifting, removal, replacement, or transcription of a ruling; the core sense is "to efface and substitute."
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal theology, abrogation (naskh) is the divine lifting of an established sharʿī ruling, not a mere nullification of an intrinsic rational fact.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Used literally (ḥaqīqah) for lifting a legal obligation; metaphorically (majāz) if applied to non-juristic matters like conditions or intrinsic states.
- Root: ج-ز-ء (j-z-ʾ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: A part (juzʾ) as a constituent portion of a whole; also sufficiency (mujziʾ) meaning "rendering adequate."
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In worship, "part" (baʿḍ) is that which is commanded as a component of the act; "sufficiency" (ijzāʾ) is the legal validity of an act fulfilling the command.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for quantitative division; metaphorical when applied to conditions (shurūṭ) that are not intrinsic parts.
- Root: ش-ر-ط (sh-r-ṭ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: A mark or sign; in law, a condition (sharṭ) that is external to the essence of the act but required for its validity.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): A condition is a stipulated prerequisite (muqaddimah) whose absence prevents validity but whose presence does not constitute the act itself.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for a contractual stipulation; extended to legal prerequisites in worship.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Exceptive Syntax (al-sharṭ wa al-jazāʾ) — The apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is governed by the protasis (sharṭ); here, the legal conditional "if a part is abrogated" determines the consequent ruling, requiring precise parsing of what is abrogated (the obligation) versus what remains (the act's essence).
chapters.translation:
I say: If part of an act of worship is abrogated, or its condition, or one of its sunnahs — for example, if two rakʿahs are dropped from four, or the condition of purity (ṭahārah) is dropped — some have said: this is an abrogation of the very act of worship itself. Others said: abrogating the condition is not abrogating the essence; but abrogating a part is abrogating the essence, and they did not permit calling the condition a "part." And among them are those who applied the term broadly [to both].

The uncovering of the matter, in our view, is to say: If one is obligated to perform four rakʿahs, then the obligation is restricted to two, then the essence of the act of worship has been abrogated. For the reality of abrogation (naskh) is lifting and replacement. The ruling of the four was obligation (wujūb); its obligation has been lifted entirely. The two rakʿahs are another act of worship, not a part of the four. For if they were a part, then one who prayed the dawn prayer as four would have performed the obligatory act plus an excess — just as if he prayed with two salutations [in a four-rakʿah prayer], or just as if one owed a dirham and gave two dirhams in charity [the extra would be voluntary, not obligatory].

If it is said: When the four are reduced to one rakʿah, the one rakʿah previously had the ruling that it was not sufficient (ghayr mujziʾah), and now it becomes sufficient — is this another abrogation alongside the abrogation of the four? We say: The fact that one rakʿah is not sufficient means that its existence is like its non-existence. This is an original rational (ʿaqlī) ruling, not from the Sacred Law (sharʿ). Abrogation is the lifting of what is established by the Sacred Law. If the term "abrogation" meant only "lifting," however it occurs, without regard to what is lifted, then this would be abrogation — but we have already shown in the definition of abrogation the contrary of that.

As for when purity is dropped: the obligation of purity has been abrogated, while the prayer remains obligatory. Indeed, the ruling of prayer without purity was that it was not sufficient, and now it becomes sufficient. But this is a change in an original ruling, not in a sharʿī ruling. For prayer without purity was not sufficient because it was not commanded by the Sacred Law.

If it is said: The validity (ṣiḥḥah) of prayer was attached to purity; the abrogation of the attachment of its validity to purity is sharʿī, so it is an abrogation pertaining to the very act of worship. Thus prayer with purity is not the same as prayer with impurity (ḥadath), just as three is not the same as four. So let this be an abrogation of that prayer and an obligation of another. We say: It is because of this that some imagined that abrogating a condition of worship is like abrogating a part. There is no doubt that if one were obligated to pray with impurity, alongside the obligation to pray with purity, this would be another act of worship. But if prayer is permitted however it occurs — with purity or without purity — then prayer without purity was not sufficient because it remained under the original ruling, since it was not commanded. Now it has been made sufficient, and the original ruling has been lifted. As for the validity of prayer and its attachment to purity — is the abrogation of this attachment an abrogation of the essence of the act, or an abrogation of the attachment of validity and the meaning of conditionality? This requires scrutiny, but the matter is of little consequence, for no great benefit hangs upon it.

As for when a sunnah of the act is abrogated — one that does not affect sufficiency (ijzāʾ), such as standing to the right of the imam or covering the head — there is no doubt that this does not touch the act of worship with abrogation. Thus, dividing the quantity (miqdār) of the act of worship is an abrogation of the essence of the act; dividing a sunnah does not touch the act; and dividing a condition requires scrutiny — but upon investigation, likening it to dividing the quantity of the act is more appropriate.

chapters.title_en: Addition to the Text (Al-Ziyādah ʿAlā al-Naṣṣ): Is It Abrogation (Naskh) or Not?
chapters.arabic_text:
الزيادة على النص نسخ عند قوم وليست بنسخ عند قوم
والمختار عندنا التفصيل فنقول ينظر إلى تعلق الزيادة بالمزيد عليه.
والمراتب فيه ثلاثة:
الأولى: أن يعلم أنه لا يتعلق به كما إذا أوجب الصلاة والصوم ثم أوجب
الزكاة والحج لم يتغير حكم المزيد عليه، إذ بقي وجوبه وإجزاؤه، والنسخ هو
رفع حكم وتبديل ولم يرتفع.
الرتبة الثانية: وهي في أقصى البعد عن الأولى أن تتصل الزيادة بالمزيد
عليه اتصال اتحاد يرفع التعدد والانفصال كما لو زيد في الصبح ركعتان، فهذا
نسخ إذ كان حكم الركعتين الإجزاء والصحة وقد ارتفع.
نعم الأربعة استؤنف إيجابها ولم تكن واجبة، وهذا ليس بنسخ إذ المرفوع هو
الحكم الأصلي دون الشرعي. فإن قيل: اشتملت الأربعة على الثنتين وزيادة فهما
قارتان لم ترفعا وضمت إليهما ركعتان. قلنا: النسخ رفع الحكم لا رفع المحكوم
فيه فقد كان من حكم الركعتين الإجزاء والصحة وقد ارتفع، كيف وقد بينا أنه
ليس الأربعة ثلاثا وزيادة بل هي نوع آخر؟ إذ لو كان لكانت الخمسة أربعة
وزيادة. فإذا أتى بالخمسة فينبغي أن تجزئ ولا صائر إليه.
الرتبة الثالثة: وهي بين المرتبتين زيادة عشرين جلدة على ثمانين جلدة في
القذف، وليس انفصال هذه الزيادة كانفصال الصوم عن الصلاة ولا اتصالها
كاتصال الركعات.
وقد قال أبو حنيفة - رحمه الله -: هو نسخ، وليس بصحيح بل هو بالمنفصل
أشبه؛ لأن الثمانين نفي وجوبها وإجزاؤها عن نفسها ووجبت زيادة عليها مع
بقائها فالمائة ثمانون وزيادة، ولذلك لا ينتفي الإجزاء عن الثمانين بزيادة
عليها بخلاف الصلاة. وفائدة هذه المسألة جواز إثبات التغريب بخبر الواحد
عندنا ومنعه عندهم، لأن القرآن لا ينسخ بخبر الواحد. فإن قيل: قد كانت
الثمانون حدا كاملا فنسخ اسم الكمال رفع لحكمه لا محالة.
قلنا هو رفع، ولكن ليس ذلك حكما مقصودا شرعيا بل المقصود وجوده وإجزاؤه
وقد بقي كما كان، فلو أثبت مثبت كونه حكما مقصودا شرعيا لامتنع نسخه بخبر
الواحد، بل هو كما لو أوجب الشرع الصلاة فقط فمن أتى بها فقد أدى كلية ما
أوجبه الله تعالى عليه بكماله، فإذا أوجب  الصوم خرجت الصلاة عن كونها كلية
الواجب لكن ليس هذا حكما مقصودا. فإن قيل: هو نسخ لوجوب الاقتصار على
الثمانين، لأن إيجاب الثمانين مانع من الزيادة.
قلنا ليس
منع الزيادة بطريق المنطوق بل بطريق المفهوم ولا يقولون به ولا نقول به
ههنا ثم رفع المفهوم كتخصيص العموم، فإنه رفع بعض مقتضى اللفظ فيجوز بخبر
الواحد. ثم إنما يستقيم هذا لو ثبت أنه ورد حكم المفهوم واستقر ثم ورد
التغريب بعده، وهذا لا سبيل إلى معرفته، بل لعله ورد بيانا لإسقاط المفهوم
متصلا به أو قريبا منه. فإن قيل: التفسيق ورد الشهادة يتعلق بالثمانين،
فإذا زيد عليها زال تعلقه بها.
قلنا: يتعلق التفسيق ورد الشهادة بالقذف لا بالحد، ولو سلمنا لكان ذلك
حكما تابعا للحد لا مقصودا وكان كحل النكاح بعد انقضاء أربعة أشهر وعشر من
عدة الوفاة، وتصرف الشرع في العدة بردها من حول إلى أربعة أشهر وعشر ليس
تصرفا في إباحة النكاح بل في نفس العدة والنكاح تابع. فإن قيل: فلو أمر
بالصلاة مطلقا ثم زيد شرط الطهارة فهل هو نسخ؟ قلنا: نعم، لأنه كان حكم
الأول إجزاء الصلاة بغير طهارة فنسخ إجزاؤها وأمر بصلاة مع طهارة.
فإن قيل: فيلزمكم المصير إلى إجزاء طواف المحدث؛ لأنه تعالى قال:
{وليطوفوا بالبيت العتيق} [الحج: 29] ولم يشرط الطهارة والشافعي - رحمه
الله - منع الإجزاء لقوله - صلى الله عليه وسلم -: «الطواف بالبيت صلاة»
وهو خبر الواحد وأبو حنيفة - رحمه الله - قضى بأن هذا الخبر يؤثر في إيجاب
الطهارة أما في إبطال الطواف وإجزائه وهو معلوم بالكتاب فلا. قلنا لو استقر
قصد العموم في الكتاب واقتضى إجزاء الطواف محدثا ومع الطهارة فاشتراط
الطهارة رفع ونسخ ولا يجوز بخبر الواحد، ولكن قوله تعالى: {وليطوفوا بالبيت
العتيق} [الحج: 29] يجوز أن يكون أمرا بأصل الطواف ويكون بيان شروطه موكولا
إلى الرسول - عليه السلام -، فيكون قوله بيانا وتخصيصا للعموم لا نسخا،
فإنه نقصان من النص لا زيادة على النص، لأن عموم النص يقتضي إجزاء الطواف
بطهارة وغير طهارة فأخرج  خبر الواحد أحد القسمين من لفظ القرآن فهو نقصان
من النص لا زيادة عليه، ويحتمل أن يكون رفعا إن استقر العموم قطعا وبيانا
إن لم يستقر، ولا معنى لدعوى استقراره بالتحكم.
وهذا نظير قوله تعالى: {فتحرير رقبة} [المجادلة: 3] ، فإنه يعم المؤمنة
وغير المؤمنة، فيجوز تخصيص العموم إذ قد يراد بالآية ذكر أصل الكفارة ويكون
أمرا بأصل الكفارة دون قيودها وشروطها، فلو استقر العموم وحصل القطع يكون
العموم مرادا لكان نسخه ورفعه بالقياس وخبر الواحد ممتنعا. فإن قيل: فما
قولكم في تجويز المسح على الخفين هل هو نسخ لغسل الرجلين؟ قلنا: ليس نسخا
لإجزائه ولا لوجوبه لكنه نسخ لتضييق وجوبه وتعينه وجاعل إياه أحد الواجبين،
ويجوز أن يثبت بخبر الواحد.
فإن قيل: فالكتاب أوجب غسل الرجلين على التضييق. قلنا: قد بقي تضييقه في
حق من لم يلبس خفا على الطهارة وأخرج من عمومه من لبس الخف على الطهارة،
وذلك في ثلاثة أيام أو يوم وليلة. فإن قيل: فقوله تعالى: {واستشهدوا شهيدين
من رجالكم} [البقرة: 282] الآية، توجب إيقاف الحكم على شاهدين، فإذا حكم
بشاهد ويمين بخبر الواحد فقد رفع إيقاف الحكم فهو نسخ.
قلنا: ليس كذلك، فإن الآية لا تقتضي إلا كون الشاهدين حجة وجواز الحكم
بقولهما، أما امتناع الحكم بحجة أخرى فليس من الآية بل هو كالحكم بالإقرار،
وذكر حجة واحدة لا يمنع وجود حجة أخرى. وقولهم ظاهر
الآية أن لا حجة سواه، فليس هذا ظاهر منطوقه ولا حجة عندهم بالمفهوم، ولو
كان فرفع المفهوم رفع بعض مقتضى اللفظ وكل ذلك لو سلم استقرار المفهوم
وثباته، وقد ورد خبر الشاهد واليمين بعده وكل ذلك غير مسلم
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ز-ي-د (Z-Y-D)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is "increase" or "augmentation" — an addition that attaches to an existing entity, whether physically or legally.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal theology, ziyādah denotes an added stipulation or component to a revealed ruling; its status as naskh (abrogation) hinges on whether it alters the original divine command's essence or merely supplements it.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literally, ziyādah is an increment; metaphorically (majāz), it may signify a new independent obligation, distinguished from a true alteration of the prior ruling.
- Root: ن-س-خ (N-S-Kh)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Root meaning is "to erase," "to remove," or "to supersede" — a lifting of a previously established legal effect.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Naskh is the divine lifting of a ḥukm (ruling) after its establishment, replacing it with another; it requires the removal of the original obligation's validity.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal removal of a ruling; not to be confused with takhṣīṣ (specification), which narrows a general text without negating its core.
- Root: ج-ز-ء (J-Z-ʾ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Root meaning is "to suffice" or "to be sufficient" — the quality of an act fulfilling the legal requirement.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Ijzāʾ denotes the legal efficacy of an act in satisfying the divine command, such that no further performance is required.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sufficiency; in legal discourse, it is the property of an act being valid and complete in meeting the obligation.
- Sībawayh Rule: Taʿlīq al-Ḥukm ʿalā al-ʿIllah (Conditioning of a ruling on its cause) — The syntactic attachment of a conditional clause (e.g., "if the addition is connected...") determines whether the ruling is modified or abrogated, mirroring how grammatical dependency (iḍāfah) affects meaning.
chapters.translation:
I say: Addition to the text (al-ziyādah ʿalā al-naṣṣ) is considered abrogation (naskh) by some scholars, and it is not abrogation by others. The chosen position for us is the detailed distinction, so we say: one must examine the relation of the addition to that which is added upon (al-mazīd ʿalayh). The ranks therein are three:

The first rank: That it is known that the addition does not relate to it, as when He obligates prayer (ṣalāh) and fasting (ṣawm), then obligates alms (zakāh) and pilgrimage (ḥajj) — the ruling of the added-upon is not altered, for its obligation and its sufficiency (ijzāʾ) remain. And abrogation is the lifting of a ruling and its replacement, and nothing has been lifted.

The second rank: Which is at the farthest distance from the first — that the addition connects to the added-upon with a connection of unity (ittiṣāl ittiḥād) that removes multiplicity and separation, as if two units (rakʿāt) are added to the dawn prayer (al-ṣubḥ). This is abrogation, for the ruling of the two units was sufficiency and validity, and it has been lifted. Indeed, the four units are newly obligated (mustaʾnafah) and were not obligatory before. This is not abrogation, for what is lifted is the original ruling (al-ḥukm al-aṣlī) rather than the legal one (al-sharʿī). If it is said: The four units comprise the two units plus an addition, so the two are preserved and not lifted, with two units appended to them. We say: Abrogation is the lifting of the ruling, not the lifting of the subject of the ruling (al-maḥkūm fīh). For it was the ruling of the two units to be sufficient and valid, and that has been lifted. How so, when we have clarified that the four are not three plus an addition, but rather another type (nawʿ ākhar)? For if it were so, then five would be four plus an addition. Thus, if one performs five, it should suffice, but no one holds this.

The third rank: Which lies between the two ranks — the addition of twenty lashes to eighty lashes in the case of slander (al-qadhf). The separation of this addition is not like the separation of fasting from prayer, nor is its connection like the connection of the units (rakʿāt). Abū Ḥanīfah — may God have mercy on him — said: It is abrogation. But this is not correct; rather, it is more akin to the disconnected (al-munfaṣil), because the eighty lashes — their obligation and their sufficiency for themselves are not negated, and an addition is obligated upon them while they remain. Thus, the hundred is eighty plus an addition. Therefore, sufficiency is not negated from the eighty by the addition upon them, unlike the case of prayer. The benefit of this issue is the permissibility of establishing exile (al-taghrīb) through a solitary report (khabar al-wāḥid) according to us, and its prohibition according to them, because the Qurʾān is not abrogated by a solitary report. If it is said: The eighty lashes were a complete punishment (ḥadd kāmil), so the abrogation of the name of completeness is the lifting of its ruling without doubt. We say: It is a lifting, but that is not an intended legal ruling (ḥukm maqṣūd sharʿī); rather, the intended thing is its existence and its sufficiency, and that has remained as it was. So if someone were to establish that it is an intended legal ruling, its abrogation by a solitary report would be impermissible. Rather, it is like when the Lawgiver obligates only prayer — whoever performs it has fulfilled the entirety of what God — exalted is He — obligated upon him in its completeness. Then when He obligates fasting, prayer exits from being the entirety of the obligation, but this is not an intended ruling. If it is said: It is an abrogation of the obligation to restrict oneself to the eighty, because the obligation of the eighty prevents increase. We say: The prevention of increase is not by way of the expressed wording (al-manṭūq) but by way of the implied meaning (al-mafhūm), and they do not adhere to it, nor do we adhere to it here. Then the lifting of the implied meaning is like the specification of the general (takhṣīṣ al-ʿumūm), for it is the lifting of part of what the wording entails, so it is permissible through a solitary report. Moreover, this would only be sound if it were established that the ruling of the implied meaning was revealed and settled, then exile was revealed afterward. But there is no way to know this; rather, perhaps it was revealed as an explanation (bayān) to nullify the implied meaning, connected to it or close to it. If it is said: The declaration of corruption (tafsīq) and the rejection of testimony (radd al-shahādah) are attached to the eighty lashes, so when an addition is made upon them, its attachment to them is removed. We say: The declaration of corruption and the rejection of testimony are attached to the slander (al-qadhf), not to the punishment (al-ḥadd). And even if we conceded that, it would be a ruling subsidiary to the punishment, not intended in itself, like the permissibility of marriage after the expiration of four months and ten days from the waiting period of widowhood (ʿiddat al-wafāh). The Lawgiver's disposition regarding the waiting period, changing it from a year to four months and ten days, is not a disposition regarding the permissibility of marriage but rather regarding the waiting period itself, and marriage is subsidiary. If it is said: If one is commanded to pray absolutely, then the condition of purity (ṭahārah) is added, is that abrogation? We say: Yes, because the ruling of the first was the sufficiency of prayer without purity, so its sufficiency was abrogated, and one is commanded to pray with purity.

If it is said: Then you must concede the sufficiency of the circumambulation (ṭawāf) of the one in a state of minor impurity (al-muḥdith), for God — exalted is He — said: {«And let them circumambulate the Ancient House»} [al-Ḥajj 22:29], and He did not stipulate purity. And al-Shāfiʿī — may God have mercy on him — prohibited its sufficiency due to his saying — peace be upon him: «The circumambulation of the House is a prayer» — and it is a solitary report. And Abū Ḥanīfah — may God have mercy on him — ruled that this report affects the obligation of purity, but not the invalidation of the circumambulation and its sufficiency, for that is known by the Book, so it does not. We say: If the intent of generality (qaṣd al-ʿumūm) in the Book were established and it entailed the sufficiency of circumambulation while in a state of impurity and with purity, then stipulating purity would be a lifting and an abrogation, impermissible through a solitary report. But His saying — exalted is He: {«And let them circumambulate the Ancient House»} [al-Ḥajj 22:29] — may be a command regarding the essence of circumambulation, with the explanation of its conditions delegated to the Messenger — peace be upon him. Thus, his saying would be an explanation and a specification of the general, not an abrogation, for it is a reduction from the text (nuqṣān min al-naṣṣ), not an addition to the text. Because the generality of the text entails the sufficiency of circumambulation with purity and without purity, so the solitary report excludes one of the two categories from the wording of the Qurʾān. Thus, it is a reduction from the text, not an addition upon it. And it is possible that it is a lifting if the generality is definitively established, and an explanation if it is not. There is no meaning to the claim of its definitive establishment by arbitrary assertion (taḥakkum).

This is analogous to His saying — exalted is He: {«Then the freeing of a neck»} [al-Mujādilah 58:3], for it encompasses the believing and the non-believing. So it is permissible to specify the general, since the verse may intend the mention of the essence of the expiation (al-kaffārah) and be a command regarding the essence of the expiation without its restrictions and conditions. So if the generality were established and certainty obtained that the general is intended, then its abrogation and lifting by analogy (qiyās) and solitary report would be impermissible. If it is said: What is your position regarding permitting wiping over the leather socks (al-masḥ ʿalā al-khuffayn) — is it an abrogation of the washing of the feet? We say: It is not an abrogation of its sufficiency nor of its obligation, but it is an abrogation of its restricted specification (taḍyīq) and its determinacy (taʿayyun), making it one of two obligations. And it is permissible to establish it through a solitary report. If it is said: The Book obligated the washing of the feet with restriction. We say: Its restriction has remained for the one who has not worn socks upon purity, and from its generality is excluded the one who wore socks upon purity, and that is for three days or a day and a night. If it is said: His saying — exalted is He: {«And call to witness two witnesses from among your men»} [al-Baqarah 2:282] — obligates suspending the ruling on two witnesses. So when one rules with a witness and an oath (shāhid wa yamīn) through a solitary report, one has lifted the suspension of the ruling, and that is abrogation. We say: It is not so, for the verse entails only that two witnesses are a proof (ḥujjah) and the permissibility of ruling by their testimony. As for the impermissibility of ruling by another proof, that is not from the verse; rather, it is like ruling by confession (al-iqrār). The mention of one proof does not prevent the existence of another proof. And their saying that the apparent meaning of the verse is that there is no proof besides it — this is not the apparent meaning of its expressed wording, nor is it a proof for them by the implied meaning. And even if it were, then lifting the implied meaning is lifting part of what the wording entails, and all of that is conceded only if the establishment and stability of the implied meaning are granted. But the report of the witness and the oath came after it, and all of that is not conceded.

chapters.title_en: The Abrogation of a Ruling Without a Substitute, Abrogation by the Heavier, and Abrogation Regarding One Who Has Not Received the Report
chapters.arabic_text:
### | [مسألة ليس من شرط النسخ إثبات بدل غير المنسوخ]

ليس من شرط النسخ إثبات بدل غير المنسوخ
وقال قوم: يمتنع ذلك. فنقول: يمتنع ذلك عقلا أو سمعا؟ ولا يمتنع عقلا.
جوازه إذ لو امتنع لكان الامتناع لصورته أو لمخالفته المصلحة والحكمة، ولا
يمتنع لصورته إذ يقول قد أوجبت عليك القتال ونسخته عنك ورددتك إلى ما  كان
قبل من الحكم الأصلي، ولا يمتنع للمصلحة فإن الشرع لا ينبني عليها وإن
ابتنى فلا يبعد أن تكون المصلحة في رفعه من غير إثبات بدل. وإن منعوا جوازه
سمعا فهو تحكم، بل نسخ النهي عن ادخار لحوم الأضاحي وتقدمة الصدقة أمام
المناجاة ولا بدل لها وإن نسخت القبلة إلى بدل ووصية الأقربين إلى بدل وغير
ذلك. وحقيقة النسخ هو الرفع فقط، أما قوله تعالى: {ما ننسخ من آية أو ننسها
نأت بخير منها أو مثلها} [البقرة: 106] إن تمسكوا به فالجواب من أوجه،
الأول: أن هذا لا يمنع الجواز وإن منع الوقوع عند من يقول بصيغة العموم،
ومن لا يقول، بها فلا يلزمه أصلا، ومن قال بها فلا يلزمه من هذا أنه لا
يجوز في جميع المواضع إلا ببدل بل يتطرق التخصيص إليه بدليل الأضاحي
والصدقة أمام المناجاة، ثم ظاهره أنه أراد أن نسخ آية بآية أخرى مثلها لا
يتضمن الناسخ إلا رفع المنسوخ أو يتضمن مع ذلك، فكل ذلك محتمل.

### | [مسألة يجوز النسخ بالأخف ولا يجوز بالأثقل]

مسألة: قال قوم: يجوز النسخ بالأخف ولا يجوز بالأثقل قال قوم: يجوز النسخ
بالأخف ولا يجوز بالأثقل.
فنقول امتناع النسخ بالأثقل عرفتموه عقلا أو شرعا؟ ولا يستحيل عقلا لأنه
لا يمتنع لذاته ولا للاستصلاح، فإنا ننكره وإن قلنا به، فلم يستحيل أن تكون
المصلحة في التدريج والترقي من الأخف إلى الأثقل كما كانت المصلحة في
ابتداء التكليف ورفع الحكم الأصلي. فإن قيل: إن الله تعالى رءوف رحيم
بعباده ولا يليق به التشديد. قلنا: فينبغي أن لا يليق به ابتداء التكليف
ولا تسليط المرض والفقر وأنواع العذاب على الخلق.
فإن قالوا: إنه يمتنع سمعا لقوله تعالى: {يريد الله بكم اليسر ولا يريد
بكم العسر} [البقرة: 185] ولقوله تعالى: {يريد الله أن يخفف عنكم} [النساء:
28] قلنا: فينبغي أن يتركهم وإباحة الفعل ففيه اليسر، ثم ينبغي أن لا ينسخ
بالمثل لأنه لا يسر فيه إذ اليسر في رفعه إلى غير بدل أو بالأخف، وهذه
الآيات وردت  في صور خاصة أريد بها التخفيف وليس فيه منع إرادة التثقيل
والتشديد.
فإن قيل فقد قال: {ما ننسخ من آية أو ننسها} [البقرة: 106] الآية، وهذا
خير عام والخير ما هو خير لنا وإلا فالقرآن خير كله، والخير لنا ما هو أخف
علينا. قلنا: لا بل الخير ما هو أجزل ثوابا وأصلح لنا في المآل وإن كان
أثقل في الحال. فإن قيل: لا يمتنع ذلك عقلا بل سمعا؛ لأنه لم يوجد في الشرع
نسخ بالأثقل.
قلنا: ليس كذلك، إذ أمر الصحابة أولا بترك القتال والإعراض ثم بنصب
القتال مع التشديد بثبات الواحد للعشرة، وكذلك نسخ التخيير بين الصوم
والفدية بالإطعام بتعيين الصيام وهو تضييق، وحرم الخمر ونكاح المتعة والحمر
الأهلية بعد إطلاقها، ونسخ جواز تأخير الصلاة عند الخوف إلى إيجابها في
أثناء القتال،
ونسخ صوم عاشوراء بصوم رمضان وكانت الصلاة ركعتين عند قوم فنسخت بأربع في
الحضر.

### | [مسألة النسخ في حق من لم يبلغه الخبر]

مسألة: اختلفوا في النسخ في حق من لم يبلغه الخبر اختلفوا في النسخ في حق
من لم يبلغه الخبر.
فقال قوم: النسخ حصل في حقه وإن كان جاهلا به وقال قوم: ما لم يبلغه لا
يكون نسخا في حقه والمختار أن للنسخ حقيقة وهو ارتفاع الحكم السابق ونتيجة
وهو وجوب القضاء وانتفاء الإجزاء بالعمل السابق، أما حقيقته فلا يثبت في حق
من لم يبلغه وهو رفع الحكم لأن من أمر باستقبال بيت المقدس فإذا نزل النسخ
بمكة لم يسقط الأمر عمن هو باليمن في الحال بل هو مأمور بالتمسك بالأمر
السابق ولو ترك لعصى وإن بان أنه كان منسوخا، ولا يلزمه استقبال الكعبة بل
لو استقبلها لعصى وهذا لا يتجه فيه خلاف.
وأما لزوم القضاء للصلاة إذا عرف النسخ فيعرف ذلك بدليل نص أو قياس وربما
يجب القضاء حيث لا يجب الأداء، كما في الحائض لو صامت عصت ويجب عليها
القضاء، فكذلك يجوز أن يقال هذا لو استقبل الكعبة عصى ويلزمه استقبالها في
القضاء، وكما نقول  في النائم والمغمى عليه إذا تيقظ وأفاق يلزمهما قضاء ما
لم يكن واجبا لأن من لا يفهم لا يخاطب.
فإن قيل: إذا علم النسخ ترك تلك القبلة بالنسخ أو بعلمه بالنسخ والعلم لا
تأثير له، فدل أن الحكم انقطع بنزول الناسخ، لكنه جاهل به وهو مخطئ فيه
لكنه معذور. قلنا: الناسخ هو الرافع، لكن العلم شرط ويحال عند وجود الشرط
على الناسخ ولكن لا نسخ قبل وجود الشرط؛ لأن الناسخ خطاب ولا يصير خطابا في
حق من لم يبلغه.
وقولهم: إنه مخطئ، محال؛ لأن اسم الخطأ يطلق على من طلب شيئا فلم يصب أو
على من وجب عليه الطلب فقصر، ولا يتحقق شيء منه في محل النزاع.
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ن-س-خ (n-s-kh)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To erase, remove, transfer, or supersede; the core sense is obliteration of a prior state and its replacement by another.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal theology, abrogation (naskh) is the divine lifting of an established ruling (ḥukm) by a subsequent address, entailing a temporal limitation of the earlier command.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage denotes removal; metaphorical (majāz) usage may imply substitution, but the essence is the act of lifting alone.
- Root: ب-د-ل (b-d-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Exchange, substitute, or replacement; a thing given in place of another.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In jurisprudential discourse, a substitute (badal) is a new ruling that occupies the position of the abrogated one; its absence does not negate the validity of the abrogation itself.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal exchange of objects; metaphorically, the replacement of one legal obligation with another, though not a necessary condition for the act of lifting.
- Root: خ-ف-ف (kh-f-f)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Lightness, ease, reduction of burden; the opposite of heaviness (thiqal).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal theory, the lighter (akhaff) ruling is one that diminishes the subject's hardship; the heavier (athqal) increases it, and both are within divine capacity.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal physical lightness; metaphorically, ease in obligation, as in the divine attribute of desiring ease for servants.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause with Suppressed Protasis (al-sharṭ al-maḥdhūf) — In phrases like "if they say... we reply," the protasis is implied, and the apodosis carries the full logical force, requiring precise parsing of the dialectical exchange.
chapters.translation:
I say: It is not a condition of abrogation (naskh) that a substitute (badal) for the abrogated ruling be established. Some have said: That is impossible. We say: Is its impossibility [affirmed] by reason or by revelation? It is not impossible by reason. Its permissibility [is established], for if it were impossible, the impossibility would arise either from its very form or from its contravention of [divine] wisdom and benefit (maṣlaḥah). It is not impossible by its form, for [God] may say: "I have obligated you to fight, and I have abrogated it from you, returning you to what was before of the original ruling." Nor is it impossible on account of benefit, for the Law (sharʿ) is not built upon it; and even if it were built upon it, it is not far-fetched that the benefit lies in its removal without establishing a substitute. If they prohibit its permissibility by revelation, that is sheer arbitrariness (taḥakkum). Indeed, the abrogation of the prohibition on storing the meat of sacrificial animals, and the abrogation of the requirement of advancing charity before private counsel [with the Prophet] — these had no substitute. Yet the abrogation of the qiblah had a substitute, and the bequest to near relatives had a substitute, and other such cases. The reality of abrogation is merely the lifting [of the ruling]. As for His saying, the Exalted: {«What verse We abrogate or cause to be forgotten, We bring a better one or its like»} [al-Baqarah 2:106] — if they cling to this, the answer is from several angles. The first: This does not negate permissibility, even if it negates actual occurrence for one who holds to the general import (ṣīghat al-ʿumūm). As for one who does not hold to it, it imposes no obligation upon him at all. And for one who does hold to it, it does not follow from this that [abrogation] is not permissible in all cases except with a substitute; rather, specification (takhṣīṣ) may enter upon it, as evidenced by the case of the sacrificial meats and the charity before private counsel. Moreover, its apparent meaning is that He intended the abrogation of a verse by another verse like it — [and this] does not entail that the abrogator includes only the lifting of the abrogated, or that it includes more than that; all of that is possible.

I say: Some have said: Abrogation by the lighter (al-akhaff) is permissible, but abrogation by the heavier (al-athqal) is not. We say: Have you known the impossibility of abrogation by the heavier by reason or by revelation? It is not impossible by reason, for it is not impossible in itself, nor on account of [the principle of] seeking benefit (al-istiṣlāḥ) — for we deny that [as a basis of law], even if we were to affirm it. Thus, it is not impossible that the benefit lies in gradual progression and ascent from the lighter to the heavier, just as the benefit lay in the initial imposition of obligation (taklīf) and in the lifting of the original ruling. If it is said: God, the Exalted, is kind and merciful to His servants, and severity does not befit Him — we say: Then it should not befit Him to initiate obligation at all, nor to inflict illness, poverty, and various kinds of torment upon creation. If they say: It is impossible by revelation, due to His saying, the Exalted: {«God desires ease for you, and does not desire hardship for you»} [al-Baqarah 2:185], and His saying, the Exalted: {«God desires to lighten [burdens] for you»} [al-Nisāʾ 4:28] — we say: Then He should have left them [without obligation] and permitted the act, for therein is ease. Then He should not abrogate by an equivalent, for there is no ease in that, since ease lies in lifting [the ruling] without a substitute, or by the lighter. These verses were revealed concerning specific cases in which alleviation was intended, and they do not negate the intention of burdening and severity [in other cases]. If it is said: He has said: {«What verse We abrogate or cause to be forgotten»} [al-Baqarah 2:106] — and this is a general good (khayr), and the good is what is good for us; otherwise, the entire Quran is good. And what is good for us is what is lighter upon us. We say: No, rather the good is what is more abundant in reward and more beneficial for us in the final outcome, even if it is heavier in the present moment. If it is said: This is not impossible by reason, but by revelation, because no abrogation by the heavier has occurred in the Law — we say: Not so. For the Companions were first commanded to abandon fighting and turn away, then they were commanded to engage in fighting with severity, [such as] the steadfastness of one against ten. Likewise, the abrogation of the choice between fasting and ransom by [requiring] feeding [the poor] — with the specification of fasting [as obligatory] — is a restriction. And [God] prohibited wine, temporary marriage (nikāḥ al-mutʿah), and the flesh of domesticated donkeys after having permitted them. And He abrogated the permissibility of delaying prayer during fear to the obligation of performing it in the midst of battle. And He abrogated the fast of ʿĀshūrāʾ with the fast of Ramaḍān. And prayer was two units (rakʿatān) according to some, and it was abrogated to four in residence.

I say: They differed concerning abrogation regarding one who has not received the report [of it]. Some said: Abrogation occurs in his case even if he is ignorant of it. Others said: As long as it has not reached him, it is not abrogation in his case. The chosen [position] is that abrogation has a reality — which is the lifting of the prior ruling — and a consequence — which is the obligation of making up (qaḍāʾ) and the negation of validity (ijzāʾ) for the prior act. As for its reality, it is not established in the case of one who has not received the report, namely the lifting of the ruling. For one who was commanded to face the Sacred House [in Jerusalem] — when the abrogation was revealed in Mecca, the command did not lapse for one in Yemen at that very moment; rather, he was commanded to adhere to the prior command, and had he abandoned it, he would have disobeyed, even if it later became clear that it had been abrogated. Nor was he obligated to face the Kaʿbah; indeed, had he faced it, he would have disobeyed. There is no room for dispute in this. As for the obligation of making up the prayer when he learns of the abrogation, that is known by a textual proof (naṣṣ) or by analogy (qiyās). And perhaps making up is obligatory where the performance (adāʾ) was not, as in the case of a menstruating woman: if she fasts, she disobeys, yet making up is obligatory upon her. Likewise, it may be said of this one: if he faced the Kaʿbah [before learning], he disobeyed, and facing it is incumbent upon him in making up. And just as we say regarding the sleeper and the unconscious one — when they awaken and regain consciousness, making up is incumbent upon them for what was not obligatory [at the time], because one who does not comprehend is not addressed. If it is said: When he learns of the abrogation, he abandons that qiblah — [is it] by the abrogation or by his knowledge of it? Knowledge has no effect. This indicates that the ruling was severed by the descent of the abrogator, but he was ignorant of it and mistaken in it, yet excused. We say: The abrogator is the lifter, but knowledge is a condition; and when the condition exists, [the lifting] is attributed to the abrogator. But there is no abrogation before the existence of the condition, because the abrogator is an address (khiṭāb), and it does not become an address in the case of one who has not received it. As for their saying that he is mistaken — that is impossible, for the name "mistake" (khaṭaʾ) is applied to one who sought something and did not attain it, or to one upon whom seeking was obligatory and he fell short. Neither of these is realized in the case under dispute.

chapters.title_en: Section 60 — The Pillars of Abrogation (Naskh) and Its Conditions
chapters.arabic_text:
### | [الباب الثاني في أركان النسخ وشروطه]

أركان النسخ وشروطه
ويشتمل على تمهيد لمجامع الأركان والشروط وعلى مسائل تتشعب من أحكام
الناسخ والمنسوخ. أما التمهيد، فاعلم أن أركان النسخ أربعة: النسخ،
والناسخ، والمنسوخ، والمنسوخ عنه. فإذا كان النسخ حقيقته رفع الحكم،
فالناسخ هو الله تعالى فإنه الرافع للحكم، والمنسوخ هو الحكم المرفوع،
والمنسوخ عنه هو المتعبد المكلف، والنسخ قوله الدال على رفع الحكم الثابت.
وقد يسمى الدليل ناسخا على سبيل المجاز، فيقال: هذه الآية ناسخة لتلك.
وقد يسمى الحكم ناسخا مجازا، فيقال: صوم رمضان ناسخ لصوم عاشوراء. والحقيقة
هو الأول؛ لأن النسخ هو الرفع، والله تعالى هو الرافع بنصب الدليل على
الارتفاع وبقوله الدال عليه. وأما مجامع شروطه فالشروط أربعة:
الأول: أن يكون المنسوخ حكما شرعيا لا عقليا أصليا، كالبراءة الأصلية
التي ارتفعت بإيجاب العبادات.
الثاني: أن يكون النسخ بخطاب، فارتفاع الحكم بموت المكلف ليس نسخا إذ ليس
المزيل خطابا رافعا لحكم خطاب سابق، ولكنه قد قيل أولا الحكم عليك ما دمت
حيا. فوضع الحكم قاصر على الحياة فلا يحتاج إلى الرفع.
الثالث: أن لا يكون الخطاب المرفوع حكمه مقيدا بوقت.
يقتضي دخوله زوال الحكم، كقوله تعالى: {ثم أتموا الصيام إلى الليل}
[البقرة: 187] .
الرابع: أن يكون الخطاب الناسخ متراخيا، لا كقوله تعالى: {ولا تقربوهن
حتى يطهرن} [البقرة: 222] وقوله تعالى: {حتى يعطوا الجزية عن يد وهم
صاغرون} [التوبة: 29] .
وليس يشترط فيه تسعة أمور:
الأول: أن يكون رافعا للمثل بالمثل بل أن يكون رافعا فقط.
الثاني: أن لا يشترط ورود النسخ بعد دخول وقت المنسوخ بل يجوز قبل دخول
وقته.
الثالث: أن لا يشترط أن يكون المنسوخ مما يدخله الاستثناء والتخصيص بل
يجوز ورود النسخ على الأمر بفعل واحد في وقت واحد.
الرابع: أن لا يشترط أن يكون نسخ القرآن بالقرآن والسنة بالسنة فلا تشرط
الجنسية بل يكفي أن يكون مما يصح النسخ به.
الخامس: أن لا يشترط أن يكونا نصين قاطعين إذ يجوز نسخ خبر الواحد بخبر
الواحد وبالمتواتر وإن كان لا يجوز نسخ المتواتر بخبر الواحد.
السادس: لا يشترط أن يكون الناسخ منقولا بمثل لفظ المنسوخ بل أن يكون
ثابتا بأي طريق كان، فإن التوجه إلى بيت المقدس لم ينقل إلينا بلفظ القرآن
والسنة وناسخه نص صريح في القرآن، وكذلك لا يمتنع نسخ الحكم المنطوق به
باجتهاد النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - وقياسه وإن لم يكن ثابتا بلفظ ذي
صيغة وصورة ويجب نقلها.
السابع: لا يشترط أن يكون الناسخ مقابلا للمنسوخ حتى لا ينسخ الأمر إلا
بالنهي ولا النهي إلا بالأمر بل يجوز أن ينسخ كلاهما بالإباحة وأن ينسخ
الواجب المضيق بالموسع، وإنما يشترط أن يكون الناسخ رافعا حكما من المنسوخ
كيف كان.
الثامن: لا يشترط كونهما ثابتين بالنص بل لو كان بلحن القول وفحواه
وظاهره وكيف كان بدليل أن النبي - عليه السلام - بين أن آية وصية الأقارب
نسخت بقوله: «إن الله تعالى قد أعطى كل ذي حق حقه، ألا لا وصية لوارث» مع
أن الجمع بين الوصية والميراث ممكن فليسا متنافيين تنافيا قاطعا.
التاسع: لا يشترط نسخ الحكم ببدل أو بما هو أخف بل يجوز بالمثل والأثقل
وبغير بدل كما سبق.

### | [مسائل تتشعب عن النظر في ركني المنسوخ والناسخ]

### | [مسألة ما من حكم شرعي إلا وهو قابل للنسخ]

ولنذكر الآن مسائل تتشعب عن  النظر في ركني المنسوخ والناسخ، وهي مسألتان
في المنسوخ وأربع مسائل في المنسوخ به.
مسألة: ما من حكم شرعي إلا وهو قابل للنسخ
، خلافا للمعتزلة فإنهم قالوا من الأفعال ما لها صفات نفسية تقتضي حسنها
وقبحها فلا يمكن نسخها. مثل معرفة الله تعالى والعدل وشكر المنعم فلا يجوز
نسخ وجوبه، ومثل الكفر والظلم والكذب فلا يجوز نسخ تحريمه. وبنوا هذا على
تحسين العقل وتقبيحه وعلى وجوب الأصلح على الله تعالى، وحجروا بسببه على
الله تعالى في الأمر والنهي. وربما بنوا هذا على صحة إسلام الصبي وأن وجوبه
بالعقل وأن استثناء الصبي غير ممكن. وهذه أصول أبطلناها وبينا أنه لا يجب
أصل التكليف على الله تعالى كان فيه صلاح العباد أو لم يكن، نعم بعد أن
كلفهم لا يمكن أن ينسخ جميع التكاليف إذ لا يعرف النسخ إلا الله عز وجل
ويجب على المكلف معرفة النسخ والناسخ والدليل المنصوب عليه، فيبقى هذا
التكليف بالضرورة. ونسلم أيضا أنه لا يجوز أن يكلفهم أن لا يعرفوه وأن يحرم
عليهم معرفته، لأن قوله: أكلفك أن لا تعرفني،
يتضمن المعرفة، أي: عرفني لأني كلفتك أن لا تعرفني، وذلك محال فيمتنع
التكليف فيه عند من يمنع تكليف المحال. وكذلك لا يجوز أن يكلفه معرفة شيء
من الحوادث على خلاف ما هو به لأنه محال لا يصح فعله ولا تركه.
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ن-س-خ (n-s-kh)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is "to efface, remove, transfer, or supersede" — the act of lifting or replacing an established thing.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In Sharīʿah, naskh denotes the divine lifting of a previously established legal ruling (ḥukm) by a subsequent address (khiṭāb), not the nullification of an eternal truth.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage applies to God as the true abrogator; metaphorical (majāz) usage applies to the textual evidence (dalīl) or the ruling itself being called "abrogating."
- Sībawayh Rule: ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Clarification) — The listing of the four pillars (arkān) functions as a coordinated explanatory series, each term defined by its precise relational role in the act of abrogation.
chapters.translation:
I say: Know that the pillars of abrogation (naskh) are four: the abrogation itself, the abrogator (nāsikh), the abrogated (mansūkh), and the one from whom the abrogated ruling is lifted (al-mansūkh ʿanhu). If the reality of abrogation is the lifting (rafʿ) of a ruling, then the abrogator is God Most High, for He is the One who lifts the ruling; the abrogated is the ruling that is lifted; the one from whom it is lifted is the legally accountable servant (al-mutʿabbad al-mukallaf); and the abrogation itself is His speech indicating the lifting of an established ruling. The evidence (dalīl) may be called "abrogating" metaphorically, so one says: "This verse abrogates that one." Likewise, the ruling may be called "abrogating" metaphorically, so one says: "The fast of Ramaḍān abrogates the fast of ʿĀshūrāʾ." But the literal truth is the first [usage]; for abrogation is the lifting, and God Most High is the lifter, by virtue of His erecting the evidence for the lifting and by His speech indicating it.

As for the comprehensive conditions (majāmiʿ al-shurūṭ), they are four:
First: That the abrogated matter be a Sharʿī ruling, not a purely rational one — such as the original presumption of innocence (al-barāʾah al-aṣliyyah), which was lifted by the imposition of acts of worship.
Second: That the abrogation occur through a [divine] address (khiṭāb); for the lifting of a ruling by the death of the legally accountable person is not abrogation, since the remover is not an address lifting the ruling of a prior address. Rather, it was said initially: "The ruling applies to you as long as you are alive." Thus the ruling's applicability is confined to life and needs no lifting.
Third: That the address whose ruling is lifted not be restricted to a specific time whose expiration entails the cessation of the ruling — as His saying: {«Then complete the fast until the night»} [al-Baqarah 2:187].
Fourth: That the abrogating address be subsequent [to the abrogated one], not simultaneous — unlike His saying: {«And do not approach them until they become pure»} [al-Baqarah 2:222], and His saying: {«Until they pay the jizyah out of hand while they are humbled»} [al-Tawbah 9:29].

Nine things are not required as conditions:
First: That the abrogator lift [the ruling] by an equivalent [ruling]; rather, it suffices that it merely lift.
Second: That abrogation occur only after the time of the abrogated [ruling] has entered; rather, it is permissible before its time enters.
Third: That the abrogated matter be of the kind admitting exception (istithnāʾ) and specification (takhṣīṣ); rather, abrogation may occur upon a command to a single act at a single time.
Fourth: That the Qurʾān be abrogated only by the Qurʾān and the Sunnah only by the Sunnah; homogeneity of kind is not required — rather, it suffices that [the abrogator] be of the kind by which abrogation is valid.
Fifth: That both [abrogator and abrogated] be definitive texts (naṣṣān qāṭiʿān); for it is permissible to abrogate a solitary report (khabar al-wāḥid) by another solitary report or by a mutawātir report, though it is not permissible to abrogate a mutawātir report by a solitary one.
Sixth: That the abrogator be transmitted in the same wording as the abrogated; rather, it suffices that it be established by any means whatsoever. For the orientation toward Jerusalem (Bayt al-Maqdis) was not transmitted to us in the wording of the Qurʾān or the Sunnah, yet its abrogator is an explicit text in the Qurʾān. Likewise, it is not impossible to abrogate a ruling expressed in [divine] speech by the Prophet's — peace be upon him — own ijtihād and analogical reasoning (qiyās), even if it is not established by a wording possessing a [specific] form and image that must be transmitted.
Seventh: That the abrogator be the opposite of the abrogated, such that a command is abrogated only by a prohibition and a prohibition only by a command; rather, it is permissible for both to be abrogated by permission (ibāḥah), and for the narrowly obligatory (al-wājib al-muḍayyaq) to be abrogated by the expansive (al-muwassaʿ). What is required is only that the abrogator lift a ruling from the abrogated, however that may be.
Eighth: That both be established by explicit text (naṣṣ); rather, [abrogation is valid] even if [the abrogated ruling] is [established] by the implication of the wording (laḥn al-qawl), its import (faḥwāhu), or its apparent meaning (ẓāhiruhu), however it may be. This is proven by the fact that the Prophet — peace be upon him — explained that the verse concerning bequests to relatives was abrogated by his saying: «God Most High has given every possessor of a right his right; indeed, no bequest to an heir.» For combining the bequest with inheritance is possible — they are not mutually contradictory with a definitive contradiction.
Ninth: That the abrogated ruling be replaced by a substitute (badal) or by something lighter; rather, it is permissible [to abrogate] by an equivalent, by something heavier, or without any substitute, as has preceded.

### | [Issues Branching from Consideration of the Two Pillars: The Abrogated and the Abrogator]

### | [Issue: No Sharʿī Ruling Exists Except That It Is Susceptible to Abrogation]

Now let us mention issues that branch from the consideration of the two pillars — the abrogated and the abrogator. These are two issues concerning the abrogated and four issues concerning that by which abrogation occurs.

Issue: No Sharʿī ruling exists except that it is susceptible to abrogation — contrary to the Muʿtazilah, who said that among acts there are those possessing intrinsic attributes (ṣifāt nafsiyyah) that necessitate their goodness or evil, such that they cannot be abrogated. Examples include knowledge of God Most High, justice, and gratitude to the Benefactor — the obligation of these cannot be abrogated; and examples include unbelief, injustice, and falsehood — the prohibition of these cannot be abrogated. They built this upon [their doctrine of] reason's discernment of good and evil (taḥsīn al-ʿaql wa taqbīḥuhu), upon the obligation of the most beneficial (wujūb al-aṣlaḥ) upon God Most High, and thereby restricted God Most High in His commanding and prohibiting. They perhaps also built this upon the validity of a child's Islam, that its obligation is [known] by reason, and that exempting the child is impossible. These are principles we have refuted, and we have shown that the origin of obligation (aṣl al-taklīf) is not incumbent upon God Most High, whether it involves the welfare of the servants or not. Yes — after He has obligated them, it is not possible to abrogate all obligations at once, for abrogation is known only to God — Mighty and Majestic — and the legally accountable person is obligated to know the abrogation, the abrogator, and the evidence erected upon it; thus this [very] obligation remains by necessity. We also concede that it is not permissible for Him to obligate them not to know Him, nor to prohibit them from knowing Him; for His saying, "I obligate you not to know Me," entails knowledge — i.e., "Know Me, for I have obligated you not to know Me" — and that is impossible (muḥāl). Thus obligation in such a case is precluded for anyone who deems obligation of the impossible invalid. Likewise, it is not permissible to obligate one to know any contingent thing contrary to its actual state, for that is impossible — neither its doing nor its omission can be validly performed.

chapters.title_en: On the Question of an Āyah Containing a Ruling: The Permissibility of Abrogating Its Recitation
chapters.arabic_text:
### | [مسألة الآية إذا تضمنت حكما يجوز نسخ تلاوتها]

الآية إذا تضمنت حكما
يجوز نسخ تلاوتها دون حكمها ونسخ حكمها دون تلاوتها ونسخهما جميعا، وظن
قوم استحالة ذلك. فنقول: هو جائز عقلا وواقع شرعا، أما جوازه عقلا فإن
التلاوة وكتبتها في القرآن وانعقاد الصلاة بها كل ذلك حكمها، كما أن
التحريم والتحليل المفهوم من لفظها حكمها وكل حكم فهو قابل للنسخ، وهذا حكم
فهو إذن قابل للنسخ.
وقد قال قوم نسخ التلاوة أصلا ممتنع لأنه لو كان المراد منها الحكم لذكر
على لسان رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - وما أنزله الله تعالى عليه إلا
ليتلى ويثاب عليه،  فكيف يرفع؟ قلنا: وأي استحالة في أن يكون المقصود مجرد
الحكم دون التلاوة لكن أنزل على رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - بلفظ
معين.
فإن قيل: فإن جاز نسخها فلينسخ الحكم معها؛ لأن الحكم تبع للتلاوة، فكيف
يبقى الفرع مع نسخ الأصل؟ قلنا: لا بل التلاوة حكم وانعقاد الصلاة بها حكم
آخر فليس بأصل، وإنما الأصل دلالتها، وليس في نسخ تلاوتها، والحكم بأن
الصلاة لا تنعقد بها نسخ لدلالتها فكم من دليل لا يتلى ولا تنعقد به صلاة،
وهذه الآية دليل لنزولها وورودها لا لكونها متلوة في القرآن، والنسخ لا
يرفع ورودها ونزولها ولا يجعلها كأنها غير واردة بل يلحقها بالوارد الذي لا
يتلى، كيف ويجوز أن ينعدم الدليل ويبقى المدلول؟ فإن الدليل علامة لا علة
فإذا دل فلا ضرر في انعدامه، كيف والموجب للحكم كلام الله تعالى القديم ولا
ينعدم ولا يتصور رفعه ونسخه؟ فإذا قلنا الآية منسوخة أردنا به انقطاع
تعلقها عن العبد وارتفاع مدلولها وحكمها لا ارتفاع ذاتها. فإن قيل نسخ
الحكم مع بقاء التلاوة متناقض لأنه رفع للمدلول مع بقاء الدليل.
قلنا: إنما يكون دليلا عند انفكاكه عما يرفع حكمه فإذا جاء خطاب ناسخ
لحكمه زال شرط دلالته. ثم الذي يدل على وقوعه سمعا قوله تعالى {وعلى الذين
يطيقونه فدية طعام مسكين} [البقرة: 184] الآية، وقد بقيت تلاوتها ونسخ
حكمها بتعيين الصوم. والوصية للوالدين والأقربين متلوة في القرآن وحكمها
منسوخ بقوله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - «لا وصية لوارث» ونسخ تقديم الصدقة
أمام المناجاة والتلاوة باقية، ونسخ التربص حولا عن المتوفى عنها زوجها،
والحبس والأذى عن اللاتي يأتين الفاحشة بالجلد والرجم مع بقاء التلاوة.
وأما نسخ التلاوة فقد تظاهرت الأخبار بنسخ تلاوة آية الرجم مع بقاء
حكمها، وهي قوله تعالى: الشيخ والشيخة إذا زنيا فارجموهما ألبتة نكالا من
الله والله عزيز حكيم ". واشتهر عن عائشة - رضي الله عنها - أنها قالت:
أنزلت عشر رضعات محرمات فنسخن بخمس. وليس ذلك في الكتاب.
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ن-س-خ (n-s-kh)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To efface, remove, transfer, or supersede; in legal terms, the lifting of a prior ruling by a subsequent divine address.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Abrogation (naskh) pertains to the temporal cessation of a ruling's applicability, not the annihilation of the divine speech itself, which is eternal.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal usage denotes removal of a physical trace; metaphorical (majāz) usage applies to the lifting of a legal obligation while the textual artifact may remain.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause with Inverted Protasis-Apodosis (Sharṭ muqaddam) — The phrase "if it is said" (fa-in qīla) introduces an objection, requiring the response (qulnā) to be parsed as the apodosis, maintaining logical sequence in dialectical discourse.
chapters.translation:
I say: An āyah, if it comprises a ruling, permits the abrogation of its recitation without its ruling, the abrogation of its ruling without its recitation, and the abrogation of both together. Yet a group of people deemed this impossible. We respond: It is permissible by reason and has occurred by revelation. As for its rational permissibility: the recitation, its inscription in the Qur’an, and the validity of prayer through it — all of these are rulings pertaining to it, just as the prohibition and permission understood from its wording are its rulings. And every ruling is susceptible to abrogation; this is a ruling, so it is therefore susceptible to abrogation.

Some have said that abrogating the recitation is absolutely impossible, for if the intent were the ruling alone, it would have been mentioned upon the tongue of the Messenger of God — peace be upon him — and God Most High only revealed it to be recited and to earn reward thereby. So how could it be lifted? We respond: What impossibility is there in the purpose being merely the ruling without the recitation, yet it was revealed to the Messenger of God — peace be upon him — in a specific wording?

If it is said: If its abrogation is permissible, then let the ruling be abrogated along with it, for the ruling is subordinate to the recitation; how can the branch remain while the root is abrogated? We respond: No, rather the recitation is one ruling, and the validity of prayer through it is another ruling; it is not a root. The root is only its signification. And in abrogating its recitation, along with the ruling that prayer is not valid through it, there is abrogation of its signification. For how many an evidence (dalīl) is there that is not recited and by which no prayer is validated? This āyah is an evidence by virtue of its descent and its occurrence, not by virtue of its being recited in the Qur’an. And abrogation does not lift its occurrence and descent, nor does it render it as though it had never occurred; rather, it attaches it to that which has occurred but is not recited. How so, when it is permissible for the evidence to cease while the evidenced remains? For the evidence is a sign (ʿalāmah), not a cause (ʿillah); so when it has indicated, there is no harm in its ceasing. How so, when that which necessitates the ruling is the eternal speech of God Most High, which does not cease, nor is its lifting or abrogation conceivable? So when we say "the āyah is abrogated," we mean thereby the severance of its connection to the servant and the lifting of its indicated content and its ruling — not the lifting of its essence.

If it is said: Abrogating the ruling while the recitation remains is contradictory, because it is a lifting of the indicated while the evidence remains. We respond: It is only an evidence when it is free of what lifts its ruling; so when an address abrogating its ruling arrives, the condition of its signification is removed. Then what indicates its actual occurrence by revelation is the saying of God Most High: {«And upon those who are able to bear it, a ransom of feeding a poor person»} [al-Baqarah: 184] — the āyah — and its recitation has remained while its ruling was abrogated by the specification of fasting. Likewise, the bequest to parents and near relatives is recited in the Qur’an, yet its ruling is abrogated by his saying — peace be upon him — «No bequest to an heir.» And the abrogation of advancing the charity before private counsel, with the recitation remaining, and the abrogation of the waiting period of a year for the woman whose husband has died, and the confinement and harm [prescribed] for those who commit lewdness, [all replaced] by flogging and stoning, while the recitation remains.

As for the abrogation of recitation, the reports have been transmitted successively regarding the abrogation of the recitation of the stoning āyah while its ruling remains, namely His saying Most High: "The elderly man and the elderly woman, if they commit fornication, stone them both absolutely, as a punishment from God, and God is Mighty, Wise." And it is well-known from ʿĀ’ishah — may God be pleased with her — that she said: "Ten sucklings were revealed as prohibitions, then they were abrogated by five." And that is not in the Book.

chapters.title_en: The Abrogation of the Qur'an by the Sunnah and the Sunnah by the Qur'an
chapters.arabic_text:
### | [مسألة نسخ القرآن بالسنة والسنة بالقرآن]

يجوز نسخ  القرآن بالسنة والسنة بالقرآن
؛ لأن الكل من عند الله عز وجل، فما المانع منه؟ ولم يعتبر التجانس مع أن
العقل لا يحيله، كيف وقد دل السمع على وقوعه؟ إذ التوجه إلى بيت المقدس ليس
في القرآن وهو في السنة وناسخه في القرآن، وكذلك قوله تعالى: {فالآن
باشروهن} [البقرة: 187] نسخ لتحريم المباشرة وليس التحريم في
القرآن، ونسخ صوم عاشوراء بصوم رمضان وكان عاشوراء ثابتا بالسنة وصلاة
الخوف وردت في القرآن ناسخة لما ثبت في السنة من جواز تأخيرها إلى انجلاء
القتال، حتى قال - عليه السلام - يوم الخندق وقد أخر الصلاة: «حشا الله
قبورهم نارا» لحبسهم له عن الصلاة، وكذلك قوله تعالى: {فلا ترجعوهن إلى
الكفار} [الممتحنة: 10] نسخ لما قرره - عليه السلام - من العهد والصلح.
وأما نسخ القرآن بالسنة فنسخ الوصية للوالدين والأقربين بقوله - صلى الله
عليه وسلم -: «ألا لا وصية لوارث» ؛ لأن آية الميراث لا تمنع الوصية
للوالدين والأقربين، إذ الجمع ممكن. وكذلك قال - صلى الله عليه وسلم -: «قد
جعل الله لهن سبيلا البكر بالبكر جلد مائة وتغريب عام والثيب بالثيب جلد
مائة والرجم» . فهو ناسخ لإمساكهن في البيوت. وهذا فيه نظر؛ لأنه - صلى
الله عليه وسلم - بين أن آية الميراث نسخت آية الوصية ولم ينسخها هو بنفسه
- صلى الله عليه وسلم -، وبين أن الله تعالى جعل لهن سبيلا وكان قد وعد به
فقال: {أو يجعل الله لهن سبيلا} [النساء: 15] فإن قيل قال الشافعي - رحمه
الله -: لا يجوز نسخ السنة بالقرآن كما لا يجوز نسخ القرآن بالسنة، وهو أجل
من أن لا يعرف هذه الوجوه في النسخ، فكأنه يقول: إنما تلتغي السنة بالسنة
إذ يرفع النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - سنته بسنته ويكون هو مبينا لكلام
نفسه وللقرآن ولا يكون القرآن مبينا للسنة، وحيث لا يصادف ذلك فلأنه لم
ينقل وإلا فلم يقع النسخ إلا كذلك.
قلنا: هذا إن كان في جوازه عقلا، فلا يخفى أنه يفهم من القرآن وجوب
التحول إلى الكعبة وإن كان التوجه إلى بيت المقدس ثابتا بالسنة،  وكذلك عكسه
ممكن. وإن كان يقول لم يقع هذا فقد نقلنا وقوعه، ولا حاجة إلى تقدير سنة
خافية مندرسة؛ إذ لا ضرورة في هذا التقدير والحكم بأن ذلك لم يقع أصلا تحكم
محض. وإن قال: الأكثر كان ذلك فربما لا ينازع فيه.
احتجوا بقوله تعالى {قال الذين لا يرجون لقاءنا ائت بقرآن غير هذا أو
بدله قل ما يكون لي أن أبدله من تلقاء نفسي إن أتبع إلا ما يوحى إلي}
[يونس: 15] . فدل أنه لا ينسخ القرآن بالسنة. قلنا: لا خلاف في أنه لا ينسخ
من تلقاء نفسه بل بوحي يوحى إليه، لكن لا يكون بنظم القرآن. وإن جوزنا
النسخ بالاجتهاد فالإذن في الاجتهاد يكون من الله عز وجل، والحقيقة أن
الناسخ هو الله عز وجل على لسان رسوله - صلى الله عليه وسلم -.
والمقصود أنه ليس من شرطه أن ينسخ حكم القرآن بقرآن، بل على لسان رسوله -
