### | [الفصل الأول في عدد المزكي]

الباب الثالث: في الجرح والتعديل وفيه أربعة فصول: الأول: في عدد المزكي.
وقد اختلفوا فيه، فشرط بعض المحدثين العدد في المزكي والجارح كما في مزكي
الشاهد وقال القاضي لا يشترط العدد في تزكية الشاهد ولا في تزكية الراوي
وإن كان الأحوط في الشهادة الاستظهار بعد المزكي وقال قوم: يشترط في
الشهادة
دون الرواية، وهذه مسألة فقهية. والأظهر عندنا أنه يشترط في الشهادة دون
الرواية، وهذا لأن العدد الذي تثبت به الرواية لا يزيد على نفس الرواية.
فإن قيل: صح من الصحابة قبول رواية الواحد ولم يصح قبول تزكية الواحد فيرجع
فيه إلى قياس الشرع. قلنا: نحن نعلم مما فعلوه كثيرا مما لم يفعلوه، إذ
نعلم أنهم كما قبلوا حديث الصديق - رضي الله عنه - كانوا يقبلون تعديله لمن
روى الحديث. وكيف يزيد شرط الشيء على أصله. والإحصان يثبت بقول اثنين، وإن
لم يثبت الزنا إلا بأربعة ولم يقس عليه. وكذلك نقول: تقبل تزكية العبد
والمرأة في الرواية كما تقبل روايتهما. وهذه مسائل فقهية ثبتت بالمقاييس
الشبهية فلا معنى للإطناب فيها في الأصول.

### | [الفصل الثاني سبب الجرح والتعديل]

الفصل الثاني: في ذكر سبب الجرح والتعديل.
قال  الشافعي: يجب ذكر سبب الجرح دون التعديل، إذ قد يجرح بما لا يراه
جارحا لاختلاف المذاهب فيه، وأما العدالة فليس لها إلا سبب واحد وقال قوم
مطلق الجرح يبطل الثقة، ومطلق التعديل لا يحصل الثقة لتسارع الناس إلى
البناء على الظاهر، فلا بد من ذكر سببه. وقال قوم: لا بد من السبب فيهما
جميعا أخذا بمجامع كلام الفريقين. وقال القاضي: لا يجب ذكر السبب فيهما
جميعا؛ لأنه إن لم يكن بصيرا بهذا الشأن فلا يصلح للتزكية، وإن كان بصيرا
فأي معنى للسؤال؟ والصحيح عندنا أن هذا يختلف باختلاف حال المزكي، فمن حصلت
الثقة ببصيرته وضبطه يكتفى بإطلاقه، ومن عرفت عدالته في نفسه ولم تعرف
بصيرته بشروط العدالة فقد نراجعه إذا فقدنا عالما بصيرا به، وعند ذلك
نستفصله. أما إذا تعارض الجرح والتعديل قدمنا الجرح، فإن الجارح اطلع على
زيادة ما اطلع عليها المعدل ولا نفاها، فإن نفاها بطلت عدالة المزكي إذ
النفي لا يعلم إلا إذا جرحه بقتل إنسان فقال المعدل: رأيته حيا بعده
تعارضا. وعدد المعدل إذا زاد قيل إنه يقدم على الجارح. وهو ضعيف؛ لأن سبب
تقديم الجرح اطلاع الجارح على مزيد ولا ينتفي ذلك بكثرة العدد.

### | [الفصل الثالث في نفس التزكية]

وذلك إما بالقول، أو بالرواية عنه، أو بالعمل بخبره، أو بالحكم بشهادته،
فهذه أربعة أعلاها صريح القول. وتمامه أن يقول: هو عدل رضا لأني عرفت منه
كيت وكيت. فإن لم يذكر السبب وكان بصيرا بشروط العدالة كفى. الثانية أن
يروي عنه خبرا. وقد اختلفوا في كونه تعديلا، والصحيح أنه إن عرف من عادته
أو بصريح قوله أنه لا يستجيز الرواية إلا من عدل كانت الرواية تعديلا وإلا
فلا، إذ من عادة أكثرهم الرواية من كل من سمعوه، ولو كلفوا الثناء عليهم
سكتوا، فليس في روايته ما يصرح بالتعديل. فإن قيل: لو عرفه بالفسق ثم روى
عنه كان غاشا في الدين. قلنا: لم نوجب على غيره العمل، لكن قال: سمعت فلانا
قال كذا وصدق فيه، ثم لعله  لم يعرفه بالفسق ولا العدالة فروى ووكل البحث
إلى من أراد القبول.
الثالثة: العمل بالخبر إن أمكن حمله على الاحتياط أو على العمل بدليل آخر
وافق الخبر فليس بتعديل، وإن عرفنا يقينا أنه عمل بالخبر فهو تعديل، إذ لو
عمل بخبر غير العدل لفسق وبطلت عدالته. فإن قيل لعله ظن أن مجرد الإسلام مع
عدم الفسق عدالة. قلنا: هذا يتطرق إلى التعديل بالقول، ونحن نقول العمل
كالقول، وهذا الاحتمال ينقطع بذكر سبب العدالة.
وما ذكرناه تفريع على الاكتفاء بالتعديل المطلق، إذ لو شرط ذكر السبب
لشرط في شهادة البيع والنكاح عد جميع شرائط الصحة، وهو بعيد. فإن قيل: لعله
عرفه عدلا ويعرفه غيره بالفسق. قلنا: من عرفه لا جرم لا يلزمه العمل به،
كما لو عدل جريحا. الرابعة: أن يحكم بشهادته، فذلك أقوى من تزكيته بالقول.
أما ترك الحكم بشهادته وبخبره فليس جرحا؛ إذ قد يتوقف في شهادة العدل
وروايته لأسباب سوى الجرح، كيف وترك العمل لا يزيد على الجرح المطلق وهو
غير مقبول عند الأكثرين؟ وبالجملة إن لم ينقدح وجه لتزكية العمل من تقديم
أو دليل آخر فهو كالجرح المطلق.
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ز-ك-و (z-k-w)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Growth, purity, and increase; in juridical context, declaring probity (ʿadālah) and moral soundness.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Technical term for attestation of moral probity requisite for accepting testimony or narration.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is purification/growth; metaphorical (majāz) usage denotes legal certification of a person's trustworthiness.
- Root: ج-ر-ح (j-r-ḥ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Wounding, inflicting a bodily injury; extended to defaming or impugning a witness's or narrator's credibility.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In ḥadīth methodology, the act of identifying a defect (qādiḥ) in a narrator's probity or memory.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal wounding of the body; metaphorical usage for damaging a person's evidentiary standing.
- Root: ع-د-ل (ʿ-d-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Straightness, equity, moderation; a person of upright character whose testimony is acceptable.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The moral and religious quality rendering one's report or testimony authoritative.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal straightness vs. crookedness; legally, the established probity of a narrator.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Exceptive Constructions (al-sharṭ wa al-istithnāʾ) — Governing the logical structure of "if...then..." arguments and the scope of exceptions in legal reasoning, as applied in the dialectical objections and replies.
chapters.translation:
I say: The third book concerns impugnment (al-jarḥ) and certification of probity (al-taʿdīl), comprising four chapters. The first chapter: on the number of those who certify probity.

Scholars have differed on this matter. Some traditionists (al-muḥaddithūn) stipulated a plurality of certifiers for both the one who declares probity and the one who impugns, just as in the certification of witnesses. The Judge (al-Qāḍī) held that plurality is not required for certifying a witness's probity nor for certifying a narrator's probity, although in testimony the more cautious course is to seek corroboration beyond the certifier. Another group held that plurality is required for testimony but not for narration. This is a jurisprudential question. The more apparent position in our school is that plurality is required for testimony but not for narration, for the plurality by which narration is established does not exceed the narration itself.

If it is objected: "It is authentically established that the Companions accepted the report of a single narrator, but it is not authentically established that they accepted the certification of probity by a single person; therefore, the matter should be referred to analogical reasoning from the revealed law." We reply: We know from their practice many things they did not do explicitly, for we know that just as they accepted the ḥadīth of al-Ṣiddīq — may God be pleased with him — they likewise accepted his certification of probity for one who narrated a ḥadīth. How could the condition of a thing exceed its very foundation? Moreover, legal chastity (iḥṣān) is established by the testimony of two persons, even though fornication is not established except by four witnesses, and this was not analogically extended. Likewise, we hold: the certification of probity by a slave or a woman is accepted in narration just as their narration is accepted. These are jurisprudential questions established by analogies of resemblance (al-maqāyīs al-shabahiyyah), so there is no point in elaborating upon them in uṣūl.

The second chapter: on mentioning the ground for impugnment and certification of probity.

Al-Shāfiʿī said: The ground of impugnment must be mentioned, but not the ground of certification of probity, for a person may be impugned for something the impugner himself does not regard as a defect, due to differences of legal schools on the matter. As for probity, it has only one ground. Another group said: An unqualified impugnment destroys trust, while an unqualified certification does not establish trust, because people are quick to build upon outward appearances; hence the ground must be mentioned. Another group said: The ground must be mentioned in both cases, combining the comprehensive import of both parties' statements. The Judge said: The ground need not be mentioned in either case; for if the certifier is not discerning in this matter, he is unfit for certification, and if he is discerning, what is the point of asking? The correct position in our school is that this varies according to the condition of the certifier. Whoever has earned trust in his discernment and precision, his unqualified statement suffices. But whoever is known for his own probity yet not known for discernment regarding the conditions of probity, we may question him when we lack a discerning scholar in the matter, and at that point we elicit details from him.

As for when impugnment and certification conflict, we give precedence to impugnment, for the impugner has come to know something additional that the certifier did not come to know, nor did the certifier negate it. If the certifier negates it, then the certifier's probity is nullified, for negation is not known except [by direct observation]. If the impugner impugns him for killing a person, and the certifier says, "I saw him alive after that," then the two statements conflict. If the number of certifiers increases, it is said that they take precedence over the impugner. This is weak, for the reason for giving precedence to impugnment is the impugner's access to additional information, and this is not negated by multiplicity of number.

The third chapter: on the modes of certification of probity itself.

This occurs either by explicit statement, or by narrating from the person, or by acting upon his report, or by adjudicating upon his testimony. These are four modes, the highest of which is explicit statement. Its complete form is that he says: "He is a just, upright person, because I have known such-and-such from him." If he does not mention the ground but is discerning regarding the conditions of probity, it suffices.

The second mode: that he narrates a report from him. Scholars have differed on whether this constitutes certification. The correct position is that if it is known from his habit or from his explicit statement that he does not deem it permissible to narrate except from a just person, then the narration constitutes certification; otherwise not. For the habit of most narrators is to narrate from anyone they have heard, and if they were tasked with praising them, they would remain silent. Thus, there is nothing in his narration that explicitly affirms probity. If it is objected: "If he knew him to be corrupt (fāsiq) and then narrated from him, he would be deceiving the religion." We reply: We have not obligated others to act upon it; rather, he said, "I heard so-and-so say such-and-such," and he was truthful in that. Perhaps he did not know him to be corrupt nor just, so he narrated and delegated the investigation to whoever wishes to accept.

The third mode: acting upon the report. If it is possible to interpret the action as precautionary, or as acting upon another evidence that agrees with the report, then it is not certification. But if we know with certainty that he acted upon the report, then it is certification, for if he had acted upon the report of one who is not just, he would have sinned and his own probity would be nullified. If it is objected: "Perhaps he thought that mere Islam, along with absence of corruption, constitutes probity." We reply: This same possibility applies to certification by explicit statement, and we hold that action is like statement; this possibility is cut off by mentioning the ground of probity.

What we have mentioned is a ramification of deeming unqualified certification sufficient. For if mentioning the ground were required, then in the testimony of sale and marriage one would have to enumerate all the conditions of validity, which is far-fetched. If it is objected: "Perhaps he knew him to be just, while another knows him to be corrupt." We reply: Whoever knows him to be corrupt is not obligated to act upon him, just as if one certified a wounded person as just. The fourth mode: that he adjudicates upon his testimony. This is stronger than certifying him by statement. As for refraining from adjudicating upon his testimony and his report, this is not impugnment, for one may withhold from a just person's testimony and narration for reasons other than impugnment. How could refraining from action not exceed unqualified impugnment, which is itself unacceptable to most scholars? In sum, if no basis for certification by action can be discerned — whether from preference or another evidence — then it is like unqualified impugnment.

chapters.title_en: Section 81 — On the Probity (ʿAdālah) of the Companions (Ṣaḥābah)
chapters.arabic_text:
### | [الفصل الرابع في عدالة الصحابة]

- رضي الله عنهم -
والذي عليه سلف الأمة، وجماهير الخلف، أن عدالتهم معلومة بتعديل الله عز
وجل إياهم وثنائه عليهم في كتابه، فهو معتقدنا فيهم إلا أن يثبت بطريق قاطع
ارتكاب واحد لفسق مع علمه به، وذلك مما لا يثبت فلا حاجة لهم إلى التعديل
قال الله تعالى: {كنتم خير أمة أخرجت للناس} [آل عمران: 110] وقال تعالى:
{وكذلك جعلناكم أمة وسطا لتكونوا شهداء على الناس} [البقرة: 143] وهو خطاب
مع الموجودين في ذلك العصر.
وقال تعالى: {لقد رضي الله عن المؤمنين إذ يبايعونك تحت الشجرة} [الفتح:
18] وقال عز وجل: {والسابقون الأولون} [التوبة: 100] وقد ذكر الله تعالى
المهاجرين والأنصار في عدة مواضع وأحسن الثناء عليهم، وقال: - صلى الله
عليه وسلم - " خير الناس قرني ثم الذين يلونهم " وقال: - صلى الله عليه
وسلم - «لو أنفق أحدكم ملء الأرض ذهبا  ما بلغ مد أحدهم ولا نصيفه» وقال -
صلى الله عليه وسلم -: «إن الله اختار لي أصحابا وأصهارا وأنصارا» .
فأي تعديل أصح من تعديل علام الغيوب - سبحانه - وتعديل رسوله - صلى الله
عليه وسلم -؟ كيف ولو لم يرد الثناء لكان فيما اشتهر وتواتر من حالهم في
الهجرة والجهاد وبذل المهج والأموال وقتل الآباء والأهل في موالاة رسول
الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - ونصرته كفاية في القطع بعدالتهم؟ وقد زعم قوم
أن حالهم كحال غيرهم في لزوم البحث. وقال قوم: حالهم العدالة في بداية
الأمر إلى ظهور الحرب والخصومات، ثم تغير الحال وسفكت الدماء فلا بد من
البحث.
وقال جماهير المعتزلة عائشة وطلحة والزبير وجميع أهل العراق والشام فساق
بقتال الإمام الحق. وقال قوم من سلف القدرية: يجب رد شهادة علي وطلحة
والزبير مجتمعين ومفترقين لأن فيهم فاسقا لا نعرفه بعينه. وقال قوم: نقبل
شهادة كل واحد إذا انفرد لأنه لم يتعين فسقه، أما إذا كان مع مخالفه فشهدا
ردا إذ نعلم أن أحدهما فاسق.
وشك بعضهم في فسق عثمان وقتلته. وكل هذا جراءة على السلف على خلاف السنة،
بل قال قوم: ما جرى بينهم ابتني على الاجتهاد وكل مجتهد مصيب، أو المصيب
واحد، والمخطئ معذور لا ترد شهادته، وقال قوم: ليس ذلك مجتهدا فيه، ولكن
قتلة عثمان والخوارج مخطئون قطعا لكنهم جهلوا خطأهم وكانوا متأولين،
والفاسق المتأول لا ترد روايته، وهذا أقرب من المصير إلى سقوط تعديل القرآن
مطلقا.
فإن قيل: القرآن أثنى على الصحابة، فمن الصحابي؟ أمن عاصر رسول الله -
صلى الله عليه وسلم - أو من لقيه مرة أو من صحبه ساعة أو من طالت صحبته؟
وما حد
طولها؟ قلنا: الاسم لا يطلق إلا على من صحبه.
ثم يكفي للاسم من حيث الوضع الصحبة ولو ساعة، ولكن العرف يخصص الاسم بمن
كثرت صحبته، ويعرف ذلك بالتواتر والنقل الصحيح وبقول الصحابي كثرت صحبتي،
ولا حد لتلك الكثرة بتقدير بل بتقريب.

### | [الباب الرابع في مستند الراوي وكيفية ضبطه]
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ع-د-ل (ʿ-d-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning of evenness, balance, and moral uprightness; the state of being straight and just in conduct.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Probity (ʿadālah) as a legal-theological status rendering one's testimony and narration authoritative; here, divinely conferred, not earned.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage — an intrinsic moral quality; metaphorical (majāz) would imply mere outward conformity, which is not intended.
- Root: ث-ن-ا (th-n-ā)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Praise and commendation, often repeated or public.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Divine commendation (thanāʾ) as a definitive legislative act establishing probity.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — explicit verbal praise; not metaphorical.
- Root: ص-ح-ب (ṣ-ḥ-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Companionship, association, or accompanying another.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Technical term (ṣuḥbah) for the Companions of the Prophet, with juristic implications for their collective probity.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — physical accompaniment; metaphorical extension to prolonged association by customary usage (ʿurf).
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause (al-Sharṭ) — The phrase "if it were established by a decisive proof" (law thabata) governs a hypothetical that is negated, requiring the apodosis to be understood as impossible; also, the use of "kamā" (just as) for analogical extension in legal reasoning.
chapters.translation:
I say: The position held by the early predecessors (salaf) of the community and the vast majority of the later scholars (khalaf) is that their probity (ʿadālah) is known through God's — Mighty and Majestic — own declaration of their probity and His praise of them in His Book. This is our creed regarding them, unless it be established by a decisive proof that one of them committed an act of immorality (fisq) while knowing it to be such. But such a matter cannot be established, and thus they have no need for any external declaration of probity. God — Exalted is He — said: {«You are the best community brought forth for mankind»} [Āl ʿImrān: 110], and He said: {«Thus We have made you a middle nation, that you may be witnesses over mankind»} [al-Baqarah: 143] — and this address is directed to those living in that era.

And He said: {«God was well pleased with the believers when they pledged allegiance to you under the tree»} [al-Fatḥ: 18], and He — Mighty and Majestic — said: {«And the foremost forerunners»} [al-Tawbah: 100]. God — Exalted is He — has mentioned the Emigrants (Muhājirūn) and the Helpers (Anṣār) in numerous places and bestowed upon them the finest praise. And the Prophet — peace and blessings be upon him — said: "The best of people is my generation, then those who follow them." And he — peace and blessings be upon him — said: {«If one of you were to spend the equivalent of Mount Uhud in gold, he would not reach the measure of even a mudd of one of them, nor half of it»} And he — peace and blessings be upon him — said: {«Indeed, God has chosen for me companions, in-laws, and helpers»}.

So what declaration of probity could be more sound than the declaration of the Knower of the Unseen — Glorified be He — and the declaration of His Messenger — peace and blessings be upon him? How could it be otherwise, for even if no praise had been reported, what is widely known and mass-transmitted (mutawātir) of their condition — in emigration (hijrah), jihad, sacrificing their lives and wealth, and slaying their own fathers and families in loyalty to the Messenger of God — peace and blessings be upon him — and in supporting him — would suffice as a decisive proof of their probity?

Some people have claimed that their condition is like that of others, requiring investigation. Others have claimed that their probity held at the beginning of the matter, until the outbreak of war and disputes, after which the situation changed, blood was shed, and thus investigation becomes necessary.

The majority of the Muʿtazilah have declared ʿĀʾishah, Ṭalḥah, al-Zubayr, and all the people of Iraq and Syria to be immoral (fussāq) for fighting against the rightful Imam. Some of the Qadariyyah predecessors said: The testimony of ʿAlī, Ṭalḥah, and al-Zubayr must be rejected whether they testify together or separately, because among them is an immoral person whom we do not identify by name. Others said: We accept the testimony of each one when he is alone, because his immorality has not been specifically established; but if he testifies alongside his opponent, both testimonies are rejected, for we know that one of them is immoral.

Some even doubted the immorality of ʿUthmān and his killers. All of this constitutes audacity against the predecessors (salaf) and contravenes the Sunnah. Rather, some have said: What occurred between them was based on independent reasoning (ijtihād), and every mujtahid is correct — or the correct one is single, and the mistaken one is excused, and his testimony is not rejected. Others said: This is not a matter of ijtihād at all; rather, the killers of ʿUthmān and the Khawārij are definitively mistaken, but they were ignorant of their error and acted on misinterpretation (taʾwīl), and the immoral person who acts on misinterpretation does not have his narration rejected. This latter view is closer to the truth than resorting to the nullification of the Quran's declaration of probity altogether.

If it is said: The Quran praised the Companions — so who is a Companion? Is it one who lived contemporaneously with the Messenger of God — peace and blessings be upon him — or one who met him once, or one who accompanied him for an hour, or one whose companionship was prolonged? And what is the limit of its prolongation? We say: The term is only applied to one who accompanied him. Then, for the term's application by virtue of linguistic convention (waḍʿ), companionship suffices even if for an hour. However, customary usage (ʿurf) restricts the term to one whose companionship was frequent, and that is known through mass transmission (tawātur), sound narration, and the Companion's own statement, "My companionship was frequent." There is no precise limit for that frequency — it is determined by approximation, not exact specification.

chapters.arabic_text:
### | [مراتب الرواية]

الباب الرابع في  مستند الراوي وكيفية ضبطه.
ومستنده إما قراءة الشيخ عليه، أو قراءته على الشيخ، أو إجازته، أو
مناولته، أو رؤيته بخطه في كتاب، فهي خمس مراتب.
الأولى وهي الأعلى: قراءة الشيخ في معرض الإخبار ليروى عنه وذلك يسلط
الراوي على أن يقول " حدثنا " و " أخبرنا " و " قال فلان " و " سمعته يقول
".
الثانية: أن يقرأ على الشيخ وهو ساكت، فهو كقول " هذا صحيح " فتجوز
الرواية به خلافا لبعض أهل الظاهر؛ إذ لو لم يكن صحيحا لكان سكوته وتقريره
عليه فسقا قادحا في عدالته، ولو جوزنا ذلك لجوزنا أن يكذب إذا نطق بكونه
صحيحا.
نعم لو كان ثم مخيلة قلة اكتراث أو غفلة فلا يكفي السكوت، وهذا يسلط
الراوي على أن يقول " أخبرنا وحدثنا فلان قراءة عليه ". أما قوله حدثنا "
مطلقا أو " سمعت فلانا اختلفوا فيه، والصحيح أنه لا يجوز لأنه يشعر بالنطق؛
لأن الخبر والحديث والمسموع كل ذلك نطق، وذلك منه كذب إلا إذا علم بصريح
قوله أو بقرينة حاله أنه يريد به القراءة على الشيخ دون سماع حديثه.
الثالثة: الإجازة، وهو أن يقول: " أجزت لك أن تروي عني الكتاب الفلاني أو
ما صح عندك من مسموعاتي " وعند ذلك يجب الاحتياط في تعيين المسموع، أما إذا
اقتصر على قوله: " هذا مسموعي من فلان " فلا تجوز الرواية عنه؛ لأنه لم
يأذن في الرواية، فلعله لا يجوز الرواية لخلل يعرفه فيه وإن سمعه، وكذلك لو
قال: " عندي شهادة " لا يشهد ما لم يقل: " أذنت لك في أن تشهد على شهادتي "
أو لم تقم تلك الشهادة في مجلس الحكم؛ لأن الرواية شهادة والإنسان قد
يتساهل في الكلام، لكن عند جزم الشهادة قد يتوقف.
ثم الإجازة تسلط الراوي على أن يقول: حدثنا وأخبرنا إجازة. أما قوله: "
حدثنا " مطلقا جوزه قوم، وهو فاسد لأنه يشعر بسماع كلامه وهو كذب كما
ذكرناه في القراءة على الشيخ.
الرابعة: المناولة، وصورته أن يقول: " خذ هذا الكتاب وحدث به عني فقد
سمعته من فلان " ومجرد المناولة دون هذا اللفظ لا معنى  له، وإذا وجد هذا
اللفظ فلا معنى للمناولة فهو زيادة تكلف أحدثه بعض المحدثين بلا فائدة، كما
يجوز رواية الحديث بالإجازة فيجب العمل به خلافا لبعض أهل الظاهر؛ لأن
المقصود معرفة صحة الخبر لا عين الطريق المعرف.
وقوله: " هذا الكتاب مسموعي فاروه عني " في التعريف كقراءته والقراءة
عليه، وقولهم: " إنه قادر على أن يحدثه به " فهو كذلك، لكن أي حاجة إليه؟
ويلزم أن لا تصح القراءة عليه لأنه قادر على القراءة بنفسه، ويجب أن لا
يروي في حياة الشيخ لأنه قادر على الرجوع إلى الأصل كما في الشهادة، فدل أن
هذا لا يعتبر في الرواية. الخامسة: الاعتماد على الخط بأن يرى مكتوبا بخطه
" إني سمعت على فلان كذا " فلا يجوز أن يروي عنه لأن روايته شهادة عليه
بأنه قاله.
والخط لا يعرفه هذا، نعم يجوز أن يقول: " رأيت مكتوبا في كتاب بخط ظننت
أنه خط فلان "، فإن الخط أيضا قد يشبه الخط. أما إذا قال: " هذا خطي " قبل
قوله: " ولكن " لا يروي عنه ما لم يسلطه على الرواية بصريح قوله أو بقرينة
حاله في الجلوس لرواية الحديث.
أما إذا
قال عدل: " هذه نسخة صحيحة من صحيح البخاري " مثلا فرأى فيه حديثا، فليس
له أن يروي عنه، لكن هل يلزمه العمل؟ إن كان مقلدا فعليه أن يسأل المجتهد،
وإن كان مجتهدا فقال قوم: لا يجوز له العمل به ما لم يسمعه. وقال قوم: إذا
علم صحة النسخة بقول عدل جاز العمل، لأن أصحاب رسول الله - صلى الله عليه
وسلم - كانوا يحملون صحف الصدقات إلى البلاد وكان الخلق يعتمدون تلك الصحف
بشهادة حامل الصحف بصحته دون أن يسمعه كل واحد منه، فإن ذلك يفيد سكون
النفس وغلبة الظن.
وعلى الجملة فلا ينبغي أن يروي إلا ما يعلم سماعه أولا وحفظه وضبطه إلى
وقت الأداء، بحيث يعلم أن ما أداه هو الذي سمعه ولم يتغير منه حرف، فإن شك
في شيء منه فليترك الرواية.
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ر-ت-ب (r-t-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Ordering, ranking, stationing in sequence; a rank (martabah) is a fixed station of degree.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Hierarchical ordering of epistemic avenues—each rank corresponds to a distinct mode of certitude (yaqīn) or predominant conjecture (ghalabat al-ẓann) in transmission.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is spatial/sequential ordering; metaphorical extension to degrees of authority and evidentiary strength in legal epistemology.
- Root: ض-ب-ط (ḍ-b-ṭ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To guard, retain firmly, bind; mastery over something such that it does not escape.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The internal preservation of what is heard—the transmitter's cognitive fidelity ensuring no alteration (taghyīr) between audition and delivery.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: physical binding/restraint; metaphorical: the mind's firm retention of transmitted content.
- Root: ج-و-ز (j-w-z)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To pass through, be permissible; permissibility (jawāz) as crossing a threshold of legitimacy.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Legal permissibility—what is not prohibited, distinct from obligation (wujūb) and recommendation (nadb).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: spatial passage; metaphorical: legal license to act or transmit.
- Sībawayh Rule: Taqdīr al-Maḥdhūf (Ellipsis Restoration) — When a speaker says "ḥaddathanā" (he narrated to us), the underlying structure presumes direct audition (samāʿ) unless a qualifying phrase (e.g., "ijāzatan" or "qirāʾatan ʿalayhi") is explicitly appended; the default semantic load of the verb dictates the presumption.
chapters.translation:
I say: The fourth chapter concerns the transmitter's basis (mustanad) and the manner of his retention (ḍabṭ) of it. His basis is either: the shaykh's reading to him, or his reading to the shaykh, or his license (ijāzah), or his hand-delivery (munāwalah), or his seeing it in the shaykh's own handwriting in a book. These are five ranks.

The first—and it is the highest—is the shaykh's reading in the context of reporting (al-ikhbār) so that it may be related from him. This empowers the transmitter to say: "He narrated to us (ḥaddathanā)," "He informed us (akhbaranā)," "So-and-so said," and "I heard him saying."

The second: that he reads to the shaykh while the shaykh is silent. This is equivalent to his saying "This is sound (ṣaḥīḥ)." Thus, transmission by this mode is permissible, contrary to some of the Ẓāhirīs—for if it were not sound, then his silence and tacit approval (taqrīr) of it would be an act of immorality (fisq) impugning his probity (ʿadālah). And if we permitted that [i.e., that a probity-bearing scholar could silently approve an unsound reading], we would permit that he could lie when he explicitly states that it is sound.

Yes—if there were some indication of carelessness (qillat iktirāt) or heedlessness (ghaflah) on his part, then silence would not suffice. This [mode] empowers the transmitter to say: "So-and-so informed us and narrated to us, it being read to him." As for his saying "ḥaddathanā" absolutely, or "I heard so-and-so"—there is disagreement about it. The sound [position] is that it is not permissible, because it suggests oral utterance (nuṭq); for "the report (khabar)," "the narration (ḥadīth)," and "the heard (masmūʿ)" are all [forms of] speech, and that [claim] from him would be a lie—unless he knows by the shaykh's explicit statement or by an indication of his state (qarīnat ḥāl) that he means thereby the reading to the shaykh, not the hearing of his speech.

The third: the license (ijāzah)—that he says: "I have licensed you to relate from me such-and-such book, or whatever is authenticated to you of my auditions." At that point, caution (iḥtiyāṭ) is obligatory in specifying the auditioned [content]. But if he restricts himself to saying: "This is my audition from so-and-so," transmission from him is not permissible—because he has not authorized transmission. Perhaps transmission is not permissible due to some defect he knows in it, even though he heard it. Likewise, if he said: "I have a testimony (shahādah)," he does not testify unless he says: "I have authorized you to testify upon my testimony," or unless that testimony was established in a court of judgment (majlis al-ḥukm)—because transmission is testimony, and a person may be lax in speech, but when testimony is affirmed, he may hesitate.

Then, the license empowers the transmitter to say: "He narrated to us and informed us by license (ijāzah)." As for his saying "ḥaddathanā" absolutely—some permitted it, but it is corrupt (fāsid), because it suggests hearing his speech, and that is a lie, as we mentioned in the case of reading to the shaykh.

The fourth: the hand-delivery (munāwalah). Its form is that he says: "Take this book and narrate from me upon it, for I have heard it from so-and-so." Mere hand-delivery without this utterance has no meaning. And when this utterance is found, then hand-delivery has no meaning—it is a superfluous formality (takalluf) that some traditionists (muḥaddithūn) innovated without benefit. Just as transmission of a ḥadīth by license is permissible, so action upon it is obligatory, contrary to some of the Ẓāhirīs—because the objective is knowledge of the soundness of the report, not the specific path of identification [itself].

His saying: "This book is my audition, so narrate it from me"—in identification, it is like his reading and the reading to him. And their saying: "He is able to narrate it to him"—so he is, but what need is there for it? It would follow that reading to him would not be valid, because he is able to read himself. And he must not narrate during the shaykh's lifetime, because he is able to return to the original, as in testimony. This indicates that this [condition] is not considered in transmission.

The fifth: reliance upon handwriting (al-khaṭ)—that he sees written in the shaykh's hand: "I heard from so-and-so such-and-such." It is not permissible for him to narrate from him, because his narration is a testimony against him that he said it. And handwriting does not establish this. Yes—he may say: "I saw written in a book in a handwriting I conjectured to be so-and-so's handwriting," for handwriting may resemble handwriting. But if he says: "This is my handwriting," before his saying "but"—he does not narrate from him unless he empowers him to narrate by his explicit statement or by an indication of his state in sitting for the narration of ḥadīth.

But if a probity-bearing person (ʿadl) said: "This is a sound copy (nuskhah ṣaḥīḥah) of Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī," for example, and he saw in it a ḥadīth—he may not narrate from him. But is action upon it obligatory upon him? If he is a taqlīd-follower (muqallid), he must ask the mujtahid. And if he is a mujtahid, some said: it is not permissible for him to act upon it unless he has heard it. And some said: if he knows the soundness of the copy by the statement of a probity-bearing person, action is permissible—because the Companions of the Messenger of God—may God's peace and blessings be upon him—used to carry the scrolls of alms (ṣuḥuf al-ṣadaqāt) to the lands, and the people relied upon those scrolls by the testimony of the scroll-bearer to their soundness, without each one of them having heard it [directly]. For that produces tranquility of the soul (sukūn al-nafs) and predominance of conjecture (ghalabat al-ẓann).

In sum: he should not narrate except what he knows he heard first, and its retention and mastery (ḍabṭ) until the time of delivery—such that he knows that what he delivered is what he heard, with not a single letter altered from it. For if he doubts anything of it, let him abandon the narration.

chapters.title_en: The Case of Doubt Concerning What One Has Heard from al-Zuhrī, and Related Issues
chapters.arabic_text:
### | [مسألة الشك في مسموعاته عن الزهري مثلا حديث واحد  شك أنه سمعه من الزهري أم لا]

ويتفرع عن هذا الأصل مسائل
مسائل إذا كان في مسموعاته عن الزهري مثلا حديث واحد شك أنه سمعه من
الزهري أم لا، لم يجز له أن يقول: " سمعت الزهري " ولا أن يقول: " قال
الزهري "، لأن قوله: " قال الزهري " شهادة على الزهري، فلا يجوز إلا عن
علم، فلعله سمعه من غيره فهو كمن سمع إقرارا ولم يعلم أن المقر زيد أو
عمرو، فلا يجوز أن يشهد على زيد، بل نقول: لو سمع مائة حديث من شيخ وفيها
حديث واحد علم أنه لم يسمعه ولكنه التبس عليه عينه فليس له روايته، بل ليس
له رواية شيء من الأحاديث عنه، إذ ما من حديث إلا ويمكن أن يكون هو الذي لم
يسمعه.
ولو غلب على ظنه في حديث أنه مسموع من الزهري لم تجز الرواية بغلبة الظن
وقال قوم: يجوز؛ لأن الاعتماد في هذا الباب على غلبة الظن.
وهو بعيد؛ لأن الاعتماد في الشهادة على غلبة الظن ولكن في حق الحاكم فإنه
لا يعلم صدق الشاهد. أما الشاهد فينبغي أن يتحقق لأن تكليفه أن لا يشهد إلا
على المعلوم فيما تمكن فيه المشاهدة ممكن، وتكليف الحاكم أن لا يحكم إلا
بصدق الشاهد محال، وكذلك الراوي لا سبيل له إلى معرفة صدق الشيخ ولكن له
طريق إلى معرفة قوله بالسماع، فإذا لم يتحقق فينبغي أن لا يروي.
فإن قيل: فالواحد في عصرنا يجوز أن يقول " قال رسول الله - صلى الله عليه
وسلم - " ولا يتحقق ذلك. قلنا: لا طريق له إلى تحقق ذلك ولا يفهم من قوله:
" قال رسول الله " - صلى الله عليه وسلم - أنه سمعه، لكن يفهم منه أنه سمع
هذا الحديث من غيره أو رواه في كتاب يعتمد عليه وكل من سمع ذلك لا يلزمه
العمل به لأنه مرسل لا يدري من أين يقوله، وإنما يلزم العمل إذا ذكر مستنده
حتى ينظر في حاله وعدالته والله أعلم.

### | [مسألة إذا أنكر الشيخ الحديث إنكار جاحد قاطع بكذب  الراوي ولم يعمل به]

إذا أنكر الشيخ الحديث إنكار جاحد قاطع بكذب الراوي ولم يعمل به لم يصر
الراوي مجروحا؛ لأن الجرح ربما لا يثبت بقول واحد ولأنه مكذب شيخه كما أن
شيخه مكذب له وهما عدلان، فهما كبينتين متكاذبتين، فلا يوجب الجرح. أما إذا
أنكر إنكار متوقف وقال: " لست أذكره " فيعمل بالخبر؛ لأن الراوي جازم أنه
سمعه منه وهو ليس بقاطع بتكذيبه وهما عدلان فصدقهما إذا ممكن. وذهب الكرخي
إلى أن نسيان الشيخ الحديث يبطل الحديث، وبنى عليه اطراح خبر الزهري «أيما
امرأة نكحت بغير إذن وليها» ، واستدل بأنه الأصل ولأنه ليس للشيخ أن يعمل
بالحديث والراوي فرعه، فكيف يعمل به؟ قلنا: للشيخ أن يعمل به إذا روى العدل
له عنه، فإن بقي شك له مع رواية العدل فليس له العمل به، وعلى
الراوي العمل إذا قطع بأنه سمع، وعلى غيرهما العمل جمعا بين تصديقهما.
والحاكم يجب عليه العمل بقول الشاهد المزور الظاهر العدالة ويحرم على
الشاهد. ويجب على العامي العمل بفتوى المجتهد وإن تغير اجتهاده إذا لم يعلم
تغير اجتهاده، والمجتهد لا يعمل به بعد التغير لأنه علمه، فعمل كل واحد على
حسب حاله. وقد ذهب إلى العمل به مالك والشافعي وجماهير المتكلمين؛ وهذا لأن
النسيان غالب على الإنسان وأي محدث يحفظ في حينه جميع ما رواه في عمره؟
فصار كشك الشيخ في زيادة في الحديث أو في إعراب في الحديث، فإن ذلك لما لم
يبطل الحديث لكثرة وقوع الشك فيه فكذلك أصل الحديث.

### | [مسألة انفراد الثقة بزيادة في الحديث]

عن جماعة النقلة مقبول عند الجماهير سواء كانت الزيادة من حيث اللفظ أو
من حيث المعنى؛ لأنه لو انفرد بنقل حديث عن جميع الحفاظ لقبل، فكذلك إذا
انفرد بزيادة لأن العدل لا يتهم بما أمكن. فإن قيل: يبعد انفراده بالحفظ مع
إصغاء الجميع. قلنا تصديق الجميع أولى إذا كان ممكنا وهو قاطع بالسماع
والآخرون ما قطعوا بالنفي، فلعل الرسول - صلى الله عليه وسلم - ذكره في
مجلسين: فحيث ذكر  الزيادة لم يحضر إلا الواحد أو كرر في مجلس واحد وذكر
الزيادة في إحدى الكرتين ولم يحضر إلا الواحد. ويحتمل أن يكون راوي النقص
دخل في أثناء المجلس فلم يسمع التمام، أو اشتركوا في الحضور ونسوا الزيادة
إلا واحدا، أو طرأ في أثناء الحديث سبب شاغل مدهش فغفل به البعض عن الإصغاء
فيختص بحفظ الزيادة المقبل على الإصغاء، أو عرض لبعض السامعين خاطر شاغل عن
الزيادة أو عرض له مزعج يوجب قيامه قبل التمام، فإذا احتمل ذلك فلا يكذب
العدل ما أمكن.

### | [مسألة رواية بعض الخبر]

ممتنعة عند أكثر من منع نقل الحديث بالمعنى،
ومن جوز النقل على المعنى جوز ذلك إن كان قد رواه مرة بتمامه ولم يتعلق
المذكور بالمتروك تعلقا يغير معناه، وأما إذا تعلق كشرط العبادة أو ركنها
أو ما به التمام فنقل البعض تحريف وتلبيس، أما إذا روى الحديث مرة تاما
ومرة ناقصا نقصانا لا يغير فهو جائز ولكن بشرط أن لا يتطرق إليه سوء الظن
بالتهمة، فإذا علم أنه يتهم باضطراب النقل وجب عليه الاحتراز عن ذلك.
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ش-ه-د (sh-h-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To be present, to witness, to testify; shahādah is an informed declaration of what one has directly witnessed.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Testimony (shahādah) in legal-theological context requires certain knowledge (ʿilm), not conjecture (ẓann), for it is a report binding upon others.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal usage denotes ocular presence; metaphorical extension to auditory testimony is permissible only where certainty obtains.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Restriction (al-sharṭ al-muqayyid) — the permissibility of an action is conditioned upon the realization of its epistemic ground (ʿilm), and its negation follows from the negation of that ground.
chapters.translation:
I say: Branching from this principle are several issues.

**First Issue:** If, among the reports he has heard from al-Zuhrī — for example — there is a single ḥadīth concerning which he doubts whether he heard it from al-Zuhrī or not, it is not permissible for him to say: "I heard al-Zuhrī say," nor to say: "al-Zuhrī said." For his statement "al-Zuhrī said" constitutes testimony (shahādah) concerning al-Zuhrī, and testimony is not permissible except upon knowledge. Perhaps he heard it from someone other than him. This is like one who hears an acknowledgment (iqrār) but does not know whether the acknowledger was Zayd or ʿAmr — he may not testify against Zayd. Rather, we say: even if he heard a hundred ḥadīths from a shaykh, and among them there is one ḥadīth which he knows he did not hear from him, but its specific identity is confused for him, then he may not narrate it. Indeed, he may not narrate anything whatsoever from that shaykh, for there is no ḥadīth among them except that it could be the very one he did not hear.

And if his dominant presumption (ghalabat al-ẓann) inclines toward a particular ḥadīth being heard from al-Zuhrī, narration based on dominant presumption is still not permissible. Some have said: it is permissible, because reliance in this domain is upon dominant presumption. But this is far-fetched; for reliance upon dominant presumption applies to testimony — but only on the part of the judge, who cannot know the truthfulness of the witness. As for the witness himself, he must be certain, because his obligation is not to testify except upon what is known, inasmuch as direct observation is possible for him. The judge's obligation, by contrast, is not to judge except upon the truthfulness of the witness — which is impossible [to verify directly]. Likewise, the narrator has no path to knowing the truthfulness of the shaykh, but he does have a path to knowing his utterance through direct hearing (samāʿ). Therefore, if he is not certain, he ought not to narrate.

If it is said: "The single narrator in our age may say 'The Messenger of God — peace be upon him — said,' without being certain of that," we reply: He has no path to certainty in that matter, and his statement "The Messenger of God — peace be upon him — said" is not understood to mean that he himself heard it directly. Rather, it is understood to mean that he heard this ḥadīth from someone else, or that he narrated it from a book upon which reliance is placed. Whoever hears such a narration is not obliged to act upon it, for it is a disconnected report (mursal) — one does not know from where he is saying it. Action becomes obligatory only when he mentions his chain of transmission (sanad), so that his condition and integrity may be examined. And God knows best.

**Second Issue:** If the shaykh denies the ḥadīth with the denial of one who rejects it outright — decisively affirming the narrator's falsehood — and does not act upon it, the narrator does not thereby become impaired (majrūḥ). For impairment is not established by a single person's statement, and because the narrator is accusing his shaykh of falsehood just as his shaykh is accusing him — and both are upright (ʿadl) — they are like two mutually contradictory testimonies, which does not necessitate impairment. However, if the shaykh denies it with the denial of one who suspends judgment, saying: "I do not recall it," then the report is acted upon. For the narrator is certain that he heard it from him, while the shaykh is not decisive in accusing him of falsehood, and both are upright — so affirming both is possible. Al-Karkhī held that the shaykh's forgetfulness invalidates the ḥadīth, and upon this he based his rejection of al-Zuhrī's report: {«أيما امرأة نكحت بغير إذن وليها»} ("Any woman who marries without the permission of her guardian..."). He argued that the shaykh is the origin (aṣl), and it is not permissible for the shaykh to act upon the ḥadīth [he has forgotten], while the narrator is his branch (farʿ) — so how could the branch act upon it? We reply: It is permissible for the shaykh to act upon it when an upright narrator has narrated it to him from himself. If doubt remains for him despite the upright narrator's narration, then it is not permissible for him to act upon it. But the narrator must act upon it, since he is certain that he heard it; and others must act upon it as well, combining affirmation of both [narrator and shaykh]. The judge is obligated to act upon the testimony of a witness who is outwardly upright even if the witness has fabricated it — while it is forbidden for the witness himself [to testify falsely]. Likewise, the common person (ʿāmmī) must act upon the fatwā of a mujtahid even if the mujtahid's own ijtihād has changed, so long as the common person is unaware of that change; while the mujtahid himself does not act upon it after the change, because he knows of it. Thus each acts according to his own condition. Mālik, al-Shāfiʿī, and the majority of the theologians have held that [the report is acted upon despite the shaykh's forgetfulness]. This is because forgetfulness is predominant over man — and which narrator preserves at any given moment everything he has narrated throughout his life? It thus becomes like the shaykh's doubt concerning an addition (ziyādah) in the ḥadīth or concerning an inflection (iʿrāb) in it — for just as that does not invalidate the ḥadīth due to the frequency of doubt occurring therein, so likewise the origin of the ḥadīth [is not invalidated by forgetfulness].

**Third Issue:** The exclusive narration (infirād) of a trustworthy narrator concerning an addition (ziyādah) in a ḥadīth is accepted by the majority — whether the addition is in wording (lafẓ) or in meaning (maʿnā). For if he were alone in narrating an entire ḥadīth from all the preservers (ḥuffāẓ), it would be accepted; so likewise if he is alone in an addition — because an upright narrator is not accused [of falsehood] as long as [an alternative explanation] remains possible. If it is said: "His exclusive preservation [of the addition] is improbable given that all were listening attentively," we reply: Affirming the [truthfulness of the] narrator is more appropriate when it is possible. For he is decisive about having heard it, while the others did not decisively affirm its negation. Perhaps the Messenger of God — peace be upon him — mentioned it in two sessions: where the addition was mentioned, only that one narrator was present; or he repeated it in a single session and mentioned the addition in one of the two repetitions, with only that one present. It is also possible that the narrator of the shorter version entered mid-session and did not hear the completion; or they were all present together but forgot the addition except for one; or during the session an absorbing, distracting cause arose, and some became heedless of listening while the one attentive to listening was uniquely preserved in the addition; or some of the listeners were overtaken by a distracting thought concerning the addition, or by something distressing that obliged them to leave before completion. When such possibilities exist, the upright narrator is not accused of falsehood as long as [such explanation] remains possible.

**Fourth Issue:** Narrating part of a ḥadīth is prohibited according to most of those who prohibit narrating the ḥadīth by meaning (bi-l-maʿnā). As for one who permits narration by meaning, he permits this [partial narration] provided that he has once narrated it in full, and that what is mentioned is not connected to what is omitted in a manner that alters its meaning. But if there is such a connection — as with a condition (sharṭ) of worship, or its pillar (rukn), or that by which its completion is achieved — then narrating part is distortion (taḥrīf) and obfuscation (talbīs). As for one who narrates the ḥadīth once in full and once in abbreviated form, with an abbreviation that does not alter [the meaning], this is permissible — but on the condition that he does not thereby expose himself to suspicion of unreliability. If he knows that he will be accused of disordered transmission, he must guard against that.

chapters.title_en: The Transmission of Hadith by Meaning Rather Than Wording
chapters.arabic_text:
### | [مسألة نقل الحديث بالمعنى دون اللفظ]

حرام على الجاهل بمواقع الخطاب ودقائق الألفاظ، أما العالم بالفرق بين
المحتمل وغير المحتمل، والظاهر والأظهر، والعام والأعم، فقد جوز له الشافعي
ومالك وأبو حنيفة وجماهير الفقهاء أن ينقله على المعنى إذا فهمه، وقال
فريق: لا يجوز إلا إبدال اللفظ بما يرادفه ويساويه في المعنى، كما يبدل
القعود بالجلوس والعلم بالمعرفة والاستطاعة بالقدرة والإبصار بالإحساس
بالبصر والحظر بالتحريم وسائر ما لا يشك فيه، وعلى الجملة ما لا يتطرق إليه
تفاوت بالاستنباط والفهم.
وإنما ذلك فيما فهمه قطعا لا فيما فهمه بنوع استدلال يختلف فيه الناظرون.
ويدل على جواز ذلك للعالم الإجماع على جواز شرح الشرع للعجم بلسانهم، فإذا
جاز إبدال العربية بعجمية ترادفها فلأن يجوز عربية بعربية ترادفها وتساويها
أولى، وكذلك كان سفراء رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - في
البلاد يبلغونهم أوامره بلغتهم، وكذلك من سمع شهادة الرسول - صلى الله
عليه  وسلم - فله أن يشهد على شهادته بلغة أخرى، وهذا لأنا نعلم أنه لا تعبد
في اللفظ وإنما المقصود فهم المعنى وإيصاله إلى الخلق، وليس ذلك كالتشهد
والتكبير وما تعبد فيه باللفظ.
فإن قيل فقد قال: - صلى الله عليه وسلم - «نضر الله امرأ سمع مقالتي
فوعاها فأداها كما سمعها، فرب مبلغ أوعى من سامع ورب حامل فقه ليس بفقيه
ورب حامل فقه إلى من هو أفقه منه» . قلنا: هذا هو الحجة؛ لأنه ذكر العلة
وهو اختلاف الناس في الفقه، فما لا يختلف الناس فيه من الألفاظ المترادفة
فلا يمنع منه.
وهذا الحديث بعينه قد نقل بألفاظ مختلفة والمعنى واحد، وإن أمكن أن تكون
جميع الألفاظ قول رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - في أوقات مختلفة، لكن
الأغلب أنه حديث واحد ونقل بألفاظ مختلفة، فإنه روي «رحم الله امرأ» و «نضر
الله امرأ» وروي: «ورب حامل فقه لا فقه له» وروي «حامل فقه غير فقيه» وكذلك
الخطب المتحدة والوقائع المتحدة رواها الصحابة - رضي الله عنهم - بألفاظ
مختلفة فدل ذلك على الجواز.
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ن-ق-ل (naqala)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To transfer, convey, transmit; carrying something from one place to another, whether physical or abstract.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Technical transmission of reports (naql al-ḥadīth) — the conveyance of prophetic statements across generations, distinct from riwāyah in its emphasis on the act of transfer itself.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for physical carrying; metaphorical (majāz) for conveying speech or meaning, as in "naqala al-khabar" (he transmitted the report).
- Root: ت-ر-ا-د-ف (tarāduf)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Synonymy; multiple words sharing a single meaning, from radafa (to follow, ride behind).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In uṣūl al-fiqh, the question of whether perfect synonymy exists in language; here used to denote words of equal semantic value.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Rhetorical equivalence — words that can substitute without altering the intended sense.
- Root: ع-ب-د (ʿabada)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To worship, serve with humility; also to adhere to a binding command.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Taʿabbud — ritual obligation tied to the very wording (al-taʿabbud bi-al-lafẓ), as in prayer formulas, where the form itself is divinely mandated.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal here — the act of being bound to the letter, not merely the meaning.
- Sībawayh Rule: Taqdīr al-ʿāmil (Ellipsis of the Governing Element) — In the phrase "حرام على الجاهل" the predicate is understood as a complete nominal sentence with an implied copula; the conditional structure "أما... فقد جوز" requires parsing the protasis as a topic (mubtadaʾ) with the apodosis as its comment (khabar), a standard pattern for legal reasoning (istidlāl).
chapters.translation:
I say: Transmission of hadith by meaning rather than wording is forbidden to one ignorant of the loci of discourse and the subtleties of expressions. As for one who knows the difference between the probable and the improbable, the apparent and the more apparent, the general and the more general — al-Shāfiʿī, Mālik, Abū Ḥanīfah, and the majority of jurists have permitted him to transmit it by meaning when he comprehends it. But a faction said: It is not permissible except to replace the wording with what is synonymous with it and equal to it in meaning — just as one replaces "sitting" (al-quʿūd) with "seating" (al-julūs), "knowledge" (al-ʿilm) with "cognition" (al-maʿrifah), "capacity" (al-istiṭāʿah) with "power" (al-qudrah), "seeing" (al-ibṣār) with "sensing by sight" (al-iḥsās bi-al-baṣar), "prohibition" (al-ḥaẓr) with "forbiddance" (al-taḥrīm), and all other cases where there is no doubt — in sum, whatever admits no variance through inference and understanding.

This permissibility applies only to what he comprehends with certainty, not to what he comprehends through a kind of reasoning in which the investigators differ.

The evidence for its permissibility for the learned is the consensus (ijmāʿ) on the permissibility of explaining the Sacred Law to non-Arabs in their own tongues. If replacing Arabic with a synonymous non-Arabic language is permissible, then replacing Arabic with synonymous and equivalent Arabic is all the more fitting. Likewise, the envoys of the Messenger of God — may God bless him and grant him peace — used to convey his commands to the lands in their own languages. Similarly, one who heard the testimony of the Messenger — may God bless him and grant him peace — may bear witness to his testimony in another language. This is because we know that there is no ritual binding (taʿabbud) in the wording itself; rather, the purpose is to comprehend the meaning and convey it to creation. This is not like the tashahhud, the takbīr, and what is ritually bound to its wording.

If it is said: He — may God bless him and grant him peace — said: {«نضر الله امرأ سمع مقالتي فوعاها فأداها كما سمعها، فرب مبلغ أوعى من سامع ورب حامل فقه ليس بفقيه ورب حامل فقه إلى من هو أفقه منه»} ("May God brighten a man who heard my saying, grasped it, and conveyed it as he heard it; for perhaps a transmitter is more perceptive than a hearer, and perhaps a carrier of jurisprudence is not a jurist, and perhaps a carrier of jurisprudence carries it to one more juristic than he") — we say: This very hadith is the proof; for he mentioned the cause (ʿillah), namely the difference among people in jurisprudence. What does not differ among people — namely synonymous expressions — is not prevented.

This very hadith has indeed been transmitted with different wordings while the meaning is one. Even if it is possible that all the wordings were the speech of the Messenger of God — may God bless him and grant him peace — at different times, the more probable is that it is a single hadith transmitted with different wordings. For it was narrated as {«رحم الله امرأ»} ("May God have mercy on a man") and {«نضر الله امرأ»} ("May God brighten a man"), and it was narrated as {«ورب حامل فقه لا فقه له»} ("and perhaps a carrier of jurisprudence who has no jurisprudence") and {«حامل فقه غير فقيه»} ("a carrier of jurisprudence who is not a jurist"). Likewise, the unified sermons and unified events were narrated by the Companions — may God be pleased with them — with different wordings, and that indicates permissibility.

chapters.title_en: The Mursal Report is Accepted [According to Some] and Rejected [According to Others]
chapters.arabic_text:
### | [مسألة المرسل مقبول]

عند مالك وأبي حنيفة والجماهير.
ومردود عند الشافعي والقاضي وهو المختار وصورته أن يقول: " قال رسول الله
" - صلى الله عليه وسلم - من لم يعاصره أو قال من لم يعاصر أبا هريرة " قال
أبو هريرة " والدليل أنه لو ذكر شيخه ولم يعدله وبقي مجهولا عندنا لم
نقبله، فإذا لم يسمه فالجهل أتم، فمن لا يعرف عينه كيف تعرف عدالته؟ فإن
قيل: رواية العدل عنه تعديل.
فالجواب من وجهين:
الأول: أنا لا نسلم، فإن العدل قد يروي عمن لو سئل عنه لتوقف فيه أو
جرحه، وقد رأيناهم رووا عمن إذا سئلوا عنه عدلوه مرة وجرحوه أخرى أو قالوا
لا ندري، فالراوي عنه ساكت عن تعديله. ولو كان السكوت عن الجرح تعديلا لكان
السكوت عن التعديل جرحا، ولوجب أن يكون الراوي إذا جرح من روى عنه مكذبا
نفسه؛ ولأن شهادة الفرع ليس تعديلا للأصل ما لم يصرح. وافتراق الرواية
والشهادة في  بعض التعبدات لا يوجب فرقا في هذا المعنى كما لم يوجب فرقا في
منع قبول رواية المجروح والمجهول.
وإذا لم يجز أن يقال: لا يشهد العدل إلا على شهادة عدل، لم يجز ذلك في
الرواية ووجب فيها معرفة عين الشيخ والأصل حتى ينظر في حالهما. فإن قيل:
العنعنة كافية في الرواية مع أن قوله " روى فلان عن فلان عن فلان " يحتمل
ما لم يسمعه فلان عن فلان، بل بلغه بواسطة ومع الاحتمال يقبل ومثل ذلك في
الشهادة لا يقبل. قلنا: هذا إذا لم يوجب فرقا في رواية المجهول.
والمرسل مروي عن مجهول، فينبغي أن لا يقبل. ثم العنعنة جرت العادة بها في
الكتبة، فإنهم استثقلوا أن يكتبوا عند كل اسم " روى عن فلان سماعا منه "
وشحوا على القرطاس والوقت أن يضيعوه فأوجزوا. وإنما يقبل في الرواية ذلك
إذا علم بصريح لفظه أو عادته أنه يريد به السماع، فإن لم يرد السماع فهو
متردد بين المسند والمرسل فلا يقبل.
الجواب الثاني: أنا إن سلمنا جدلا أن الرواية تعديل فتعديله المطلق لا
يقبل ما لم يذكر السبب، فلو صرح بأنه سمعه من عدل ثقة لم يلزم قبوله، وإن
سلم قبول التعديل
المطلق فذلك في حق شخص نعرف عينه ولا يعرف بفسق، أما من لم نعرف عينه
فلعله لو ذكره لعرفناه بفسق لم يطلع عليه المعدل، وإنما يكتفى في كل مكلف
بتعريف غيره عند العجز عن معرفة نفسه ولا يعلم عجزه ما لم يعرفه بعينه.
وبمثل هذه العلة لم يقبل تعديل شاهد الفرع مطلقا ما لم يعرف الأصل ولم
يعينه، فلعل الحاكم يعرفه بفسق وعداوة، وغيره احتجوا باتفاق الصحابة
والتابعين على قبول مرسل العدل، فابن عباس مع كثرة روايته قيل: إنه لم يسمع
من رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - إلا أربعة أحاديث لصغر سنه، وصرح بذلك
في حديث الربا في النسيئة وقال: " حدثني به أسامة بن زيد " وروى «أن رسول
الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - لم يزل يلبي حتى رمى جمرة العقبة»  ، فلما روجع
قال: " حدثني به أخي الفضل بن عباس ".
وروى ابن عمر عن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - أنه قال: «من صلى على
جنازة فله قيراط» ثم أسنده إلى أبي هريرة. وروى أبو هريرة: أن «من أصبح
جنبا في رمضان فلا صوم له» وقال: ما أنا قلتها ورب الكعبة. ولكن محمدا -
صلى الله عليه وسلم - قالها، فلما روجع قال: " حدثني به الفضل بن عباس،
وقال البراء بن عازب: ما كل ما نحدثكم به سمعناه من رسول الله - صلى الله
عليه وسلم -، لكن سمعنا بعضه وحدثنا أصحابه ببعضه.
أما التابعون فقد قال النخعي: إذا قلت حدثني فلان عن عبد الله فهو حدثني،
وإذا قلت قال عبد الله فقد سمعته من غير واحد. وكذلك نقل عن جماعة من
التابعين قبول المرسل. والجواب من وجهين، الأول: أن هذا صحيح ويدل على قبول
بعضهم المراسيل، والمسألة في محل الاجتهاد ولا يثبت فيها إجماع أصلا.
وفيه ما يدل على أن الجملة لم يقبلوا المراسيل ولذلك باحثوا ابن عباس
وابن عمر وأبا هريرة مع جلالة قدرهم لا لشك في عدالتهم ولكن للكشف عن
الراوي. فإن قيل: قبل بعضهم وسكت الآخرون فكان إجماعا. قلنا: لا نسلم ثبوت
الإجماع بسكوتهم لا سيما في محل الاجتهاد، بل لعله سكت مضمرا للإنكار أو
مترددا فيه.
والجواب الثاني: أن من المنكرين للمرسل من قبل مرسل الصحابي لأنهم يحدثون
عن الصحابة وكلهم عدول، ومنهم من أضاف إليه مراسيل التابعين لأنهم يروون عن
الصحابة، ومنهم من خصص كبار التابعين بقبول مرسله.
والمختار على قياس رد المرسل أن التابعي والصحابي إذا عرف بصريح خبره أو
بعادته أنه لا يروي إلا عن صحابي قبل مرسله، وإن لم يعرف ذلك فلا يقبل؛
لأنهم قد يروون عن غير الصحابي من الأعراب الذين لا صحبة لهم، وإنما ثبتت
لنا عدالة أهل الصحبة.
قال الزهري بعد الإرسال: حدثني به رجل على باب عبد الملك. وقال عروة بن
الزبير فيما أرسله عن بسرة: حدثني به بعض الحرس.
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To send forth, dispatch; a message conveyed by a messenger; hence "mursal" as a report whose chain is severed from the Companion.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In uṣūl al-fiqh, the mursal is a narration where the Successor (tābiʿī) omits the Companion and reports directly from the Prophet (ﷺ); its epistemic status hinges on the unknown intermediary.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is "sent" or "released"; metaphorically, the chain is "released" from its anchor, leaving the transmitter unidentified.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause (al-Sharṭ) — The phrase "if he had mentioned his shaykh... we would not accept" establishes a hypothetical counterfactual, governing the logical parity between named-but-unknown and unnamed transmitters.
chapters.translation:
I say: The mursal report is accepted according to Mālik, Abū Ḥanīfah, and the majority of scholars. It is rejected according to al-Shāfiʿī and al-Qāḍī, and this rejection is the position I choose. Its form is that the narrator says: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said" — while he did not live in his era — or he says: "Abū Hurayrah said" — while he did not live in Abū Hurayrah's era.

The proof [for rejection] is that if he had mentioned his shaykh and had not declared him upright (ʿadl), and the shaykh remained unknown to us, we would not accept his report. So if he does not even name him, the ignorance is more complete. For how can one know the uprightness (ʿadālah) of one whose very identity is unknown? If it is said: "The upright narrator's transmission from him constitutes a declaration of his uprightness," the answer is from two angles:

The first: We do not concede this. For an upright narrator may transmit from someone who, if questioned about him, would hesitate regarding him or even impugn him. We have indeed seen them transmit from persons who, when asked, sometimes declared them upright and at other times impugned them, or said: "We do not know." Thus the transmitter from him remains silent about his uprightness. And if silence about impugnment were a declaration of uprightness, then silence about uprightness would have to be an impugnment. It would then follow that a narrator who impugns the one from whom he transmitted would be accusing himself of falsehood. Moreover, the testimony of a secondary witness is not a declaration of the primary witness's uprightness unless he explicitly states it. And the distinction between transmission (riwāyah) and testimony (shahādah) in certain devotional matters does not necessitate a distinction in this particular meaning — just as it did not necessitate a distinction in the prohibition of accepting the report of the impugned and the unknown.

And just as it is not permissible to say: "An upright man does not testify except upon the testimony of an upright man," so too it is not permissible in transmission. Rather, it is obligatory therein to know the very identity of the shaykh and the original source, so that their condition may be examined. If it is said: "The chain of ʿanʿanah (saying 'so-and-so from so-and-so') is sufficient in transmission, even though his saying 'so-and-so narrated from so-and-so from so-and-so' admits the possibility that the latter did not hear it directly from the former, but rather it reached him through an intermediary — and despite this possibility, it is accepted, whereas the like of this in testimony is not accepted." We say: This [concession] does not necessitate a distinction regarding the narration of the unknown. For the mursal is narrated from an unknown person, and therefore it ought not to be accepted.

Then, as for ʿanʿanah, the customary practice of the scribes has established it, for they found it burdensome to write at every name: "He narrated from so-and-so, having heard it directly from him." They were frugal with parchment and time, unwilling to waste them, so they abbreviated. And this [abbreviation] is only accepted in transmission when it is known — either by his explicit wording or by his established habit — that he intends by it direct hearing (samāʿ). If he does not intend direct hearing, then he is wavering between the connected (musnad) and the severed (mursal), and thus it is not accepted.

The second answer: Even if we concede for the sake of argument that his transmission is a declaration of uprightness, his absolute declaration of uprightness is not accepted unless he mentions the reason. For if he explicitly stated that he heard it from an upright, trustworthy person, it would not be obligatory to accept it. And even if we concede the acceptance of an absolute declaration of uprightness, that applies to a person whose identity we know and who is not known for immorality. As for one whose identity we do not know, perhaps if he had named him, we would have known him to be immoral in a way the one who declared him upright did not perceive. For every legally responsible person (mukallaf) is only excused by another's identification of him when he is unable to know him himself — and his inability is not known until his identity is known.

And by this very rationale, the absolute declaration of uprightness by a secondary witness is not accepted unless the primary witness is known and identified. For perhaps the judge knows him to be immoral or hostile. Others have argued by the consensus of the Companions and the Successors on accepting the mursal of an upright narrator. Thus Ibn ʿAbbās — despite the abundance of his narrations — it is said that he heard from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) only four hadiths due to his young age. He explicitly stated this in the hadith of usury (ribā) in the deferred sale, saying: "Usāmah ibn Zayd narrated it to me." And he narrated that «the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) continued to recite the talbiyah until he stoned the Jamrat al-ʿAqabah» — but when he was questioned, he said: "My brother al-Faḍl ibn ʿAbbās narrated it to me."

And Ibn ʿUmar narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: «Whoever prays over a funeral, for him is a qīrāṭ» — then he traced it back to Abū Hurayrah. And Abū Hurayrah narrated that «whoever wakes up in a state of major impurity (junub) during Ramadan, his fast is void» — and he said: "By the Lord of the Kaʿbah, I did not say this; rather, Muḥammad (ﷺ) said it." But when he was questioned, he said: "Al-Faḍl ibn ʿAbbās narrated it to me." And al-Barāʾ ibn ʿĀzib said: "Not everything we narrate to you did we hear from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ); rather, we heard some of it, and his Companions narrated some of it to us."

As for the Successors, al-Nakhaʿī said: "When I say, 'So-and-so narrated to me from ʿAbdullāh,' then it is as if he narrated to me directly. And when I say, 'ʿAbdullāh said,' then I have heard it from more than one person." Likewise, it is transmitted from a group of the Successors that they accepted the mursal. The answer is from two angles:

The first: This is true and indicates that some of them accepted the mursal reports. But the matter is a locus of juristic reasoning (ijtihād), and no consensus (ijmāʿ) is established therein at all. Indeed, in what we have mentioned there is evidence that the majority did not accept the mursal reports — for this reason they interrogated Ibn ʿAbbās, Ibn ʿUmar, and Abū Hurayrah, despite their great stature — not out of doubt regarding their uprightness, but to uncover the identity of the narrator. If it is said: "Some accepted and the others remained silent, so this constituted a consensus," we say: We do not concede the establishment of consensus by their silence — especially in a locus of ijtihād. Rather, perhaps the one who remained silent was inwardly disapproving or undecided about it.

The second answer: Among those who reject the mursal, some accept the mursal of a Companion, because they narrate from the Companions, all of whom are upright. Some of them extend this to the mursal of the Successors, because they narrate from the Companions. And some of them restrict acceptance to the mursal of the senior Successors.

The position I choose, by analogy with the rejection of the mursal, is that when a Successor or a Companion is known — by his explicit statement or by his established habit — that he narrates only from a Companion, his mursal is accepted. If this is not known, it is not accepted. For they may narrate from non-Companions among the Bedouins who have no companionship [with the Prophet]. And the uprightness of the people of companionship is established for us only [as a class].

Al-Zuhrī, after sending a mursal report, said: "A man at the door of ʿAbd al-Malik narrated it to me." And ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr, regarding what he sent from Busrah, said: "Some of the guards narrated it to me."

chapters.arabic_text:
### | [مسألة خبر الواحد  فيما تعم به البلوى]

مقبول خلافا للكرخي وبعض أصحاب الرأي؛ لأن كل ما نقله العدل وصدقه فيه
ممكن وجب تصديقه، فمس الذكر مثلا نقله العدل وصدقه فيه ممكن فإنا لا نقطع
بكذب ناقله، بخلاف ما لو انفرد واحد بنقل ما تحيل العادة فيه أن لا يستفيض
كقتل أمير في السوق وعزل وزير وهجوم في الجامع منع الناس من الجمعة أو كخسف
أو زلزلة أو انقضاض كوكب عظيم وغيره من العجائب، فإن الدواعي تتوفر على
إشاعة جميع ذلك ويستحيل انكتامه، وكذلك القرآن لا يقبل فيه خبر الواحد
لعلمنا بأنه - صلى الله عليه وسلم -
تعبد بإشاعته واعتنى بإلقائه إلى كافة الخلق، فإن الدواعي تتوفر على
إشاعته ونقله لأنه أصل الدين، والمنفرد برواية سورة أو آية كاذب قطعا، فأما
ما تعم به البلوى فلا نقطع بكذب خبر الواحد فيه.
فإن قيل: بم تنكرون على من يقطع بكذبه؛ لأن الخارج من السبيلين لما كان
الإنسان لا ينفك عنه في اليوم والليلة مرارا وكانت الطهارة تنتقض به لا يحل
لرسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - أن لا يشيع حكمه ويناجي به الآحاد؛ إذ
يؤدي إلى إخفاء الشرع وإلى أن تبطل صلاة العباد وهم لا يشعرون، فتجب
الإشاعة في مثله ثم تتوفر الدواعي على نقله، وكذلك مس الذكر مما يكثر وقوعه
فكيف يخفى حكمه؟ قلنا: هذا يبطل أولا بالوتر وحكم الفصد والحجامة والقهقهة
ووجوب الغسل من غسل الميت وإفراد الإقامة وتثنيتها وكل ذلك مما تعم به
البلوى وقد أثبتوها بخبر الواحد.
فإن زعموا أن ليس عموم البلوى فيها كعمومها في الأحداث، فنقول: فليس عموم
البلوى في اللمس والمس كعمومها في خروج الأحداث، فقد يمضي على الإنسان مدة
لا يلمس ولا يمس الذكر إلا في حالة الحدث كما لا يفتصد ولا يحتجم إلا
أحيانا فلا فرق. والجواب الثاني وهو التحقيق: أن الفصد والحجامة وإن كان لا
يتكرر كل يوم ولكنه يكثر، فكيف أخفي حكمه حتى يؤدي إلى بطلان صلاة خلق
كثير؟ وإن لم يكن هو الأكثر فكيف  وكل ذلك إلى الآحاد؟ ولا سبب إلا أن الله
تعالى لم يكلف رسوله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - إشاعة جميع الأحكام، بل كلفه
إشاعة البعض وجوز له رد الخلق إلى خبر الواحد في البعض، كما جوز له ردهم
إلى القياس في قاعدة الربا، وكان يسهل عليه أن يقول: لا تبيعوا المطعوم
بالمطعوم أو المكيل بالمكيل، حتى يستغنى عن الاستنباط من الأشياء الستة،
فيجوز أن يكون ما تعم به البلوى من جملة ما تقتضي مصلحة الخلق أن يردوا فيه
إلى خبر الواحد ولا استحالة فيه، وعند ذلك يكون صدق الراوي ممكنا فيجب
تصديقه، وليس علة الإشاعة عموم الحاجة أو ندورها، بل علته التعبد والتكليف
من الله، وإلا فما يحتاج إليه كثير كالفصد والحجامة كما يحتاج إليه الأكثر
في كونه شرعا لا ينبغي أن يخفى.
فإن قيل: فما الضابط لما تعبد الرسول - صلى الله عليه وسلم - فيه
بالإشاعة؟ قلنا: إن طلبتم ضابطا لجوازه عقلا فلا ضابط بل لله تعالى أن يفعل
في تكليف رسوله من ذلك ما يشاء، وإن أردتم وقوعه فإنما يعلم ذلك من فعل
رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم -. وإذا استقرينا السمعيات وجدناها أربعة
أقسام، الأول: القرآن، وقد علمنا أنه عني بالمبالغة في إشاعته.
الثاني: مباني الإسلام الخمس، ككلمتي الشهادة والصلاة والزكاة والصوم
والحج وقد أشاعه إشاعة اشترك في معرفته العام والخاص. الثالث: أصول
المعاملات التي ليست ضرورية مثل أصل البيع والنكاح فإن ذلك أيضا قد تواتر،
بل كالطلاق والعتاق والاستيلاد والتدبير والكتابة، فإن هذا تواتر عند أهل
العلم وقامت به الحجة القاطعة إما بالتواتر وإما بنقل الآحاد في مشهد
الجماعات مع سكوتهم، والحجة تقوم به، ولكن العوام لم يشاركوا العلماء في
العلم، بل فرض العوام فيه القبول من العلماء.
الرابع: تفاصيل هذه الأصول، فما يفسد الصلاة والعبادات وينقض الطهارة من
اللمس والمس والقيء وتكرار مسح الرأس، فهذا الجنس منه ما شاع ومنه ما نقله
الآحاد، ويجوز أن يكون مما تعم به البلوى،
فما نقله الآحاد فلا استحالة فيه ولا  مانع، فإن ما أشاعه كان يجوز أن لا
يتعبد فيه بالإشاعة، وما وكله إلى الآحاد كان يجوز أن يتعبد فيه بالإشاعة،
لكن وقوع هذه الأمور يدل على أن التعبد وقع كذلك فما كان يخالف أمر الله
سبحانه وتعالى في شيء من ذلك. هذا تمام الكلام في الأخبار والله أعلم.

### | [الأصل الثالث من أصول الأدلة الإجماع وفيه أبواب]

### | [الباب الأول في إثبات كون الإجماع حجة على منكريه]
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ب-ل-و (b-l-w)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Testing, affliction, trial; a matter that repeatedly befalls and afflicts the community, making its concealment inconceivable.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): A divine test (ibtilāʾ) entailing widespread practical need; in uṣūl, it denotes a ruling whose non-dissemination would cause pervasive hardship and ritual invalidation.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense of "calamity befalling" (nazalat); here used metaphorically (majāz) for the frequency of occurrence necessitating public transmission.
- Root: ش-ي-ع (sh-y-ʿ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To spread, publicize, make manifest; the opposite of concealment (kitmān).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The prophetic mandate (taʿabbud) to disseminate a ruling widely, rendering its concealment impossible given the convergence of motives (tawāfur al-dawāʿī).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: scattering/spreading; rhetorical: the legal obligation to make a matter known to the general public (kāffah).
- Root: ح-ص-ر (ḥ-ṣ-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Confinement, restriction, enumeration; to delimit a category.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The exhaustive inductive survey (istiqrāʾ) of revealed matters (samʿiyyāt) to determine what was divinely mandated for dissemination.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: encircling; metaphorical: the intellectual enumeration of the four divisions of transmitted rulings.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause with Rebuttal (al-Sharṭ wa al-Jawāb) — The phrase "فإن قيل... قلنا" (If it is said... we reply) follows the classical dialectical structure where the protasis introduces the opponent's objection and the apodasis delivers the refutation, governed by the rules of ʿaṭf and istiʾnāf.
chapters.translation:
I say: The single-narrator report (khabar al-wāḥid) is accepted [as proof] in matters of general necessity (ʿumūm al-balawā), contrary to al-Karkhī and some of the proponents of personal opinion (aṣḥāb al-raʾy). This is because whenever a trustworthy narrator (al-ʿadl) transmits something, and his veracity therein is possible, it becomes obligatory to affirm his truthfulness. Thus, for example, the touching of the penis (mass al-dhakr) — a trustworthy narrator transmitted it, and his veracity therein is possible, for we do not have certain knowledge of the transmitter's falsehood.

This differs from the case where a single individual alone transmits something whose widespread dissemination is rendered impossible by custom (mā taḥīlu al-ʿādah fīhi an lā yastafīḍ) — such as the killing of a commander in the marketplace, the dismissal of a vizier, an assault in the congregational mosque that prevented the people from the Friday prayer, or a lunar eclipse, an earthquake, the falling of a great star, and other marvels. For the motives (al-dawāʿī) converge upon the dissemination of all such matters, and their concealment is impossible (yastaḥīlu inkitāmuhu).

Likewise, the Qurʾān is not accepted through a single-narrator report, because we know with certainty that he — peace be upon him — was divinely commanded (tuʿabbida) to disseminate it and took great care in delivering it to all of creation. For the motives converge upon its dissemination and transmission, since it is the foundation of the religion (aṣl al-dīn). Thus, one who alone narrates a sūrah or a verse is certainly a liar. As for matters of general necessity, we do not pass certain judgment on the falsehood of the single-narrator report therein.

If it is said: "On what grounds do you reject one who passes certain judgment on its falsehood? For since a human being is never free from the two passages (al-khārij min al-sabīlayn) — i.e., urine and feces — many times in a day and night, and ritual purity (al-ṭahārah) is nullified by it, it was not permissible for the Messenger of Allah — peace be upon him — to refrain from disseminating its ruling and to confide it only to individuals (yunājī bihi al-āḥād). For that would lead to the concealment of the Sacred Law (ikhfāʾ al-sharʿ) and to the invalidation of the prayers of the servants while they are unaware. Thus, dissemination (al-ishāʿah) becomes obligatory in such a matter, and then the motives would converge upon its transmission. Likewise, the touching of the penis is something that occurs frequently — how then could its ruling remain hidden?"

We reply: This [argument] is refuted, first, by the witr prayer, the ruling on venesection (al-faṣd), cupping (al-ḥijāmah), loud laughter (al-qahqahah) [in prayer], the obligation of the major ablution (al-ghusl) from washing a corpse, and the single versus repeated call to prayer (ifrād al-iqāmah wa tathniyatuhā). All of these are matters of general necessity, and yet [our opponents] have established them through single-narrator reports.

If they claim that the generality of necessity in these matters is not like its generality in the case of ritual impurities (al-aḥdāth), we say: Then the generality of necessity in the case of touching (al-lams) and the touching of the penis (al-mass) is likewise not like its generality in the case of the emission of impurities. For a person may pass a period of time without touching [a woman] or touching his penis, except in a state of impurity — just as he does not undergo venesection or cupping except occasionally. Thus, there is no difference [between the two cases].

The second reply — and this is the verified one (al-taḥqīq) — is that venesection and cupping, although they do not recur every day, nevertheless occur frequently. How then could their ruling have been concealed, such that it would lead to the invalidation of the prayers of many people? Even if [those affected] were not the majority, how [could this be]? And all of this [was relegated] to single-narrator reports? There is no cause for this except that Allah — exalted be He — did not charge His Messenger — peace be upon him — with the dissemination of all rulings. Rather, He charged him with the dissemination of some, and permitted him to refer the people to single-narrator reports in others — just as He permitted him to refer them to analogical reasoning (al-qiyās) in the principle of usury (ribā). For it would have been easy for him to say: "Do not sell food for food, or measured things for measured things," so as to obviate the need for derivation (al-istinbāṭ) from the six specified items. Thus, it is possible that matters of general necessity fall among those things for which the welfare of creation (maṣlaḥat al-khalq) requires that they be referred to single-narrator reports, and there is no impossibility in that. In that case, the veracity of the narrator becomes possible, and so affirming his truthfulness becomes obligatory.

It is not the cause of dissemination (al-ishāʿah) that the need is general or rare; rather, its cause is the divine command and obligation (al-taʿabbud wa al-taklīf) from Allah. Otherwise, that which is needed frequently — like venesection and cupping — just as it is needed by the majority, being a prescribed ruling (sharʿ), ought not to remain hidden.

If it is said: "Then what is the criterion (al-ḍābiṭ) for that which the Messenger — peace be upon him — was divinely commanded to disseminate?"

We reply: If you seek a criterion for its permissibility by reason (ʿaqlan), then there is no criterion — for Allah has the right to do, in charging His Messenger, whatever He wills. But if you intend its actual occurrence (wuqūʿan), then that is known only from the practice of the Messenger of Allah — peace be upon him. When we conduct an inductive survey (istiqrāʾ) of the revealed matters (al-samʿiyyāt), we find them to be of four divisions:

The first: the Qurʾān — and we know that he took great care in the utmost dissemination of it.

The second: the five pillars of Islam (mabānī al-Islām) — such as the two testimonies of faith (kalimatā al-shahādah), prayer (al-ṣalāh), alms (al-zakāh), fasting (al-ṣawm), and pilgrimage (al-ḥajj). He disseminated these with a dissemination in which the commoner and the elite shared equally in knowledge.

The third: the foundational principles of transactions (uṣūl al-muʿāmalāt) that are not [known by] necessity — such as the principle of sale (al-bayʿ) and marriage (al-nikāḥ). For this too has been transmitted by mass transmission (tawātur). Likewise, divorce (al-ṭalāq), manumission (al-ʿitāq), the enslavement of a child-bearing concubine (al-istīlād), the contract of deferred manumission (al-tadbīr), and the contract of kitābah — for these have been transmitted by mass transmission among the people of knowledge, and the conclusive proof (al-ḥujjah al-qāṭiʿah) is established thereby — either through mass transmission or through single-narrator reports delivered in the presence of congregations (mashhad al-jamāʿāt) with their silence [as approval]. The proof is established thereby. However, the commoners (al-ʿawāmm) did not share with the scholars in this knowledge; rather, the obligation of the commoners therein is acceptance from the scholars.

The fourth: the details (tafāṣīl) of these foundational principles. Thus, whatever invalidates prayer and acts of worship, and nullifies ritual purity — such as touching (al-lams), the touching of the penis (al-mass), vomiting (al-qayʾ), and the repetition of wiping the head (takrār masḥ al-raʾs) — this category includes what has been widely disseminated and what has been transmitted by single narrators. And it is possible that [some of it] falls under matters of general necessity.

Thus, what has been transmitted by single narrators — there is no impossibility in it, nor any impediment. For what he disseminated could have been such that he was not divinely commanded to disseminate it, and what he delegated to single narrators could have been such that he was divinely commanded to disseminate it. However, the actual occurrence of these matters indicates that the divine command (al-taʿabbud) occurred in this manner. Thus, nothing in any of this contravened the command of Allah — glory be to Him and exalted be He.

This completes the discourse on reports (al-akhbār), and Allah knows best.

chapters.arabic_text:
الأصل الثالث من أصول الأدلة الإجماع وفيه أبواب
الباب الأول: في إثبات كونه حجة على منكريه. ومن حاول إثبات كون الإجماع
حجة افتقر إلى تفهيم لفظ الإجماع أولا وبيان تصوره ثانيا وبيان إمكان
الاطلاع عليه ثالثا وبيان الدليل على كونه حجة رابعا. أما تفهيم لفظ
الإجماع فإنما نعني به اتفاق أمة محمد - صلى الله عليه وسلم - خاصة على أمر
من الأمور الدينية، ومعناه في وضع اللغة الاتفاق والإزماع، وهو مشترك
بينهما. فمن أزمع وصمم العزم على إمضاء أمر يقال: أجمع، والجماعة إذا
اتفقوا يقال: أجمعوا. وهذا يصلح لإجماع اليهود والنصارى وللاتفاق في غير
أمر الدين، لكن العرف خصص اللفظ بما ذكرناه. وذهب النظام إلى أن الإجماع
عبارة عن كل قول قامت حجته وإن كان قول واحد وهو على خلاف اللغة والعرف،
لكنه سواه على مذهبه إذ لم ير الإجماع حجة، وتواتر إليه بالتسامع تحريم
مخالفة الإجماع، فقال: هو كل قول قامت حجته.
أما الثاني، وهو تصوره: فدليل تصوره وجوده، فقد وجدنا الأمة مجمعة على أن
الصلوات خمس، وأن صوم رمضان واجب، وكيف يمتنع تصوره والأمة كلهم متعبدون
باتباع النصوص والأدلة القاطعة ومعرضون للعقاب بمخالفتها؟ فكما لا يمتنع
اجتماعهم على الأكل والشرب لتوافق الدواعي فكذلك على اتباع الحق واتقاء
النار. فإن قيل: الأمة مع كثرتها واختلاف دواعيها في الاعتراف بالحق
والعناد فيه كيف تتفق آراؤها؟ فذلك محال منها كاتفاقهم على أكل الزبيب مثلا
في يوم واحد. قلنا: لا صارف لجميعهم إلى تناول الزبيب خاصة، ولجميعهم باعث
على الاعتراف بالحق، كيف وقد تصور إطباق اليهود مع  كثرتهم على الباطل، فلم
