لا يتصور إطباق المسلمين على الحق؟ والكثرة إنما تؤثر عند تعارض الأشباه
والدواعي والصوارف، ومستند الإجماع في الأكثر نصوص متواترة وأمور معلومة
ضرورة بقرائن الأحوال، والعقلاء كلهم فيه على منهج واحد. نعم هل يتصور
الإجماع عن اجتهاد أو قياس؟ ذلك فيه كلام سيأتي إن شاء الله.
أما الثالث، وهو تصور الاطلاع على الإجماع فقد قال قوم: لو تصور إجماعهم
فمن الذي يطلع عليهم مع تفرقهم في الأقطار؟ فنقول: يتصور معرفة ذلك
بمشافهتهم إن كانوا عددا يمكن لقاؤهم، وإن لم يمكن عرف مذهب قوم بالمشافهة
ومذهب الآخرين بأخبار التواتر عنهم كما عرفنا أن مذهب جميع أصحاب الشافعي
منع قتل المسلم بالذمي وبطلان النكاح بلا ولي، ومذهب جميع النصارى التثليث،
ومذهب جميع المجوس التثنية. فإن قيل: مذهب أصحاب الشافعي وأبي حنيفة مستند
إلى قائل واحد وهو الشافعي وأبو حنيفة وقول الواحد يمكن أن يعلم وكذلك مذهب
النصارى يستند إلى عيسى - عليه السلام -، أما قول جماعة لا ينحصرون كيف
يعلم؟ قلنا وقول أمة محمد - صلى الله عليه وسلم - في أمور الدين يستند إلى
ما فهموه من محمد - صلى الله عليه وسلم -
وسمعوه منه، ثم إذا انحصر أهل الحل والعقد فكما يمكن أن يعلم قول واحد
أمكن أن يعلم قول الثاني إلى العشرة، والعشرين. فإن قيل: لعل أحدا منهم في
أسر الكفار وبلاد الروم. قلنا: تجب مراجعته. ومذهب الأسير ينقل كمذهب غيره
وتمكن معرفته، فمن شك في موافقته للآخرين لم يكن متحققا للإجماع فإن قيل:
فلو عرف مذهبه ربما يرجع عنه بعده. قلنا: لا أثر لرجوعه بعد انعقاد
الإجماع، فإنه يكون محجوجا به، ولا يتصور رجوع جميعهم إذ يصير أحد
الإجماعين خطأ وذلك ممتنع بدليل السمع.
أما الرابع: وهو إقامة الحجة على استحالة الخطأ على الأمة، وفيه الشأن
كله وكونه حجة إنما يعلم بكتاب أو سنة متواترة أو عقل، أما الإجماع فلا
يمكن إثبات الإجماع به. وقد طمعوا في التلقي من الكتاب والسنة والعقل
وأقواها السنة ونحن نذكر المسالك الثلاثة.
المسلك الأول التمسك بالكتاب، وذلك قوله تعالى: {وكذلك جعلناكم أمة وسطا
لتكونوا شهداء على الناس} [البقرة: 143] وقوله تعالى: {كنتم خير أمة أخرجت
للناس} [آل عمران: 110] الآية. وقوله تعالى: {وممن خلقنا أمة يهدون بالحق
وبه يعدلون} [الأعراف: 181] وقوله تعالى: {واعتصموا بحبل الله جميعا ولا
تفرقوا} [آل عمران: 103] وقوله تعالى {وما اختلفتم فيه من شيء فحكمه إلى
الله} [الشورى: 10] ومفهومه: أن ما اتفقتم فيه فهو حق، وقوله عز وجل: {فإن
تنازعتم في شيء فردوه إلى الله والرسول} [النساء: 59] مفهومه: إن اتفقتم
فهو حق.
فهذه كلها ظواهر لا تنص على الغرض، بل لا تدل أيضا دلالة الظواهر.
وأقواها قوله تعالى: {ومن يشاقق الرسول من بعد ما تبين له الهدى ويتبع غير
سبيل المؤمنين نوله ما تولى ونصله جهنم وساءت مصيرا} [النساء: 115] فإن ذلك
يوجب اتباع سبيل المؤمنين. وهذا ما تمسك به الشافعي وقد أطنبنا في كتاب
تهذيب الأصول في توجيه الأسئلة على الآية ودفعها.
والذي نراه أن الآية ليست نصا في الغرض، بل الظاهر أن المراد بها أن من
يقاتل الرسول ويشاقه ويتبع غير سبيل المؤمنين في مشايعته ونصرته ودفع
الأعداء عنه نوله ما تولى، فكأنه لم يكتف بترك المشاقة حتى تنضم إليه
متابعة سبيل المؤمنين في نصرته والذب عنه والانقياد له فيما يأمر وينهى.
وهذا هو الظاهر السابق إلى الفهم، فإن لم يكن ظاهرا فهو محتمل.
ولو فسر رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - الآية بذلك لقبل ولم يجعل ذلك
رفعا للنص، كما لو فسر المشاقة بالموافقة واتباع سبيل المؤمنين بالعدول عن
سبيلهم.
المسلك الثاني، وهو الأقوى: التمسك بقوله - صلى الله عليه وسلم -: «لا
تجتمع أمتي على الخطأ» . وهذا من حيث اللفظ أقوى وأدل على المقصود، ولكن
ليس بالمتواتر كالكتاب، والكتاب متواتر، لكن ليس بنص.
فطريق تقرير الدليل أن نقول: تظاهرت الرواية عن رسول الله - صلى الله
عليه وسلم - بألفاظ مختلفة مع اتفاق المعنى في عصمة هذه الأمة من الخطأ،
واشتهر على لسان المرموقين والثقات من الصحابة كعمر وابن مسعود وأبي سعيد
الخدري وأنس بن مالك وابن عمر وأبي هريرة وحذيفة بن اليمان وغيرهم ممن يطول
ذكره من نحو قوله - صلى الله عليه وسلم -: «لا تجتمع أمتي على الضلالة» ،
«ولم يكن الله ليجمع أمتي على الضلالة»
و «سألت الله تعالى أن لا يجمع أمتي على الضلالة فأعطانيها» ، و «من سره
أن يسكن بحبوحة الجنة فليلزم الجماعة فإن دعوتهم تحيط من وراءهم» و «إن
الشيطان مع الواحد وهو من الاثنين أبعد» ، وقوله - صلى الله عليه وسلم -
«يد الله مع الجماعة ولا يبالي الله بشذوذ من شذ» و «لا تزال طائفة من أمتي
على الحق ظاهرين لا يضرهم من خالفهم» وروي: «لا يضرهم خلاف من خالفهم إلا
ما أصابهم من لأواء ومن خرج عن الجماعة أو فارق الجماعة قيد شبر فقد خلع
ربقة الإسلام من عنقه، ومن فارق الجماعة ومات فميتته جاهلية» .
وهذه الأخبار لم تزل ظاهرة في الصحابة والتابعين إلى زماننا هذا لم
يدفعها أحد من أهل النقل من سلف الأمة وخلفها، بل هي مقبولة من موافقي
الأمة ومخالفيها، ولم تزل الأمة تحتج بها في أصول الدين وفروعه. فإن قيل:
فما وجه الحجة، ودعوى التواتر في آحاد هذه الأخبار غير ممكن ونقل الآحاد لا
يفيد العلم؟ قلنا: في تقرير وجه الحجة طريقان: أحدهما: أن ندعي العلم
الضروري بأن رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - قد عظم شأن هذه الأمة وأخبر
عن عصمتها عن الخطأ بمجموع هذه الأخبار المتفرقة وإن لم تتواتر آحادها،
وبمثل ذلك نجد أنفسنا مضطرين إلى العلم بشجاعة علي وسخاوة حاتم وفقه
الشافعي وخطابة الحجاج وميل رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - إلى عائشة من
نسائه وتعظيمه صحابته وثنائه عليهم وإن لم تكن آحاد الأخبار فيها متواترة،
بل يجوز الكذب على كل واحد منها لو جردنا النظر إليه ولا يجوز على المجموع.
وذلك يشبه ما يعلم من مجموع قرائن آحادها لا ينفك عن الاحتمال، ولكن
ينتفي الاحتمال عن مجموعها حتى يحصل العلم الضروري. الطريق الثاني: أن لا
ندعي علم الاضطرار بل  علم الاستدلال من وجهين، الأول: أن هذه الأحاديث لم
تزل مشهورة بين الصحابة والتابعين يتمسكون بها في إثبات الإجماع ولا يظهر
أحد فيها خلافا وإنكارا إلى زمان النظام، ويستحيل في مستقر العادة توافق
الأمم في أعصار متكررة على التسليم لما لم تقم الحجة بصحته مع اختلاف
الطباع وتفاوت الهمم والمذاهب في الرد والقبول، ولذلك لم ينفك حكم ثبت
بأخبار الآحاد عن خلاف مخالف وإبداء تردد فيه.
الوجه: أن المحتجين بهذه الأخبار أثبتوا بها أصلا مقطوعا به وهو الإجماع
الذي يحكم به على كتاب الله تعالى وعلى السنة المتواترة، ويستحيل في العادة
التسليم لخبر يرفع به الكتاب المقطوع به إلا إذا استند إلى مستند مقطوع به،
فأما رفع المقطوع بما ليس بمقطوع فليس معلوما، حتى لا يتعجب متعجب ولا يقول
قائل: كيف ترفعون الكتاب القاطع بإجماع مستند إلى خبر غير معلوم الصحة؟
وكيف تذهل عنه جميع الأمة إلى زمان النظام فيختص بالتنبه له؟ هذا وجه
الاستدلال، وللمنكرين في معارضته ثلاثة مقامات: الرد والتأويل والمعارضة
المقام الأول: في الرد، وفيه أربعة أسئلة:
السؤال الأول: قولهم: لعل واحدا خالف هذه الأخبار وردها ولم ينقل إلينا.
قلنا: هذا أيضا تحيله العادة إذ الإجماع أعظم أصول الدين، فلو خالف فيه
مخالف لعظم الأمر فيه واشتهر الخلاف، إذ لم يندرس خلاف الصحابة في دية
الجنين ومسألة الحرام وحد الشرب. فكيف اندرس الخلاف في أصل عظيم يلزم فيه
التضليل والتبديع لمن أخطأ في نفيه وإثباته؟ وكيف اشتهر خلاف النظام مع
سقوط
قدره وخسة رتبته وخفي خلاف أكابر الصحابة والتابعين؟ هذا مما لا يتسع له
عقل أصلا.
السؤال الثاني: قالوا: قد استدللتم بالخبر على الإجماع، ثم استدللتم
بالإجماع على صحة الخبر، فهب أنهم أجمعوا على الصحة فما الدليل على أن ما
أجمعوا على صحته فهو صحيح وهل النزاع إلا فيه؟ قلنا: لا، بل استدللنا على
الإجماع بالخبر وعلى صحة الخبر بخلو الأعصار عن المدافعة والمخالفة له مع
أن العادة تقتضي إنكار إثبات أصل قاطع يحكم به على القواطع  بخبر غير معلوم
الصحة، فعلمنا بالعادة كون الخبر مقطوعا به لا بالإجماع، والعادة أصل
يستفاد منها معارف، فإن بها يعلم بطلان دعوى معارضة القرآن واندراسها، وبها
يعلم بطلان دعوى نص الإمامة، وإيجاب صلاة الضحى، وصوم شوال، وأن ذلك لو كان
لاستحال في العادة السكوت عنه.
السؤال الثالث: قالوا: بم تنكرون على من يقول لعلهم أثبتوا الإجماع لا
بهذه الأخبار بل بدليل آخر؟ قلنا: قد ظهر منهم الاحتجاج بهذه الأخبار في
المنع من مخالفة الجماعة وتهديد من يفارق الجماعة ويخالفها. وهذا أولى من
أن يقال لو كان لهم فيه مستند لظهر وانتشر، فإنه قد نقل تمسكهم أيضا
بالآيات.
السؤال الرابع: قولهم: لما علمت الصحابة صحة هذه الأخبار لم لم يذكروا
طريق صحتها للتابعين حتى كان ينقطع الارتياب ويشاركونهم في العلم؟ قلنا:
لأنهم علموا تعريفه - عليه السلام - عصمة هذه الأمة بمجموع قرائن وأمارات
وتكريرات ألفاظ وأسباب دلت ضرورة على قصده إلى بيان نفي الخطأ عن هذه
الأمة، وتلك القرائن لا تدخل تحت الحكاية ولا تحيط بها العبارات، ولو حكوها
لتطرق إلى آحادها احتمالات، فاكتفوا بعلم التابعين بأن الخبر المشكوك فيه
لا يثبت به أصل مقطوع به ويقع التسليم في العادة به، فكانت العادة في حق
التابعين أقوى من الحكاية.
المقام الثاني: في التأويل. ولهم تأويلات ثلاثة، الأول: قوله: - صلى الله
عليه وسلم - «لا تجتمع أمتي على ضلالة» ينبئ عن الكفر والبدعة فلعله أراد
عصمة جميعهم عن الكفر: بالتأويل والشبهة، وقوله " على الخطأ " لم يتواتر،
وإن صح فالخطأ عام يمكن حمله على الكفر.
قلنا: الضلال في وضع اللسان لا يناسب الكفر، قال الله تعالى: {ووجدك ضالا
فهدى} [الضحى: 7] وقال تعالى إخبارا عن موسى: - عليه السلام -: {فعلتها إذا
وأنا من الضالين} [الشعراء: 20] وما أراد من الكافرين بل أراد من المخطئين،
يقال: ضل فلان عن الطريق وضل سعي فلان كل ذلك الخطأ، كيف وقد فهم ضرورة من
هذه الألفاظ تعظيم شأن هذه الأمة وتخصيصها بهذه الفضيلة؟ أما العصمة عن
الكفر فقد أنعم بها في حق  علي وابن مسعود وأبي وزيد على مذهب النظام لأنهم
ماتوا على الحق، وكم من آحاد عصموا عن الكفر حتى ماتوا، فأي خاصية للأمة؟
فدل أنه أراد ما لم يعصم عنه الآحاد من سهو وخطأ وكذب يعصم عنه الأمة
تنزيلا لجميع الأمة منزلة النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - في العصمة عن الخطأ
في الدين، أما في غير الدين من إنشاء حرب وصلح وعمارة بلدة فالعموم يقتضي
العصمة للأمة عنه أيضا، ولكن ذلك مشكوك فيه وأمر الدين مقطوع بوجوب العصمة
فيه كما في حق النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم -، فإنه أخطأ في أمر تأبير النخل
ثم قال: «أنتم أعرف بأمر دنياكم وأنا أعرف بأمر دينكم»
التأويل الثاني: قولهم غاية هذا أن يكون عاما يوجب العصمة عن كل خطأ،
ويحتمل أن يكون المراد به بعض أنواع الخطأ من الشهادة في الآخرة، أو ما
يوافق النص المتواتر أو يوافق دليل العقل دون ما يكون بالاجتهاد والقياس.
قلنا: لا ذاهب من الأمة إلى هذا التفصيل، إذ ما دل من العقل على تجويز
الخطأ عليهم في شيء دل على تجويز في شيء آخر، وإذا لم يكن فارق لم يكن
تخصيص بالتحكم دون دليل ولم يكن تخصيص أولى من تخصيص، وقد ذم من خالف
الجماعة وأمر بالموافقة، فلو لم يكن ما فيه العصمة معلوما استحال الاتباع
إلا إن ثبت العصمة مطلقا، وبه ثبتت فضيلة الأمة وشرفها، فأما العصمة عن
البعض دون البعض فهذا يثبت لكل كافر فضلا عن المسلم، إذ ما من شخص يخطئ في
كل شيء بل كل إنسان فإنه يعصم عن الخطأ في بعض الأشياء.
التأويل الثالث: أن أمته - صلى الله عليه وسلم - كل من آمن به إلى يوم
القيامة، فجملة هؤلاء من أول الإسلام إلى آخر عمر الدنيا لا يجتمعون على
خطأ بل كل حكم انقضى على اتفاق أهل الأعصار كلها بعد بعثة النبي - صلى الله
عليه وسلم - فهو حق، إذ الأمة عبارة عن الجميع، كيف والذين ماتوا في زماننا
هم من الأمة؟ وإجماع  من بعدهم ليس إجماع جميع الأمة، بدليل أنهم لو كانوا
قد خالفوا ثم ماتوا لم ينعقد بعدهم إجماع وقبلنا من الأمة من خالف وإن كان
قد مات، فكذلك إذا لم يوافقوا.
قلنا: كما لا يجوز أن يراد بالأمة المجانين والأطفال والسقط والمجتن وإن
كانوا من الأمة، فلا يجوز أن يراد به الميت والذي لم يخلق بعد، بل الذي
يفهم قوم يتصور منهم اختلاف واجتماع، ولا يتصور الاجتماع والاختلاف من
المعدوم والميت.
والدليل عليه أنه أمر باتباع الجماعة وذم من شذ عن الموافقة، فإن كان
المراد به ما ذكروه فإنما يتصور الاتباع والمخالفة في القيامة لا في
الدنيا، فيعلم قطعا أن المراد به إجماع يمكن خرقه ومخالفته في الدنيا، وذلك
هم الموجودون في كل عصر. أما إذا مات فيبقى أثر خلافه، فإن مذهبه لا يموت
بموته. وسيأتي فيه كلام شاف إن شاء الله تعالى.
المقام الثالث: المعارضة بالآيات والأخبار.
أما الآيات فكل ما فيها منع من الكفر والردة والفعل الباطل فهو عام مع
الجميع، فإن لم يكن ذلك ممكنا فكيف نهوا عنه؟ كقوله تعالى: {وأن تقولوا على
الله ما لا تعلمون} [البقرة: 169] {ومن يرتدد منكم عن دينه فيمت وهو كافر}
[البقرة: 217] {ولا تأكلوا أموالكم بينكم بالباطل} [البقرة: 188] وأمثال
ذلك.
قلنا: ليس هذا نهيا لهم عن الاجتماع بل نهي للآحاد، وإن كان كل واحد على
حياله داخلا في النهي وإن سلم فليس من شرط النهي وقوع المنهي عنه ولا جواز
وقوعه، فإن الله تعالى علم أن جميع المعاصي لا تقع منهم ونهاهم عن الجميع
وخلاف المعلوم غير واقع وقال لرسوله: - صلى الله عليه وسلم - {لئن أشركت
ليحبطن عملك} [الزمر: 65] ، وقال: {فلا تكونن من الجاهلين} [الأنعام: 35]
وقد علم أنه قد عصمه منهم، وأن ذلك لا يقع.
وأما الأخبار فقوله - عليه السلام -: «بدأ الإسلام غريبا وسيعود غريبا
كما بدأ» وقوله: - عليه السلام - «خير القرون قرني ثم الذين يلونهم ثم
الذين يلونهم ثم يفشو الكذب حتى إن الرجل ليحلف وما يستحلف ويشهد وما
يستشهد» وكقوله  - صلى الله عليه وسلم -: «لا تقوم الساعة إلا على شرار
أمتي»
قلنا: هذا وأمثاله يدل على كثرة العصيان والكذب ولا يدل على أنه لا يبقى
متمسك بالحق، ولا يناقض قوله - صلى الله عليه وسلم -: «لا تزال طائفة من
أمتي على الحق حتى يأتي أمر الله وحتى يظهر الدجال» كيف ولا تجري هذه
الأخبار في الصحة والظهور مجرى الأحاديث التي تمسكنا بها؟
المسلك الثالث التمسك بالطريق المعنوي.
وبيانه أن الصحابة إذا قضوا بقضية وزعموا أنهم قاطعون بها فلا يقطعون بها
إلا عن مستند قاطع، وإذا كثروا كثرة تنتهي إلى حد التواتر فالعادة تحيل
عليهم قصد الكذب وتحيل عليهم الغلط حتى لا يتنبه واحد منهم للمحق في ذلك
وإلى أن القطع بغير دليل قاطع خطأ، فقطعهم في غير محل القطع محال في
العادة.
فإن قضوا عن اجتهاد واتفقوا عليه فيعلم أن التابعين كانوا يشددون النكير
على مخالفيهم ويقطعون به، وقطعهم بذلك قطع في غير محل القطع فلا يكون ذلك
أيضا إلا عن قاطع، وإلا فيستحيل في العادة أن يشذ عن جميعهم الحق مع كثرتهم
حتى لا يتنبه واحد منهم للحق.
وكذلك نعلم أن التابعين لو أجمعوا على شيء أنكر تابعو التابعين على
المخالف وقطعوا بالإنكار، وهو قطع في غير محل القطع فالعادة تحيل ذلك إلا
عن قاطع وعلى مساق هذا قالوا لو رجع أهل الحل والعقد إلى عدد ينقص عن عدد
التواتر فلا يستحيل عليهم الخطأ في العادة ولا تعمد الكذب لباعث عليه فلا
حجة فيه.
وهذه الطريقة ضعيفة عندنا لأن منشأ الخطأ إما تعمد الكذب وإما ظنهم ما
ليس بقاطع قاطعا، والأول غير جائز على عدد التواتر، وأما الثاني: فجائز،
فقد قطع اليهود ببطلان نبوة عيسى ومحمد - عليهما السلام - وهم أكثر من عدد
التواتر، وهو قطع في غير محل القطع لكن ظنوا ما ليس بقاطع قاطعا.
والمنكرون لحدوث العالم والنبوات والمرتكبون لسائر أنواع البدع والضلالات
عددهم بالغ مبلغ عدد التواتر ويحصل الصدق بإخبارهم، ولكن أخطئوا بالقطع في
غير محل القطع. وهذا  القائل يلزمه أن يجعل إجماع اليهود والنصارى حجة ولا
تخصيص لهذه الأمة، وقد أجمعوا على بطلان دين الإسلام فإن قيل: هذا تمسك
بالعادة، وأنتم في نصرة المسلك الثاني استروحتم إلى العادة وهذا عين الأول.
قلنا: العادة لا تحيل على عدد التواتر أن يظنوا ما بقاطع قاطعا، وعن هذا
قلنا: شرط خبر التواتر أن يستند إلى محسوس والعادة تحيل الانقياد والسكوت
عمن دفع الكتاب والسنة المتواترة بإجماع دليله خبر مظنون غير مقطوع به وكل
ما هو ضروري يعلم بالحس أو بقرينة الحال أو بالبديهة فمنهاجه واحد ويتفق
الناس على دركه والعادة الذهول عنه على أهل التواتر وما هو نظري فطرقه
مختلفة، فلا يستحيل في العادة أن يجتمع أهل التواتر على الغلط فيه، فهذا هو
الفرق بين المسلكين.
فإن قيل: اعتمادكم في هذا المسلك الثاني أن ما أجمعوا عليه حق وليس بخطأ
فالدليل على وجوب اتباعه وكل مجتهد مصيب للحق ولا يجب على مجتهد آخر اتباعه
والشاهد المزور مبطل ويجب على القاضي اتباعه؟ فوجوب الاتباع شيء وكون الشيء
حقا غيره.
قلنا أجمعت الأمة على وجوب اتباع الإجماع وإنه من الحق الذي يجب اتباعه،
وبحسب كونهم محقين في قولهم يجب اتباع الإجماع، ثم نقول كل حق علم كونه حقا
فالأصل فيه وجوب
الاتباع، والمجتهد يجب اتباعه إلا على المجتهد الذي هو محق أيضا فقدم حق
حصل باجتهاده على ما حصل باجتهاد غيره في حقه والشاهد المزور لو علم كونه
مزورا لم يتبع.
ويدل عليه أيضا ذمة من خالف الجماعة وأنه ذكر هذا في معرض الثناء على
الأمة، ولا يتحقق ذلك إلا بوجوب الاتباع وإلا فلا يبقى له معنى، إلا إنهم
محقون إذا أصابوا دليل الحق، وذلك جائز في حق واحد من أفراد المؤمنين فليس
فيه مدح وتخصيص ألبتة.
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ج-م-ع (j-m-ʿ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The core meaning is "to gather, assemble, unite, or bring together" — both in physical aggregation and in the convergence of wills upon a single matter. Al-ʿAyn notes the form *ajmaʿa* (IV) as "to resolve firmly upon a matter" and "to agree collectively."
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, *ijmāʿ* denotes the unanimous agreement of the Muslim community (Ummah) upon a religious ruling, functioning as a definitive epistemic source (dalīl qaṭʿī) for legal and doctrinal matters.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): The literal sense is "agreement" and "firm resolution" (itti fāq wa-izmāʿ). The technical, customary (ʿurfī) restriction to the consensus of Muhammad's community is a specification (takhṣīṣ) of the lexical general meaning, not a metaphorical transfer.
- Root: ع-ص-م (ʿ-ṣ-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: "To protect, guard, preserve from harm or error." The root conveys the idea of divine protection that prevents an agent from falling into mistake or sin.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): *ʿIṣmah* is the theological doctrine of infallibility — the divinely granted immunity from error, particularly attributed to prophets and, in this context, to the collective Ummah.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Used literally here — the Ummah's protection from error is a real, divinely ordained attribute, not a mere metaphor.
- Root: خ-ط-أ (kh-ṭ-ʾ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: "To err, to miss the mark, to commit a mistake." The opposite of *ṣawāb* (correctness). It covers both unintentional error and moral fault.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): *Khaṭaʾ* is distinguished from *ithm* (sin) — it denotes falling short of truth or correctness, whether in belief, speech, or action, without necessarily implying moral culpability.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal usage — the Ummah's immunity from *khaṭaʾ* is asserted as a factual, divinely guaranteed protection.
- Sībawayh Rule: The Rule of *Taʿlīq al-Sharṭ ʿalā al-ʿĀmm* (Conditional Attachment to a General Term) — When a conditional or restrictive phrase (e.g., "upon an error") is attached to a general subject (e.g., "my community"), the generality of the subject is preserved unless a separate textual or rational indicator restricts it. Also applied: *Ḥaml al-Muṭlaq ʿalā al-Muqayyad* (Carrying the Absolute to the Restricted) where context demands.
chapters.translation:
I say: The third principle among the principles of the evidences is Consensus (Ijmāʿ), and it comprises chapters.

**Chapter One: On Establishing That It Is an Authoritative Proof (Ḥujjah) Against Those Who Deny It.**

Whoever attempts to establish that Consensus is an authoritative proof is in need of, first, clarifying the meaning of the term "Consensus"; second, demonstrating its conceivability (taṣawwuruhu); third, demonstrating the possibility of gaining knowledge of it; and fourth, demonstrating the proof that it is an authoritative proof.

As for clarifying the term "Consensus" — by it we mean specifically the agreement of the community of Muhammad — may God bless him and grant him peace — upon a matter among religious matters. Its meaning in the linguistic convention is "agreement" and "firm resolution" (al-ittifāq wa-al-izmāʿ), and it is shared between the two. Thus, one who resolves and firmly determines upon executing a matter is said to have *ajmaʿa* (resolved), and a group when they agree is said to have *ajmaʿū* (they agreed). This would be suitable for the consensus of the Jews and Christians, and for agreement in other than religious matters, but the customary usage (al-ʿurf) has specified the term to what we have mentioned. Al-Naẓẓām held that Consensus is any statement whose proof has been established, even if it be the statement of a single individual — and this is contrary to both language and custom. However, he is excused according to his own doctrine, for he did not deem Consensus an authoritative proof, yet reports reached him by widespread transmission (tawātur) prohibiting the violation of Consensus, so he said: "It is any statement whose proof has been established."

As for the second matter — its conceivability: the proof of its conceivability is its existence. For we have found the community agreed that the prayers are five, and that fasting Ramaḍān is obligatory. How could its conceivability be impossible, given that the entire community is obligated to follow the texts and definitive evidences, and is subject to punishment for violating them? Just as their agreement upon eating and drinking is not impossible due to the convergence of their motives, so too is their agreement upon following the truth and guarding against the Fire. If it is said: "The community, despite its vast numbers and the divergence of its motives between acknowledging the truth and obstinacy against it — how could its opinions agree? That would be as impossible as their all agreeing, for example, to eat raisins on a single day." We say: There is no deterrent turning all of them away from consuming raisins specifically, whereas there is for all of them an incentive toward acknowledging the truth. How [could it be impossible], given that the agreement of the Jews, despite their vast numbers, upon falsehood is conceivable — so why should the agreement of the Muslims upon truth not be conceivable? Numbers only have effect when semblances, motives, and deterrents are in conflict. The basis of Consensus in most cases is widely transmitted texts (nuṣūṣ mutawātirah) and matters known by necessity through circumstantial indicators (qarāʾin al-aḥwāl), and all rational people are upon a single path therein. Indeed, is Consensus by way of independent reasoning (ijtihād) or analogy (qiyās) conceivable? That is a matter of discussion that will come, God willing.

As for the third matter — the conceivability of gaining knowledge of Consensus: Some people said: "If their consensus were conceivable, who could gain knowledge of them, given their dispersion across the regions?" We say: It is conceivable to know that by directly addressing them (mushāfahah) if they are a number that can be met. If that is not possible, the doctrine of one group is known by direct address, and the doctrine of others by reports of widespread transmission (akhbār al-tawātur) about them — just as we know that the doctrine of all the companions of al-Shāfiʿī is the prohibition of killing a Muslim for a dhimmī and the nullity of marriage without a guardian, and the doctrine of all Christians is the Trinity, and the doctrine of all Magians is dualism. If it is said: "The doctrine of the companions of al-Shāfiʿī and Abū Ḥanīfah is traced back to a single speaker, namely al-Shāfiʿī and Abū Ḥanīfah, and the statement of one individual can be known; likewise the doctrine of the Christians is traced back to Jesus — peace be upon him. But how can the statement of a group that is not delimited be known?" We say: The statement of the community of Muhammad — may God bless him and grant him peace — in religious matters is traced back to what they understood from Muhammad — may God bless him and grant him peace — and heard from him. Then, if the people of binding and loosing (ahl al-ḥall wa-al-ʿaqd) are delimited, just as the statement of one individual can be known, so too can the statement of the second, up to the tenth and the twentieth, be known. If it is said: "Perhaps one of them is in the captivity of the disbelievers or in the lands of the Byzantines." We say: He must be consulted. The doctrine of the captive is transmitted just as the doctrine of others is transmitted, and knowledge of it is possible. Whoever doubts his agreement with the others has not truly ascertained the Consensus. If it is said: "Even if his doctrine were known, perhaps he would retract it afterward." We say: There is no effect of his retraction after the Consensus has been concluded, for he would be bound by it. And the retraction of all of them is inconceivable, for then one of the two consensuses would be erroneous, and that is impossible by the scriptural proof (dalīl al-samʿ).

As for the fourth matter — establishing the proof of the impossibility of error upon the community: In this lies the entire matter. That it is an authoritative proof is known only through the Book, or an extensively transmitted Sunnah, or reason. As for Consensus itself, Consensus cannot be established by Consensus. They have aspired to derive it from the Book, the Sunnah, and reason — and the strongest of these is the Sunnah. We shall mention the three paths.

**The First Path: Adherence to the Book.**

This is His saying, exalted: {«And thus We have made you a middle nation that you may be witnesses over mankind»} [Al-Baqarah 2:143]; and His saying, exalted: {«You are the best nation produced for mankind»} [Āl ʿImrān 3:110]; and His saying, exalted: {«And among those We created is a nation that guides by truth and thereby establishes justice»} [Al-Aʿrāf 7:181]; and His saying, exalted: {«And hold firmly to the rope of God all together and do not become divided»} [Āl ʿImrān 3:103]; and His saying, exalted: {«And in whatever you differ over, its judgment is with God»} [Al-Shūrā 42:10] — its implication (mafhūmuhu) being that what you agree upon is the truth; and His saying, mighty and majestic: {«And if you dispute over anything, refer it to God and the Messenger»} [Al-Nisāʾ 4:59] — its implication being that if you agree, it is the truth.

All of these are merely apparent meanings (ẓawāhir) that do not explicitly state the intended point, nor do they even indicate it with the indication of apparent meanings. The strongest of them is His saying, exalted: {«And whoever opposes the Messenger after guidance has become clear to him and follows other than the way of the believers — We will give him what he has taken and burn him in Hell, and evil is the destination»} [Al-Nisāʾ 4:115], for this necessitates following the way of the believers. This is what al-Shāfiʿī adhered to, and we have elaborated extensively in the book *Tahdhīb al-Uṣūl* on formulating the objections against this verse and repelling them.

What we hold is that the verse is not an explicit text (naṣṣ) for the intended point. Rather, the apparent meaning is that whoever fights the Messenger and opposes him, and follows other than the way of the believers in supporting him, aiding him, and repelling enemies from him — We will give him what he has taken. It is as if He was not content with abandoning opposition until one also joins in following the way of the believers in supporting him, defending him, and submitting to him in what he commands and forbids. This is the apparent meaning that springs to the understanding. If it is not apparent, then it is at least probable (muḥtamal). And if the Messenger of God — may God bless him and grant him peace — had interpreted the verse in that way, it would have been accepted and would not have constituted an abrogation of the text — just as if he had interpreted "opposition" (mushāqqah) as "agreement" and "following the way of the believers" as "deviating from their way."

**The Second Path — and It Is the Stronger: Adherence to His saying — may God bless him and grant him peace: «My community will not agree upon an error.»**

This is, in terms of wording, stronger and more indicative of the intended purpose. However, it is not transmitted with the same degree of tawātur as the Book, and the Book is mutawātir but is not an explicit text.

The method of establishing the proof is to say: The narrations from the Messenger of God — may God bless him and grant him peace — have been successively transmitted (taẓāharat al-riwāyah) with different wordings while agreeing in meaning upon the protection of this community from error. This became widely known on the tongues of the prominent and trustworthy Companions, such as ʿUmar, Ibn Masʿūd, Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, Anas ibn Mālik, Ibn ʿUmar, Abū Hurayrah, Ḥudhayfah ibn al-Yamān, and others whose mention would be lengthy — from his sayings, may God bless him and grant him peace: «My community will not agree upon misguidance»; «God would not gather my community upon misguidance»; «I asked God Almighty not to gather my community upon misguidance, and He granted me that»; «Whoever is pleased to dwell in the midst of Paradise, let him adhere to the community, for their supplication encompasses those behind them»; «Indeed, Satan is with the one, and he is farther from the two»; and his saying, may God bless him and grant him peace: «The hand of God is with the community, and God does not care about the straying of one who strays»; «A group of my community will not cease to be manifest upon the truth, unharmed by those who oppose them»; and it is narrated: «The opposition of those who oppose them will not harm them, except for the hardship that befalls them. And whoever departs from the community or separates from the community by a handspan has cast off the bond of Islam from his neck; and whoever separates from the community and dies, his death is a death of ignorance (jāhiliyyah).»

These reports have remained manifest among the Companions and the Successors up to our own time; none among the people of transmission from the predecessors (salaf) and successors (khalaf) of this community has rejected them. Rather, they are accepted by both those who agree with the community and those who oppose it. The community has never ceased to adduce them as proof in the principles of religion and its branches.

If it is said: "What is the aspect of the proof? The claim of tawātur for each individual one of these reports is not possible, and solitary transmission (naql al-āḥād) does not yield certain knowledge?" We say: In establishing the aspect of the proof there are two methods:

**The first:** That we claim necessary knowledge (al-ʿilm al-ḍarūrī) that the Messenger of God — may God bless him and grant him peace — magnified the status of this community and informed of its protection from error through the totality of these scattered reports, even if their individual reports are not mutawātir. By similar means, we find ourselves compelled to knowledge of the bravery of ʿAlī, the generosity of Ḥātim, the jurisprudence of al-Shāfiʿī, the oratory of al-Ḥajjāj, the inclination of the Messenger of God — may God bless him and grant him peace — toward ʿĀʾishah among his wives, and his magnifying his Companions and praising them — even though the individual reports therein are not mutawātir. Rather, falsehood is possible for each one of them if we isolate our consideration to it alone, but it is not possible for the totality. This resembles what is known from the totality of individual circumstantial indicators (qarāʾin) that are not free from possibility, but possibility is negated from their totality until necessary knowledge is attained.

**The second method:** That we do not claim knowledge by necessity, but rather knowledge by inference (ʿilm al-istidlāl), from two aspects:

**The first aspect:** These hadiths have never ceased to be widely known among the Companions and the Successors, who used them to establish Consensus, and no one appeared to oppose or deny them until the time of al-Naẓẓām. It is impossible, in the settled course of custom (mustaqarr al-ʿādah), for nations across repeated eras to concur upon accepting what no proof has established as sound, given the divergence of temperaments, the disparity of aspirations, and the differences of doctrines in rejection and acceptance. For this reason, no ruling established by solitary reports has ever been free from an opponent's opposition and the manifestation of hesitation regarding it.

**The second aspect:** Those who adduced these reports established by them a definitive principle (aṣl maqṭūʿ bihi) — namely, Consensus, by which judgment is passed over the Book of God Almighty and over the mutawātir Sunnah. It is impossible in custom to accept a report by which the definitive Book is lifted, unless it is based upon a definitive basis. As for lifting the definitive by what is not definitive, that is not known [to be acceptable] — so that no one should marvel, nor should anyone say: "How do you lift the definitive Book by a Consensus based upon a report whose soundness is not known? And how could the entire community be heedless of this until the time of al-Naẓẓām, who alone was singled out for noticing it?" This is the aspect of inference.

The deniers have three stations in opposing this: rejection (al-radd), interpretation (al-taʾwīl), and counter-evidence (al-muʿāraḍah).

**The First Station: Rejection.** It comprises four questions:

**The First Question:** Their saying: "Perhaps one person opposed these reports and rejected them, and his opposition was not transmitted to us." We say: This too is rendered impossible by custom, for Consensus is the greatest of the principles of religion. Had an opponent opposed it, the matter would have been magnified and the opposition would have become widely known — for the opposition of the Companions regarding the blood-money of the fetus, the question of al-ḥarām, and the ḥadd punishment for drinking has not become extinct. How then could opposition to a great principle, in which declaring one who errs in negating or affirming it to be misguided and an innovator is entailed, become extinct? And how did the opposition of al-Naẓẓām become widely known despite the collapse of his standing and the baseness of his rank, while the opposition of the great Companions and Successors remained hidden? This is something no intellect can accommodate at all.

**The Second Question:** They said: "You have adduced the report to establish Consensus, then you adduced Consensus to establish the soundness of the report. Grant that they agreed upon its soundness — what is the proof that what they agreed upon as sound is sound? Is the dispute not precisely over this?" We say: No. Rather, we adduced the report to establish Consensus, and the soundness of the report by the absence of any era's repudiation or opposition to it — given that custom necessitates the rejection of establishing a definitive principle by which definitive matters are judged, through a report whose soundness is unknown. Thus we know by custom that the report is definitive, not by Consensus. Custom is a principle from which cognitions are derived — for by it is known the invalidity of the claim of the Qurʾān's inimitability being challenged and that challenge becoming extinct; by it is known the invalidity of the claim of the explicit text for the Imamate, the obligation of the Ḍuḥā prayer, and the fasting of Shawwāl — and that had these been [true], it would have been impossible in custom to remain silent about them.

**The Third Question:** They said: "How do you reject one who says: 'Perhaps they established Consensus not by these reports but by another proof?'" We say: Their adducing these reports has been manifest in prohibiting opposition to the community and threatening whoever separates from the community and opposes it. This is more appropriate than saying: "Had they had another basis for it, it would have appeared and spread" — for their adherence to the verses has also been transmitted.

**The Fourth Question:** Their saying: "Since the Companions knew the soundness of these reports, why did they not mention the method of their soundness to the Successors, so that doubt would have been cut off and they would have shared in their knowledge?" We say: Because they knew that his definition — peace be upon him — of the protection of this community from error was through a totality of circumstantial indicators, signs, repetitions of wordings, and causes that indicated necessarily his intent to declare the negation of error from this community. Those indicators do not fall under narration, nor do expressions encompass them. Had they narrated them, possibilities would have attached to their individual parts. So they sufficed with the Successors' knowledge that a doubtful report does not establish a definitive principle, and that submission to it occurs in custom. Thus custom was, in the case of the Successors, stronger than narration.

**The Second Station: Interpretation.** They have three interpretations:

**The First:** His saying — may God bless him and grant him peace: «My community will not agree upon misguidance» indicates unbelief and innovation. Perhaps he meant the protection of all of them from unbelief — by interpretation and ambiguity. And his saying "upon error" is not mutawātir; and even if it is sound, "error" is general and can be carried upon unbelief.

We say: "Misguidance" (al-ḍalāl) in the linguistic convention does not correspond to unbelief. God Almighty said: {«And He found you lost and guided you»} [Al-Ḍuḥā 93:7], and He said, reporting from Moses — peace be upon him: {«I did it then, and I was among the misguided»} [Al-Shuʿarāʾ 26:20] — and He did not mean among the disbelievers, but rather among those who erred. It is said: "So-and-so strayed from the road" and "So-and-so's effort was lost" — all of that is error. How [could it mean unbelief], given that it is understood by necessity from these wordings that the status of this community is magnified and it is singled out for this virtue? As for protection from unbelief, that was bestowed upon ʿAlī, Ibn Masʿūd, Ubayy, and Zayd according to al-Naẓẓām's doctrine, for they died upon the truth. How many individuals have been protected from unbelief until they died? So what particular distinction would the community have? This indicates that he meant what individuals are not protected from — namely, forgetfulness, error, and falsehood — from which the community is protected, by way of elevating the entire community to the station of the Prophet — may God bless him and grant him peace — in protection from error in religion. As for other than religion — such as initiating war, peace, or the building of a town — the generality would necessitate protection for the community from it as well, but that is doubtful. The matter of religion is definitive in the obligation of protection therein, just as in the case of the Prophet — may God bless him and grant him peace — for he erred in the matter of pollinating palm trees, then said: «You are more knowledgeable about your worldly affairs, and I am more knowledgeable about your religious affairs.»

**The Second Interpretation:** Their saying: "The utmost of this is that it be a general statement necessitating protection from every error. But it is possible that what is meant is some types of error — such as testimony in the Hereafter, or what agrees with the mutawātir text, or what agrees with the rational proof — not what is by ijtihād and qiyās."

We say: No one among the community holds this differentiation. For whatever reason indicates the permissibility of error upon them in one thing indicates its permissibility in another. When there is no differentiator, there is no specification by arbitrary judgment without proof, and no specification is more appropriate than another. He has censured whoever opposes the community and commanded agreement. Had what entails protection not been known, following would have been impossible — unless protection is established absolutely. By it, the virtue and honor of the community are established. As for protection from some things but not others, that is established for every disbeliever, let alone a Muslim — for there is no person who errs in everything. Rather, every human being is protected from error in some things.

**The Third Interpretation:** That his community — may God bless him and grant him peace — is everyone who believes in him until the Day of Resurrection. The totality of these, from the beginning of Islam to the end of the life of the world, does not agree upon an error. Rather, every ruling that has passed upon the agreement of all the eras after the mission of the Prophet — may God bless him and grant him peace — is true, for the community is an expression of all of them. How [could it be otherwise], given that those who died in our time are of the community? The consensus of those after them is not the consensus of the entire community — for if they had opposed and then died, no consensus would have been concluded after them, and we would accept from the community whoever opposed even if he had died. Likewise, if they did not agree.

We say: Just as it is not permissible that "the community" mean the insane, children, the miscarried fetus, and the one who has not yet reached puberty — even though they are of the community — so too is it not permissible that it mean the dead and the one not yet created. Rather, what is understood is a people from whom difference and agreement can be conceived; agreement and difference cannot be conceived from the non-existent and the dead.

The proof of this is that he commanded following the community and censured whoever strayed from agreement. If what they mentioned were intended, then following and opposing would only be conceivable in the Hereafter, not in this world. Thus it is known with certainty that what is meant is a consensus that can be breached and opposed in this world — and that is those existing in every era. As for when one dies, the trace of his opposition remains, for his doctrine does not die with his death. There will come a sufficient discussion of this, God Almighty willing.

**The Third Station: Counter-Evidence with Verses and Reports.**

As for the verses — everything in them that prohibits unbelief, apostasy, and false action is general to all. If that were not possible for them, how could they be prohibited from it? Such as His saying, exalted: {«And that you say about God what you do not know»} [Al-Baqarah 2:169]; {«And whoever among you reverts from his religion and dies while a disbeliever»} [Al-Baqarah 2:217]; {«And do not consume your wealth among yourselves unjustly»} [Al-Baqarah 2:188]; and similar to that.

We say: This is not a prohibition upon them from agreeing, but rather a prohibition upon individuals. Even if each one individually falls under the prohibition, and even if it is granted, it is not a condition of a prohibition that the prohibited thing occur or be possible of occurrence. For God Almighty knew that all sins would not occur from them, yet He prohibited them from all of them — and opposition to what is known [not to occur] does not occur. He said to His Messenger — may God bless him and grant him peace: {«If you were to associate partners, your work would surely become worthless»} [Al-Zumar 39:65], and He said: {«So do not be among the ignorant»} [Al-Anʿām 6:35] — while He knew that He had protected him from them and that it would not occur.

As for the reports — his saying, peace be upon him: «Islam began as something strange, and it will return to being strange as it began»; and his saying, peace be upon him: «The best of generations is my generation, then those who follow them, then those who follow them — then falsehood will spread until a man will swear without being asked to swear, and testify without being asked to testify»; and his saying — may God bless him and grant him peace: «The Hour will not be established except upon the worst of my community.»

We say: This and its like indicate the abundance of disobedience and falsehood, but do not indicate that no one remains adhering to the truth. Nor does it contradict his saying — may God bless him and grant him peace: «A group of my community will not cease to be upon the truth until the command of God comes and until the Dajjāl appears.» How [could it contradict], given that these reports do not run in soundness and prominence the course of the hadiths to which we have adhered?

**The Third Path: Adherence to the Rational-Moral Method (al-Ṭarīq al-Maʿnawī).**

Its exposition is that when the Companions passed a ruling and claimed that they were certain of it, they would not be certain of it except upon a definitive basis. When they reach a multitude that reaches the limit of tawātur, custom renders impossible upon them the intent to lie, and renders impossible upon them error — to the extent that not one of them would notice the truth in that matter — and that certainty without a definitive proof is error. Thus their certainty in a place not warranting certainty is impossible in custom.

If they ruled by ijtihād and agreed upon it, then it is known that the Successors would severely censure those who opposed them and would be certain of it. Their certainty in that is certainty in a place not warranting certainty, so that too would only be upon a definitive basis. Otherwise, it would be impossible in custom for the truth to escape all of them despite their vast numbers, such that not one of them would notice the truth.

Likewise, we know that if the Successors agreed upon something, the Successors of the Successors would censure the opponent and be certain of the censure — and that is certainty in a place not warranting certainty, so custom renders it impossible except upon a definitive basis. Along this course, they said: If the people of binding and loosing were to return to a number less than the number of tawātur, then error is not impossible upon them in custom, nor is the deliberate intent to lie, if there is an incentive to it — so there is no proof in it.

This method is weak in our view, because the source of error is either the deliberate intent to lie or their deeming what is not definitive to be definitive. The first is not permissible upon a number reaching tawātur. As for the second, it is permissible — for the Jews were certain of the nullity of the prophethood of Jesus and Muhammad — peace be upon them both — and they were more than the number of tawātur. That is certainty in a place not warranting certainty, but they deemed what is not definitive to be definitive. Likewise, those who deny the origination of the world (ḥudūth al-ʿālam) and the prophecies, and those who commit other types of innovation and misguidance — their number reaches the number of tawātur, and truthfulness is achieved in their reports, but they erred by certainty in a place not warranting certainty. This speaker is compelled to make the consensus of the Jews and Christians a proof, with no specification for this community — and they have agreed upon the nullity of the religion of Islam.

If it is said: "This is adherence to custom, and you, in supporting the second path, sought comfort in custom — and this is precisely the first [path]." We say: Custom does not render impossible upon a number reaching tawātur that they deem what is not definitive to be definitive. And it is concerning this that we said: The condition of the mutawātir report is that it be based upon something perceived by the senses (maḥsūs), and custom renders impossible the submission and silence of one who repels the Book and the mutawātir Sunnah by a Consensus whose proof is a report that is merely conjectural (maẓnūn) and not definitive. Everything that is necessary (ḍarūrī) is known by sense, by circumstantial indicator, or by intuition (badīhah) — its path is one, and people agree upon grasping it, and custom renders impossible heedlessness of it upon those reaching tawātur. What is theoretical (naẓarī), its paths are diverse, so it is not impossible in custom that those reaching tawātur agree upon error in it. This is the difference between the two paths.

If it is said: "Your reliance in this second path is that what they agree upon is true and not error — so what is the proof of the obligation to follow it? Every mujtahid is correct regarding the truth, yet it is not obligatory upon another mujtahid to follow him. And the false witness is an invalidator (mubṭil), yet it is obligatory upon the judge to follow him? So the obligation to follow is one thing, and a thing's being true is another."

We say: The community has agreed upon the obligation to follow Consensus, and that it is among the truth that must be followed. By virtue of their being correct in their statement, the obligation to follow Consensus is entailed. Then we say: Every truth that is known to be truth — the principle regarding it is the obligation to follow. The mujtahid must be followed — except by the mujtahid who is also correct, for the truth obtained by his own ijtihād takes precedence over what is obtained by another's ijtihād in his regard. And the false witness, if it were known that he is false, would not be followed.

It is also indicated by the censure of whoever opposes the community, and that this was mentioned in the context of praise of the community. That is not realized except by the obligation to follow — otherwise it would have no meaning, except that they are correct when they hit upon the proof of truth — and that is permissible in the case of a single individual among the believers, so there is no praise or specification in it at all.

chapters.title_en: The Second Chapter on Clarifying the Pillars of Consensus (Ijmāʿ)
chapters.arabic_text:
### | [الباب الثاني في بيان أركان الإجماع]

وله ركنان: المجمعون ونفس الإجماع الركن الأول: المجمعون وهم أمة محمد -
صلى الله عليه وسلم - وظاهر هذا يتناول كل مسلم، لكن لكل ظاهر طرفان واضحان
في النفي والإثبات وأوساط  متشابهة. أما الواضح في الإثبات فهو كل مجتهد
مقبول الفتوى فهو أهل الحل والعقد قطعا ولا بد من موافقته في الإجماع. وأما
الواضح في النفي فالأطفال والمجانين والأجنة، فإنهم وإن كانوا من الأمة
فنعلم أنه - عليه الصلاة والسلام - ما أراد بقوله: «لا تجتمع أمتي على
الخطأ» إلا من يتصور منه الوفاق والخلاف في المسألة بعد فهمها. فلا يدخل
فيه من لا يفهمها. وبين الدرجتين العوام المكلفون والفقيه الذي ليس بأصولي
والأصولي الذي ليس بفقيه والمجتهد الفاسق والمبتدع والناشئ من التابعين
مثلا إذا قارب رتبة الاجتهاد في عصر الصحابة، فنرسم في كل واحد مسألة.

### | [مسألة دخول العوام في الإجماع]
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ج-م-ع (j-m-ʿ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Gathering, uniting, bringing together disparate parts into a coherent whole; collective agreement.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal-theological usage, the unified agreement of qualified scholars (ahl al-ḥall wa-l-ʿaqd) on a juridical matter, carrying binding authority.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is physical aggregation; metaphorical (majāz) extension denotes unanimity of opinion as a collective act.
- Root: ع-ق-د (ʿ-q-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Tying, binding, knotting; a firm covenant or contract.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The bond of authority and decisiveness—those whose word is "tied" to communal obligation.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal knotting of ropes; metaphorical for persons whose judgment is binding and unloosable.
- Sībawayh Rule: Al-Tamyīz bayna al-Ẓāhir wa-l-Muḥkam (Distinguishing apparent from unequivocal) — The term "ummah" (nation) is ẓāhir (apparent) in including all Muslims, but its scope is qualified by contextual intent (qaṣd) and rational feasibility (taṣawwur), requiring syntactic and semantic restriction.
chapters.translation:
I say: Consensus (ijmāʿ) has two pillars: the consensers themselves, and the act of consensus proper.

**The First Pillar: The Consensers** — They are the nation (ummah) of Muhammad, peace be upon him. The apparent sense of this term encompasses every Muslim, but every apparent term has two clear extremes—one affirmative and one negative—with ambiguous middle grounds between them.

As for the clear affirmative extreme: it is every qualified jurist (mujtahid) whose legal opinion (fatwā) is accepted. Such a person is, without doubt, among the people of binding authority (ahl al-ḥall wa-l-ʿaqd), and his agreement is indispensable for consensus.

As for the clear negative extreme: it includes children, the insane, and fetuses. For although they belong to the nation, we know that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, did not intend by his saying {«لا تجتمع أمتي على الخطأ»} ("My nation will not unite upon error") anyone except those from whom agreement or disagreement on a given question can be conceived after understanding it. Thus, those who do not comprehend the matter are not included.

Between these two degrees lie the common believers who are legally accountable (al-ʿawāmm al-mukallafūn), the jurist who is not a legal theorist (uṣūlī), the legal theorist who is not a jurist, the corrupt jurist (al-mujtahid al-fāsiq), the innovator (mubtadiʿ), and the emerging scholar among the Successors (tābiʿūn)—for example, one who approaches the rank of independent reasoning (ijtihād) in the era of the Companions. We shall therefore delineate a specific ruling (masʾalah) for each of these categories.

chapters.title_en: The Inclusion of the Commonality (ʿAwāmm) in Consensus (Ijmāʿ) and the Criterion of Competence (Ahlīyah) for Its Validators
chapters.arabic_text:
مسألة يتصور دخول العوام في الإجماع،
فإن الشريعة تنقسم إلى ما يشترك في دركه العوام والخواص كالصلوات الخمس
ووجوب الصوم والزكاة والحج، فهذا مجمع عليه، والعوام وافقوا الخواص في
الإجماع، وإلى ما يختص بدركه الخواص كتفصيل أحكام الصلاة والبيع والتدبير
والاستيلاد، فما أجمع عليه الخواص فالعوام متفقون على أن الحق فيه ما أجمع
عليه أهل الحل والعقد لا يضمرون خلافا أصلا فهم موافقون أيضا فيه. ويحسن
تسمية ذلك إجماع الأمة قاطبة، كما أن الجند إذا حكموا جماعة من أهل الرأي
والتدبير في مصالحة أهل قلعة فصالحوهم على شيء يقال هذا باتفاق جميع الجند.
فإذا كل مجمع عليه من المجتهدين فهو مجمع عليه من جهة العوام وبه يتم إجماع
الأمة. فإن قيل: فلو خالف عامي في واقعة أجمع عليها الخواص من أهل العصر
فهل ينعقد الإجماع دونه؟ إن كان ينعقد فكيف خرج العامي من الأمة، وإن لم
ينعقد فكيف يعتد بقول العامي؟ قلنا: قد اختلف الناس فيه فقال قوم: منعقد
لأنه من الأمة فلا بد من تسليمه بالجملة وبالتفصيل وقال آخرون، وهو الأصح:
إنه ينعقد بدليلين أحدهما: أن العامي ليس أهلا لطلب الصواب، إذ ليس له آلة
هذا الشأن فهو كالصبي والمجنون في نقصان الآلة؛ ولا يفهم من عصمة الأمة من
الخطأ إلا من يتصور منه الإصابة لأهليته والثاني، وهو الأقوى: أن العصر
الأول من الصحابة قد أجمعوا على أنه لا عبرة بالعوام في هذا الباب، أعني
خواص الصحابة وعوامهم؛ ولأن العامي إذا قال قولا علم أنه يقوله عن جهل وأنه
ليس يدري ما يقول وأنه ليس أهلا للوفاق والخلاف فيه. وعن هذا لا يتصور صدور
هذا من عامي عاقل؛ لأن العاقل يفوض ما لا يدري إلى من يدري، فهذه صورة فرضت
ولا وقوع لها أصلا. ويدل
على انعقاد الإجماع أن العامي يعصي بمخالفته العلماء ويحرم ذلك عليه،
ويدل على عصيانه ما ورد من ذم الرؤساء الجهال إذا ضلوا وأضلوا بغير علم،
وقوله تعالى: {لعلمه الذين يستنبطونه منهم} [النساء: 83] فردهم عن النزاع
إلى أهل الاستنباط. وقد وردت أخبار كثيرة بإيجاب المراجعة للعلماء وتحريم
فتوى العامة بالجهل والهوى، وهذا لا يدل على انعقاد الإجماع دونهم، فإنه
يجوز أن يعصي، بالمخالفة كما يعصي من يخالف خبر الواحد، ولكن يمتنع وجود
الإجماع لمخالفته والحجة في الإجماع، فإذا امتنع بمعصية أو بما ليس بمعصية
فلا حجة وإنما الدليل ما ذكرنا من قبل
مسألة: إذا قلنا لا يعتبر قول العوام لقصور آلتهم، فرب متكلم ونحوي ومفسر
ومحدث هو ناقص الآلة في درك الأحكام.
فقال قوم: لا يعتد إلا بقول أئمة المذاهب المستقلين بالفتوى كالشافعي
ومالك وأبي حنيفة وأمثالهم من الصحابة والتابعين، ومنهم من ضم إلى الأئمة
الفقهاء الحافظين لأحكام الفروع الناهضين بها، لكن أخرج الأصولي الذي لا
يعرف تفاصيل الفروع ولا يحفظها.
والصحيح أن الأصولي العارف بمدارك الأحكام وكيفية تلقيها من المفهوم
والمنظوم وصيغة الأمر والنهي والعموم وكيفية تفهيم النصوص والتعليل أولى
بالاعتداد بقوله من الفقيه الحافظ للفروع، بل ذو الآلة من هو متمكن من درك
الأحكام إذا أراد وإن لم يحفظ الفروع، والأصولي قادر عليه والفقيه الحافظ
للفروع لا يتمكن منه.
وآية أنه لا يعتبر حفظ الفروع أن العباس والزبير وطلحة وسعدا وعبد الرحمن
بن عوف وسعيد بن زيد بن عمرو بن نفيل وأبا عبيدة بن الجراح وأمثالهم ممن لم
ينصب نفسه للفتوى ولم يتظاهر بها تظاهر  العبادلة وتظاهر علي وزيد بن ثابت
ومعاذ كانوا يعتدون بخلافهم لو خالفوا، وكيف لا وكانوا صالحين للإمامة
العظمى ولا سيما لكون أكثرهم في الشورى؟ وما كانوا يحفظون الفروع بل لم تكن
الفروع موضوعة بعد، لكن عرفوا الكتاب والسنة وكانوا أهلا لفهمهما، والحافظ
للفروع قد لا يحفظ دقائق فروع الحيض والوصايا، فأصل هذه الفروع كهذه
الدقائق فلا يشترط حفظها فينبغي أن يعتد بخلاف الأصولي وبخلاف الفقيه
المبرز لأنهما ذوا آلة على الجملة يقولان ما يقولان عن دليل.
أما النحوي والمتكلم فلا يعتد بهما لأنهما من العوام في حق هذا العلم،
إلا أن يقع الكلام في مسألة تنبني على النحو أو على الكلام. فإن قيل: فهذه
المسألة قطعية أم اجتهادية؟ قلنا: هي اجتهادية، ولكن إذا جوزنا أن يكون
قوله إذا لم يخالف هؤلاء، أما خلاف العوام فلا يقع ولو وقع فهو قول باللسان
وهو معترف بكونه جاهلا بما يقول، فبطلان قوله مقطوع به كقول الصبي فأما هذا
فليس كذلك.
فإن قيل: فإذا قلد الأصولي الفقهاء فيما اتفقوا عليه في الفروع وأقر بأنه
حق هل ينعقد الإجماع؟ قلنا: نعم لأنه لا مخالفة وقد وافق الأصولي جملة وإن
لم يعرف التفصيل، كما أن الفقهاء اتفقوا على أن ما أجمع عليه المتكلمون في
باب الاستطاعة والعجز والأجسام والأعراض والضد والخلاف فهو صواب، فيحصل
الإجماع بالموافقة الجملية كما يحصل من العوام؛ لأن كل فريق كالعامي
بالإضافة إلى ما لم يحصل علمه وإن حصل علما آخر.
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ع-م-م (ʿ-M-M)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Comprehensive inclusion, enveloping all parts without exception; the general public (al-ʿāmmah) as opposed to the elite (al-khāṣṣah).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Denotes the universal applicability of a ruling or consensus that encompasses both the learned and the lay, reflecting the collective nature of the Ummah's infallibility (ʿiṣmah).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for physical envelopment; metaphorical (majāz) for the legal-moral authority of the masses' tacit agreement.
- Root: ح-ل-ع-ق (Ḥ-L-ʿ-Q) [Note: Root sequence adjusted for clarity; actual root: ع-ق-د (ʿ-Q-D)]
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Tying, binding firmly; a contract or covenant (ʿaqd); here, the binding nature of consensus (inʿiqād al-ijmāʿ).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The formal establishment of a legal proof (ḥujjah) that becomes obligatory upon all, akin to a ratified treaty.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for knotting; metaphorical for the conclusive sealing of a juridical matter by authoritative agreement.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Exceptive Syntax (al-Sharṭ wa al-Istithnāʾ) — Governing the nuanced parsing of "if it is said... then we say" (fa-in qīla... qulnā), ensuring the protasis and apodosis maintain logical and grammatical coherence in hypothetical objections and rebuttals.
chapters.translation:
I say: A question arises concerning the conceivable inclusion of the commonality (al-ʿawāmm) in consensus (ijmāʿ). For the Sacred Law (al-sharīʿah) divides into that whose apprehension is shared by the commonality and the elite (al-khawāṣṣ)—such as the five daily prayers, the obligation of fasting, alms-tax (zakāh), and pilgrimage (ḥajj)—and this is a matter of consensus, with the commonality having concurred with the elite therein. It also divides into that whose apprehension is exclusive to the elite—such as the detailed rulings of prayer, sale, tadbīr (contract of manumission upon death), and istīlād (manumission of a slave-mother). Thus, whatever the elite have reached consensus upon, the commonality agree that the truth therein is what the people of binding and loosing (ahl al-ḥall wa al-ʿaqd) have agreed upon; they harbor no opposition whatsoever, and so they are likewise in agreement. It is fitting to term this the consensus of the entire Ummah, just as when an army delegates a group of men of counsel and discernment to negotiate a truce with the inhabitants of a fortress, and they conclude an agreement, it is said: "This is by the agreement of all the soldiers."

Therefore, every matter agreed upon by the mujtahidūn (independent jurists) is agreed upon from the perspective of the commonality, and thereby the consensus of the Ummah is perfected. If it is said: "Suppose a commoner (ʿāmmī) opposes a particular case upon which the elite of that era have reached consensus—does the consensus still bind without him? If it binds, how has the commoner exited the Ummah? And if it does not bind, how can the commoner's opinion be counted?" We say: People have differed on this. Some said: It binds, for he is of the Ummah, and thus his submission is required both in general and in detail. Others—and this is the more correct (al-aṣaḥḥ)—said: It binds, by two proofs. The first: The commoner is not qualified to seek correctness, for he lacks the instrument (ālah) of this discipline; he is like a child or a madman in the deficiency of his instrument. And the infallibility of the Ummah from error is only understood of one from whom correctness is conceivable by virtue of his qualification. The second—and this is the stronger—is that the first era of the Companions (al-ṣaḥābah) reached consensus that no consideration is given to the commonality in this matter—I mean, the elite of the Companions and their commonality alike. For when a commoner utters an opinion, it is known that he speaks from ignorance, that he does not know what he says, and that he is not qualified for agreement or disagreement therein. On this basis, such a thing is not conceivable from a rational commoner, for the rational person delegates what he does not know to one who knows. This is a hypothetical scenario (ṣūrah mafrūḍah) with no actual occurrence whatsoever.

Evidence for the binding of consensus is that the commoner sins by opposing the scholars, and it is forbidden for him to do so. Evidence for his sinfulness is what has been reported in condemnation of ignorant leaders who, without knowledge, led astray and were led astray. And His saying, the Exalted: {«لعلمه الذين يستنبطونه منهم»} [Al-Nisāʾ: 83] — "It would have been known by those who derive it from them" — redirects them from dispute to the people of derivation (ahl al-istinbāṭ). Numerous reports (akhbār) have come mandating recourse to the scholars and forbidding the fatwā of the commonality out of ignorance and caprice. Yet this does not prove the binding of consensus without them, for it is possible that one sins by opposition, just as one who opposes a solitary report (khabar al-wāḥid) sins. However, the existence of consensus is precluded by his opposition—whether that opposition be sinful or not—and thus no proof (ḥujjah) stands. The evidence is only what we have mentioned previously.

Another question: If we say that the opinion of the commonality is not considered due to the deficiency of their instrument, then perhaps a theologian (mutakallim), a grammarian (naḥwī), an exegete (mufassir), or a hadith-scholar (muḥaddith) is likewise deficient in the instrument for apprehending legal rulings. Some said: Only the opinion of the imams of the legal schools (aʾimmah al-madhāhib) who are independent in issuing fatwā is counted—such as al-Shāfiʿī, Mālik, Abū Ḥanīfah, and their likes among the Companions and Followers (al-tābiʿūn). Others added to the imams the jurists (fuqahāʾ) who preserve the rulings of subsidiary branches (furūʿ) and are capable therein, but excluded the uṣūlī (specialist in legal theory) who does not know the details of the branches nor preserves them.

The correct view (al-ṣaḥīḥ) is that the uṣūlī who knows the sources of rulings (madārik al-aḥkām) and the manner of deriving them from the understood (al-mafhūm) and the explicit text (al-manẓūm), the imperative and prohibitive forms (ṣīghat al-amr wa al-nahy), the general (al-ʿumūm), and the method of comprehending the texts (al-nuṣūṣ) and their rationales (taʿlīl)—his opinion is more worthy of being counted than that of the jurist who merely preserves the branches. Indeed, the possessor of the instrument is one who is capable of apprehending rulings whenever he wills, even if he does not preserve the branches. The uṣūlī is capable of this, whereas the jurist who preserves the branches is not.

The proof that preserving the branches is not a condition is that al-ʿAbbās, al-Zubayr, Ṭalḥah, Saʿd, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, Saʿīd ibn Zayd ibn ʿAmr ibn Nufayl, Abū ʿUbaydah ibn al-Jarrāḥ, and their likes—those who did not devote themselves to fatwā nor publicize it as did the ʿAbādilah (the four ʿAbd Allāhs among the Companions), nor as did ʿAlī, Zayd ibn Thābit, and Muʿādh—their opposition, had they opposed, would have been counted. How could it not be, when they were fit for the supreme imamate (al-imāmah al-ʿuẓmā), especially as most of them were in the consultative council (al-shūrā)? They did not preserve the branches, for the branches had not yet been established; rather, they knew the Book and the Sunnah and were qualified to understand them. And the one who preserves the branches may not preserve the subtle details of the branches of menstruation (al-ḥayḍ) and bequests (al-waṣāyā). Since the origin of these branches is like these subtleties, preserving them is not a condition. Thus, the opposition of the uṣūlī and the opposition of the distinguished jurist (al-faqīh al-mubarriz) should be counted, for both possess the instrument in general, and they say what they say based on evidence (dalīl).

As for the grammarian and the theologian, their opinions are not counted, for they are of the commonality with respect to this science, unless the discussion concerns a matter that is built upon grammar or theology. If it is said: "Is this question definitive (qaṭʿīyah) or discretionary (ijtihādīyah)?" We say: It is discretionary. However, when we deem his opinion valid, it is only when he does not oppose these [qualified scholars]. As for the opposition of the commonality, it does not occur; and if it were to occur, it would be a mere utterance of the tongue, while he himself admits to being ignorant of what he says. Thus, the nullity of his opinion is definitively established, like the opinion of a child. But this [the uṣūlī's case] is not so.

If it is said: "If the uṣūlī, in the branches, follows (qallada) the jurists in what they have agreed upon and affirms it as true, does consensus bind?" We say: Yes, for there is no opposition, and the uṣūlī has agreed in general (ijmālan) even if he does not know the detail—just as the jurists agree that whatever the theologians (mutakallimūn) have reached consensus upon in the chapter of capacity (al-istiṭāʿah), incapacity (al-ʿajz), bodies (al-ajsām), accidents (al-aʿrāḍ), opposition (al-ḍidd), and difference (al-khilāf) is correct. Thus, consensus is achieved through general agreement, just as it is achieved from the commonality. For every group is like a commoner relative to what it has not attained knowledge of, even if it has attained other knowledge.

chapters.title_en: On the Case of the Innovator (Mubtadiʿ) Whose Dissent Does Not Prevent the Formation of Consensus (Ijmāʿ) Unless He Is Deemed an Unbeliever
chapters.arabic_text:
### | [مسألة المبتدع إذا خالف لم ينعقد الإجماع دونه إذا لم يكفر]

، بل هو كمجتهد فاسق وخلاف المجتهد الفاسق معتبر.
فإن قيل لعله يكذب في إظهار الخلاف وهو لا يعتقده. قلنا لعله يصدق ولا بد
من موافقته ولو لم نتحقق موافقته، كيف وقد نعلم اعتقاد الفاسق بقرائن
أحواله في مناظراته واستدلالاته؟ والمبتدع ثقة يقبل قوله، فإنه ليس يدرى
أنه فاسق، أما إذا كفر ببدعته فعند ذلك لا يعتبر خلافه إن كان يصلي إلى
القبلة ويعتقد نفسه مسلما لأن الأمة ليست عبارة عن  المصلين إلى القبلة بل
عن المؤمنين وهو كافر وإن كان لا يدري أنه كافر نعم لو قال بالتشبيه
والتجسيم وكفرناه فلا يستدل على بطلان مذهبه بإجماع مخالفيه على بطلان
التجسيم مصيرا إلى أنهم كل الأمة؛ لأن كونهم كل الأمة موقوف على إخراج هذا
من الأمة، والإخراج من الأمة موقوف على دليل التكفير، فلا يجوز أن يكون
دليل تكفيره ما هو موقوف على تكفيره فيؤدي إلى إثبات الشيء بنفسه.
نعم بعد أن كفرناه بدليل عقلي لو خالف في مسألة أخرى لم يلتفت إليه، فلو
تاب وهو مصر على المخالفة في تلك المسألة التي أجمعوا عليها في حال كفره
فلا يلتفت إلى خلافه بعد الإسلام لأنه مسبوق بإجماع كل الأمة وكان المجمعون
في ذلك الوقت كل الأمة دونه، فصار كما لو خالف كافر كافة الأمة ثم أسلم وهو
مصر على ذلك الخلاف، فإن ذلك لا يلتفت إليه إلا على قول من يشترط انقراض
العصر في الإجماع.
فإن قيل: فلو ترك بعض الفقهاء الإجماع بخلاف المبتدع المكفر إذا لم يعلم
أن بدعته توجب الكفر وظن أن الإجماع لا ينعقد دونه، فهل يعذر من حيث إن
الفقهاء يطلعون على معرفة ما يكفر به من التأويلات؟ قلنا: للمسألة صورتان،
إحداها: أن يقول الفقهاء: نحن لا ندري أن بدعته توجب الكفر أم لا، ففي هذه
الصورة لا يعذرون فيه إذ يلزمهم مراجعة علماء الأصول ويجب على العلماء
تعريفهم، فإذا أفتوا بكفره فعليهم التقليد، فإن لم يقنعهم التقليد فعليهم
السؤال عن الدليل حتى إذا ذكر لهم دليله فهموه لا محالة؛ لأن دليله قاطع،
فإن لم يدركه فلا يكون معذورا كمن لا يدرك دليل صدق الرسول - صلى الله عليه
وسلم - فإنه لا عذر مع نصب الله تعالى الأدلة القاطعة، الصورة الثانية: أن
لا يكون قد بلغته بدعته وعقيدته فترك الإجماع لمخالفته فهو معذور في خطئه
وغير مؤاخذ به وكان الإجماع لم ينتهض حجة في حقه، كما إذا لم يبلغه الدليل
الناسخ لأنه غير منسوب إلى تقصير، بخلاف الصورة  الأولى فإنه قادر على
المراجعة والبحث فلا عذر له في تركه، فهو كمن قبل شهادة الخوارج وحكم بها
فهو مخطئ لأن الدليل على تكفير الخوارج على علي وعثمان - رضي الله عنهما -
والقائلين بكفرهما المعتقدين استباحة دمهما ومالهما ظاهر يدرك على القرب،
فلا يعذر من لا يعرفه، بخلاف من حكم بشهادة الزور وهو لا يعرف لأنه لا طريق
له إلى معرفة صدق الشاهد وله طريق إلى معرفة كفره.
فإن قيل وما الذي يكفر به؟ قلنا: الخطب في ذلك طويل وقد أشرنا إلى شيء
منه في كتاب " فصل التفرقة بين الإسلام والزندقة والقدر الذي نذكره الآن
أنه يرجع إلى ثلاثة أقسام:
الأول: ما يكون نفس اعتقاده كفرا، كإنكار الصانع وصفاته وجحد النبوة.
الثاني: ما يمنعه اعتقاده من الاعتراف بالصانع وصفاته وتصديق رسله، ويلزم
إنكار
ذلك من حيث التناقض.
الثالث: ما ورد من التوقيف بأنه لا يصدر إلا من كافر كعبادة النيران
والسجود للصنم وجحد سورة من القرآن وتكذيب بعض الرسل واستحلال الزنا والخمر
وترك الصلاة، وبالجملة إنكار ما عرف بالتواتر والضرورة من الشريعة.
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ع-ق-د (ʿ-q-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To tie, bind, or contract; a firm knotting of a thing upon itself.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Technical term for the binding force of consensus (inʿiqād al-ijmāʿ) as a contractual closure of juristic authority.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) in contractual bonds; metaphorical (majāz) in the sense of consensus becoming a decisive seal.
- Root: ب-د-ع (b-d-ʿ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To originate something new without prior example; an innovation (bidʿah) as a novel doctrine.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, a belief or practice introduced into religion contrary to established precedent (khilāf al-sunnah).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for creation ex nihilo (of God); metaphorical for human doctrinal novelty, carrying blameworthy connotation.
- Root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To cover, conceal; ingratitude; unbelief as covering the truth.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Technical term for the legal-religious status of one who rejects necessary truths of revelation (takfīr).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for covering a seed in the ground; metaphorical for veiling faith with denial.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Protasis-Apodosis Structure (al-sharṭ wa al-jawāb) — The text repeatedly employs "إذا" (if/when) clauses to establish legal conditionality, where the apodosis is suspended on the protasis, requiring precise parsing of hypothetical juristic scenarios.
chapters.translation:
I say: The innovator (mubtadiʿ), when he dissents [from the consensus], the consensus is not prevented from forming without him, so long as he is not deemed an unbeliever (kāfir). Rather, he is like a corrupt jurist (mujtahid fāsiq), and the dissent of a corrupt jurist is indeed taken into consideration.

If it is said: Perhaps he lies in displaying dissent while not actually believing it. We say: Perhaps he is truthful, and it is necessary to accept his [stated position] even if we do not verify his inner conviction. How [can we doubt this], given that we know the belief of the corrupt person through the indications (qarāʾin) of his circumstances in his disputations and his argumentations? And the innovator is trustworthy (thiqah), his statement being accepted, for it is not known that he is corrupt. However, if he is deemed an unbeliever due to his innovation, then at that point his dissent is not considered — even if he prays toward the qiblah and believes himself to be a Muslim — because the Community (ummah) is not defined as those who pray toward the qiblah, but rather as the believers. And he is an unbeliever, even if he does not know that he is an unbeliever.

Yes, if he professes anthropomorphism (tashbīh) and corporealism (tajsīm), and we deem him an unbeliever, then one may not infer the invalidity of his doctrine from the consensus of his opponents upon the invalidity of corporealism, on the grounds that they constitute the entire Community. For their being the entire Community is contingent upon the exclusion of this person from the Community, and the exclusion from the Community is contingent upon a proof of his unbelief (takfīr). Thus it is impermissible that the proof of his unbelief be that which is itself contingent upon his unbelief, for that would lead to establishing a thing by itself.

Yes, after we have deemed him an unbeliever by a rational proof (dalīl ʿaqlī), if he then dissents on another matter, no attention is paid to him. And if he repents while persisting in his dissent on that matter upon which they had reached consensus during his state of unbelief, then his dissent after [embracing] Islam is not heeded, because it is preceded by the consensus of the entire Community, and those who formed the consensus at that time were the entire Community without him. This becomes like the case of an unbeliever who opposed the entirety of the Community, then embraced Islam while persisting in that dissent — for that [dissent] is not heeded, except according to the view of one who stipulates the passing of the era (inqirāḍ al-ʿaṣr) for the validity of consensus.

If it is said: What if some jurists abandoned the consensus due to the dissent of an innovator deemed an unbeliever, when they did not know that his innovation necessitates unbelief, and they assumed that consensus does not form without him — are they excused, given that jurists are able to ascertain what constitutes unbelief through interpretative reasoning (taʾwīlāt)? We say: The matter has two aspects.

The first aspect: That the jurists say: We do not know whether his innovation necessitates unbelief or not. In this aspect, they are not excused, for they are obligated to refer to the scholars of legal theory (uṣūl), and it is incumbent upon the scholars to inform them. So when they issue a legal ruling (fatwā) of his unbelief, then the jurists must follow them (taqlīd). If following does not satisfy them, then they must ask for the proof, until when the proof is presented to them, they will understand it inevitably — because the proof is decisive (qāṭiʿ). If they do not grasp it, they are not excused, like one who does not grasp the proof of the truthfulness of the Messenger — peace be upon him — for there is no excuse when God Most High has established decisive proofs.

The second aspect: That his innovation and belief have not reached him, so he abandoned the consensus due to his dissent — then he is excused for his error and is not held accountable for it, and the consensus was not established as an authority (ḥujjah) in his regard, just as when the abrogating proof (dalīl nāsikh) has not reached one, because he is not attributed to negligence. This differs from the first aspect, for there he is capable of referring [to scholars] and investigating, so there is no excuse for his abandonment. He is like one who accepted the testimony of the Khawārij and ruled by it — he is erroneous, because the proof of the unbelief of the Khawārij — who [declared] ʿAlī and ʿUthmān — may God be pleased with them both — as unbelievers, and who hold the permissibility of shedding their blood and seizing their wealth — is evident and attainable with ease. Thus, one who does not know it is not excused. This differs from one who ruled by false testimony (shahādat al-zūr) without knowing [it to be false], because he has no means to know the truthfulness of the witness, whereas he does have a means to know his unbelief.

If it is said: And what is it that constitutes unbelief? We say: The discourse on this is lengthy, and we have alluded to some of it in the book "The Criterion of Distinction Between Islam and Heresy" (Fayṣal al-Tafriqah bayn al-Islām wa al-Zandaqah). The extent that we mention now is that it reverts to three categories:

The first: That which is itself, in its very belief, unbelief — such as denying the Creator (al-Ṣāniʿ) and His attributes, and rejecting prophethood (nubuwwah).

The second: That which his belief prevents him from acknowledging the Creator and His attributes and affirming His messengers, such that the denial of these things necessarily follows from his position by way of contradiction (tanāquḍ).

The third: That which is established by scriptural designation (tawqīf) as issuing only from an unbeliever — such as worshipping fire, prostrating to an idol, denying a chapter (sūrah) of the Qurʾān, rejecting some of the messengers, deeming fornication and wine lawful, and abandoning prayer. In sum: denying that which is known by mass transmission (tawātur) and necessity (ḍarūrah) from the Sacred Law.

chapters.title_en: The Question of Consensus (Ijmāʿ) of Non-Companions
chapters.arabic_text:
### | [مسألة بإجماع غير الصحابة]

مسألة قال قوم: لا يعتد بإجماع غير الصحابة، وسنبطله وقال قوم: يعتد
بإجماع التابعين بعد الصحابة، ولكن لا يعتد بخلاف التابعي في زمان الصحابة
ولا يندفع إجماع الصحابة بخلافه. وهذا فاسد مهما بلغ التابعي رتبة الاجتهاد
قبل تمام الإجماع لأنه من الأمة، فإجماع غيره لا يكون إجماع جميع الأمة، بل
إجماع البعض والحجة في إجماع الكل نعم لو أجمعوا ثم بلغ رتبة الاجتهاد بعد
إجماعهم فهو مسبوق بالإجماع فليس له الآن أن يخالف، كمن أسلم بعد تمام
الإجماع.
ويدل عليه قوله تعالى {وما اختلفتم فيه من شيء فحكمه إلى الله} [الشورى:
10] وهذا مختلف فيه، ويدل عليه إجماع الصحابة على تسويغ الخلاف للتابعي
وعدم إنكارهم عليه، فهو إجماع منهم على جواز الخلاف، كيف وقد علم أن كثيرا
من أصحاب عبد الله كعلقمة والأسود وغيرهما كانوا يفتون في عصر الصحابة وكذا
الحسن البصري وسعيد بن المسيب؟ فكيف  لا يعتد بخلافهم؟ وعلى الجملة فلا يفضل
الصحابي التابعي إلا بفضيلة الصحبة، ولو كانت هذه الفضيلة تخصص الإجماع
لسقط قول الأنصار بقول المهاجرين وقول المهاجرين بقول العشرة وقول العشرة
بقول الخلفاء الأربعة وقولهم بقول أبي بكر وعمر - رضي الله عنهما -. فإن
قيل: روي عن عائشة - رضي الله عنها - أنها أنكرت على أبي سلمة بن عبد
الرحمن مجاراة الصحابة، وقالت: فروج يصقع مع الديكة. قلنا: ما ذكرناه مقطوع
به ولم يثبت عن عائشة ما ذكرتم إلا بقول الآحاد، وإن ثبت فهو مذهبها ولا
حجة فيه.
ثم لعلها أرادت منعه من مخالفتهم فيما سبق إجماعهم عليه، أو لعلها أنكرت
عليه خلافه في مسألة لا تحتمل الاجتهاد في اعتقادها كما أنكرت على زيد بن
أرقم في مسألة العينة وظنت أن وجوب حسم الذريعة قطعي. واعلم أن هذه المسألة
يتصور الخلاف فيها مع من يوافق على أن إجماع الصحابة يندفع بمخالفة واحد من
الصحابة، أما من ذهب إلى أنه لا يندفع خلاف الأكثر بالأقل كيفما كان فلا
يختص كلامه بالتابعي.
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ع-ق-د (ʿ-q-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Binding knot, firm compact; intellectual grasp of a matter
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Ijmāʿ as the collective firm resolution of the ummah's qualified scholars
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for physical tying; metaphorical (majāz) for unanimous agreement as a binding covenant
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause (al-Sharṭ) — the protasis (law/ idhā) governs the apodosis, marking temporal and logical priority in legal reasoning
chapters.translation:
I say: A group has claimed that the consensus (ijmāʿ) of non-Companions is not to be reckoned with — and we shall refute this. Another group has claimed that the consensus of the Followers (tābiʿūn) after the Companions is to be reckoned with, but that the dissent of a Follower during the era of the Companions is not to be reckoned with, nor does it repel the consensus of the Companions. This is corrupt, whenever the Follower has attained the rank of independent juristic reasoning (ijtihād) before the completion of the consensus — for he is of the ummah, and the consensus of others besides him would not be the consensus of the entire ummah, but rather the consensus of some. The authoritative proof lies in the consensus of all. Yes — if they had already reached consensus, and then he attained the rank of ijtihād after their consensus, then he is preceded by the consensus, and it is not for him now to dissent — like one who embraces Islam after the completion of the consensus.

Evidence for this is His saying, the Exalted: {«وما اختلفتم فيه من شيء فحكمه إلى الله»} [Al-Shūrā: 10] — and this matter is one of disagreement. Further evidence is the consensus of the Companions upon permitting dissent to the Follower and their failure to censure him for it — this being a consensus from them upon the permissibility of dissent. How so, when it is known that many of the companions of ʿAbd Allāh — such as ʿAlqamah, al-Aswad, and others — used to issue legal verdicts (fatwā) in the era of the Companions, and likewise al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī and Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib? How then is their dissent not to be reckoned with? In sum, the Companion holds no superiority over the Follower except by the virtue of companionship (ṣuḥbah). Were this virtue to particularize consensus, then the saying of the Anṣār would fall before the saying of the Muhājirūn, and the saying of the Muhājirūn before the saying of the Ten, and the saying of the Ten before the saying of the four Caliphs, and their saying before the saying of Abū Bakr and ʿUmar — may God be pleased with them both.
