If it is said: It is narrated from ʿĀʾishah — may God be pleased with her — that she censured Abū Salamah ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān for vying with the Companions, saying: "A chick crowing with the roosters." We reply: What we have mentioned is definitively established, and what you have mentioned from ʿĀʾishah is not established except by solitary report (khabar al-āḥād). Even if it were established, it is her own juristic opinion (madhhab), and there is no proof in it.

Moreover, perhaps she intended to prevent him from dissenting from them in matters upon which their consensus had already preceded — or perhaps she censured his dissent in a matter that, in her belief, did not admit of ijtihād, just as she censured Zayd ibn Arqam regarding the matter of ʿīnah (sale with deferred payment), deeming the obligation of blocking the means (sadd al-dharīʿah) to be definitive. Know that this question is conceivable as a point of disagreement only with one who agrees that the consensus of the Companions is repelled by the dissent of a single Companion. As for one who holds that the dissent of the majority is not repelled by the minority, however it may be, his discourse is not specifically confined to the Follower.

chapters.title_en: The Consensus of the Majority Is Not an Authoritative Proof When Opposed by the Minority
chapters.arabic_text:
### | [مسألة الإجماع من الأكثر ليس بحجة مع مخالفة الأقل]

وقال قوم هو حجة وقال قوم: إن بلغ عدد الأقل عدد التواتر اندفع الإجماع
وإن نقص فلا يندفع.
والمعتمد عندنا أن العصمة إنما تثبت للأمة بكليتها، وليس هذا إجماع
الجميع بل هو مختلف فيه، وقد قال تعالى: {وما اختلفتم فيه من شيء فحكمه إلى
الله} [الشورى: 10] فإن قيل: قد تطلق الأمة ويراد بها الأكثر، كما يقال بنو
تميم يحمون الجار ويكرمون الضيف، ويراد الأكثر.
قلنا من يقول بصيغة العموم يحمل ذلك على الجميع، ولا يجوز التخصيص
بالتحكم بل بدليل وضرورة ولا ضرورة ههنا، ومن لا يقول به فيجوز أن يريد به
الأقل وعند ذلك لا يتميز البعض المراد عما ليس بمراد ولا بد من إجماع
الجميع ليعلم أن البعض المراد داخل فيه، كيف وقد وردت أخبار تدل على قلة
أهل الحق حيث قال «وهم يومئذ الأقلون»
وقال - صلى الله عليه وسلم - «سيعود الدين غريبا كما  بدأ غريبا» وقال
تعالى {وأكثرهم لا يعقلون} [المائدة: 103] وقال تعالى: {وقليل من عبادي
الشكور} [سبأ: 13] وقال تعالى: {كم من فئة قليلة} [البقرة: 249] الآية.
وإذا لم يكن ضابط ولا مرد فلا خلاص إلا باعتبار قول الجميع. الدليل
الثاني إجماع الصحابة على تجويز الخلاف للآحاد، فكم من مسألة قد انفرد فيها
الآحاد بمذهب كانفراد ابن عباس بالعول فإنه أنكره. فإن قيل: لا بل أنكروا
على ابن عباس القول بتحليل المتعة وأن الربا في النسيئة، وأنكرت عائشة على
ابن أرقم مسألة العينة، وأنكروا على أبي موسى الأشعري قوله: " النوم لا
ينقض الوضوء وعلى أبي طلحة القول بأن أكل البرد لا يفطر وذلك لانفرادهم به
قلنا لا بل لمخالفتهم السنة الواردة فيه المشهورة بينهم أو لمخالفتهم أدلة
ظاهرة قامت عندهم.
ثم نقول: هب أنهم أنكروا انفراد المنفرد، والمنفرد منكر عليهم إنكارهم
ولا ينعقد الإجماع، فلا حجة في إنكارهم مع مخالفة الواحد. ولهم شبهتان:
الشبهة الأولى: قولهم: قول الواحد فيما يخبر عن نفسه لا يورث العلم، فكيف
يندفع به قول عدد حصل العلم بإخبارهم عن أنفسهم لبلوغهم عدد التواتر؟ وعن
هذا قال قوم: عدد الأقل إلى أن يبلغ مبلغ التواتر يدفع الإجماع. وهذا فاسد
من ثلاثة أوجه.
الأول: أن صدق الأكثر وإن علم فليس ذلك صدق جميع الأمة واتفاقهم والحجة
في اتفاق الجميع، فسقطت الحجة لأنهم ليسوا كل الأمة.
الثاني: أن كذب الواحد ليس بمعلوم فلعله صادق، فلا تكون المسألة اتفاقا
من جميع الصادقين إن كان صادقا.
الثالث: أنه لا نظر إلى ما يضمرون بل التعبد متعلق بما يظهرون فهو مذهبهم
وسبيلهم لا ما أضمروه، فإن قيل: فهل يجوز أن تضمر الأمة خلاف ما تظهر؟
قلنا: ذلك إن كان إنما يكون عن تقية وإلجاء وذلك يظهر ويشتهر وإن لم يشتهر
فهو محال لأنه يؤدي إلى اجتماع الأمة على ضلالة وباطل، وهو ممتنع بدليل
السمع.
الشبهة الثانية: أن مخالفة الواحد شذوذ عن الجماعة وهو منهي عنه، فقد ورد
ذم الشاذ وأنه كالشاذ من الغنم عن القطيع.  قلنا: الشاذ عبارة عن الخارج عن
الجماعة بعد الدخول فيها، ومن دخل في الإجماع لا يقبل خلافه بعده وهو
الشذوذ، أما الذي لم يدخل أصلا فلا يسمى شاذا. فإن قيل: فقد قال - عليه
السلام -: «عليكم بالسواد الأعظم فإن الشيطان مع الواحد وهو عن الاثنين
أبعد» .
قلنا: أراد به الشاذ الخارج على الإمام بمخالفة الأكثر على وجه يثير
الفتنة وقوله: «وهو عن الاثنين أبعد» أراد به الحث على طلب الرفيق في
الطريق، ولهذا قال - عليه السلام -: «والثلاثة ركب» . وقد قال بعضهم قول
الأكثر حجة وليس بإجماع. وهو متحكم بقوله إنه حجة إذ لا دليل عليه وقال
بعضهم: مرادي به أن اتباع الأكثر أولى.
قلنا: هذا يستقيم في الأخبار وفي حق المقلد إذا لم يجد ترجيحا بين
المجتهدين سوى الكثرة، وأما المجتهد فعليه اتباع الدليل دون الأكثر لأنه إن
خالفه واحد لم يلزمه اتباعه وإن انضم إليه مخالف آخر لم يلزمه الاتباع.
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ع-ص-م (ʿ-ṣ-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Protection, preservation from error or harm; the act of guarding against corruption.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, ʿiṣmah denotes the divinely granted infallibility of the community (ummah) collectively from unanimous error.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is physical protection; metaphorical extension applies to moral and doctrinal immunity from error.
- Root: ش-ذ-ذ (sh-dh-dh)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Isolation, separation from the main body; a single straying from the group.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal theory, shudhūdh refers to an opinion that departs from the established consensus after having been part of it.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: a sheep separating from the flock; metaphorical: a jurist deviating from the community's agreed position.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Exceptive Constructions (al-sharṭ wa al-istithnāʾ) — The parsing of "إن بلغ... وإن نقص" requires the protasis to govern the apodosis, and the exceptive clause "إلا باعتبار" restricts the preceding negation.
chapters.translation:
I say: Some have held that the consensus of the majority is an authoritative proof, while others have held that if the number of the minority reaches the number required for tawātur (mass transmission), then consensus is nullified; but if it falls short of that, it is not nullified.

The position relied upon with us is that infallibility (ʿiṣmah) is established only for the community (ummah) in its entirety. Now, this is not a consensus of all — rather, it is a matter of disagreement. And Allah Most High has said: {وما اختلفتم فيه من شيء فحكمه إلى الله} [al-Shūrā: 10] — "And in whatever you differ, its judgment is with Allah."

If it is said: "The term 'community' (ummah) may be used loosely to mean the majority, just as one says 'the Banū Tamīm protect the neighbor and honor the guest,' meaning the majority of them" — we reply: Whoever affirms the general import of the expression (ṣīghat al-ʿumūm) applies it to all, and specification (takhṣīṣ) is not permissible by arbitrary decree but only by evidence and necessity — and there is no necessity here. As for one who does not affirm the general import, he may intend by it the minority; and in that case, the intended part cannot be distinguished from what is not intended. Thus, the consensus of all is indispensable, so that one may know that the intended part is included within it.

How [can it be otherwise], when reports have come indicating the scarcity of the people of truth, where he said: «وهم يومئذ الأقلون» — "And they on that day are the few." And he — peace be upon him — said: «سيعود الدين غريبا كما بدأ غريبا» — "Religion will return to being a stranger just as it began as a stranger." And Allah Most High said: {وأكثرهم لا يعقلون} [al-Māʾidah: 103] — "And most of them do not reason." And He said: {وقليل من عبادي الشكور} [Sabaʾ: 13] — "And few of My servants are grateful." And He said: {كم من فئة قليلة} [al-Baqarah: 249] — "How many a small company..." — the verse.

And when there is no criterion and no recourse, there is no deliverance except by considering the statement of all.

The second proof: The consensus of the Companions upon permitting disagreement to individuals. How many a matter in which individuals held a solitary position, such as the solitary position of Ibn ʿAbbās regarding the ʿawl (proportional reduction of shares in inheritance) — for he was censured for it. If it is said: "No — rather, they censured Ibn ʿAbbās for his position permitting mutʿah (temporary marriage) and that ribā applies only to deferred payment; and ʿĀʾishah censured Ibn Arqam regarding the matter of ʿīnah (sell-buyback); and they censured Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī for his statement that sleep does not nullify ablution; and Abū Ṭalḥah for his position that eating snow does not break the fast — all this because of their solitary positions" — we reply: No — rather, [they censured them] for contradicting the well-known Sunnah transmitted among them, or for contradicting manifest evidences established with them.

Then we say: Grant that they censured the solitary individual's isolation — yet the solitary individual censures them in turn for their censure, and no consensus is thereby concluded. So there is no proof in their censure when a single one opposes.

They have two doubts:

The first doubt: Their statement: "The statement of a single person reporting about himself does not yield certain knowledge — so how can it nullify the statement of a number whose report about themselves has yielded knowledge by reaching the number of tawātur?" And on this basis, some said: "The minority, until it reaches the level of tawātur, nullifies consensus." This is corrupt on three counts:

First: Even if the truthfulness of the majority is known, that is not the truthfulness of all the community nor their agreement — and the proof lies in the agreement of all. So the proof falls, because they are not the entire community.

Second: The falsehood of the single one is not known — perhaps he is truthful. Thus the matter is not an agreement of all the truthful ones, if he is truthful.

Third: There is no consideration of what they conceal; rather, the legal obligation (taʿabbud) attaches to what they manifest. It is their doctrine and their way — not what they have concealed.

If it is said: "Is it permissible for the community to conceal what contradicts what they manifest?" — we reply: That, if it occurs, is only out of taqiyyah (dissimulation) or compulsion, and that becomes manifest and well-known. And if it does not become well-known, it is impossible, because it would lead to the community's agreement upon error and falsehood — which is precluded by the evidence of revelation (samʿ).

The second doubt: The opposition of a single one is a deviation (shudhūdh) from the group, and deviation is prohibited. For censure has been reported against the deviant, and that he is like the stray sheep from the flock.

We reply: "Deviant" (shādhdh) is an expression for one who exits from the group after having entered into it. Whoever has entered into consensus, his opposition after that is not accepted — and that is the deviation. As for one who never entered at all, he is not called deviant.

If it is said: "He — peace be upon him — said: «عليكم بالسواد الأعظم فإن الشيطان مع الواحد وهو عن الاثنين أبعد» — 'Hold to the great mass, for Satan is with the single one, and he is farther from the two'" — we reply: He intended by it the deviant who rebels against the Imam by opposing the majority in a manner that stirs sedition. And his statement "he is farther from the two" intended urging the seeking of a companion on the road — and for this reason he — peace be upon him — said: «والثلاثة ركب» — "And three are a caravan."

Some have said: "The statement of the majority is a proof, though not a consensus." He is arbitrary in his claim that it is a proof, for there is no evidence for it. And some said: "I mean by it that following the majority is more appropriate."

We reply: This holds in reports (akhbār) and in the case of the lay follower (muqallid) when he finds no preponderance between the mujtahids except by number. As for the mujtahid, he must follow the evidence rather than the majority — for if a single one opposes him, he is not obliged to follow him; and if another opponent joins him, he is still not obliged to follow.

chapters.title_en: The Authority of the Consensus of the People of Medina; The Requirement of Tawātur-Level Numbers for Consensus; No Authority in Post-Companion Consensus
chapters.arabic_text:
### | [مسألة حجية إجماع أهل المدينة]

مسألة: قال مالك: الحجة في إجماع أهل المدينة فقط.
وقال قوم: المعتبر إجماع أهل الحرمين مكة والمدينة والمصرين الكوفة
والبصرة وما أراد المحصلون بهذا إلا أن هذه
البقاع قد جمعت في زمن الصحابة أهل الحل والعقد، فإن أراد مالك أن
المدينة هي الجامعة لهم فمسلم له ذلك لو جمعت وعند ذلك لا يكون للمكان فيه
تأثير، وليس ذلك بمسلم بل لم تجمع المدينة جميع العلماء لا قبل الهجرة ولا
بعدها بل ما زالوا متفرقين في الأسفار والغزوات والأمصار، فلا وجه لكلام
مالك إلا أن يقول عمل أهل المدينة حجة لأنهم الأكثرون والعبرة بقول
الأكثرين وقد أفسدناه، أو يقول يدل اتفاقهم في قول أو عمل أنهم استندوا إلى
سماع قاطع فإن الوحي الناسخ نزل فيهم فلا تشذ عنهم مدارك الشريعة. وهذا
تحكم إذ لا يستحيل أن يسمع غيرهم حديثا من رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم
- في سفر أو في المدينة لكن يخرج منها قبل نقله، فالحجة في الإجماع ولا
إجماع. وقد تكلف لمالك تأويلات ومعاذير  استقصيناها في كتاب " تهذيب الأصول
" ولا حاجة إليها ههنا. وربما احتجوا بثناء رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم
- على المدينة وعلى أهلها، وذلك يدل على فضيلتهم وكثرة ثوابهم لسكناهم
المدينة ولا يدل على تخصيص الإجماع بهم. وقد قال قوم: الحجة في اتفاق
الخلفاء الأربعة. وهو تحكم لا دليل عليه إلا ما تخيله جماعة في أن قول
الصحابي حجة، وسيأتي في موضعه.

### | [مسألة هل يشترط أن يبلغ أهل الإجماع عدد التواتر]

مسألة اختلفوا في أنه هل يشترط أن يبلغ أهل الإجماع عدد التواتر
؟ أما من أخذه من دليل العقل واستحالة الخطأ بحكم العادة فيلزمه
الاشتراط، والذين أخذوه من السمع اختلفوا، فمنهم من شرط ذلك لأنه إذا نقص
عددهم فنحن لا نعلم إيمانهم بقولهم فضلا عن غيره. وهذا فاسد من وجهين
أحدهما أنه يعلم إيمانهم لا بقولهم لكن بقوله - صلى الله عليه وسلم -: «لا
تزال طائفة من أمتي على الحق حتى يأتي أمر الله وحتى يظهر الدجال» فإذا لم
يكن على وجه الأرض مسلم سواهم فهم على الحق الثاني أنا لم نتعبد بالباطن،
وإنما أمة محمد من آمن بمحمد - صلى الله عليه وسلم - ظاهرا؛ إذ لا وقوف على
الباطن.
وإذا ظهر أنا متعبدون باتباعهم فيجوز أن يستدل بهذا على أنهم صادقون؛ لأن
الله تعالى لا يتعبدنا باتباع الكاذب وتعظيمه والاقتداء به فإن قيل: كيف
يتصور رجوع عدد المسلمين إلى ما دون عدد التواتر وذلك يؤدي إلى انقطاع
التكليف، فإن التكليف يدوم بدوام الحجة والحجة تقوم بخبر التواتر عن أعلام
النبوة وعن وجود محمد - صلى الله عليه وسلم - وتحديه بالنبوة، والكفار لا
يقومون بنشر أعلام النبوة بل يجتهدون في طمسها، والسلف من الأئمة مجمعون
على دوام التكليف إلى القيامة وفي ضمنه الإجماع على استحالة اندراس
الأعلام، وفي نقصان عدد التواتر ما يؤدي إلى الاندراس، وإذا لم يتصور وجود
هذه الحادثة فكيف نخوض في حكمها؟
قلنا: يحتمل أن يقال ذلك ممتنع لهذه الأدلة، وإنما معنى تصور هذه المسألة
رجوع عدد أهل الحل والعقد إلى  ما دون عدد التواتر، وإن قطعنا بأن قول
العوام لا يعتبر فتدوم أعلام الشرع بتواتر العوام. ويحتمل أن يقال يتصور
وقوعها والله تعالى يديم الأعلام بالتواتر الحاصل من جهة المسلمين والكفار
فيتحدثون بوجود محمد - صلى الله عليه وسلم - ووجود معجزته وإن لم يعترفوا
بكونها معجزة أو يخرق الله تعالى العادة فيحصل العلم بقول القليل حتى تدوم
الحجة، بل نقول قول القليل مع القرائن المعلومة
في مناظرته وتسديده قد يحصل العلم من غير خرق عادة فبجميع هذه الوجوه
يبقى الشرع محفوظا.
فإن قيل: فإذا جاز أن يقل عدد أهل الحل والعقد فلو رجع إلى واحد فهل يكون
مجرد قوله حجة قاطعة؟ قلنا: إن اعتبرنا موافقة العوام فإذا قال قولا وساعده
عليه العوام ولم يخالفوه فيه فهو إجماع الأمة فيكون حجة؛ إذ لو لم يكن قد
اجتمعت الأمة على الضلالة والخطأ وإن لم نلتفت إلى قول العوام فلم يوجد ما
يتحقق به اسم الاجتماع؛ إذ يستدعي ذلك عددا بالضرورة حتى يسمى إجماعا ولا
أقل من اثنين أو ثلاثة.
وهذا كله يتصور على مذهب من يعتبر إجماع من بعد الصحابة، فأما من لا يقول
إلا بإجماع الصحابة فلا يلزمه شيء من ذلك لأن الصحابة قد جاوز عددهم عدد
التواتر.

### | [مسألة لا حجة في إجماع من بعد الصحابة]
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ح-ج-ج (ḥ-j-j)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The root denotes "proof," "argument," or "authoritative evidence" — that which establishes a claim decisively.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In uṣūl al-fiqh, ḥujjiyyah signifies the binding evidentiary force of a source (e.g., ijmāʿ) in establishing legal obligation (taklīf).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Used literally (ḥaqīqah) for a conclusive proof; metaphorically (majāz) for a mere indicator lacking decisive force.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Exceptive Constructions (al-sharṭ wa al-istithnāʾ) — Governing the logical structure of "if X, then Y" and "except Z," crucial for parsing the hypothetical objections and rebuttals.
chapters.translation:
I say: The scholars have differed over whether the consensus of the people of Medina alone constitutes an authoritative proof (ḥujjah).

**Section on the Authority of the Consensus of the People of Medina**

Question: Mālik said: The proof lies only in the consensus of the people of Medina. Another group said: What is considered is the consensus of the people of the Two Sanctuaries (al-ḥaramayn), Mecca and Medina, and of the two garrison cities (al-miṣrayn), Kufa and Basra. By this, the investigators (al-muḥaṣṣilūn) intended nothing other than that these regions, in the era of the Companions, gathered the people of loosing and binding (ahl al-ḥall wa al-ʿaqd). If Mālik meant that Medina alone was the gathering place for them, that is granted to him — were it actually to have gathered them. But even then, the place itself would have no intrinsic effect. This, however, is not granted; for Medina never gathered all the scholars, neither before the Hijrah nor after it. Rather, they remained dispersed across journeys, military expeditions, and various garrison cities. Thus, there is no basis for Mālik's statement except that he might say: The practice (ʿamal) of the people of Medina is a proof because they are the majority, and consideration is given to the statement of the majority — and we have already refuted this. Or he might say: Their agreement upon a statement or practice indicates that they relied upon a decisive hearing (samāʿ qāṭiʿ), for the abrogating revelation (al-waḥy al-nāsikh) descended among them, so the sources of the Law (madārik al-sharīʿah) cannot escape them. This, however, is arbitrary (taḥakkum), for it is not impossible that someone other than them heard a ḥadīth from the Messenger of Allah — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — either on a journey or in Medina, but then departed from it before transmitting it. So the proof lies in consensus (al-ijmāʿ), and there is no [such] consensus [exclusive to them]. People have strained to produce interpretations and excuses for Mālik, which we have exhaustively covered in our book "Tahdhīb al-Uṣūl," and there is no need for them here. They might also adduce the praise of the Messenger of Allah — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — upon Medina and its people. That indicates their virtue and the abundance of their reward for dwelling in Medina, but it does not indicate the restriction of consensus to them. Another group said: The proof lies in the agreement of the four Caliphs. This is arbitrary, with no evidence for it except what some have imagined — that the statement of a Companion is a proof — and this will be discussed in its proper place.

**Section on Whether the People of Consensus Must Reach the Number of Tawātur**

Question: They differed over whether the people of consensus must reach the number of tawātur (conclusive transmission). As for one who derives consensus from rational proof and the impossibility of error by customary necessity (istiḥālat al-khaṭaʾ bi-ḥukm al-ʿādah), he is obliged to stipulate this condition. Those who derive it from revelation (al-samʿ) differed: some stipulated it, arguing that if their number falls short, we cannot know their faith from their own statements, let alone anything else. This is corrupt on two counts. First: we know their faith not from their statements, but from his statement — may Allah bless him and grant him peace: {«لَا تَزَالُ طَائِفَةٌ مِنْ أُمَّتِي عَلَى الْحَقِّ حَتَّى يَأْتِيَ أَمْرُ اللَّهِ وَحَتَّى يَظْهَرَ الدَّجَّالُ»} ("A group of my community will not cease to be upon the truth until the command of Allah comes and until the Dajjāl appears"). So if there is no Muslim on the face of the earth other than them, they are upon the truth. Second: we are not commanded to know the inner state (al-bāṭin); rather, the community of Muhammad consists of whoever believes in Muhammad — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — outwardly (ẓāhir), for we have no access to the inner. And since it is established that we are commanded to follow them, it is permissible to use this as evidence that they are truthful; for Allah — exalted is He — does not command us to follow a liar, to honor him, or to emulate him. If it is said: How can the number of Muslims be conceived to fall below the number of tawātur? That would lead to the cessation of obligation (taklīf), for obligation endures as long as the proof endures, and the proof is established by tawātur transmission of the signs of prophethood (aʿlām al-nubuwwah), of the existence of Muhammad — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — and his challenge (taḥaddī) with prophethood. The disbelievers do not propagate the signs of prophethood; rather, they strive to obliterate them. The early scholars (al-salaf) among the imams are unanimously agreed upon the endurance of obligation until the Day of Resurrection, and included in this is the consensus upon the impossibility of the effacement (indirās) of these signs. A decrease in the number of tawātur would lead to effacement. And if the occurrence of this event is inconceivable, how can we delve into its ruling? We say: It is possible to hold that this is impossible for these proofs, and the meaning of conceiving this question is merely that the number of the people of loosing and binding falls below the number of tawātur — even if we are certain that the statements of the commoners (al-ʿawāmm) are not considered — so the signs of the Law endure through the tawātur of the commoners. It is also possible to hold that its occurrence is conceivable, and Allah — exalted is He — perpetuates the signs through tawātur obtained from both Muslims and disbelievers, who will narrate the existence of Muhammad — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — and the existence of his miracle, even if they do not acknowledge it as a miracle. Or Allah — exalted is He — might break the custom (kharq al-ʿādah), such that knowledge is obtained from the statement of the few, so that the proof endures. Indeed, we say: the statement of the few, accompanied by known contextual indicators (qarāʾin) — in his disputation and his being guided — may yield knowledge without breaking the custom. By all these ways, the Law remains preserved. If it is said: If the number of the people of loosing and binding may decrease, then if it falls to one, would his mere statement be a decisive proof (ḥujjah qāṭiʿah)? We say: If we consider the agreement of the commoners, then if he states something and the commoners support him and do not oppose him, that is the consensus of the community (ijmāʿ al-ummah) and thus a proof; for the community does not agree upon error (ḍalālah) or mistake. But if we do not heed the statement of the commoners, then nothing exists by which the name "gathering" (ijtimāʿ) is realized; for that necessarily requires a number, such that it is called consensus, and no less than two or three. All of this is conceivable on the doctrine of one who considers the consensus of those after the Companions. As for one who affirms only the consensus of the Companions, none of this applies to him, for the Companions' number has already exceeded the number of tawātur.

**Section on There Being No Proof in the Consensus of Those After the Companions**

chapters.title_en: The Refutation of the Ẓāhirī Denial of Post-Ṣaḥābah Consensus and the Exposition of the Second Pillar
chapters.arabic_text:
مسألة ذهب داود وشيعته من أهل الظاهر إلى أنه لا حجة في إجماع من بعد
الصحابة.
وهو فاسد لأن الأدلة الثلاثة على كون الإجماع حجة، أعني الكتاب والسنة
والعقل، لا تفرق بين عصر وعصر. فالتابعون إذا أجمعوا فهو إجماع من جميع
الأمة، ومن خالفهم فهو سالك غير سبيل المؤمنين. ويستحيل بحكم العادة أن يشذ
الحق عنهم مع كثرتهم عند من يأخذه من العادة. ولهم شبهتان، أضعفهما قولهم:
الاعتماد على الخبر والآية، وهو قوله تعالى: {ويتبع غير سبيل المؤمنين}
[النساء: 115] يتناول الذين نعتوا بالإيمان وهم الموجودون وقت نزول الآية،
فإن المعدوم لا يوصف بالإيمان ولا يكون له سبيل وقوله - عليه السلام -: «لا
تجتمع أمتي على الخطأ» يتناول  أمته الذين آمنوا به وتصور إجماعهم واختلافهم
وهم الموجودون.
وهذا باطل؛ إذ يلزم على مساقه أن لا ينعقد إجماع بعد موت سعد بن معاذ
وحمزة ومن استشهد من المهاجرين والأنصار ممن كانوا موجودين عند نزول الآية،
فإن إجماع من وراءهم ليس إجماع جميع المؤمنين وكل الأمة، ويلزم أن لا يعتد
بخلاف من أسلم بعد نزول الآية وكملت آلته بعد ذلك. وقد أجمعنا وإياهم
والصحابة على أن موت واحد من الصحابة لا يحسم باب الإجماع، بل إجماع
الصحابة بعد النبي حجة بالاتفاق، وكم من صحابي استشهد في حياة رسول الله -
صلى الله عليه وسلم - بعد نزول الآية.
الشبهة الثانية: أن الواجب اتباع سبيل جميع المؤمنين وإجماع جميع الأمة،
وليس التابعون جميع الأمة فإن الصحابة وإن ماتوا لم يخرجوا بموتهم عن الأمة
ولذلك لو خالف واحد من الصحابة إجماع التابعين لا يكون قول جميع الأمة ولا
يحرم الأخذ بقول الصحابي، فإذا كان خلاف بعض الصحابة يدفع إجماع التابعين
فعدم وفاقهم أيضا يدفع لأنهم بالموت لم يخرجوا عن كونهم من الأمة. قالوا:
وقياس هذا يقتضي أن لا يثبت وصف الكلية أيضا للصحابة بل ينتظر لحوق
التابعين وموافقتهم من بعدهم إلى القيامة فإنهم كل الأمة، لكن لو اعتبر ذلك
لم ينتفع بالإجماع إلا في القيامة، فثبت أن وصف الكلية إنما هو لمن دخل في
الوجود دون من لم يدخل فلا سبيل إلى إخراج الصحابة من الجملة، وعند ذلك لا
يثبت وصف كلية الأمة للتابعين.
والجواب أنه كما بطل على القطع الالتفات إلى اللاحقين بطل الالتفات إلى
الماضين، ولولا ذلك لما تصور إجماع بعد موت واحد من المسلمين في زمان
الصحابة والتابعين ولا بعد أن استشهد حمزة وقد اعترفوا بصحة إجماع
الصحابة بعد رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - وبعد موت من مات بعد رسول
الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم -، وليس ذلك إلا لأن الماضي لا يعتبر والمستقبل
لا ينتظر وأن وصف كلية الأمة حاصل لكل من الموجودين في كل وقت.
وأما إجماع التابعين على  خلاف قول واحد من الصحابة فقد قال قوم: يصير قول
الصحابي مهجورا لأنهم كل الأمة وإن سلمنا - وهو الصحيح - فنقول: إن اتفقوا
على وفق قوله انعقد الإجماع؛ إذ موافقته إن لم تقو الإجماع فلا تقدح فيه،
وإن أجمعوا على خلاف قوله فلا يصير ذلك القول عندنا مهجورا حتى يحرم على
تابعي التابعين موافقته؛ لأنه بعد أن أفتى في المسألة فليس فتوى التابعين
فيها فتوى جميع الأمة بل فتوى البعض.
فإن قيل: إن ثبت نعت الكلية للتابعين فليكن خلاف قولهم بعدهم حراما وإن
قال به صحابي قبلهم وإن لم يكونوا كل الأمة، فينبغي أن لا تقوم الحجة
بإجماعهم ولا يحرم خلافهم؛ إذ خلاف بعض الأمة ليس بحرام، أما أن تكون كلية
الأمة في شيء دون شيء فهذا متناقض وجمع بين النفي والإثبات.
قلنا: ليس بمتناقض؛ لأن الكلية إنما تثبت بالإضافة إلى المسألة التي
خاضوا فيها، فإذا نزلت مسألة بعد الصحابة فالتابعون فيها كل الأمة إذا
أجمعوا فيها، أما ما أفتى فيها الصحابي ففتواه ومذهبه لا ينقطع بموته. وهذا
كالصحابي إذا مات بعد الفتوى وأجمع الباقون على خلافه لا يكون ذلك إجماعا
من الأمة، ولو مات ثم نزلت واقعة بعده انعقد الإجماع على كل مذهب وتكون
الكلية حاصلة بالإضافة.
فإن قيل: إن كان في الأمة غائب لا ينعقد الإجماع دونه، وإن لم يكن لذلك
الغائب خبر من الواقعة ولا فتوى فيها، لكن نقول لو كان حاضرا لكان له قول
فيها فلا بد من موافقته، فليكن الميت قبل التابعين كالغائب. قلنا: يبطل
بالميت الأول من الصحابة، فإن الإجماع انعقد دونه ولو كان غائبا لم ينعقد؛
لأن الغائب في الحال ذو مذهب ورأي بالقوة فتمكن موافقته ومخالفته فيحتمل أن
يوافق أو يخالف إذا عرضت المسألة عليه بخلاف الميت فإنه لا يتصور في حقه
خلاف أو وفاق لا بالقوة ولا بالفعل بل المجنون والمريض الزائل العقل والطفل
لا ينتظر لأنه بطل منه إمكان الوفاق والخلاف.
فإن قيل: فما أجمع عليه التابعون يندفع بخلاف واحد من  الصحابة إذا نقل،
فإن لم ينقل فلعله خالف، ولكن لم ينقل إلينا، فلا يستيقن إجماع كل الأمة.
قلنا: يبطل بالميت الأول من الصحابة، فإن إمكان خلافه لا يكون كحقيقة
خلافه. وهذا التحقيق، وهو أنه لو فتح باب الاحتمال لبطلت الحجج؛ إذ ما من
حكم إلا ويتصور تقدير نسخه وانفراد الواحد بنقله وموته قبل أن ينقل إلينا،
فيبطل إجماع الصحابة لاحتمال أن واحدا منهم أضمر المخالفة، وإنما أظهر
الموافقة لسبب ويرد خبر الواحد لاحتمال أن يكون كاذبا.
وإذا عرف الإجماع وانقرض العصر أمكن رجوع واحد منهم قبل الموت وإن لم
ينقل إلينا، فيبطل الإجماع على مذهب من يشترط انقراض العصر. فإن قيل: إن
الأصل عدم النسخ وعدم الرجوع. قلنا: والأصل عدم خوضه في الواقعة وعدم
الخلاف والوفاق جميعا، ومع أن الأصل العدم فالاحتمال لا ينتفي، وإذا ثبت
الاحتمال حصل الشك فيصير الإجماع غير مستيقن مع الشك، ولكن يقال: لا يندفع
الإجماع بكل شك.
فإن قيل: في مسألة تجويز النسخ وتجويز الرجوع شك بعد استيقان أصل الحجة
وإنما
الشك في دوامها، وههنا الشك في أصل الإجماع؛ لأن الإجماع موقوف على حصول
نعت الكلية لهم، ونعت الكلية موقوف على معرفة انتفاء الخلاف، فإذا شككنا في
انتفاء الخلاف شككنا في الكلية فشككنا في الإجماع.
قلنا: لا بل نعت الكلية حاصل للتابعين، وإنما ينتفي بمعرفة الخلاف فإذا
لم يعرف بقيت الكلية، وما ذكروه يضاهي قول القائل: الحجة في نص مات الرسول
- عليه السلام - قبل نسخه، فإذا لم يعرف موته قبل نسخه شككنا في الحجة،
والحجة الإجماع المنقرض عليه العصر، فإذا شككنا في الرجوع فقد شككنا في
الحجة، وكذلك القول في قول الميت الأول من الصحابة فإنا لا نقول: صار كلية
الباقين مشكوكا فيها هذا تمام الكلام في الركن الأول.
الركن الثاني: في نفس الإجماع. ونعني به اتفاق فتاوى الأمة في المسألة في
لحظة واحدة انقرض عليه العصر أو لم ينقرض أفتوا عن اجتهاد أو عن نص مهما
كانت الفتوى نطقا صريحا وتمام النظر في هذا  الركن ببيان أن السكوت ليس
كالنطق وأن انقراض العصر ليس بشرط وأن الإجماع قد ينعقد عن اجتهاد، فهذه
ثلاث مسائل.
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ج-م-ع (j-m-ʿ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To gather, assemble, unite; collective agreement (ijmāʿ) as the unified stance of a community.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Ijmāʿ as the unanimous concord of the qualified scholars (ahl al-ḥall wa-l-ʿaqd) on a juridical matter, signifying infallible communal authority.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for physical gathering; metaphorical (majāz) for concord of opinion, where the "whole" (kulliyyah) is a legal construct, not a physical totality.
- Root: خ-ل-ف (kh-l-f)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To come after, succeed; opposition, disagreement (khilāf).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Khilāf as the contrary stance that breaks unanimity; the "successor" (khalaf) as one who follows in time, not in authority.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for temporal succession; metaphorical for doctrinal opposition, where the past (māḍī) is juridically inert.
- Root: ك-ل-ل (k-l-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Totality, universality; the all-encompassing attribute (kulliyyah).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Kulliyyah as the legal description of the entire ummah at any given time, contingent on existential presence (wujūd), not on all past or future members.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for exhaustive inclusion; metaphorical for legal competence, where the "whole" is defined by those alive, not by the dead or unborn.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Exceptive Syntax (al-sharṭ wa-l-istithnāʾ) — The parsing of "if...then" constructions (e.g., "if they agree... then consensus is established") and exceptive clauses (e.g., "except the dead") to distinguish hypothetical possibility from actual legal effect.
chapters.translation:
I say: The question [of whether consensus after the Companions is authoritative]. Dāwūd [al-Ẓāhirī] and his partisans among the Ahl al-Ẓāhir held that there is no proof in the consensus of those after the Companions. This is corrupt, because the three proofs that consensus is authoritative — namely, the Book, the Sunnah, and reason — do not differentiate between one era and another. Thus, if the Followers (tābiʿūn) reach consensus, it is a consensus of the entire ummah, and whoever opposes them is one traversing a path other than that of the believers. And it is impossible, by the custom of habit (ʿādah), that the truth should escape them given their multitude, for one who derives [this principle] from habit. They have two specious arguments, the weaker of which is their saying: The reliance is on the report and the verse, namely His saying, the Exalted: {and follows a path other than that of the believers} [al-Nisāʾ 4:115]. This addresses those described by faith, who are those existing at the time of the verse's descent, for the non-existent cannot be described by faith nor have a path. And his saying, peace be upon him: «My ummah will not agree upon an error» addresses his ummah who believed in him, and whose consensus and disagreement are conceivable — namely, those existing [then].

This is false; for by its own logic, no consensus could be established after the death of Saʿd ibn Muʿādh, Ḥamzah, and those martyred among the Emigrants and Helpers who were present at the verse's descent, since the consensus of those after them would not be the consensus of all believers nor of the entire ummah. It would also entail that no weight be given to the opposition of one who embraced Islam after the verse's descent and whose [legal] capacity was completed thereafter. Yet we, they, and the Companions have agreed that the death of a single Companion does not seal the door of consensus; rather, the consensus of the Companions after the Prophet is authoritative by agreement. How many a Companion was martyred during the lifetime of the Messenger of God — peace be upon him — after the verse's descent!

The second specious argument: The obligation is to follow the path of all believers and the consensus of the entire ummah, but the Followers are not the entire ummah, for the Companions, though dead, did not exit the ummah by their death. Therefore, if a single Companion opposed the consensus of the Followers, it would not be the saying of the entire ummah, nor would it be forbidden to adopt the Companion's saying. So if the opposition of some Companions repels the consensus of the Followers, then their lack of agreement also repels it, because by death they did not exit from being part of the ummah. They said: The analogy of this entails that the attribute of totality (kulliyyah) is not established for the Companions either, but rather one must await the joining of the Followers and their agreement after them until the Day of Resurrection, for they are the entire ummah. But if that were considered, consensus would be of no use except on the Day of Resurrection. Thus it is established that the attribute of totality belongs only to those who have entered into existence, not to those who have not entered, so there is no way to exclude the Companions from the whole — and in that case, the attribute of the ummah's totality is not established for the Followers.

The answer: Just as it is categorically false to pay heed to those who come later, so too is it false to pay heed to those who have passed. Were it not so, no consensus could be conceived after the death of a single Muslim in the era of the Companions and Followers, nor after Ḥamzah was martyred — yet they have acknowledged the validity of the Companions' consensus after the Messenger of God — peace be upon him — and after the death of those who died after him. This is only because the past is not considered and the future is not awaited, and because the attribute of the ummah's totality is realized for all those existing in every time.

As for the Followers' consensus against the saying of a single Companion, some have said: The Companion's saying becomes abandoned because they are the entire ummah. Even if we grant this — and it is the correct view — we say: If they agree in accordance with his saying, consensus is established; for his agreement, if it does not strengthen the consensus, does not vitiate it. And if they agree against his saying, that saying does not become abandoned in our view such that it would be forbidden for a follower of the Followers to agree with it; for since he had issued a legal opinion (fatwā) on the matter, the Followers' fatwā on it is not the fatwā of the entire ummah, but rather the fatwā of some.

If it is said: If the attribute of totality is established for the Followers, then opposition to their saying after them should be forbidden, even if a Companion before them held it — and if they are not the entire ummah, then no proof should stand by their consensus, nor should opposition to them be forbidden, since opposition of some of the ummah is not forbidden. But that the ummah's totality should be [established] in one matter and not another is contradictory, a combination of negation and affirmation.

We say: It is not contradictory; for totality is established only in relation to the matter in which they deliberated. Thus, when a matter arises after the Companions, the Followers are therein the entire ummah if they reach consensus on it. As for what a Companion had opined on, his fatwā and his school (madhhab) do not terminate with his death. This is like a Companion who dies after issuing a fatwā, and the rest agree against him — that is not a consensus of the ummah. But if he dies and then a new case arises after him, consensus is established on every school, and totality is realized in relation [to that case].

If it is said: If there is an absent one in the ummah, consensus is not established without him — even if that absent one has no report of the case nor a fatwā on it — but we say: Were he present, he would have a saying on it, so his agreement is necessary. Thus, let the dead before the Followers be like the absent. We say: This is refuted by the first dead among the Companions, for consensus was established without him; had he been absent, it would not have been established. For the absent one presently has a school and an opinion in potentiality (bi-l-quwwah), so his agreement and disagreement are possible, and he might agree or disagree if the matter were presented to him — unlike the dead, for whom disagreement or agreement is inconceivable neither in potentiality nor in actuality. Rather, the insane, the one whose mind is lost through illness, and the child are not awaited, because the possibility of agreement and disagreement is nullified for them.

If it is said: What the Followers agreed upon is repelled by the opposition of a single Companion if it is transmitted; but if it is not transmitted, perhaps he opposed it but it was not conveyed to us, so the consensus of the entire ummah is not certain. We say: This is refuted by the first dead among the Companions, for the possibility of his opposition is not like the reality of his opposition. And this is the verification: If the door of possibility were opened, all proofs would be nullified; for there is no ruling except that one can conceive its abrogation (naskh), or a single person's solitary transmission of it, or his death before conveying it to us. Thus the Companions' consensus would be nullified by the possibility that one of them concealed opposition while outwardly showing agreement for some reason; and the solitary report (khabar al-wāḥid) would be rejected by the possibility that the transmitter is lying.

And when consensus is known and the era has passed, it is possible that one of them retracted before death without it being conveyed to us, which would nullify the consensus on the view of those who stipulate the passing of the era. If it is said: The principle is the absence of abrogation and the absence of retraction. We say: The principle is also the absence of his deliberation on the case and the absence of both disagreement and agreement. Yet despite the principle of absence, the possibility is not negated; and when possibility is established, doubt arises, so consensus becomes uncertain with doubt. But it is said: Consensus is not repelled by every doubt.

If it is said: In the matter of permitting abrogation and permitting retraction, there is doubt after the certainty of the proof's origin; the doubt is only about its continuance. But here the doubt is about the very origin of consensus; for consensus is contingent upon the attainment of the attribute of totality for them, and the attribute of totality is contingent upon knowing the negation of opposition. So if we doubt the negation of opposition, we doubt the totality, and thus we doubt the consensus. We say: No — rather, the attribute of totality is realized for the Followers, and it is only negated by the knowledge of opposition. If opposition is not known, the totality remains. What they mentioned resembles the saying of one who says: The proof is in a text (naṣṣ) that the Messenger — peace be upon him — died before its abrogation; if his death before its abrogation is not known, we doubt the proof. And the proof is the consensus over which the era has passed; if we doubt the retraction, we have doubted the proof. Likewise is the saying regarding the first dead among the Companions, for we do not say that the totality of the rest has become doubtful. This completes the discourse on the first pillar.

The second pillar: Concerning consensus itself. By it we mean the agreement of the ummah's legal opinions (fatāwā) on a matter in a single moment, whether the era has passed over it or not, whether they opined by independent reasoning (ijtihād) or by a text, however the fatwā may be — explicit speech. The complete examination of this pillar consists in explaining that silence is not like speech, that the passing of the era is not a condition, and that consensus may be established by ijtihād. These are three matters.

chapters.title_en: On a Fatwa Issued by Some Companions While Others Remained Silent
chapters.arabic_text:
### | [مسألة أفتى بعض الصحابة بفتوى وسكت الآخرون]

مسألة إذا أفتى بعض الصحابة بفتوى وسكت الآخرون لم ينعقد الإجماع ولا
ينسب إلى ساكت قول، وقال قوم: إذا انتشر وسكتوا، فسكوتهم كالنطق حتى يتم به
الإجماع.
وشرط قوم انقراض العصر على السكوت، وقال قوم: هو حجة وليس بإجماع، وقال
قوم: ليس بحجة ولا إجماع، ولكنه دليل تجويزهم الاجتهاد في المسألة،
والمختار أنه ليس بإجماع ولا حجة، ولا هو دليل على تجويز الاجتهاد في
المسألة إلا إذا دلت قرائن الأحوال على أنهم سكتوا مضمرين الرضا وجواز
الأخذ به عند السكوت.
والدليل عليه أن فتواه إنما تعلم بقوله الصريح الذي لا يتطرق إليه احتمال
وتردد، والسكوت متردد فقد يسكت من غير إضمار الرضا لسبعة أسباب:
الأول: أن يكون في باطنه مانع من إظهار القول، ونحن لا نطلع عليه، وقد
تظهر قرائن السخط عليه مع سكوته
الثاني: أن يسكت؛ لأنه يراه قولا سائغا لمن أداه إليه اجتهاده، وإن لم
يكن هو موافقا عليه بل كان يعتقد خطأه.
الثالث: أن يعتقد أن كل مجتهد مصيب فلا يرى الإنكار في المجتهدات أصلا
ولا يرى الجواب إلا فرض كفاية، فإذا كفاه من هو مصيب سكت، وإن خالف
اجتهاده.
الرابع: أن يسكت وهو منكر لكن ينتظر فرصة الإنكار ولا يرى البدار مصلحة
لعارض من العوارض ينتظر زواله ثم يموت قبل زوال ذلك العارض أو يشتغل عنه.
الخامس: أن يعلم أنه لو أنكر لم يلتفت إليه وناله ذل وهوان كما قال ابن
عباس في سكوته عن إنكار العول في حياة عمر كان رجلا مهيبا فهبته.
السادس: أن يسكت؛ لأنه متوقف في المسألة؛ لأنه بعد في مهلة النظر.
السابع: أن يسكت لظنه أن غيره قد كفاه الإنكار وأغناه عن الإظهار ثم يكون
قد غلط فيه فترك الإنكار عن توهم؛ إذ رأى الإنكار فرض كفاية وظن أنه قد كفي
وهو مخطئ في  وهمه. فإن قيل: لو كان فيه خلاف لظهر.
قلنا: ولو كان فيه وفاق لظهر، فإن تصور عارض يمنع من ظهور الوفاق تصور
مثله في ظهور الخلاف. وبهذا يبطل قول الجبائي حيث شرط انقراض العصر في
السكوت؛ إذ من العوارض المذكورة ما يدوم إلى آخر العصر. أما من قال: هو
حجة، وإن لم يكن إجماعا، فهو
تحكم؛ لأنه قول بعض الأمة، والعصمة إنما تثبت للكل فقط. فإن قيل: نعلم
قطعا أن التابعين كانوا إذا أشكل عليهم مسألة فنقل إليهم مذهب بعض الصحابة
مع انتشاره وسكوت الباقين كانوا لا يجوزون العدول عنه، فهو إجماع منهم على
كونه حجة.
قلنا: هذا إجماع غير مسلم، بل لم يزل العلماء مختلفين في هذه المسألة،
ويعلم المحصلون أن السكوت متردد، وأن قول بعض الأمة لا حجة فيه.
chapters.anchors:
- Root: س ك ت (s-k-t)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Silence; abstention from speech; the state of one who refrains from utterance, whether by choice or impediment.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In uṣūl al-fiqh, silence (sukūt) is a non-assertive act; it carries no probative force unless conjoined with external indicators (qarāʾin) of assent.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) silence is mere absence of speech; metaphorical (majāz) silence-as-approval requires contextual evidence, else it remains ambiguous (mutaraddid).
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause with Implied Protasis (al-sharṭ al-muḍmar) — The phrase "if they remained silent" (fa-sakatū) functions as a conditional whose apodosis is inferred from the preceding ruling, demanding syntactic resolution of whether silence equals speech (ka-l-nuṭq) or remains a distinct, weaker category.
chapters.translation:
I say: A question arises: If some Companions issued a fatwa and the others remained silent, no consensus (ijmāʿ) is thereby established, nor is any statement attributed to the one who remained silent. Some scholars held: If the fatwa spread widely and they remained silent, their silence is tantamount to explicit speech, such that consensus is completed thereby. Another group stipulated the extinction of the entire generation (inqirāḍ al-ʿaṣr) as a condition for [counting] the silence. Another group said: It is a proof (ḥujjah) but not consensus. Another group said: It is neither a proof nor consensus, but it is an indication that they permitted independent reasoning (ijtihād) in the matter. The chosen position (al-mukhtār) is that it is neither consensus nor a proof, nor is it an indication of their permitting ijtihād in the matter — unless circumstantial indicators (qarāʾin al-aḥwāl) demonstrate that they remained silent while inwardly approving (muḍmirīn al-riḍā) and deeming it permissible to act upon it despite their silence.

The evidence for this is that a Companion's fatwa is only known through his explicit statement (qawl ṣarīḥ), which admits of no possibility of ambiguity or hesitation. But silence is ambiguous (mutaraddid), for one may remain silent without inwardly approving, due to seven causes:

First: He may have an internal impediment preventing him from voicing his objection, which we cannot perceive; yet indicators of his displeasure may appear despite his silence.

Second: He may remain silent because he deems the fatwa a permissible opinion (qawl sāʾigh) for the one whose ijtihād led him to it, even though he himself does not concur with it — rather, he believes it to be erroneous.

Third: He may hold that every mujtahid is correct (kull mujtahid muṣīb), and thus he sees no ground for rejecting ijtihād-based rulings at all; he regards responding [to the question] as merely a communal obligation (farḍ kifāyah). So when one who is correct has fulfilled it, he remains silent, even if it contradicts his own ijtihād.

Fourth: He may remain silent while disapproving, but he awaits an opportune moment for objection and does not deem haste beneficial due to some temporary obstacle whose removal he awaits; then he dies before that obstacle is removed, or he is distracted from it.

Fifth: He may know that if he objected, he would not be heeded and would suffer humiliation and contempt — as Ibn ʿAbbās said regarding his silence over not objecting to the doctrine of ʿawl during ʿUmar's lifetime: "He was a man of awe, and I stood in awe of him."

Sixth: He may remain silent because he is suspending judgment (mutawaqqif) on the matter, still being within the period of deliberation (muhlat al-naẓar).

Seventh: He may remain silent because he assumes that someone else has sufficed in objecting and spared him the need to voice it; but he may have erred in that assumption, thus abandoning objection due to a mistaken supposition — for he regarded objection as a communal obligation and thought it had been fulfilled, while he was wrong in his assumption.

If it is said: "Had there been disagreement, it would have become manifest" — we reply: And had there been agreement, it would likewise have become manifest. For if an obstacle preventing the manifestation of agreement is conceivable, the like of it is conceivable in preventing the manifestation of disagreement. By this, the position of al-Jubbāʾī is refuted, for he stipulated the extinction of the generation regarding silence; yet among the aforementioned obstacles are those that persist until the end of the generation.

As for the one who says it is a proof (ḥujjah) even if not consensus — this is arbitrary (taḥakkum), for it is merely the statement of some of the community (baʿḍ al-ummah), and infallibility (ʿiṣmah) is established only for the whole. If it is said: "We know with certainty that when the Followers (tābiʿūn) faced a difficult issue, and the doctrine of some Companion was transmitted to them with its wide circulation and the silence of the rest, they did not deem it permissible to deviate from it — so this is a consensus from them that it is a proof" — we reply: This consensus is not conceded. Rather, scholars have never ceased differing on this very question, and those who are rigorous (muḥaṣṣilūn) know that silence is ambiguous, and that the statement of some of the community carries no probative force.

chapters.title_en: On the Binding Nature of Consensus (Ijmāʿ) at the Moment of Agreement
chapters.arabic_text:
### | [مسألة إذا اتفقت كلمة الأمة ولو في لحظة انعقد الإجماع]

ووجبت عصمتهم عن الخطأ. وقال قوم: لا بد من انقراض العصر وموت الجميع.
وهذا فاسد؛ لأن الحجة في اتفاقهم لا في موتهم وقد حصل قبل الموت فلا
يزيده الموت تأكيدا، وحجة الإجماع الآية والخبر، وذلك لا يوجب اعتبار
العصر. فإن قيل: ما داموا في الأحياء فرجوعهم متوقع وفتواهم غير مستقرة.
قلنا: والكلام في رجوعهم فإنا لا نجوز الرجوع من جميعهم؛ إذ يكون أحد
الإجماعين خطأ وهو محال، أما بعضهم فلا يحل له الرجوع؛ لأنه برجوعه خالف
إجماع الأمة التي وجبت عصمتها عن الخطأ.
نعم يمكن أن يقع الرجوع من بعضهم ويكون به عاصيا فاسقا والمعصية تجوز على
بعض الأمة ولا تجوز على الجميع. فإن قيل: كيف يكون مخالفا للإجماع وبعد ما
تم الإجماع، وإنما يتم بانقراض العصر؟ قلنا: إن عنيتم به أنه لا يسمى
إجماعا فهو بهت على اللغة والعرف، وإن عنيتم أن حقيقته لم تتحقق فما حده؟
وما الإجماع إلا اتفاق فتاويهم، والاتفاق قد حصل وما بعد ذلك استدامة
للاتفاق لا إتمام للاتفاق.
ثم نقول: كيف يدعى ذلك ونحن نعلم أن التابعين في زمان بقاء أنس بن مالك
وأواخر الصحابة كانوا يحتجون بإجماع الصحابة ولم يكن جواز الاحتجاج
بالإجماع مؤقتا بموت آخر الصحابة؛ ولهذا قال بعضهم: يكفي موت الأكثر، وهو
تحكم آخر لا مستند له. ثم نقول: هذا يؤدي إلى تعذر الإجماع، فإنه إن بقي
واحد من الصحابة جاز للتابعي أن يخالف إذا لم يتم الإجماع وما دام واحد من
عصر التابعين أيضا لا يستقر الإجماع منهم فيجوز لتابعي الخلاف.
وهذا خبط لا أصل له. ولهم شبه.
الشبهة الأولى: قولهم: إنه ربما قال بعضهم ما قاله عن وهم وغلط فيتنبه
له، فكيف يحجر عليه في الرجوع عن الغلط؟ وكيف يؤمن ذلك باتفاق يجري في ساعة
واحدة؟ قلنا: وبأن يموت من أين يحصل أمان من غلطه؟ وهل يؤمن من الغلط إلا
دلالة النص على وجوب عصمة الأمة؟ وأما إذا رجع وقال: تبينت أني غلطت فنقول:
إنما يتوهم عليك الغلط إذا انفردت، وأما ما قلته في موافقة الأمة فلا يحتمل
الخطأ.
فإن قال: تحققت أني قلت: ما قلته دليل كذا، وقد انكشف لي خلافه قطعا،
فنقول: إنما أخطأت في الطريق لا في نفس المسألة، بل موافقة الأمة تدل على
أن الحكم حق، وإن كنت في طريق الاستدلال مخطئا.
الشبهة الثانية: أنهم ربما قالوا عن اجتهاد وظن، ولا حجر على المجتهد إذا
تغير اجتهاده أن يرجع، وإذا جاز الرجوع دل أن الإجماع لم يتم.
قلنا: لا حجر على المجتهد في الرجوع إذا انفرد باجتهاده، أما ما وافق فيه
اجتهاده اجتهاد الأمة فلا يجوز الخطأ فيه ويجب كونه حقا والرجوع عن الحق
ممنوع.
الشبهة الثالثة: أنه لو مات المخالف لم تصر المسألة إجماعا بموته
والباقون هم كل الأمة، لكنهم في بعض العصر، فلذلك لا يصير مذهب المخالف
مهجورا، فإن كان العصر لا يعتبر فليبطل مذهب المخالف.
قلنا: قال قوم: يبطل مذهبه ويصير مهجورا؛ لأن الباقين هم كل الأمة في ذلك
الوقت. وهو غير صحيح عندنا، بل الصحيح أنهم ليسوا كل الأمة بالإضافة إلى
تلك المسألة التي أفتى فيها الميت، فإن فتواه لا  ينقطع حكمها بموته. وليس
هذا للعصر فإنه جار في الصحابي الواحد إذا قال: قولا وأجمع التابعون في
جميع عصرهم على خلافه فقد بينا أنه لا يبطل مذهبه؛ لأنهم ليسوا كل الأمة
بالإضافة إلى هذه المسألة.
الشبهة الرابعة: ما روي عن علي - رضي الله عنه - أنه قال: " اجتمع رأيي
ورأي عمر على منع بيع أمهات الأولاد، وأنا الآن أرى بيعهن " فقال عبيدة
السلماني: رأيك في الجماعة أحب إلينا من رأيك في الفرقة. قلنا: لو صح إجماع
الصحابة قاطبة لما كان هذا يدل من مذهب علي على اشتراط انقراض العصر، ولو
ذهب إلى هذا صريحا لم يجب تقليده، كيف ولم يجتمع إلا رأيه ورأي عمر كما
قال؟ وأما قول عبيدة: رأيك في الجماعة، ما أراد به موافقة الجماعة إجماعا،
وإنما أراد به أن رأيك في زمان الألفة والجماعة والاتفاق والطاعة للإمام
أحب إلينا من رأيك في الفتنة والفرقة وتفرق الكلمة وتطرق التهمة إلى علي في
البراءة من الشيخين - رضي الله عنهما -، فلا حجة فيما ليس صريحا في نفسه.
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ع-ق-د (ʿ-q-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To tie, bind, contract; a firm knot — hence the technical sense of 'concluding' an agreement that is irrevocably bound.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The act of 'contracting' (inʿiqād) denotes the completion of a binding obligation, here the definitive establishment of communal authority.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for physical tying; metaphorical (majāz) for the 'binding' of a legal ruling — the metaphor is operative in the juristic claim.
- Root: ع-ص-م (ʿ-ṣ-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To protect, guard, preserve from harm; immunity from error.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Divine protection (ʿiṣmah) as a theological necessity for the community's infallibility in matters of religion.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for physical protection; metaphorical for the community's collective immunity from error — a transferred sense grounded in revelation.
- Root: ق-ر-ن (q-r-n)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To join, couple; a generation (qarn) as a period of time joined to another.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The 'era' (ʿaṣr) of the scholars — the temporal frame within which consensus is debated.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for temporal conjunction; metaphorical for the 'generation' of jurists — the term is used technically, not merely chronologically.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Exceptive Syntax (al-sharṭ wa-l-istithnāʾ) — The phrase "if the consensus of the ummah agrees, even for a moment" sets a minimal condition (sharṭ) that is fully satisfied by the occurrence of agreement, without requiring a subsequent temporal extension; the exceptive clause "even for a moment" (wa-law fī laḥẓah) emphasizes the sufficiency of the condition's fulfillment.
chapters.translation:
I say: If the word of the ummah agrees — even for a single moment — then consensus (ijmāʿ) is concluded, and their immunity from error becomes obligatory. But a group said: "The passing of the entire era and the death of all [the scholars] is indispensable." This is corrupt; for the proof lies in their agreement, not in their death. Agreement has already been attained before death, so death adds no further confirmation to it. The proof for consensus is the [Quranic] verse and the [Prophetic] report, and neither of these necessitates considering the era [as a condition].

If it is said: "As long as they remain among the living, their retraction is still anticipated, and their legal opinions are not yet settled." We reply: The discussion concerns their retraction — for we do not permit retraction from all of them, since then one of the two consensuses would be erroneous, which is impossible. As for some of them, it is not lawful for them to retract, because by retracting they would oppose the consensus of the ummah whose immunity from error is obligatory.

Indeed, retraction from some of them can occur, and by it they become disobedient and sinful. Disobedience is permissible for some of the ummah but not for all of it. If it is said: "How can one be an opponent of consensus before the consensus is completed — and it is only completed by the passing of the era?" We reply: If you mean that it is not called 'consensus,' then this is a slander against language and custom. If you mean that its reality has not been actualized, then what is its definition? Consensus is nothing other than the agreement of their legal opinions, and agreement has already occurred. What follows is merely the continuation of agreement, not the completion of agreement.

Then we say: How can this be claimed, when we know that the Followers (tābiʿūn), during the lifetime of Anas ibn Mālik and the last of the Companions, used to cite the consensus of the Companions as proof — and the permissibility of citing consensus was not conditioned upon the death of the last Companion? For this reason, some said: "The death of the majority suffices" — but this is another arbitrary ruling with no basis. Then we say: This leads to the impossibility of consensus. For if one Companion remained, it would be permissible for a Follower to dissent, since consensus would not be complete; and as long as one [scholar] of the Followers' era remained, their consensus would likewise not be settled, making dissent permissible for a later Follower. This is confused rambling with no foundation.

They have [several] specious arguments.

The first specious argument: Their claim that "perhaps one of them said what he said due to delusion and error, and then becomes alerted to it — so how can he be prevented from retracting from error? And how can one be secure from that in a consensus that occurs in a single hour?" We reply: And by dying, how does one obtain security from his error? Is one secure from error except by the textual indication (dalālah al-naṣṣ) of the obligatory immunity of the ummah? As for when he retracts and says, "I have realized that I erred," we say: Error is only attributed to you when you are alone [in your opinion]. As for what you said in agreement with the ummah, it does not admit of error.

If he says: "I have ascertained that what I said was based on such-and-such evidence, and the opposite has now been decisively revealed to me." We reply: You erred in the path [of reasoning], not in the very matter [of the ruling]. Rather, your agreement with the ummah indicates that the ruling is true, even if you were mistaken in your method of inference.

The second specious argument: That they perhaps spoke on the basis of independent reasoning (ijtihād) and conjecture (ẓann), and there is no restriction on the mujtahid to retract when his reasoning changes. And if retraction is permissible, this indicates that consensus was not completed. We reply: There is no restriction on the mujtahid in retracting when he is alone in his reasoning. As for that in which his reasoning agreed with the reasoning of the ummah, error in it is not permissible, and it must be true — and retracting from truth is prohibited.

The third specious argument: That if the dissenter died, the matter would not become consensus by his death, and the remaining [scholars] are the entire ummah — but they are [only] in part of the era. Therefore, the dissenter's doctrine does not become abandoned. If the era is not considered, then let the dissenter's doctrine be nullified. We reply: A group said: "His doctrine is nullified and becomes abandoned, because the remaining [scholars] are the entire ummah at that time." But this is not correct in our view. Rather, the correct [view] is that they are not the entire ummah with respect to that particular matter in which the deceased gave his legal opinion, for the effect of his legal opinion is not terminated by his death. This is not [a matter] of the era, for it applies likewise to a single Companion: if he stated an opinion and the Followers in their entire era agreed upon its opposite, we have already shown that his doctrine is not nullified — because they are not the entire ummah with respect to that particular matter.

The fourth specious argument: What was narrated from ʿAlī — may God be pleased with him — that he said: "My opinion and the opinion of ʿUmar agreed upon prohibiting the sale of ummahāt al-awlād (mothers of children), and now I see [the permissibility of] selling them." ʿUbaydah al-Salmānī said: "Your opinion in the community (jamāʿah) is dearer to us than your opinion in separation." We reply: Even if the consensus of all the Companions were established, this would not indicate from ʿAlī's doctrine the condition of the passing of the era. And even if he had explicitly held this [view], his emulation (taqlīd) would not be obligatory. How [could it be], when only his opinion and ʿUmar's opinion had agreed, as he himself said? As for ʿUbaydah's saying, "Your opinion in the community," he did not mean by it agreement with the community as consensus. Rather, he meant: "Your opinion in a time of harmony, community, concord, and obedience to the Imam is dearer to us than your opinion in [a time of] sedition, division, disunity of the word, and the opening of suspicion against ʿAlī regarding disavowal of the two Shaykhs — may God be pleased with them both." So there is no proof in what is not explicit in itself.

chapters.title_en: The Formation of Consensus (Ijmāʿ) Through Independent Reasoning (Ijtihād) and Analogy (Qiyās)
chapters.arabic_text:
### | [مسألة انعقاد الإجماع عن اجتهاد وقياس]

مسألة: يجوز انعقاد الإجماع عن اجتهاد وقياس ويكون حجة وقال قوم: الخلق
الكثير لا يتصور اتفاقهم في مظنة الظن ولو تصور لكان حجة، وإليه ذهب ابن
جرير الطبري وقال قوم: هو متصور وليس بحجة؛ لأن القول بالاجتهاد يفتح باب
الاجتهاد ولا يحرمه، والمختار أنه متصور وأنه حجة.
وقولهم: إن الخلق الكثير كيف يتفقون على حكم واحد في مظنة الظن؟ قلنا:
هذا إنما يستنكر فيما يتساوى فيه الاحتمال، وأما الظن الأغلب فيميل إليه كل
واحد، فأي بعد في أن يتفقوا على أن النبيذ في معنى الخمر في الإسكار فهو في
معناه في التحريم؟ كيف وأكثر الإجماعات مستندة إلى عمومات وظواهر وأخبار
آحاد صحت عند المحدثين، والاحتمال يتطرق إليها؟ كيف وقد أجمعوا على التوحيد
والنبوة وفيهما من الشبه ما هو أعظم جدبا لأكثر الطباع من الاحتمال الذي في
مقابلة الظن الأظهر؟ وقد أجمعت على إبطال النبوة مذاهب باطلة ليس لها  دليل
قطعي ولا ظني، فكيف لا يجوز الاتفاق على دليل ظاهر وظن غالب ويدل عليه جواز
الاتفاق عن اجتهاد لا بطريق القياس كالاتفاق على جزاء الصيد ومقدار أرش
الجناية وتقدير النفقة وعدالة الأئمة والقضاة وكل ذلك مظنون، وإن لم يكن
قياسا؟ ولهم شبه
الأولى: قولهم: كيف تتفق الأمة على اختلاف طباعها وتفاوت أفهامها في
الذكاء والبلادة على مظنون؟
قلنا: إنما يمتنع مثل هذا الاتفاق في زمان واحد وساعة معينة؛ لأنهم في
مهلة النظر قد يختلفون، أما في أزمنة متمادية فلا يبعد أن يسبق الأذكياء
إلى الدلالة الظاهرة ويقررون ذلك عند ذوي البلادة فيقبلونه منهم ويساعدون
عليه، وأهل هذا المذهب قد جوزوا الإجماع على نفي القياس وإبطاله مع ظهور
أدلة صحته، فكيف يمتنع الإجماع على هذا؟
الشبهة الثانية: قولهم: كيف تجتمع الأمة على قياس وأصل القياس مختلف فيه؟
قلنا: إنما يفرض ذلك من الصحابة وهم متفقون عليه والخلاف حدث بعدهم، وإن
فرض بعد حدوث الخلاف فيستند القائلون بالقياس إلى القياس والمنكرون له إلى
اجتهاد ظنوا أنه ليس بقياس، وهو على التحقيق قياس؛ إذ قد يتوهم غير العموم
عموما وغير الأمر أمرا وغير القياس قياسا، وكذا عكسه.
الشبهة الثالثة: قولهم: إن الخطأ في الاجتهاد جائز، فكيف تجتمع الأمة على
ما يجوز فيه الخطأ؟ وربما قالوا: الإجماع منعقد على جواز مخالفة المجتهد،
فلو انعقد الإجماع عن قياس لحرمت المخالفة التي هي جائزة بالإجماع ولتناقض
الإجماعان. قلنا: إنما يجوز الخطأ في اجتهاد ينفرد به الآحاد، أما اجتهاد
الأمة المعصومة فلا يحتمل الخطأ كاجتهاد رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم -
وقياسه فإنه لا يجوز خلافه لثبوت عصمته، فكذا عصمة الأمة من غير فرق.
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ع-ق-د (ʿ-q-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Binding, knotting, compacting; a firm covenant or contract that ties matters together.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The intellectual and legal act of sealing a collective determination, rendering it obligatory upon all.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for physical tying; metaphorical for the binding force of unanimous agreement.
- Root: ظ-ن (ẓ-n)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Doubt, suspicion, or predominant conjecture; the middle ground between certainty and ignorance.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The epistemic status of probable belief (ẓann) that governs legal reasoning where certainty is unattainable.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for suspicion; metaphorical for the prevailing inclination of the mind toward one of two possibilities.
- Root: ق-ي-س (q-y-s)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Measuring, comparing, estimating by a standard or model.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The analogical extension of a ruling from an original case (aṣl) to a subsidiary case (farʿ) based on shared effective cause (ʿillah).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for measuring with a rod; metaphorical for juridical analogy.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Exceptive Constructions (al-Sharṭ wa al-Istithnāʾ) — The text employs repeated conditional clauses (law, idhā) and exceptive phrases (illā) to delineate the boundaries of possibility and impossibility in consensus formation, requiring precise parsing of protasis and apodosis.
chapters.translation:
I say: A question arises: Is it permissible for consensus (ijmāʿ) to be established upon the basis of independent reasoning (ijtihād) and analogy (qiyās), and would such consensus constitute an authoritative proof (ḥujjah)?

Some have said: A vast multitude cannot be conceived to agree unanimously upon a matter that is merely a locus of conjecture (maẓinnah al-ẓann); and even if such agreement were conceivable, it would still be an authoritative proof. This is the position of Ibn Jarīr al-Ṭabarī.

Others have said: Such agreement is conceivable, yet it is not an authoritative proof — because the very act of ruling by independent reasoning opens the door to further independent reasoning and does not foreclose it.

The chosen position (al-mukhtār) is that such consensus is conceivable and that it is an authoritative proof.

As for their statement: "How can a vast multitude agree upon a single ruling in a locus of conjecture?" — I say: This objection is only tenable where the probabilities are perfectly balanced. But as for the predominant conjecture (al-ẓann al-aghlab), every individual naturally inclines toward it. So what improbability is there in their agreeing that date-wine (nabīdh) shares the meaning of wine (khamr) in its intoxicating effect, and therefore shares its meaning in prohibition? How [can this be denied] when most consensus-based rulings are grounded in general expressions (ʿumūmāt), apparent meanings (ẓawāhir), and solitary reports (āḥād) deemed authentic by traditionists — and yet possibility of error attaches to all of these?

How [can this be denied] when they have unanimously agreed upon the unity of God (tawḥīd) and prophethood (nubuwwah), despite the presence therein of ambiguities (shubah) that are far more alluring to most temperaments than the possibility that stands against the most manifest conjecture? And indeed, false sects have unanimously agreed upon the nullification of prophethood without possessing any decisive or even probable proof. So how can agreement upon a manifest proof and a predominant conjecture be deemed impermissible?

This is further indicated by the permissibility of agreement arising from independent reasoning without the path of analogy — such as their agreement upon the penalty for hunting [in the state of iḥrām], the amount of compensation for injury (arsh al-jināyah), the estimation of maintenance (nafaqah), and the probity (ʿadālah) of imams and judges. All of these are matters of conjecture, even though they are not analogical.

They have [however] two doubts:

The first doubt: Their statement: "How can the community — with its divergent temperaments and varying degrees of intelligence and dullness — agree upon a matter of conjecture?"

I say: Such agreement is only impossible within a single moment and a fixed hour, because during the period of deliberation they may differ. But over extended periods of time, it is not improbable that the intelligent ones would precede [others] to the manifest evidence, establish it before those of duller intellect, and the latter would accept it from them and concur with them upon it. Moreover, the proponents of this [opposing] school have themselves permitted consensus upon the negation of analogy and its invalidation, despite the manifest proofs of its soundness. So how can consensus upon this [i.e., analogy] be deemed impossible?

The second doubt: Their statement: "How can the community agree upon an analogy when the very foundation of analogy is itself disputed?"

I say: This is only to be conceived among the Companions (al-ṣaḥābah), who were unanimous upon it — the disagreement arose only after their time. And if it is conceived after the emergence of disagreement, then those who affirm analogy base themselves upon analogy, while those who deny it base themselves upon an independent reasoning which they supposed was not analogy — though in truth it is analogy. For one may mistakenly take a general expression for non-general, a command for non-command, and an analogy for non-analogy, and likewise the reverse.

The third doubt: Their statement: "Error in independent reasoning is permissible. So how can the community agree upon that in which error is possible?" And perhaps they say: "Consensus is itself established upon the permissibility of opposing the individual mujtahid. So if consensus were formed upon the basis of analogy, then opposition — which is permissible by consensus — would become forbidden, and the two consensuses would contradict one another."

I say: Error is only possible in an independent reasoning undertaken by isolated individuals. As for the independent reasoning of the infallible community (al-ummah al-maʿṣūmah), it does not admit of error — just as the independent reasoning and analogy of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) does not admit of opposition, due to the establishment of his infallibility (ʿiṣmah). So likewise is the infallibility of the community, with no difference between them.

chapters.title_en: The Third Chapter on the Ruling of Consensus (Ijmaʿ)
chapters.arabic_text:
### | [الباب الثالث في حكم الإجماع]

وحكمه وجوب الاتباع وتحريم المخالفة والامتناع عن كل ما ينسب الأمة إلى
تضييع الحق، والنظر فيما هو خرق ومخالفة وما ليس بمخالفة، يتهذب برسم
مسائل:
مسألة: إذا اجتمعت الأمة في المسألة على قولين،
كحكمهم مثلا في الجارية المشتراة إذا وطئها المشتري ثم وجد بها عيبا فقد
ذهب  بعضهم إلى أنها ترد مع العقر، وذهب بعضهم إلى منع الرد. فلو اتفقوا على
هذين المذهبين كان المصير إلى الرد مجانا خرقا للإجماع عند الجماهير إلا
عند شذوذ من أهل الظاهر والشافعي إنما ذهب إلى الرد مجانا؛ لأن الصحابة
بجملتهم لم يخوضوا في المسألة، وإنما نقل فيها مذهب بعضهم، فلو خاضوا فيها
بجملتهم واستقر رأي جميعهم على مذهبين لم يجز إحداث مذهب ثالث.
ودليله أنه يوجب نسبة الأمة إلى تضييع الحق إذ لا بد للمذهب الثالث من
دليل ولا بد من نسبة الأمة إلى تضييعه والغفلة عنه، وذلك محال. ولهم شبه:
الشبهة الأولى: قولهم: إنهم خاضوا خوض مجتهدين ولم يصرحوا بتحريم قول
ثالث. قلنا: وإذا اتفقوا على قول واحد عن اجتهاد فهو كذلك ولم يجز خلافهم؛
لأنه يوجب نسبتهم إلى تضييع الحق والغفلة عن دليله، فكذلك ههنا.
الشبهة الثانية: قولهم: إنه لو استدل الصحابة بدليل أو علة لجاز
الاستدلال بعلة أخرى؛ لأنهم لم يصرحوا ببطلانها، فكذلك القول الثالث لم
يصرحوا ببطلانه.
قلنا: فليجز خلافهم إذا اتفقوا عن اجتهاد إذ يجوز التعليل بعلة أخرى فيما
اتفقوا عليه. لكن الجواب أنه ليس من فرض دينهم الاطلاع على جميع الأدلة بل
يكفيهم معرفة الحق بدليل واحد، فليس في إحداث علة أخرى واستنباطها نسبة إلى
تضييع الحق وفي مخالفتهم في الحكم إذا اتفقوا نسبة إلى التضييع، فكذلك إذا
اختلفوا على قولين.
الشبهة الثالثة: أنه لو ذهب بعض الصحابة إلى أن اللمس والمس ينقضان
الوضوء، وبعضهم إلى أنهما لا ينقضان الوضوء ولم يفرق واحد بينهما، فقال
تابعي: ينقض أحدهما
دون الآخر، كان هذا جائزا، وإن كان قولا ثالثا.
قلنا: لأن حكمه في كل مسألة يوافق مذهب طائفة، وليس في المسألتين حكم
واحد، وليست التسوية مقصودة ولو قصدوها وقالوا: لا فرق واتفقوا عليه لم يجز
الفرق، وإذا فرقوا بين المسألتين واتفقوا على الفرق قصدا امتنع الجمع، أما
إذا لم يجمعوا ولم يفرقوا فلا يلتئم حكم واحد من مسألتين بل نقول صريحا: لا
يخلو إنسان عن معصية  وخطأ في مسألة، فالأمة مجتمعة على المعصية والخطأ؛ وكل
ذلك ليس بمحال إنما يستحيل الخطأ بحيث يضيع الحق حتى لا يقوم به طائفة مع
قوله - عليه السلام -: «لا تزال طائفة من أمتي على الحق» فلهذا نقول: يجوز
أن تنقسم الأمة في مسألتين إلى فرقتين وتخطئ فرقة في مسألة، والفرقة الأخرى
تقوم بالحق فيها والقائمون بالحق يخطئون في المسألة الأخرى، ويقوم بالحق
فيها المخطئون في المسألة الأولى، حتى يقول مثلا أحد شطري الأمة القياس ليس
بحجة والخوارج مبطلون، ويقول فريق آخر: القياس حجة والخوارج محقون، فيشملهم
الخطأ ولكن في مسألتين، فلا يكون الحق في مسألتين مضيعا بين الأمة في كل
واحد منهما.
الشبهة الرابعة: أن مسروقا أحدث في مسألة الحرام قولا ثالثا ولم ينكر
عليه منكر. قلنا: لم يثبت استقرار كافة الصحابة على رأيين في مسألة الحرام
بل ربما كان بعضهم فيها في مهلة النظر أو لم يخض فيها، أو لعل مسروقا خالف
الصحابة في ذلك الوقت ولم ينطق بوفاقهم وكان أهلا للاجتهاد في وقت وقوع هذه
المسألة، كيف ولم يصح هذا عن مسروق إلا بأخبار الآحاد؟ فلا يدفع بها ما
ذكرنا.

### | [مسألة انعقاد الإجماع بمخالفة واحد من الأمة أو اثنان]

مسألة إذا خالف واحد من الأمة أو اثنان لم ينعقد الإجماع دونه، فلو مات
لم تصر المسألة إجماعا خلافا لبعضهم. ودليلنا أن المحرم مخالفة الأمة كافة،
ومن ذهب إلى مذهب الميت بعد عصره لا يمكن أن يقال: مذهبه خلاف كافة الأمة؛
لأن الميت من الأمة لا ينقطع مذهبه بموته، ولذلك يقال: فلان وافق الشافعي
أو خالفه، وذلك بعد موت الشافعي. فمذهب الميت لا يصير مهجورا بموته ولو صار
مهجورا لصار مذهب الجميع كالمنعدم عند موتهم حتى يجوز لمن بعدهم أن
يخالفهم. فإن قيل: فلو مات في مهلة النظر وهو بعد متوقف فماذا تقولون فيه؟
قلنا: نقطع في طرفين واضحين أحدهما: أن يموت قبل الخوض في المسألة، وقبل أن
تعرض عليه فالباقون بعده كل الأمة، وإن خاض وأفتى فالباقون بعض الأمة،  وإن
مات في مهلة النظر فهذا محتمل فإنه كما لم يخالفهم لم يوافقهم أيضا، بل
المتوقف مخالف للجازم لكنه بصدد الموافقة، فهذه المسألة محتملة عندنا والله
أعلم. .
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ع-ق-د (ʿ-q-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To tie, bind, contract; a firm knotting of a thing.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Technical term for the binding agreement of the community (ijmāʿ) as a legal proof (ḥujjah).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for physical tying; metaphorical (majāz) for the firm establishment of a collective ruling.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause (al-Sharṭ) — The protasis (law) governs the apodosis (fa-jawāb), requiring careful parsing of hypothetical legal cases.
chapters.translation:
I say: Its ruling is the obligation of following it, the prohibition of opposing it, and the abstention from everything that would attribute to the community (al-ummah) the squandering of the truth. The examination of what constitutes a breach and opposition, and what does not constitute opposition, is refined through the delineation of certain questions:

**Question:** If the community agrees upon two positions in a single matter — as, for example, their ruling concerning a purchased slave-girl whom the buyer has had intercourse with and then discovers a defect in her: some of them held that she is to be returned along with the compensation for her usufruct (al-ʿaqr), while others held that her return is prohibited. If they were to agree upon these two schools of thought, then resorting to her return without compensation would be a breach of consensus (kharq al-ijmāʿ) according to the majority — except for an aberrant view among the Ẓāhirites. Al-Shāfiʿī only adopted the ruling of return without compensation because the Companions as a whole did not delve into the matter; rather, only the position of some of them was transmitted concerning it. But if they had delved into it collectively, and the settled opinion of all of them had rested upon two positions, it would not be permissible to originate a third position.

Its proof is that it would necessitate attributing to the community the squandering of the truth. For the third position inevitably requires a proof (dalīl), and it would be unavoidable to attribute to the community the squandering of that proof and negligence regarding it — and that is impossible. They have certain doubts:

**The First Doubt:** Their saying: "They delved into it as mujtahids, and they did not explicitly declare the prohibition of a third position." We say: If they agreed upon a single position through ijtihād, the case is likewise, and opposing them is not permitted — because it would necessitate attributing to them the squandering of the truth and negligence regarding its proof. So likewise here.

**The Second Doubt:** Their saying: "If the Companions had adduced a proof or a cause (ʿillah), it would be permissible to adduce another cause — because they did not explicitly declare its invalidity. So likewise, the third position — they did not explicitly declare its invalidity." We say: Then let opposing them be permissible when they agree through ijtihād, since it is permissible to reason by another cause in what they have agreed upon. But the answer is that it is not part of the obligation of their religion to be cognizant of all proofs; rather, it suffices them to know the truth through a single proof. Thus, in originating another cause and deriving it, there is no attribution of squandering the truth; but in opposing them in the ruling when they have agreed, there is an attribution of squandering. So likewise when they differ upon two positions.

**The Third Doubt:** That if some of the Companions held that touching (al-lams) and contact (al-mas) nullify ablution, and others held that they do not nullify ablution, and no one distinguished between the two — then a Tābiʿī said: "One of them nullifies without the other," this would be permissible, even though it is a third position. We say: Because his ruling in each matter agrees with the school of a group, and there is not a single ruling covering both matters, nor is the equation between them intended. And if they had intended it and said, "There is no difference," and agreed upon it, then making a distinction would not be permissible. And if they distinguished between the two matters and agreed upon the distinction intentionally, then combining them would be prohibited. But if they neither combined nor distinguished, then no single ruling is formed from two matters. Rather, we say plainly: No person is free from sin and error in some matter, so the community is collectively upon sin and error — and all of that is not impossible. Error is only impossible in the sense that the truth would be squandered such that no group upholds it, given his saying — peace be upon him: {«لا تزال طائفة من أمتي على الحق»} ("A group of my community will not cease to be upon the truth"). For this reason, we say: It is permissible for the community to divide into two factions over two matters, with one faction erring in one matter while the other faction upholds the truth in it; and those who uphold the truth err in the other matter, while those who erred in the first matter uphold the truth in it — such that, for example, one half of the community says: "Analogical reasoning (al-qiyās) is not a proof, and the Khawārij are invalid," while another group says: "Analogical reasoning is a proof, and the Khawārij are correct." Thus error encompasses them, but in two matters — so the truth is not squandered between the community in both matters, in each one of them.

**The Fourth Doubt:** That Masrūq originated a third position in the matter of the forbidden (al-ḥarām), and no one rebuked him for it. We say: It has not been established that all of the Companions settled upon two views in the matter of the forbidden. Rather, perhaps some of them were in a period of deliberation regarding it, or did not delve into it; or perhaps Masrūq opposed the Companions at that time without voicing agreement with them, and he was qualified for ijtihād at the time this matter occurred. Moreover, this has not been authentically transmitted from Masrūq except through isolated reports (āḥād) — so what we have mentioned is not refuted by them.

### [Question on the Formation of Consensus Despite the Opposition of One or Two of the Community]

**Question:** If one or two of the community oppose, consensus is not formed without them. If such a one dies, the matter does not become consensus — contrary to some. Our proof is that what is prohibited is opposing the community in its entirety. And one who adopts the school of the deceased after his era cannot be said to hold a position opposing the community in its entirety — because the deceased is part of the community, and his school is not severed by his death.
