There is a juristic consideration in this, which we have mentioned in the question of deviating to tayammum when time is constricted, and in the case of a group taking turns at a well of water. This is a probable question. And God knows best.

chapters.title_en: The Second Art: On Taqlīd, Seeking Legal Opinion (Iftāʾ), and the Ruling Concerning the Common Folk Therein — Issue: Taqlīd Is the Acceptance of a Statement Without Proof
chapters.arabic_text:
### | [الفن الثاني في التقليد والاستفتاء وحكم العوام فيه]

### | [مسألة التقليد هو قبول قول بلا حجة]
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ق-ل-د (q-l-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To adorn with a necklace (qilādah); to hang something around the neck — implying binding or fastening oneself to another’s authority.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In juristic usage, taqlīd is the acceptance of a legal ruling (fatwā) from a qualified scholar without demanding the underlying evidence (dalīl); it is a form of intellectual submission.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is physical adornment/encircling; metaphorical (majāz) sense is the binding of one’s judgment to another’s statement, as if placing it as a collar upon one’s own reasoning.
- Root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Speech, utterance, statement (qawl); the act of articulating a proposition.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In kalām, qawl is the verbal expression of a belief or ruling; here it denotes the transmitted legal opinion of a mujtahid.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — articulated speech; metaphorical — any authoritative assertion, including written or reported rulings.
- Root: ح-ج-ج (ḥ-j-j)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To argue, to prove; the pilgrimage (ḥajj) as a repeated intent toward a goal; a proof (ḥujjah) is that which establishes a claim.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In uṣūl al-fiqh, ḥujjah is the demonstrative evidence (dalīl) that renders a ruling certain or probable; its absence defines taqlīd.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — a decisive argument; metaphorical — any scriptural or rational indicator that compels assent.
- Sībawayh Rule: ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Clarification) — The phrase «هو قبول قول بلا حجة» is a nominal sentence (jumlah ismiyyah) where the predicate (khabar) is a verbal noun construction (masdar muʾawwal) functioning as a definition; the preposition «بلا» governs a genitive (majrūr) indicating negation of accompaniment, i.e., the absence of any evidential support.
chapters.translation: I say: The second art concerns taqlīd (following authority), seeking legal opinion (istiftāʾ), and the ruling pertaining to the common folk (al-ʿawāmm) therein. The issue is that taqlīd is the acceptance of a statement (qawl) without a proof (ḥujjah).

chapters.title_en: The Second Art of This Pole: On Taqlīd, Seeking Fatwā, and the Ruling Concerning the Common Folk — Containing Four Questions
chapters.arabic_text:
الفن الثاني من هذا القطب في التقليد والاستفتاء وحكم العوام فيه وفيه
أربع مسائل: مسألة: التقليد هو قبول قول بلا حجة.
وليس ذلك طريقا إلى العلم لا في الأصول ولا
في الفروع وذهب الحشوية والتعليمية إلى أن طريق معرفة الحق التقليد وأن
ذلك هو الواجب وأن النظر والبحث حرام. ويدل على بطلان مذهبهم مسالك، الأول:
هو أن صدق المقلد لا يعلم ضرورة فلا بد من دليل.
ودليل الصدق المعجزة فيعلم صدق الرسول - عليه السلام - بمعجزته وصدق كلام
الله بإخبار الرسول عن صدقه وصدق أهل الإجماع بإخبار الرسول عن عصمتهم ويجب
على القاضي الحكم بقول العدول لا بمعنى اعتقاد صدقهم لكن من حيث دل السمع
على تعبد القضاة باتباع غلبة الظن صدق الشاهد أم كذب، ويجب على العامي
اتباع المفتي؛ إذ دل الإجماع على أن فرض العوام اتباع ذلك كذب المفتي أم
صدق أخطأ أم أصاب. فنقول: قول المفتي والشاهد لزم بحجة الإجماع فهو قبول
قول بحجة فلم يكن تقليدا، فإنا نعني بالتقليد قبول قول بلا حجة فحيث لم تقم
حجة ولم يعلم الصدق بضرورة ولا بدليل فالاتباع فيه اعتماد على الجهل.
المسلك الثاني: أن نقول: أتحيلون الخطأ على مقلدكم أم تجوزونه؟ فإن
جوزتموه فإنكم شاكون في صحة مذهبكم، وإن أحلتموه فبم عرفتم استحالته بضرورة
أم بنظر أو تقليد، ولا ضرورة ولا دليل؟ فإن قلدتموه في قوله: إن مذهبه حق
فبم عرفتم صدقه في تصديق نفسه؟ وإن قلدتم فيه غيره فبم عرفتم صدق المقلد
الآخر؟  وإن عولتم على سكون النفس إلى قوله فبم تفرقون بين سكون نفوسكم
وسكون نفوس النصارى واليهود؟ وبم تفرقون بين قول مقلدكم: إني صادق محق وبين
قول مخالفكم؟ ويقال لهم أيضا في إيجاب التقليد: هل تعلمون وجوب التقليد أم
لا؟ فإن لم تعلموه فلم قلدتم وإن علمتم فبضرورة أم بنظر أو تقليد؟ ويعود
عليهم السؤال في التقليد، ولا سبيل لهم إلى النظر والدليل فلا يبقى إلا
إيجاب التقليد بالتحكم.
فإن قيل: عرفنا صحته بأنه مذهب للأكثرين فهو أولى بالاتباع. قلنا: وبم
أنكرتم على من يقول: الحق دقيق غامض لا يدركه إلا الأقلون ويعجز عنه
الأكثرون؛ لأنه يحتاج إلى شروط كثيرة من الممارسة والتفرغ للنظر ونفاذ
القريحة والخلو عن الشواغل. ويدل عليه أنه - عليه السلام - كان محقا في
ابتداء أمره وهو في شرذمة يسيرة على
خلاف الأكثرين، وقد قال تعالى: {وإن تطع أكثر من في الأرض يضلوك عن سبيل
الله} [الأنعام: 116] كيف وعدد الكفار في زماننا أكثر؟ ثم يلزمكم أن
تتوقفوا حتى تدوروا في جميع العالم وتعدوا جميع المخالفين، فإن ساووهم
توقفوا وإن غلبوا رجحوا، كيف وهو على خلاف نص القرآن؟ قال الله تعالى:
{وقليل من عبادي الشكور} [سبأ: 13] {ولكن أكثرهم لا يعلمون} [الأنعام: 37]
{وأكثرهم للحق كارهون} [المؤمنون: 70] فإن قيل: فقد قال - عليه السلام -:
«عليكم بالسواد الأعظم» ومن سره أن يسكن بحبوحة الجنة فليلزم الجماعة
«والشيطان مع الواحد وهو من الاثنين أبعد» قلنا: أولا، بم عرفتم صحة هذه
الأخبار وليست متواترة؟ فإن كان عن تقليد فبم تتميزون عن مقلد اعتقد
فسادها؟ ثم لو صح فمتبع السواد الأعظم ليس بمقلد بل علم بقول الرسول وجوب
اتباعه وذلك قبول قول بحجة وليس بتقليد.
ثم المراد بهذه الأخبار ذكرناه في كتاب " الإجماع " وأنه الخروج عن
موافقة الإمام أو موافقة الإجماع. ولهم شبه:
الشبهة الأولى: قولهم: إن الناظر متورط في شبهات
وقد كثر ضلال الناظرين فترك الخطر وطلب السلامة أولى.
قلنا: وقد كثر ضلال المقلدين من اليهود والنصارى فبم تفرقون بين تقليدكم
وتقليد سائر الكفار حيث  قالوا: إنا وجدنا آباءنا على أمة؟ ثم نقول: إذا
وجبت المعرفة كان التقليد جهلا وضلالا فكأنكم حملتم هذا خوفا من الوقوع في
الشبهة، كمن يقتل نفسه عطشا وجوعا خيفة من أن يغص بلقمة أو يشرق بشربة لو
أكل وشرب، وكالمريض يترك العلاج رأسا خوفا من أن يخطئ في العلاج، وكمن يترك
التجارة والحراثة خوفا من نزول صاعقة فيختار الفقر خوفا من الفقر.
الشبهة الثانية: تمسكهم بقوله تعالى: {ما يجادل في آيات الله إلا الذين
كفروا} [غافر: 4] وأنه نهى عن الجدال في القدر والنظر يفتح باب الجدال
قلنا: نهى عن الجدال بالباطل كما قال تعالى: {وجادلوا بالباطل ليدحضوا به
الحق} [غافر: 5] بدليل قوله تعالى: {وجادلهم بالتي هي أحسن} [النحل: 125]
فأما القدر فنهاهم عن الجدال فيه؛ إما لأنه كان قد وقفهم على الحق بالنص
فمنعهم عن المماراة في النص أو كان في بدء الإسلام فاحترز عن أن يسمعه
المخالف فيقول: هؤلاء بعد لم تستقر قدمهم في الدين أو لأنهم كانوا مدفوعين
إلى الجهاد الذي هو أهم عندهم.
ثم إنا نعارضهم بقوله تعالى: {ولا تقف ما ليس لك به علم} [الإسراء: 36]
{وأن تقولوا على الله ما لا تعلمون} [البقرة: 169] {قل هاتوا برهانكم}
[البقرة: 111] ، هذا كله نهي عن التقليد وأمر بالعلم، ولذلك عظم شأن
العلماء وقال تعالى: {يرفع الله الذين آمنوا منكم والذين أوتوا العلم
درجات} [المجادلة: 11] وقال - عليه السلام -: «يحمل هذا العلم من كل خلف
عدوله ينفون عنه تحريف الغالين وتأويل الجاهلين وانتحال المبطلين» ولا يحصل
هذا بالتقليد بل بالعلم وقال ابن مسعود: " لا تكونن إمعة " قيل: وما إمعة؟
قال: " أن يقول الرجل أنا مع الناس إن ضلوا ضللت وإن اهتدوا اهتديت، ألا لا
يوطنن أحدكم نفسه أن يكفر إن كفر الناس ".
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ق-ل-د (q-l-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To wind or twist something around the neck (like a garland); to adorn with a necklace; hence, to bind oneself to another's authority without independent verification.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Acceptance of a statement without proof (ḥujjah); the blind following of authority, contrasted with knowledge (ʿilm) attained via demonstration (naẓar) or necessity (ḍarūrah).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is physical garlanding; metaphorical sense is the binding of the intellect to another's assertion, stripping it of its own evidential warrant.
- Root: ف-ت-ي (f-t-y)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The act of clarifying or resolving a matter; issuing a legal opinion (fatwā) that resolves ambiguity for the questioner.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The muftī's pronouncement is a definitive answer (jawāb) that the layperson (ʿāmmī) is obligated to follow, as established by consensus (ijmāʿ).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: to make something evident; metaphorical: the jurist's extraction of a ruling from the sources, which the layperson receives as binding.
- Root: ح-ش-و (ḥ-sh-w)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To stuff or fill; the Ḥashwiyyah are those who "stuff" their doctrine with uncritical acceptance of transmitted reports without rational scrutiny.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): A pejorative designation for anthropomorphists and literalists who reject rational inquiry (naẓar) in favor of sheer adherence to authority.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: filling a cushion; metaphorical: filling the mind with unexamined dogma, devoid of demonstrative content.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Disjunctive Syntax (al-sharṭ wa al-taqsīm) — The text employs intricate conditional clauses (in... fa...) and disjunctive alternatives (am... am...) to force the opponent into an inescapable dilemma, a hallmark of Ghazālī's dialectical method.
chapters.translation:
I say: The second art of this pole concerns taqlīd (blind following), seeking fatwā (legal opinion), and the ruling concerning the common folk therein. It comprises four questions.

**Question One:** Taqlīd is the acceptance of a statement without proof (ḥujjah). This is not a path to knowledge—neither in the fundamentals (uṣūl) nor in the branches (furūʿ). The Ḥashwiyyah and the Taʿlīmiyyah (Bāṭiniyyah) held that the path to knowing the truth is taqlīd, that it is obligatory, and that rational inquiry (naẓar) and investigation (baḥth) are forbidden. Several proofs demonstrate the falsity of their doctrine.

**The First Proof:** The veracity of the one followed (muqallad) is not known by necessity (ḍarūrah); therefore, a proof (dalīl) is indispensable. The proof of veracity is the miracle (muʿjizah): thus, the veracity of the Messenger (peace be upon him) is known through his miracle; the veracity of God's speech is known through the Messenger's report of his own truthfulness; and the veracity of the people of consensus (ahl al-ijmāʿ) is known through the Messenger's report of their infallibility (ʿiṣmah). The judge is obligated to rule by the testimony of upright witnesses (ʿudūl)—not in the sense of believing their truthfulness, but because the revealed law (samʿ) indicates that judges are bound to follow predominant conjecture (ghalabat al-ẓann) as to whether the witness is truthful or lying. Likewise, the layperson is obligated to follow the muftī, for consensus indicates that the duty of the common folk is to follow him—whether the muftī is truthful or lying, correct or mistaken. We say: The statement of the muftī and the witness is binding by virtue of the proof of consensus; thus, it is an acceptance of a statement with a proof, and hence it is not taqlīd. For we mean by taqlīd the acceptance of a statement without proof. Wherever no proof is established and truth is known neither by necessity nor by demonstration, following therein is reliance upon ignorance.

**The Second Proof:** We say: Do you deem error (khaṭaʾ) impossible for your muqallad, or do you deem it possible? If you deem it possible, then you are in doubt concerning the soundness of your doctrine. If you deem it impossible, then how did you come to know this impossibility—by necessity, by rational inquiry, or by taqlīd? There is no necessity and no proof. If you follow him in his statement that his doctrine is true, then how did you come to know his veracity in his self-attestation? If you follow another in his regard, then how did you come to know the veracity of that other muqallad? If you rely upon the tranquility of the soul (sukūn al-nafs) toward his statement, then how do you distinguish between the tranquility of your souls and the tranquility of the souls of the Christians and Jews? How do you distinguish between the statement of your muqallad—"I am truthful and correct"—and the statement of your opponent? It is also said to them concerning the obligation of taqlīd: Do you know the obligation of taqlīd or not? If you do not know it, then why did you follow? If you know it, then is it by necessity, by rational inquiry, or by taqlīd? The question returns upon them regarding taqlīd, and they have no recourse to rational inquiry or proof; nothing remains except the imposition of taqlīd by sheer arbitrariness (taḥakkum).

If it is said: "We came to know its soundness by the fact that it is the doctrine of the majority, and the majority is more worthy of being followed." We say: Then how do you object to one who says: "The truth is subtle and obscure, grasped only by the few, and the majority are incapable of it, for it requires numerous conditions—practice, leisure for inquiry, penetrating intellect, and freedom from distractions"? This is supported by the fact that the Prophet (peace be upon him) was upon the truth at the beginning of his mission while he was among a small band, contrary to the majority. God the Exalted has said: {«And if you obey most of those upon the earth, they will mislead you from the way of Allah»} [al-Anʿām 6:116]. How then, when the number of disbelievers in our time is greater? Moreover, you would be compelled to pause until you traverse the entire world and count all the opponents—if they equal you, you pause; if they outnumber you, you incline to them. How can this be, when it contradicts the explicit text of the Qurʾān? God the Exalted said: {«And few of My servants are grateful»} [Sabaʾ 34:13], {«But most of them do not know»} [al-Anʿām 6:37], and {«And most of them are averse to the truth»} [al-Muʾminūn 23:70].

If it is said: "The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: «Upon you is the great majority (al-sawād al-aʿẓam)», and 'Whoever is pleased to dwell in the midst of Paradise, let him adhere to the congregation (jamāʿah), for the devil is with the solitary one, and he is farther from two.'" We say: First, how did you come to know the soundness of these reports, given that they are not transmitted via tawātur (mass transmission)? If it is by taqlīd, then how are you distinguished from one who follows and deems them corrupt? Then, even if they were sound, the follower of the great majority is not a muqallid; rather, he knows by the Prophet's statement the obligation of following it—and that is an acceptance of a statement with a proof, not taqlīd. Moreover, the intended meaning of these reports we have mentioned in the book "Al-Ijmāʿ": that it is the avoidance of opposing the Imam or opposing the consensus.

**Their Doubts:**

**The First Doubt:** Their statement: "The rational inquirer is entangled in ambiguities (shubuhāt), and the misguidance of inquirers has multiplied. Thus, abandoning the risk and seeking safety is more appropriate." We say: The misguidance of the blind followers among the Jews and Christians has also multiplied. How do you distinguish between your taqlīd and the taqlīd of the rest of the disbelievers, who said: "Indeed, we found our fathers upon a religion"? Then we say: When knowledge (maʿrifah) is obligatory, taqlīd is ignorance and misguidance. It is as if you have adopted this out of fear of falling into ambiguity—like one who kills himself with thirst and hunger out of fear of choking on a morsel or being strangled by a sip were he to eat and drink; like the sick man who abandons treatment altogether out of fear of erring in the treatment; and like one who abandons trade and agriculture out of fear of a lightning strike, choosing poverty out of fear of poverty.

**The Second Doubt:** Their appeal to the statement of God the Exalted: {«None dispute concerning the signs of Allah except those who disbelieve»} [Ghāfir 40:4], claiming that it prohibits disputation (jadal) regarding destiny (qadar), and that rational inquiry opens the door to disputation. We say: He prohibited disputation with falsehood, as God the Exalted said: {«And they disputed with falsehood to refute thereby the truth»} [Ghāfir 40:5], as evidenced by His statement: {«And dispute with them in the way that is best»} [al-Naḥl 16:125]. As for destiny, He prohibited them from disputing therein—either because He had already apprised them of the truth by explicit text (naṣṣ), thus preventing them from wrangling over the text; or because it was at the beginning of Islam, and He guarded against the opponent hearing them and saying: "These people have not yet established their feet in religion"; or because they were driven toward jihad, which was more important to them at that time.

Then we counter them with the statement of God the Exalted: {«And do not pursue that of which you have no knowledge»} [al-Isrāʾ 17:36], {«And that you say concerning Allah what you do not know»} [al-Baqarah 2:169], and {«Say: Bring forth your proof»} [al-Baqarah 2:111]. All of this is a prohibition of taqlīd and a command to knowledge. For this reason, God magnified the station of the scholars, saying: {«Allah will raise those who have believed among you and those who have been given knowledge, by degrees»} [al-Mujādilah 58:11]. And the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: «The upright among every generation will bear this knowledge, warding off from it the distortion of the extremists, the false interpretations of the ignorant, and the claims of the falsifiers.» This is not attained by taqlīd, but by knowledge. Ibn Masʿūd said: "Do not be an immaʿah." It was said: "What is an immaʿah?" He said: "That a man says: 'I am with the people—if they go astray, I go astray; and if they are guided, I am guided.' Indeed, let none of you habituate his soul to disbelieve if the people disbelieve."

chapters.title_en: The Layperson Must Seek Legal Verdicts (Fatwā) and Follow the Scholars
chapters.arabic_text:
### | [مسالة العامي يجب عليه الاستفتاء واتباع العلماء]

وقال قوم من القدرية: يلزمهم النظر في الدليل واتباع الإمام المعصوم وهذا
باطل بمسلكين:
أحدهما: إجماع الصحابة فإنهم كانوا يفتون العوام ولا يأمرونهم بنيل درجة
الاجتهاد، وذلك معلوم على الضرورة والتواتر من علمائهم وعوامهم.  فإن قال
قائل من الإمامية: كان الواجب عليهم اتباع علي لعصمته وكان علي لا ينكر
عليهم تقية وخوفا من الفتنة. قلنا: هذا كلام جاهل سد على نفسه باب الاعتماد
على قول علي وغيره من الأئمة في حال ولايته إلى آخر عمره؛ لأنه لم يزل في
اضطراب من أمره، فلعل جميع ما قاله خالف فيه الحق خوفا وتقية
المسلك الثاني: أن الإجماع منعقد على أن العامي مكلف بالأحكام، وتكليفه
طلب رتبة الاجتهاد محال؛ لأنه يؤدي إلى أن ينقطع الحرث والنسل وتتعطل الحرف
والصنائع ويؤدي إلى خراب الدنيا لو اشتغل الناس بجملتهم بطلب العلم، وذلك
يرد العلماء إلى طلب المعايش ويؤدي إلى اندراس العلم بل إلى إهلاك العلماء
وخراب العالم، وإذا استحال هذا لم يبق إلا سؤال العلماء.
فإن قيل: فقد أبطلتم التقليد وهذا عين التقليد. قلنا: التقليد قبول قول
بلا حجة وهؤلاء وجب عليهم ما أفتى به المفتي بدليل الإجماع، كما وجب على
الحاكم قبول الشهود
ووجب علينا قبول خبر الواحد؛ وذلك عند ظن الصدق والظن معلوم ووجوب الحكم
عند الظن معلوم بدليل سمعي قاطع فهذا الحكم قاطع، والتقليد جهل.
فإن قيل: فقد رفعتم التقليد من الدين، وقد قال الشافعي - رحمه الله -:
ولا يحل تقليد أحد سوى النبي - عليه السلام - فقد أثبت تقليدا. قلنا: قد
صرح بإبطال التقليد رأسا إلا ما استثنى فظهر أنه لم يجعل الاستفتاء وقبول
خبر الواحد وشهادة العدول تقليدا، نعم، يجوز تسمية قبول قول الرسول تقليدا
وتوسعا واستثناؤه من غير جنسه ووجه التجوز أن قبول قوله وإن كان لحجة دلت
على صدقه جملة فلا تطلب منه حجة على غير تلك المسألة فكأنه تصديق بغير حجة
خاصة ويجوز أن يسمى ذلك تقليدا مجازا.

### | [مسألة لا يستفتي العامي إلا من عرفه بالعلم والعدالة]

أما من عرفه بالجهل فلا يسأله وفاقا، وإن سأل من لا يعرف جهله فقد قال
قوم: يجوز وليس عليه البحث؛ وهذا فاسد؛ لأن كل من وجب عليه قبول قول غيره
فيلزمه معرفة حاله فيجب على الأمة  معرفة حال الرسول بالنظر في معجزته فلا
يؤمن بكل مجهول يدعي أنه رسول الله ووجب على الحاكم معرفة حال الشاهد في
العدالة والمفتي معرفة حال الراوي وعلى الرعية معرفة حال الإمام والحاكم.
وعلى الجملة كيف يسأل من يتصور أن يكون أجهل من السائل؟ فإن قيل: إذا لم
يعرف عدالة المفتي هل يلزمه البحث؟ إن قلتم يلزمه البحث فقد خالفتم العادة؛
لأن من دخل بلدة فيسأل عالم البلدة ولا يطلب حجة على عدالته، وإن جوزتم مع
الجهل فكذلك في العلم. قلنا: من عرفه بالفسق فلا يسأله ومن عرفه بالعدالة
فيسأله، ومن لم يعرف فيحتمل أن يقال: لا يهجم بل يسأل عن عدالته أولا فإنه
لا يأمن كذبه وتلبيسه، ويحتمل أن يقال: ظاهر حال العالم العدالة لا سيما
إذا اشتهر بالفتوى، ولا يمكن أن يقال: ظاهر حال الخلق العلم ونيل درجة
الفتوى والجهل أغلب على الخلق فالناس كلهم عوام إلا الأفراد بل العلماء
كلهم عدول إلا الآحاد.
فإن قيل: فإن وجب السؤال لمعرفة عدالته أو علمه فيفتقر إلى التواتر أم لا
يفتقر إليه؟ قيل: يحتمل أن يقال: فإن ذلك ممكن. ويحتمل أن يقال: يكفي غالب
الظن الحاصل بقول عدل أو عدلين، وقد جوز قوم العمل بإجماع نقله العدل
الواحد وهذا يقرب من وجه
chapters.anchors:
- Root: س-أ-ل (sa-ʾa-la)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To ask, inquire, request; the act of seeking information or a ruling from one who possesses knowledge.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal theology, istiftāʾ (seeking a fatwā) is the layperson's obligation to defer to the qualified jurist, rooted in the Quranic command {«فَاسْأَلُوا أَهْلَ الذِّكْرِ»} (Ask the people of remembrance).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for direct questioning; metaphorical (majāz) when extended to the heart's inquiry after certainty.
- Root: ق-ل-د (qalada)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To adorn, to wind a necklace around the neck; to imitate blindly.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Taqlīd is accepting a statement without proof (ḥujjah); in Kalām, it is the antithesis of ijtihād and naẓar (rational inquiry).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for physical adornment; metaphorical for the mind's submission to authority without evidence.
- Root: ع-ص-م (ʿaṣama)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To protect, guard, preserve; ʿiṣmah is divine protection from error.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Technical term for prophetic and Imāmī infallibility; al-Ghazālī here refutes its extension to the Imāms as a basis for lay obligation.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for physical protection; metaphorical for moral and doctrinal immunity.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause with Law (Law + māḍī for protasis, māḍī for apodosis) — Used in "فإن قيل" (if it is said) to introduce hypothetical objections, a standard dialectical device in uṣūl al-fiqh.
chapters.translation:
I say: A group of the Qadariyyah (deniers of divine decree) claimed: The layperson is obligated to engage in rational inquiry into the evidence (naẓar fī al-dalīl) and to follow the infallible Imām. This is false by two lines of argument:

The first: The consensus (ijmāʿ) of the Companions, for they used to issue legal verdicts (fatwā) to the common folk and did not command them to attain the rank of ijtihād (independent juristic reasoning). This is known by necessity (ḍarūrah) and by mass transmission (tawātur) from both their scholars and their laymen. If a proponent of the Imāmiyyah (Shīʿah) says: "They were obligated to follow ʿAlī due to his infallibility (ʿiṣmah), and ʿAlī did not rebuke them out of dissimulation (taqiyyah) and fear of discord (fitnah)" — we reply: This is the speech of an ignoramus who has closed upon himself the door of relying upon the statements of ʿAlī and other Imāms during his caliphate until the end of his life; for he never ceased to be in turmoil regarding his affair. Perhaps everything he said in that period contradicted the truth out of fear and dissimulation.

The second line of argument: Consensus is established that the layperson is legally obligated (mukallaf) by the rulings (aḥkām), yet obligating him to seek the rank of ijtihād is impossible (muḥāl); for it would lead to the cessation of cultivation (ḥarth) and progeny (nasl), the suspension of crafts (ḥiraf) and industries (ṣanāʾiʿ), and would lead to the ruin of the world (kharāb al-dunyā) if all people busied themselves with seeking knowledge. This would drive the scholars to seek livelihoods (maʿāyish) and lead to the extinction of knowledge (indirās al-ʿilm), indeed to the destruction of the scholars and the ruin of the world. Since this is impossible, nothing remains except asking the scholars (suʾāl al-ʿulamāʾ).

If it is said: "You have nullified taqlīd (blind following), yet this is precisely taqlīd" — we reply: Taqlīd is the acceptance of a statement without proof (ḥujjah). These people (the laypersons) are obligated to follow what the muftī (jurisconsult) issues as a verdict by virtue of the evidence of consensus, just as the judge (ḥākim) is obligated to accept the testimony of witnesses (shuhūd), and we are obligated to accept the solitary report (khabar al-wāḥid). This is so when there is a presumption of truthfulness (ẓann al-ṣidq), and the presumption is known (maʿlūm), and the obligation of judgment upon presumption is known by a definitive scriptural proof (dalīl samʿī qāṭiʿ). Thus this ruling is definitive (qāṭiʿ), whereas taqlīd is ignorance (jahl).

If it is said: "You have removed taqlīd from religion, yet al-Shāfiʿī — may God have mercy on him — said: 'It is not permissible to follow anyone except the Prophet — peace be upon him —' thus he affirmed a form of taqlīd" — we reply: He explicitly declared the nullification of taqlīd entirely (raʾsan), except what he exempted. Thus it became clear that he did not consider seeking verdicts (istiftāʾ), accepting the solitary report, and the testimony of upright witnesses (shahādat al-ʿudūl) to be taqlīd. Yes, it is permissible to call the acceptance of the Prophet's statement "taqlīd" by way of linguistic expansion (tawassuʿ), and to exempt it from its genus (jins). The aspect of the metaphorical extension (majāz) is that accepting his statement — even though it is based on evidence that indicates his truthfulness in general (jimlah) — does not require seeking from him a proof for that particular issue. Thus it is as if it were an affirmation without a specific proof, and it is permissible to call that taqlīd metaphorically.

### | [Issue: The Layperson Should Only Seek a Verdict from One Known for Knowledge and Uprightness]

As for one known to be ignorant, he should not be asked, by agreement (wifāqan). If one asks someone whose ignorance is not known, some have said: It is permissible, and he is not obligated to investigate (baḥth). This is corrupt (fāsid); for everyone obligated to accept the statement of another must know his condition (ḥāl). Thus the community (ummah) is obligated to know the condition of the Messenger through examining his miracle (muʿjizah) — one does not believe every unknown claimant who says "I am the Messenger of God." The judge is obligated to know the condition of the witness regarding uprightness (ʿadālah), the muftī is obligated to know the condition of the narrator (rāwī), and the subjects (raʿiyyah) are obligated to know the condition of the Imām and the ruler.

In sum: How can one ask someone who may conceivably be more ignorant than the questioner himself? If it is said: "If one does not know the uprightness of the muftī, is he obligated to investigate? If you say he must investigate, you have contradicted common practice (ʿādah); for one who enters a town asks the town's scholar and does not seek proof of his uprightness. And if you permit [asking] despite ignorance of his uprightness, then likewise regarding his knowledge" — we reply: One known for wickedness (fisq) should not be asked; one known for uprightness should be asked. As for one whose condition is unknown, it may be said: He should not rush in, but rather inquire first about his uprightness, for he is not safe from his lying and dissimulation (talbīs). And it may also be said: The apparent condition (ẓāhir al-ḥāl) of a scholar is uprightness, especially if he is renowned for issuing verdicts. But it cannot be said: The apparent condition of people is knowledge and attaining the rank of fatwā, for ignorance is more prevalent among people — all people are laypersons except the few (āfād). Rather, all scholars are upright except the rare individuals (āḥād).

If it is said: "If inquiry is obligatory to ascertain his uprightness or knowledge, does it require tawātur (mass transmission) or not?" — It is said: It may be said that this is possible. And it may be said: The predominant presumption (ghālib al-ẓann) obtained from the statement of one upright person or two is sufficient. Some have permitted acting upon a consensus (ijmāʿ) transmitted by a single upright narrator, and this approximates that view.

### | [مسألة مراجعة العامى للمفتى]

مسألة إذا لم يكن في البلدة إلا مفت واحد وجب على العامي مراجعته.
وإن كانوا جماعة فله أن يسأل من شاء ولا يلزمه مراجعة الأعلم كما فعل في
زمان الصحابة إذ سأل العوام الفاضل والمفضول ولم يحجر على الخلق في سؤال
غير أبي بكر وعمر وغير الخلفاء. وقال قوم: تجب مراجعة الأفضل، فإن استووا
تخير بينهم. وهذا يخالف إجماع الصحابة إذ لم يحجر الفاضل على المفضول
الفتوى بل لا تجب إلا مراجعة من عرفه بالعلم والعدالة وقد عرف كلهم بذلك.
نعم، إذا اختلف عليه مفتيان في حكم فإن تساويا راجعهما مرة أخرى وقال
تناقض فتواكما تساويتما عندي، فما الذي يلزمني؟ فإن خيراه تخير وإن اتفقا
على الأمر بالاحتياط أو الميل إلى جانب معين فعل وإن أصرا على الخلاف لم
يبق إلا التخيير فإنه لا سبيل إلى تعطيل الحكم وليس أحدهما بأولى من الآخر
والأئمة كالنجوم فبأيهم اقتدى
اهتدى، أما إذا كان أحدهما أفضل وأعلم في اعتقاده اختار القاضي أنه يتخير
أيضا؛ لأن المفضول أيضا من أهل الاجتهاد لو انفرد فكذلك إذا كان معه غيره
فزيادة الفضل لا تؤثر
والأولى عندي أنه يلزمه اتباع الأفضل، فمن اعتقد أن الشافعي - رحمه الله
- أعلم والصواب على مذهبه أغلب فليس له أن يأخذ بمذهب مخالفه بالتشهي وليس
للعامي أن ينتقي من المذاهب في كل مسألة أطيبها عنده فيتوسع بل هذا الترجيح
عنده كترجيح الدليلين المتعارضين عند المفتي فإنه يتبع ظنه في الترجيح،
فكذلك ههنا، وإن صوبنا كل مجتهد ولكن الخطأ ممكن بالغفلة عن دليل قاطع
وبالحكم قبل تمام الاجتهاد واستفراغ الوسع، والغلط على الأعلم أبعد لا
محالة
وهذا التحقيق وهو أنا نعتقد أن لله تعالى سرا في رد العباد إلى ظنونهم
حتى لا يكونوا مهملين متبعين للهوى مسترسلين استرسال البهائم من غير أن
يزمهم لجام التكليف فيردهم من جانب إلى جانب فيتذكرون العبودية ونفاذ حكم
الله تعالى فيهم في كل حركة وسكون يمنعهم من جانب إلى جانب، فما دمنا نقدر
على ضبطهم بضابط فذلك أولى من تخييرهم وإهمالهم كالبهائم والصبيان، أما إذا
عجزنا عند تعارض مفتيين وتساويهما أو عند تعارض دليلين فذلك ضرورة.
والدليل عليه أنه إذا كان يمكن أن يقال: كل مسألة ليس لله تعالى فيها حكم
معين أو يصوب فيها كل مجتهد فلا يجب على المجتهد فيها النظر بل يتخير فيفعل
ما شاء، إذ ما من جانب إلا ويجوز أن يغلب على ظن مجتهد، والإجماع منعقد على
أنه يلزمه أولا تحصيل الظن ثم يتبع ما ظنه؛ فكذلك ظن العامي ينبغي أن يؤثر.
فإن قيل: المجتهد لا يجوز له أن يتبع ظنه قبل أن يتعلم طرق الاستدلال،
والعامي يحكم بالوهم ويغتر بالظواهر وربما يقدم المفضول على الفاضل، فإن
جاز أن يحكم بغير بصيرة فلينظر في نفس المسألة وليحكم بما يظنه فلمعرفة
مراتب الفضل أدلة غامضة ليس دركها من شأن العوام.
وهذا سؤال واقع، ولكنا نقول: من مرض له طفل وهو ليس بطبيب فسقاه دواء
برأيه كان متعديا مقصرا ضامنا، ولو راجع طبيبا لم يكن مقصرا؛ فإن كان في
البلد طبيبان فاختلفا في الدواء فخالف الأفضل عد مقصرا، ويعلم فضل الطبيبين
بتواتر الأخبار وبإذعان المفضول له وبتقديمه بأمارات تفيد غلبة الظن، فكذلك
في حق العلماء يعلم الأفضل بالتسامع وبالقرائن دون البحث عن نفس العلم،
والعامي أهل له فلا ينبغي أن يخالف الظن بالتشهي. فهذا هو الأصح عندنا
والأليق بالمعنى الكلي في ضبط الخلق بلجام التقوى والتكليف والله أعلم.

### | [الفن الثالث في الترجيح وكيفية تصرف المجتهد عند تعارض الأدلة]

### | [المقدمة الأولى في بيان ترتيب الأدلة]

الفن الثالث من القطب الرابع
في الترجيح وكيفية تصرف المجتهد عند تعارض الأدلة ويشتمل هذا الفن على
مقدمات ثلاث وبابين
أما المقدمة الأولى ففي بيان ترتيب الأدلة.
فنقول: يجب على المجتهد في كل مسألة أن يرد نظره إلى النفي الأصلي قبل
ورود الشرع ثم يبحث عن الأدلة السمعية المغيرة فينظر أول شيء في الإجماع
فإن وجد في المسألة إجماعا ترك النظر في الكتاب والسنة
فإنهما يقبلان النسخ، والإجماع يقبله، فالإجماع على خلاف ما في الكتاب
والسنة دليل قاطع على النسخ إذ لا تجتمع الأمة على الخطإ. ثم ينظر في
الكتاب والسنة المتواترة على رتبة واحدة؛ لأن كل واحد يفيد العلم القاطع
ولا يتصور التعارض في القطعيات السمعية إلا بأن يكون أحدهما ناسخا، فما وجد
فيه نص كتاب أو سنة متواترة أخذ به، وينظر بعد ذلك إلى عمومات الكتاب
وظواهره، ثم ينظر في مخصصات العموم من أخبار الآحاد ومن الأقيسة فإن عارض
قياس عموما أو خبر واحد عموما فقد ذكرنا ما يجب تقديمه منها، فإن لم يجد
لفظا نصا ولا ظاهرا نظر إلى قياس النصوص، فإن تعارض قياسان أو خبران أو
عمومان طلب الترجيح كما سنذكره،  فإن تساويا عنده توقف على رأي وتخير على
رأي آخر كما سبق.

**Section 227**

**On the Layperson's Recurse to the Mufti**

I say: If there is only one mufti in a town, it is obligatory upon the layperson (ʿāmmī) to recurse to him. If there are many, he may ask whomever he wishes, and he is not obliged to recurse to the most learned (al-aʿlam)—just as was done in the era of the Companions, when the common folk asked both the virtuous and the less virtuous, and no restriction was placed upon the people against asking other than Abū Bakr and ʿUmar, nor against the other caliphs. Some said: "It is obligatory to recurse to the most excellent (al-afḍal); if they are equal, he chooses among them." But this contradicts the consensus (ijmāʿ) of the Companions, for the virtuous did not prohibit the less virtuous from giving fatwā. Rather, nothing is obligatory except recursing to one known for knowledge and probity (ʿadālah), and all of them were known for that.

Yes—if two muftis differ for him regarding a ruling, then if they are equal [in his estimation], he should recurse to them once more and say: "Your two fatwās contradict each other, and you are equal in my view—so what is incumbent upon me?" If they give him the choice, he chooses; if they agree upon commanding caution (al-iḥtiyāṭ) or inclining to a particular side, he does so. But if they persist in disagreement, nothing remains except choice (takhyīr), for there is no way to nullify the ruling, and neither of them is more deserving than the other. The imams are like the stars—whichever of them one follows, one is guided. However, if one of them is more excellent and more learned in his belief, the judge (al-qāḍī) held that he chooses as well, because the less virtuous is also among the people of ijtihād if he were alone—so likewise when another is with him, the excess of merit has no effect.

But the more correct view in my judgment is that he is obliged to follow the more excellent. For whoever believes that al-Shāfiʿī—may God have mercy on him—is more learned and that correctness is more prevalent in his school, it is not permissible for him to adopt the school of his opponent out of caprice (bi-al-tashahhī). Nor is it for the layperson to pick and choose from the schools in every matter whatever seems most agreeable to him, thereby becoming lax. Rather, this weighing (tarjīḥ) for him is like the weighing of two conflicting evidences (dalīlayn) for the mufti—for the mufti follows his conjecture (ẓann) in weighing, and so likewise here. Even if we deem every mujtahid correct, error is still possible through heedlessness of a decisive proof (dalīl qāṭiʿ) and through judging before completing ijtihād and exhausting one's capacity (istifrāgh al-wusʿ). And error is, without doubt, more remote from the more learned.

This is the verification (taḥqīq): we hold that God—exalted is He—has a secret in returning His servants to their conjectures, so that they are not neglected, nor followers of whim, nor let loose like the letting loose of beasts (istirsāl al-bahāʾim), without the bridle of obligation (lijām al-taklīf) restraining them and turning them from side to side—so that they may remember servitude (al-ʿubūdiyyah) and the execution of God's command over them in every movement and stillness, which prevents them from side to side. Thus, as long as we are able to restrain them with a restraint, that is more appropriate than giving them choice and abandoning them like beasts and children. But when we are incapable—at the conflict of two muftis and their equality, or at the conflict of two evidences—that is a necessity (ḍarūrah).

The proof of this is that if it were possible to say: "In every matter God has no specific ruling, or every mujtahid is correct therein," then the mujtahid would not be obliged to investigate but would choose and do as he pleases—since there is no side but that it is possible for a mujtahid's conjecture to incline toward it. Yet consensus is established that he must first acquire conjecture (taḥṣīl al-ẓann), then follow what he conjectures. So likewise, the layperson's conjecture ought to be given effect.

If it is said: "The mujtahid is not permitted to follow his conjecture before learning the methods of inference (ṭuruq al-istidlāl), whereas the layperson judges by fancy (wahm) and is deceived by outward appearances (ẓawāhir), and perhaps he may prefer the less virtuous over the virtuous. If it is permissible for him to judge without insight (baṣīrah), then let him look into the matter itself and judge by what he conjectures—for knowing the ranks of merit has obscure proofs, the grasp of which is not within the capacity of the common folk."

This is a real objection. But we say: Whoever has a sick child, and he is not a physician, and he gives him medicine by his own opinion—he is a transgressor, negligent, and liable (ḍāmin). Had he consulted a physician, he would not be negligent. If there are two physicians in the town and they differ over the medicine, and he contradicts the more excellent, he is counted negligent. And the merit of the two physicians is known through recurrent reports (tawātur al-akhbār), through the less virtuous one's acknowledgment of the other, and through his precedence by indications (amārāt) that yield preponderant conjecture. So likewise regarding the scholars: the more learned is known through common report (tasāmuʿ) and through circumstantial evidence (qarāʾin), without investigating the science itself. And the layperson is capable of that—so he ought not to contradict conjecture out of caprice. This is the most sound view with us, and the most fitting to the universal principle of restraining creation with the bridle of piety (taqwā) and obligation. And God knows best.

---

**The Third Art: On Weighing (al-Tarjīḥ) and How the Mujtahid Acts When Evidences Conflict**

**First Introduction: On the Ordering of Evidences**

The third art of the fourth pole (al-quṭb al-rābiʿ) concerns weighing and how the mujtahid acts when evidences conflict. This art comprises three introductions and two chapters.

As for the first introduction, it concerns the ordering of evidences (tartīb al-adillah).

I say: It is obligatory upon the mujtahid in every matter to first direct his consideration to the original negation (al-nafy al-aṣlī) before the advent of the Sacred Law, then to search for the revealed evidences (al-adillah al-samʿiyyah) that alter it. He looks first at consensus (ijmāʿ): if he finds consensus on the matter, he abandons examination of the Book and the Sunnah—for both are subject to abrogation (naskh), whereas consensus is not. Thus, consensus contrary to what is in the Book and the Sunnah is a decisive proof of abrogation, since the community does not unite upon error. Then he looks at the Book and the mutawātir Sunnah on a single rank—for each yields decisive knowledge (al-ʿilm al-qāṭiʿ), and conflict among decisive revealed matters is inconceivable except by one being an abrogator. Whatever he finds as an explicit text (naṣṣ) of the Book or mutawātir Sunnah, he adopts it. Then he looks at the generalities (ʿumūmāt) of the Book and its apparent meanings (ẓawāhir). Then he looks at the particularizers (mukhaṣṣiṣāt) of the general—from solitary reports (akhbār al-āḥād) and from analogies (aqyisah). If an analogy conflicts with a general, or a solitary report with a general, we have already mentioned what must be given precedence among them. If he finds neither an explicit text nor an apparent meaning, he looks to the analogy of the texts (qiyās al-nuṣūṣ). If two analogies conflict, or two reports, or two generalities, he seeks weighing (tarjīḥ) as we shall mention. If they are equal in his view, he suspends judgment on one opinion, and chooses on another, as has preceded.

### | [المقدمة الثانية في حقيقة تعارض الأدلة ومحله]

المقدمة الثانية في حقيقة التعارض ومحله.
اعلم أن الترجيح إنما يجري بين ظنين؛ لأن الظنون تتفاوت في القوة، ولا
يتصور ذلك في معلومين إذ ليس بعض العلوم أقوى وأغلب من بعض وإن كان بعضها
أجلى وأقرب حصولا وأشد استغناء عن التأمل، بل بعضها يستغني عن أصل التأمل
وهو البديهي وبعضها غير بديهي يحتاج إلى تأمل لكنه بعد الحصول محقق يقيني
لا يتفاوت في كونه محققا فلا ترجيح لعلم على علم؛ ولذلك قلنا: إذا تعارض
نصان قاطعان فلا سبيل إلى الترجيح، بل إن كانا متواترين حكم بأن المتأخر
ناسخ ولا بد أن يكون أحدهما ناسخا، وإن كانا من أخبار الآحاد وعرفنا
التاريخ أيضا حكمنا بالمتأخر، وإن لم نعرف فصدق الراوي مظنون فنقدم الأقوى
في نفوسنا.
وكما لا يجوز التعارض والترجيح بين نصين قاطعين فكذلك في علتين قاطعتين،
فلا يجوز أن ينصب الله علة قاطعة للتحريم في موضع، وعلة قاطعة للتحليل في
موضع، وتدور بينهما مسألة توجد فيها العلتان، ونتعبد بالقياس؛ لأنه يؤدي
إلى أن يجتمع قاطع على التحريم وقاطع على التحليل في فرع واحد في حق مجتهد
واحد، وهو محال لا كالعلل المظنونة؛ لأن الظنون تختلف بالإضافات فلا تجتمع
في حق مجتهد واحد فإن تقاوم ظنان أوجبنا التوقف على رأي كما لو تعارض
قاطعان
ومن أمر بالتخيير أجاب بأنه لا يجوز أن يرد نصان قاطعان بالتحريم
والتحليل من غير تقدم وتأخر، ويكون معناه التخيير؛ لأن اللفظ لا يحتمل
التخيير، فكذلك التعبد بالقياس مع التصريح بالتعليل تصريح بالنفي، والإثبات
لا يحتمل التخيير من حيث اللفظ فيكون متناقضا. أما الدليل الذي دل على تعبد
المجتهد باتباع الظن فيصلح لأن ينزل على اتباع أغلب الظنين وعند التعارض
على التخيير بينهما، فإنه أمر باتباع المصلحة وبالتشبيه وبالاستصحاب فإذا
تعارضا فكيفما فعل فهو مستصحب ومشبه ومتبع للمصلحة.
أما القواطع فمتضادة ومتناقضة لا بد من أن تكون ناسخا  ومنسوخا فلا تقبل
الجمع، نعم لو أشكل التاريخ وعجزنا عن طلب دليل آخر فلا بد أن يتخير إذ ليس
أحدهما بأولى من الآخر مع تضادهما. فإن قيل: فهل يجوز أن يجتمع علم وظن؟
قلنا: لا فإن الظن لو خالف العلم فهو محال؛ لأن ما علم كيف يظن خلافه؟ وظن
خلافه شك، فكيف يشك فيما يعلم وإن وافقه؟ فإن أثر الظن بالكلية بالعلم فلا
يؤثر معه.

### | [المقدمة الثالثة في دليل وجوب الترجيح]

فإن قال قائل: لم رجحتم أحد الظنين وكل
ظن لو انفرد بنفسه لوجب اتباعه؟ وهلا قضيتم بالتخيير أو التوقف قلنا: كان
يجوز أن يرد التعبد بالتسوية بين الظنين وإن تفاوتا، لكن الإجماع قد دل على
خلافه على ما علم من السلف في تقديم بعض الأخبار على بعض لقوة الظن بسبب
علم الرواة وكثرتهم وعدالتهم وعلو منصبهم؛
فلذلك قدموا خبر أزواجه - عليه السلام - على غيرهن من النساء وقدموا خبر
عائشة - رضي الله عنها - في التقاء الختانين على خبر من روى «لا ماء إلا من
الماء» وخبر من روت من أزواجه أنه كان يصبح جنبا على ما روى أبو هريرة عن
الفضل بن عباس: أن «من أصبح جنبا فلا صوم له» وكما قوى علي خبر أبي بكر فلم
يحلفه وحلف غيره وقوى أبو بكر خبر المغيرة في ميراث الجدة لما روى معه محمد
بن مسلمة، وقوى عمر خبر أبي موسى الأشعري في الاستئذان بموافقة أبي سعيد
الخدري في الرواية، إلى غير ذلك مما يكثر تتبعه.
وكذلك إذا غلب على الظن كون الفرع أشبه بأحد الأصلين وجب اتباعه بالإجماع
فقد فهم من أهل الإجماع أنهم تعبدوا بما هو عادة للناس في حراثتهم وتجارتهم
وسلوكهم الطرق المخوفة، فإنهم عند تعارض الأسباب المخوفة يرجحون ويميلون
إلى الأقوى. فإن قيل: فلم لم ترجحوا في الشهادة بالكثرة وقوة غلبة الظن بل
يقضى بالتعارض عند تناقض البينتين؟ قلنا: لأن أهل الإجماع لم يرجحوا في
الشهادة وقد رجحوا في الرواية، وسببه أن باب الشهادة مبني على التعبد حتى
لو أتى عشرة بلفظ الإخبار دون الشهادة لم تقبل ولا تقبل شهادة مائة امرأة
ولا مائة عبد على باقة بقل. هذه هي المقدمات.

### | [الباب الأول فيما ترجح به الأخبار]

- Root: ظ-ن-ن (Ẓ-N-N)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Conjecture, doubt, or a prevailing but uncertain opinion; the opposite of certainty (yaqīn).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In uṣūl al-fiqh, ẓann denotes a probabilistic preponderance that obligates action in legal reasoning (ijtihād), distinct from ʿilm (certain knowledge).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is "suspicion"; metaphorically extended to juristic presumption (ghalabat al-ẓann) as a technical epistemic category.
- Root: ر-ج-ح (R-J-Ḥ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To weigh, outweigh, or prefer one thing over another due to superior weight or merit.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Tarjīḥ is the act of preferring one evidence (dalīl) over another when both are probabilistic, based on intrinsic strength.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: physical heaviness in scales; metaphorical: epistemic preponderance in legal reasoning.
- Root: ق-ط-ع (Q-Ṭ-ʿ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To cut off, sever; hence definitive, decisive, leaving no room for doubt.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Qaṭʿī denotes apodictic certainty in textual evidence (naṣṣ qāṭiʿ) or legal cause (ʿillah qāṭiʿah), immune to contradiction.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: cutting; metaphorical: conclusive proof that severs all contrary possibility.
- Root: ن-س-خ (N-S-Kh)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To abrogate, supersede, or transfer; in legal theory, the repeal of a prior ruling by a later revelation.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Naskh is the divine legislative act of replacing a ḥukm with a temporally subsequent one, recognized only when chronology is established.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: copying/erasing; metaphorical: juristic abrogation of one textual ruling by another.

### | [The Second Introduction: On the Reality of Contradiction (Taʿāruḍ) and Its Locus]

The second introduction concerns the reality of contradiction and its locus. Know that preponderance (tarjīḥ) only occurs between two conjectural probabilities (ẓannayn), for conjectures vary in strength. But this is inconceivable regarding two certainties (maʿlūmayn), since no one item of knowledge is stronger or more dominant than another—even if some are more evident, more readily attained, and more independent of reflection. Indeed, some knowledge is independent of reflection altogether, namely the self-evident (badīhī), while some is non-self-evident and requires reflection, yet once attained it is verified and certain (yaqīnī), not varying in its being verified. Hence, there is no preponderance of one knowledge over another. For this reason, we say: when two definitive texts (naṣṣān qāṭiʿān) contradict, there is no recourse to preponderance. Rather, if both are mass-transmitted (mutawātir), we rule that the later one is abrogating (nāsikh), and necessarily one of them must be the abrogator. If they are solitary reports (āḥād) and we know the chronology, we likewise rule by the later one. But if we do not know the chronology, then the veracity of the transmitter is merely conjectural, so we give precedence to the stronger in our estimation.

Just as contradiction and preponderance are impermissible between two definitive texts, so too between two definitive legal causes (ʿillatayn qāṭiʿatayn). Thus, God cannot establish a definitive cause for prohibition in one place and a definitive cause for permissibility in another, with a case arising between them in which both causes are present, while we are obligated to apply analogical reasoning (qiyās). For that would lead to a definitive proof of prohibition and a definitive proof of permissibility converging on a single branch-case (farʿ) for a single jurist (mujtahid)—which is impossible. This is unlike conjectural causes, for conjectures differ by relation (bi-al-iḍāfāt) and thus do not converge for a single jurist. If two conjectures are evenly balanced, we are obligated to suspend judgment (tawaqquf), just as when two certainties contradict.

Whoever commands choice (takhayyur) would answer: it is impermissible that two definitive texts be revealed—one prohibiting and one permitting—without temporal precedence or posteriority, with their meaning being choice; for the wording cannot bear the sense of choice. Likewise, being obligated to apply qiyās alongside an explicit statement of the legal cause (taʿlīl) is an explicit affirmation of negation and affirmation that cannot bear choice from the standpoint of wording, thus rendering it contradictory. As for the evidence that obligates the jurist to follow conjecture, it is apt to be interpreted as following the stronger of the two conjectures, and upon contradiction, as choosing between them. For it commands following the public interest (maṣlaḥah), analogy (tashbīh), and presumption of continuity (istisḥāb). When these conflict, whatever he does, he is still practicing istisḥāb, tashbīh, and following the maṣlaḥah.

As for the definitive proofs (qawāṭiʿ), they are mutually opposed and contradictory; necessarily one must be abrogator and the other abrogated, so they admit no reconciliation. Indeed, if the chronology is obscure and we are unable to seek another evidence, then choice is unavoidable, since neither is more worthy than the other despite their opposition. If it is said: "Is it permissible for knowledge (ʿilm) and conjecture (ẓann) to coexist?" We say: No. For if conjecture opposes knowledge, it is impossible—how can one conjecture the contrary of what one knows? Conjecturing its contrary is doubt (shakk), so how can one doubt what one knows? And if it agrees with knowledge, then the effect of conjecture is entirely nullified by knowledge; it has no effect alongside it.

---

### | [The Third Introduction: On the Evidence for the Obligation of Preponderance]

If someone says: "Why do you give preponderance to one of the two conjectures, when each conjecture, if taken alone, would obligate following it? Why do you not rule by choice (takhayyur) or suspension (tawaqquf)?" We say: It would have been permissible for the Lawgiver to obligate treating the two conjectures equally even if they differ in strength. But consensus (ijmāʿ) has indicated otherwise, as is known from the early generations (salaf) in preferring some reports over others due to the strength of conjecture arising from the knowledge of the transmitters, their number, their probity (ʿadālah), and the loftiness of their rank.

Thus, they preferred the reports of the Prophet's wives—peace be upon him—over other women. They preferred the report of ʿĀʾishah—may God be pleased with her—regarding the meeting of the two circumcisions (iltiqāʾ al-khitānayn) over the report of one who narrated «no water except from water» (lā māʾ illā min al-māʾ). And they preferred the report of one of his wives that he would wake up in a state of major ritual impurity (junub) over what Abū Hurayrah narrated from al-Faḍl ibn ʿAbbās: that «whoever wakes up junub, there is no fasting for him» (man aṣbaḥa junuban fa-lā ṣawma lahu). Likewise, ʿAlī gave preponderance to the report of Abū Bakr and thus did not administer an oath to him, while he administered it to others. Abū Bakr gave preponderance to the report of al-Mughīrah regarding the inheritance of the grandmother (mirāth al-jaddah) when Muḥammad ibn Maslamah corroborated it. ʿUmar gave preponderance to the report of Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī regarding seeking permission (al-istīʾdhān) due to the corroboration of Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī in the narration. And there are many more such instances that would require lengthy pursuit.

Likewise, when conjecture prevails that a branch-case is more analogous to one of the two root-cases (aṣlayn), following it is obligatory by consensus. For it is understood from the people of consensus (ahl al-ijmāʿ) that they were obligated by what is customary for people in their plowing, their commerce, and their traversing of dangerous roads—for when conflicting fearful causes arise, they give preponderance and incline toward the stronger.

If it is said: "Why do you not give preponderance in testimony (shahādah) by number and strength of prevailing conjecture, but rather rule by contradiction when two evidences (bayyināt) conflict?" We say: Because the people of consensus did not give preponderance in testimony, yet they did in narration (riwāyah). The reason is that the domain of testimony is built upon strict adherence (taʿabbud), such that even if ten people came with the wording of mere report (ikhbār) rather than testimony, it would not be accepted. Nor is the testimony of a hundred women or a hundred slaves accepted regarding a single bunch of greens. These are the introductions.

---

### | [Book One: On What Renders Reports Preponderant]

chapters.title_en: On the Reconciliation of Conflicting Evidences and the Preponderating Factors (Tarjīḥ) in Reports
chapters.arabic_text:
اعلم أن التعارض هو التناقض، فإن كان في خبرين فأحدهما كذب والكذب محال
على الله ورسوله، وإن كان في حكمين من أمر ونهي وحظر وإباحة فالجمع تكليف
محال فإما أن يكون أحدهما كذبا أو يكون متأخرا ناسخا، وإمكان الجمع بينهما
بالتنزيل على حالتين كما إذا قال: الصلاة واجبة على أمتي الصلاة غير واجبة
على أمتي؛ فنقول: أراد بالأول المكلفين وأراد بالثاني الصبيان والمجانين أو
في حالتي العجز والقدرة أو في زمن دون زمن. وإن عجزنا عن الجمع وعن معرفة
المتقدم والمتأخر رجحنا وأخذنا بالأقوى.
وتقوي الخبر في نفوسنا بصدق الراوي وصحته، وتضعيف الخبر في نفوسنا إما
باضطراب في متنه أو بضعف في سنده أو بأمر خارج من السند والمتن؛ أما ما
يتعلق بالسند والمتن فسبعة عشر:
الأول سلامة متن أحد الخبرين عن الاختلاف والاضطراب دون الآخر فسلامته
مرجحة فإن ما لا يضطرب فهو بقول الرسول أشبه، فإن انضاف إلى اضطراب اللفظ
اضطراب المعنى كان أبعد عن أن يكون قول الرسول فيدل على الضعف وتساهل
الراوي في الرواية. فإن قيل: فيجب أن تكون رواية الزيادة في متن الحديث
اضطرابا يوجب اطراحه.
قلنا: لا يجب؛ لأنه في معنى خبرين منفصلين إلا أن يعرف محدث بكثرة
الانفراد بالرواية عن الحفاظ فيجوز أن يقدم خبر غيره على خبره.
الثاني اضطراب السند بأن يكون في أحدهما ذكر رجال تلتبس أسماؤهم ونعوتهم
وصفاتهم بأسماء قوم ضعفاء وصفاتهم بحيث يعسر التمييز.
الثالث أن يروي أحدهما في تضاعيف قصة مشهورة متداولة بين أهل النقل
ومعارضه قد
انفرد به الراوي لا في جملة القصة، فما روى في الجماعة أقوى في النفوس
وأقرب إلى السلامة من الغلط مما يرويه الواحد عاريا عن قصته المشهورة.
الرابع أن يكون راويه معروفا بزيادة التيقظ وقلة الغلط، فالثقة بروايته
عند الناس أشد.
الخامس: أن يقول  أحدهما سمعنا النبي - عليه السلام - والآخر أن يقول كتب
إلي بكذا، فإن التحريف والتصحيف في المكتوب أكثر منه في المسموع.
السادس: أن يتطرق الخلاف إلى أحد الخبرين أنه موقوف على الراوي أو مرفوع،
فالمتفق على كونه مرفوعا أولى.
السابع: أن يكون منسوبا إليه نصا وقولا والآخر ينسب إليه اجتهادا بأن
يروى أنه كان في زمانه أو في مجلسه ولم ينكره، فما نسب إليه قولا ونصا
أقوى؛ لأن النص غير محتمل وما في زمانه ربما لم يبلغه وما في مجلسه ربما
غفل عنه.
الثامن: أن يروى أحد الخبرين عمن تعارضت الرواية عنه فنقل عنه أيضا ضده
فيقدم عليه ما لم يتعارض؛ لأن المتعارض متساقط فيبقى الآخر سليما عن
المعارضة.
التاسع: أن يكون الراوي صاحب الواقعة فهو أولى بالمعرفة من الأجنبي،
فرواية ميمونة «تزوجني النبي - عليه السلام - ونحن حلالان بعد ما رجع»
مقدمة على رواية ابن عباس «أنه نكحها وهو حرام»
العاشر: أن يكون أحد الراويين أعدل وأوثق وأضبط وأشد تيقظا وأكثر تحريا.
الحادي عشر: أن يكون أحدهما على وفق عمل أهل المدينة فهو أقوى؛ لأن ما
رآه مالك - رحمه الله - حجة وإجماعا إن لم يصلح حجة فيصلح للترجيح؛ لأن
المدينة دار الهجرة ومهبط الوحي الناسخ فيبعد أن ينطوي عليهم.
الثاني عشر: أن يوافق أحد الخبرين مرسل غيره فيرجح به من يرجح بكثرة
الرواة؛ لأن المرسل حجة عند قوم فإن لم يكن حجة فلا أقل من أن يكون مرجحا.
الثالث عشر: أن تعمل الأمة بموجب أحد الخبرين، فإنه إذا احتمل أن يكون
عملهم بدليل آخر فيحتمل أن يكون هذا الخبر فيكون صدقه أقوى في النفس
الرابع عشر: أن يشهد القرآن أو الإجماع أو النص المتواتر أو دليل العقل
لوجوب العمل على وفق الخبر فيرجح به.
فإن قيل: ذلك قاطع في تصديقه. قلنا: لا، بل يتصور أن يكذب على النبي -
عليه السلام - فيما يوافق القرآن والإجماع فيقول: سمعت ما لم يسمعه، وإنما
يجب صدقه إذا اجتمعت الأمة على صدقه لا إذا اجتمعت على  عمل يوافق خبره
ولعله عن دليل آخر.
الخامس عشر: أن يكون أحدهما أخص والآخر أعم فيقدم ما هو أخص بالمقصود،
كتقديم قوله: «في الرقة ربع العشر» في إيجابه على الطفل والبالغ على قوله:
«رفع القلم عن ثلاثة» لأن هذا تعرض لنفي الخطاب العام وليس بتعرض للزكاة
ولا لسقوط الزكاة عن الولي بإخراج زكاته، والحديث الأول متعرض لخصوص الزكاة
ومتناول لعمومه مال الصبي فهو أخص وأمس بالمقصود.
السادس عشر: أن يكون أحدهما مستقلا بالإفادة ومعارضه لا يفيد إلا بتقدير
إضمار أو حذف وذلك مما يتطرق إليه زيادة التباس لا يتطرق إلى المستقل.
السابع عشر أن يكون رواة أحد الخبرين أكثر فالكثرة تقوي الظن ولكن رب عدل
أقوى في النفس من عدلين لشدة تيقظه وضبطه، والاعتماد في ذلك على ما غلب على
ظن المجتهد. هذا ما يوجب الترجيح لأمر في سند الخبر أو في متنه؛ وقد يرجح
لأمور خارجة عنها وهي خمسة:
الأول: كيفية استعمال الخبر في محل الخبر كقوله: «لا نكاح إلا بولي» مع
قوله: «الأيم أحق بنفسها من وليها» لأنا نحمل ذلك على أنها أحق بنفسها في
الإذن لا في العقد، واللفظ يعم الإذن والعقد وهم يحملون خبرنا على الصغيرة
أو الأمة أو النكاح من غير كفء، والخلاف واقع في الكبيرة وهم صرفوا خبرنا
عن محل الخلاف ونحن استعملنا الخبرين في الكبيرة، فتأويلنا أقرب فإنه لا
ينبو عنه اللفظ بل كان اللفظ محتملا لهما، أما تنزيل خبرنا على الصغيرة
والأمة فبعيد.
الثاني: أن يكون أحد الخبرين يوجب غضا من منصب الصحابة فيكون أضعف، كما
رووا من أمر النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - الصحابة بإعادة الوضوء عند
القهقهة، فخبرنا وهو قوله: «كان يأمرنا إذا كنا مسافرين أن لا ننزع خفافنا
إلا من جنابة لا من بول أو غائط أو نوم» وليس فيه القهقهة، فهو أولى من
خبرهم.
الثالث: أن يكون أحد الخبرين متنازعا في خصوصه، والآخر متفق على تطرق
الخصوص إليه فقد قال قوم: إنه يسقط الاحتجاج به فإن لم يصح  ذلك فيدل على
ضعفه لا محالة.
الرابع: أن يكون أحد الخبرين قد قصد به بيان الحكم المتنازع فيه دون
الآخر كقوله: «أيما إهاب دبغ فقد طهر» لم يفرق فيه بين ما يؤكل وبين ما لا
يؤكل، فدلالة عمومه على جلد ما لا يؤكل أقوى من دلالة نهيه عن افتراش جلود
السباع؛ لأنه ما سيق لبيان النجاسة والطهارة بل ربما نهى عن الافتراش
للخيلاء أو لخاصية لا نعقلها.
الخامس: أن يتضمن أحد الخبرين إثبات ما ظهر تأثيره في الحكم دون الآخر
حتى تقدم رواية عائشة وابن عمر وابن عباس أن بريرة أعتقت تحت عبد على ما
روي أنها أعتقت تحت حر؛ لأن ضرورة الرق في الخيار قد ظهر أثره ولا يجري ذلك
في الحر
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ع-ر-ض (ʿ-r-ḍ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To present, oppose, or confront; the core sense is mutual exposure and encounter.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In uṣūl, taʿāruḍ denotes the apparent contradiction between two evidences that cannot both be true in their literal import.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) in the context of legal indicants; metaphorical (majāz) when used for mere apparent opposition that may be reconciled.
- Root: ر-ج-ح (r-j-ḥ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To outweigh, to be preponderant; the heavier side of a scale.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Tarjīḥ is the juristic preference of one evidence over another based on a preponderating factor that strengthens probability (ẓann).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Used literally for physical weight; metaphorically for epistemic strength in the mind of the mujtahid.
- Root: ن-س-خ (n-s-kh)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To erase, abrogate, or supersede; the removal of a prior ruling by a later one.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal theory, naskh is the divine abrogation of a ruling while the underlying wisdom remains.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for erasure of writing; metaphorical for the supersession of one legal command by another.
- Sībawayh Rule: Taqaddum al-Maʿmūl ʿalā al-ʿĀmil (The precedence of the governed term over its governor) — In the phrase "أحدهما كذب" the predicate (kadhib) is advanced for emphasis, indicating categorical exclusion of falsehood from prophetic speech.
chapters.translation:
Know that conflict (taʿāruḍ) is contradiction (tanāquḍ). If it occurs between two reports, then one of them is false — and falsehood is impossible (muḥāl) with respect to God and His Messenger. If it occurs between two rulings — a command and a prohibition, or a restriction and a permission — then combining them [in application] is an impossible obligation (taklīf muḥāl). Thus either one of them is false, or one is later and abrogating (nāsikh). And it is possible to combine them by applying each to a distinct circumstance, as when [the Prophet] said: "Prayer is obligatory upon my community; prayer is not obligatory upon my community." We then say: He intended by the first the legally responsible (mukallafūn), and by the second the children and the insane — or [he intended] the states of incapacity and capacity, or one time-period rather than another. And if we are unable to combine them, and unable to know which is earlier and which is later, we then preponderate (rajjaḥnā) and adopt the stronger.

The report is strengthened in our minds by the truthfulness of its transmitter and his soundness, and the report is weakened in our minds either by disturbance (iḍṭirāb) in its text (matn), or by weakness in its chain (sanad), or by a matter external to both chain and text. As for what pertains to the chain and the text, they are seventeen:

**First:** The soundness of the text of one of the two reports from discrepancy and disturbance, unlike the other. Its soundness is preponderating, for that which is not disturbed is more akin to the speech of the Messenger. And if to the disturbance of the wording is added disturbance of meaning, it becomes even more remote from being the speech of the Messenger, indicating weakness and the transmitter's laxity in transmission. If it is said: "Then the narration of an addition (ziyādah) in the text of a ḥadīth must be a disturbance necessitating its rejection" — we say: It does not necessarily follow, for it is in the meaning of two separate reports. However, if a transmitter is known for frequent solitary narration (infirād) against reliable memorizers (ḥuffāẓ), then it is permissible that the report of another be preferred over his.

**Second:** Disturbance in the chain, namely that in one of them there is mention of men whose names, epithets, and attributes are confounded with the names and attributes of weak people, such that discrimination becomes difficult.

**Third:** That one of them is narrated within the context of a well-known, widely circulated story among the people of transmission, while its opponent was narrated in isolation by the transmitter, not as part of the story. What is narrated within the collective [context] is stronger in the minds and closer to safety from error than what a single person narrates bare of its well-known story.

**Fourth:** That its transmitter is known for heightened vigilance (tiyaqqaẓ) and few errors, for trust in his narration among people is greater.

**Fifth:** That one of them says: "We heard the Prophet — peace be upon him" — while the other says: "He wrote to me such-and-such." For alteration (taḥrīf) and mispointing (taṣḥīf) occur more in what is written than in what is heard.

**Sixth:** That disagreement attaches to one of the two reports as to whether it is stopped (mawqūf) at the transmitter or raised (marfūʿ) [to the Prophet]. The one agreed upon as raised is more worthy.

**Seventh:** That one is attributed to him as explicit text (naṣṣ) and speech (qawl), while the other is attributed to him as ijtihād — namely, that it is narrated that [something occurred] in his time or in his assembly and he did not denounce it. What is attributed to him as speech and explicit text is stronger, for the explicit text is not susceptible [to alternative interpretation], whereas what occurred in his time perhaps never reached him, and what occurred in his assembly perhaps he was heedless of.

**Eighth:** That one of the two reports is narrated from a person regarding whom conflicting narrations have been transmitted, such that its opposite is also transmitted from him. Then the report [whose transmitter is not subject to conflicting narrations] is preferred over it, for the conflicting narrations cancel each other out (tasāquṭ), leaving the other sound and free from opposition.

**Ninth:** That the transmitter is the one who witnessed the event itself (ṣāḥib al-wāqiʿah); he is more entitled to knowledge than the outsider. Thus the narration of Maymūnah — «The Prophet married me while we were in a state of non-ritual consecration (ḥalālān) after he had returned» — is preferred over the narration of Ibn ʿAbbās «that he married her while he was in a state of ritual consecration (ḥarām)».

**Tenth:** That one of the two transmitters is more just (aʿdal), more trustworthy (awthaq), more precise (aḍbaṭ), more vigilant, and more scrupulous in verification (taḥarrī).

**Eleventh:** That one of the two reports conforms to the practice (ʿamal) of the people of Madīnah; it is therefore stronger. For what Mālik — may God have mercy on him — saw as authoritative is a proof and [tantamount to] consensus (ijmāʿ); and if it is not valid as a proof, it is at least valid for preponderance. For Madīnah is the abode of emigration (dār al-hijrah) and the place of descent of the abrogating revelation, so it is unlikely that [such practice] would be concealed from them.

**Twelfth:** That one of the two reports is supported by the mursal (disconnected) narration of another [transmitter]. It is thereby given preponderance by one who gives preponderance to multiplicity of transmitters. For the mursal is a proof (ḥujjah) according to some; and if it is not a proof, it is at minimum a preponderating factor.

**Thirteenth:** That the community (ummah) acts in accordance with one of the two reports. For if it is possible that their action is based on another evidence, it is equally possible that it is based on this report — so its truthfulness becomes stronger in the mind.

**Fourteenth:** That the Qurʾān, or consensus (ijmāʿ), or the mass-transmitted text (naṣṣ mutawātir), or a rational proof (dalīl al-ʿaql) testifies to the obligation of acting in accordance with the report; it is thereby given preponderance. If it is said: "That is decisive (qāṭiʿ) in affirming its truthfulness" — we say: No. Rather, it is conceivable that someone lied against the Prophet — peace be upon him — regarding what agrees with the Qurʾān and consensus, saying: "I heard what he did not hear." His truthfulness is only necessitated when the community agrees upon his truthfulness, not when they agree upon an action that conforms to his report — for perhaps it was based on another evidence.

**Fifteenth:** That one of the two reports is more specific (akhṣṣ) and the other more general (aʿamm); the more specific to the matter at hand is preferred. This is like preferring his saying: «In the silver of the value of two hundred dirhams, one-fortieth (rubʿ al-ʿushr) is due» — in its obligating [zakāh] upon both the child and the adult — over his saying: «The pen is lifted from three [persons]», for this [latter] addresses the negation of the general address and does not address zakāh, nor the fall of zakāh from the guardian by his paying the zakāh [of the child]. The first ḥadīth addresses the specificity of zakāh and encompasses the generality of the child's wealth, so it is more specific and more pertinent to the matter at hand.

**Sixteenth:** That one of the two reports is independently sufficient in conveying its meaning (mustaqill bi-al-ifādah), while its opponent conveys meaning only by assuming an implicit element (iḍmār) or ellipsis (ḥadhf). This introduces additional obscurity that does not attach to the independent one.

**Seventeenth:** That the transmitters of one of the two reports are more numerous. Multiplicity strengthens conjecture (ẓann), but perhaps a single just person is stronger in the mind than two just persons due to his intense vigilance and precision. Reliance in this matter is upon what predominates in the conjecture of the mujtahid.

These are the factors that necessitate preponderance due to something in the chain of the report or in its text. And it may be given preponderance due to matters external to them, which are five:

**First:** The manner of applying the report in the very locus of the dispute. This is like his saying: «No marriage except with a guardian (walī)» alongside his saying: «The previously-married woman (ayyim) has more right to herself than her guardian.» For we interpret this [latter] as meaning that she has more right to herself in giving permission (idhn), not in contracting (ʿaqd) — and the wording encompasses both permission and contracting. They, however, apply our report to the minor girl, or the slave-woman, or marriage without a suitable match (kufʾ). But the dispute is actually about the adult free woman; they have diverted our report away from the locus of dispute, whereas we have applied both reports to the adult woman. Our interpretation is therefore more fitting, for the wording does not repel it; rather, the wording was susceptible to both. As for applying our report to the minor girl and the slave-woman, that is remote.

**Second:** That one of the two reports entails a diminution of the standing (manṣib) of the Companions; it is therefore weaker. This is like what they narrated of the Prophet — peace be upon him — commanding the Companions to renew their ablution upon loud laughter (qahqahah). Our report — namely his saying: «He used to command us, when we were traveling, not to remove our leather socks (khuffāyn) except due to major impurity (janābah) — not due to urine, excrement, or sleep» — contains no mention of loud laughter, so it is more worthy than their report.

**Third:** That one of the two reports is disputed regarding its specificity (khuṣūṣ), while the other is agreed to be susceptible to specification. Some have said that [the disputed one] drops from consideration as a proof; and if that is not established, it at least indicates its weakness without doubt.

**Fourth:** That one of the two reports was intended to clarify the very ruling under dispute, unlike the other. This is like his saying: «Any hide (ihāb) that is tanned has been purified» — he did not distinguish therein between what is edible and what is not. Thus the indication of its generality upon the skin of what is not edible is stronger than the indication of his prohibition of spreading the skins of beasts of prey; for that [prohibition] was not conveyed to clarify impurity and purity, but rather he may have prohibited spreading them due to pride (khuyalāʾ) or a specific property we do not comprehend.

**Fifth:** That one of the two reports entails the affirmation of what has manifestly shown its effect (athar) upon the ruling, unlike the other. Thus the narration of ʿĀʾishah, Ibn ʿUmar, and Ibn ʿAbbās that Barīrah was manumitted while under a slave [husband] is preferred over what was narrated that she was manumitted while under a free man. For the necessity of slavery (riqq) in [establishing] the option [of annulment] has manifestly shown its effect, and this does not apply in the case of the free man.

chapters.title_en: On What Is Supposed to Be Preponderance (Tarjīḥ) But Is Not
chapters.arabic_text:
### | [القول فيما يظن أنه ترجيح وليس بترجيح]

وله أمثلة ستة:
الأول: أن يعمل أحد الراويين بالخبر دون الآخر أو يعمل بعض الأمة أو بعض
الأئمة بموجب أحد الخبرين فلا يرجح به إذ لا يجب تقليدهم، فالمعمول به وغير
المعمول به واحد.
الثاني: أن يكون أحدهما غريبا لا يشبه الأصول كحديث القهقهة وغرة الجنين
وضرب الدية على العاقلة وخبر نبيذ التمر ودفع القيمة في إحدى عيني الفرس،
فهذه الأحاديث لو صحت لا تؤخر عن معارضها الموافق للأصول؛ لأن للشارع أن
يتعبد بالغريب والمألوف، نعم لو ثبت التقاوم بين الخبرين تساقطا ورجعنا إلى
القياس وذلك ليس من الترجيح في شيء.
الثالث: الخبر الذي لا يدرأ الحد لا يقدم على الموجب وإن كان الحد يسقط
بالشبهة وقال قوم: الرافع أولى؛ وهو ضعيف؛ لأن هذا لا يوجب تفاوتا في صدق
الراوي فيما ينقله من لفظ الإيجاب أو الإسقاط.
الرابع: إذا روي خبران من فعل النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - أحدهما مثبت
والآخر ناف فلا يرجح أحدهما على الآخر لاحتمال وقوعهما في حالين فلا يكون
بينهما تعارض
وقد بينا في باب أفعال النبي - عليه السلام - محل امتناع التعارض بين
الفعلين
الخامس: خبر يتضمن العتق والآخر يتضمن نفيه، قال قوم من أهل العراق:
المثبت للعتق أولى لغلبة العتق؛ ولأنه لا يقبل الفسخ؛ وهذا ضعيف؛ لأن هذا
لا يوجب تفاوتا في صدق الراوي وثبوت نقله
السادس: الخبر الحاظر لا يرجح على المبيح
على ما ظنه قوم لأنهما حكمان شرعيان صدق الراوي فيهما على وتيرة واحدة

### | [الباب الثاني في ترجيح العلل]
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ر-ج-ح (r-j-ḥ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Weightiness, heaviness in the scale; preponderance of one thing over another in measure or merit.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Technical juristic preference of one evidence (dalīl) over a conflicting counterpart based on intrinsic strength, not mere external circumstance.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is physical weight; here used metaphorically (majāz) for epistemic superiority in legal reasoning.
- Root: ق-ه-ق-ه (q-h-q-h) [as in ḥadīth al-qahqaha]
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Loud laughter; in legal context, the specific report on laughter breaking ablution.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): A "strange" (gharīb) report whose ruling diverges from analogical principles (uṣūl).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal laughter; metaphorical extension to a legal case that is anomalous.
- Root: د-ر-أ (d-r-ʾ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Repelling, warding off; in law, averting prescribed punishments (ḥudūd) through ambiguities.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The principle "ward off punishments by doubts" (idraʾū al-ḥudūd bi-l-shubuhāt) — a canonical maxim.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal pushing away; legal metaphor for nullifying penal liability.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional clause with implicit apodosis (sharṭ muqaddar) — e.g., "if they were authentic" (law ṣaḥḥat) implies a suppressed consequent, requiring the reader to supply the legal outcome.
chapters.translation:
I say: This section comprises six examples [of false preponderance]:

**The First:** That one of the two narrators acts upon the report while the other does not, or that some of the Community or some of the imams act upon the import of one of the two reports — this does not constitute preponderance, for there is no obligation to follow them (taqlīd). The acted-upon and the non-acted-upon are equal [in evidentiary status].

**The Second:** That one of the two [reports] be strange (gharīb), bearing no resemblance to the [analogical] principles (uṣūl) — such as the ḥadīth of loud laughter [breaking ablution], the report of the fetal indemnity (ghurrat al-janīn), the imposition of blood-wit (diyah) upon the ʿāqilah [kinsmen], the report concerning date-wine (nabīdh al-tamr), and the payment of value (qīmah) for one of the two eyes of a horse. These reports, even if authentic, are not to be deferred to over their conflicting counterpart that conforms to the principles; for the Lawgiver may impose worship through both the strange and the familiar. Indeed, if mutual equivalence (taqāwum) between the two reports were established, they would both fall away and we would revert to analogical reasoning (qiyās) — and that is not a matter of preponderance at all.

**The Third:** A report that does not avert the prescribed punishment (lā yadraʾ al-ḥadd) is not preferred over one that imposes it, even though the punishment falls away through ambiguity (shubhah). Some said: "The remover is more worthy." But this is weak; for this does not entail any disparity in the truthfulness of the narrator regarding what he transmits — whether the wording be of imposition (ījāb) or of removal (isqāṭ).

**The Fourth:** If two reports are transmitted from the act of the Prophet — peace be upon him — one affirming (muthbit) and the other negating (nāfin), neither is preferred over the other, for it is possible that both occurred in two different states. Thus there is no genuine contradiction between them. We have already explained in the chapter on the acts of the Prophet — peace be upon him — the locus where contradiction between two acts is impossible.

**The Fifth:** A report that entails manumission (ʿitq) and another that entails its negation. Some people of Iraq said: "The one affirming manumission is more worthy, due to the prevalence of manumission, and because it does not admit of rescission (faskh)." But this is weak; for this does not entail any disparity in the truthfulness of the narrator and the establishment of his transmission.

**The Sixth:** The prohibitive report (al-khāẓir) is not preferred over the permissive one (al-mubīḥ), contrary to what some supposed — for both are two legal rulings (ḥukmān sharʿiyyān) in which the truthfulness of the narrator runs on a single course (watīrah wāḥidah).

### | [The Second Chapter: On the Preponderance of Causes (ʿilal)]
